Condensed Group Cohomology
Emma Brink

Abstract
Condensed mathematics as developed by Clausen and Scholze yields a version of derived functors over the category of continuous G G -modules for a Hausdorff topological group G G . In this article, we study the resulting notion of group cohomology and its relation to continuous group cohomology and the condensed/sheaf/singular cohomology of classifying spaces. While condensed group cohomology is generally a more refined invariant than continuous group cohomology, we show that for a broad class of topological groups, continuous group cohomology with solid coefficients, such as locally profinite continuous G G -modules, can be realized as a derived functor in the condensed setting. We also revisit cornerstones of condensed mathematics from [ CS19a ] , paying special attention to set-theoretic size issues. To this end, we review a framework for working with accessible (hyper)sheaves on large sites satisfying suitable accessibility conditions and show that the associated categories retain many topos-like properties. Moreover, we generalize identifications of condensed with sheaf cohomology from [ CS19a ] .



Introduction

For a topological group
G
, one would like to implement group cohomology as a derived fixed-point functor over the category of continuous
G
-modules, but since the category of continuous
G
-modules is not abelian, there is no obvious candidate for such a functor.
One strategy to address this is to embed topological spaces into a topos. This is effective since module categories in a topos are abelian and hence accessible to homological algebra.
Condensed mathematics as introduced in
[
CS19a
]
works along these lines.
Up to set-theoretic size issues, condensed sets are a 1-topos and there is a finite products-preserving functor

\displaystyle\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})

from
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces to condensed sets which is fully faithful on compactly generated topological spaces.
For a Hausdorff
1
1

1

As
\operatorname{T1}
topological groups are Hausdorff, we need to assume that
G
is Hausdorff to evaluate
\underline{(-)}
at
G
.
topological group
G
,
\underline{(-)}
induces a functor from the category of Hausdorff continuous
G
-modules to the category of condensed
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}]
-modules which is fully faithful on continuous
G
-modules whose underlying topological space is compactly generated. The category
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])
of condensed
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}]
-modules is abelian, and we define condensed group cohomology as

H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},-)\coloneqq\operatorname{Ext}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}(\mathbb{Z},-).

In this article, we study its relation to continuous group cohomology (defined in terms of continuous cochains) and the condensed/sheaf/singular cohomology of classifying spaces.

Main results

For a Hausdorff topological group
G
, the Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence (
1.5.13
) for the cover
\underline{G}\to*
yields a natural transformation

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,-)\to H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},-)\circ\underline{(-)}

relating continuous group cohomology to condensed group cohomology. This is an isomorphism in two important cases: For locally profinite groups
3
3

3

We call a group locally profinite if it is locally compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected.
and solid (
Definition

2.8.1
) coefficients, for example locally profinite continuous
G
-modules (
3.3.7
), as well as for locally compact groups and finite-dimensional, continuous real
G
-representations as coefficients (
3.3.9
).

In general, however, condensed group cohomology is a significantly more refined invariant than continuous group cohomology, as the following result illustrates:

Theorem A

(
3.4.3
,
3.4.5
)
.

Suppose
G
is a Hausdorff topological group satisfying one of the following conditions:

(i)

G
is homotopy equivalent to a locally compact Hausdorff space.

(ii)

G
is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible topological space.

For a discrete abelian group
M
, viewed as continuous
G
-module with trivial
G
-action, condensed group cohomology of
\underline{G}
with coefficients in
\underline{M}
is isomorphic to the singular/sheaf cohomology of a classifying space of numerable principal
G

BG
,

H^{*}_{\operatorname{sing}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{*}(BG,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\underline{M}).

By contrast, in the situation of the above theorem, continuous group cohomology only depends on the group of connected components
\pi_{0}G
of
G
.

The idea to define group cohomology by embedding topological spaces into a topos goes back to
[
AGV71
, Exposé IV, section 2.5]
, who worked with the gros topos. Gros topos group cohomology was studied by Flach (
[
Fla08
]
), who established analogues of the above results.
A main advantage of condensed group cohomology over gros topos group cohomology is that more short exact sequences of continuous
G
-modules induce long exact sequences in group cohomology. There is a natural comparison map from gros topos group cohomology to condensed group cohomology, which is an isomorphism in many cases (
Lemma

3.3.12
).

A central feature of the condensed formalism is that there is an extremely well-behaved notion of (non-archimedean) completeness for condensed abelian groups, called
solidity
. We review it in
Section

2.8
. Importantly, if
M
is a locally profinite abelian group, then
\underline{M}
, the image of
M
under the functor
\underline{(-)}
, is solid.
For a condensed ring
{R}
, the category of solid
{R}
-modules
\operatorname{Solid}({R})
(
Definition

2.8.1
) is abelian, has enough projectives, and the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}({R})
has a left adjoint, called
solidification
(
2.8.18
,
2.8.45
,
2.8.16
and
2.8.30
).
We show that, despite being very different from condensed group cohomology, continuous group cohomology with solid coefficients can be realized as a derived functor in the condensed setup for a large class of topological groups:

Theorem B

(
3.5.9
)
.

Suppose that
G
is a Hausdorff topological group which is a finite product of groups of the following types:

(i)

Groups homotopy equivalent to a coproduct of compact Hausdorff spaces, e.g. locally compact abelian groups and locally profinite groups.

(ii)

Groups homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible space.

(iii)

Groups which are locally connected and locally compact.

Then for all solid continuous
G
-modules
M
,

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{Solid}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}(\mathbb{Z},\underline{M}).

It is natural to define the cohomology of a condensed set
X
as

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(X,-)\coloneqq\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[X],-).

Building on results of
[
CS19a
]
, we show that condensed cohomology evaluated at the condensed set
\underline{X}
associated to a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space
X
via the functor
\underline{(-)}
recovers sheaf cohomology of
X
in many cases:

Theorem C

(
2.5.19
)
.

Suppose that
X
is a locally compact Hausdorff space and
M
is a product of a discrete abelian group and a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space.
Then condensed and sheaf cohomology of
X
with coefficients in
M
are naturally isomorphic:

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{*}(X,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{X},\underline{M}).

Theorem D

(
Lemma

2.9.4
)
.

Suppose that
M
is a Hausdorff topological group such that
\underline{M}
is
solid
(
Definition

2.8.1
), e.g.
M
is discrete or more generally locally profinite. Denote by
M^{\delta}
the underlying discrete abelian group.
Suppose
X
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space which is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible space, e.g. a CW-complex. Then there is a natural isomorphism

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{*}(X,M^{\delta})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{X},\underline{M}).

These identifications of sheaf with condensed cohomology are the essential ingredient for our comparison of condensed cohomology with continuous cohomology and the cohomology of classifying spaces.

Condensed sets are sheaves on a large site and therefore not a topos. To obtain a reasonably well-behaved category,
[
CS19a
]
chose to work with the colimit, in the very large category of large categories, over all categories of sheaves on small subsites. In the condensed setting, this is equivalent to restricting to sheaves which are accessible. We discuss this in a more general context in the first chapter and, following
[
Wat75
]
and
[
BH19
]
, formulate accessibility conditions on a large site under which this identification is valid.
While the resulting categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves are typically not presentable, they retain many topos-like features and for instance satisfy all of Girauds’s axioms except accessibility.
We also show that their categories of spectrum objects behave very similar to the stabilization of a presentable
\infty
-category/
\infty
-topos, which leads to a well-behaved notion of spectrum-valued (group) cohomology.
In the second chapter, we review cornerstones of condensed mathematics from
[
CS19a
, Lectures 1-6]
and prove
C
and
D
.
The final chapter studies condensed group cohomology. We first discuss a notion of group cohomology in the general context of
big topoi
(
Definition

1.2.1
) introduced in the first chapter, and then specialize to the condensed setting and prove
A
and
B
.

This article is written in the language of
\infty
-categories as as set down in
[
Lur17
]
,
[
Lur09
]
, and so by a category, we will from now on always mean an
(\infty,1)
-category. Analogously, topos will mean
\infty
-topos. We denote by
\operatorname{An}
the category of animae/spaces/homotopy types.

Outline

We now give a more detailed overview of the contents of this article and sketch the proofs of our main results.

I Accessible sheaves and Higher Algebra in big presentable categories

The category underlying a site is usually required to be small to guarantee the existence of a (hyper)sheafification functor.
However, there are many contexts where one wishes to study sheaves on large categories, and where no general sheafification functor exists, for example the fpqc topology on affine schemes (
[
Wat75
]
).
Following
[
Wat75
]
,
[
BH19
]
, we describe accessibility conditions on an
explicit covering site
(
Definition

1.1.1
) under which accessible presheaves can be (hyper)sheafified.
It is natural to work with accessible presheaves over a coaccessible category
\mathcal{C}
, since these are precisely the small colimits of representables.

The accessibility conditions ensure that the resulting categories of (hyper)accessible sheaves are, despite typically not presentable, reasonably well-behaved and retain many topos-like properties. For instance, they satisfy all of Giraud’s axioms except accessibility.
Adapting a result of
[
Man22
]
, we show that for a presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{C}
, categories of
\mathcal{C}
-valued accessible (hyper)sheaves on (hyper)accessible explicit covering sites inherit a closed symmetric monoidal structure (
1.1.28
).
This all follows from a description of the category of accessible (hyper)sheaves on (hyper)accessible explicit covering sites as a large filtered colimit of topoi along fully faithful, left-exact left adjoints (in the very large category of large categories).
We call (large) categories arising this way
big topoi
(
Definition

1.2.1
).
Topoi and categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves on a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site are big topoi. Moreover, if
G
is a group object in a big topos, the category of
G
-objects is itself a big topos (
3.1.4
).
More generally, we call a (possibly large) category
big presentable
if it arises as a (possibly
large) filtered colimit, taken in the category of large categories, of presentable categories along
fully faithful, left-exact left adjoints. This notion is tailored to guarantee that the category of
spectrum objects in a big presentable category behaves like the stabilization of a presentable category in many aspects:

Theorem E
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentable category.

(i)

The category
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
of spectrum objects in
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is stable
(
Lemma

1.3.2
), and big presentable (
Lemma

1.3.5
).

(ii)

The infinite loop space functor
\Omega^{\infty}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}

admits a left adjoint
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),
which factors into left adjoints

\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

(
Lemma

1.3.10
).

(iii)

There is a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
whose connective part is generated by the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
under small colimits and extensions (
Lemma

1.3.12
).

(iv)

If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big topos, then
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
factors over an equivalence
\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
.

(v)

For a stable, big presentable category
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
, pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
defines a fully faithful functor

(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}),

where
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(-,-)
refers to small colimits preserving functors. If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
admit small coproducts, then
(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}
is an equivalence (
1.3.20
).

The stabilization functor
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
moreover interacts well with (symmetric) monoidal structures. We define big presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories (
Definition

1.3.22
) and show that the (symmetric) monoidal structure on a big presentably (symmetric) monoidal category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
induces a (symmetric) monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}
such that
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
enhances to a (symmetric) monoidal functor
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}
(
Proposition

1.3.26
). This in particular applies to big topoi with the cartesian monoidal structure. For categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves, it recovers the closed symmetric monoidal structure induced by the smash product on spectra (
Lemma

1.3.28
).
We describe a universal property of the (symmetric) monoidal structure on the stabilization (
Proposition

1.3.26
), and show the following:

Lemma F

(
1.3.30
)
.

For a stable, big presentably (symmetric) monoidal category
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
, pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}
induces a fully faithful functor

(\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+})^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}),

where
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(-,-)
refers to the category of small colimits preserving, (symmetric) monoidal functors.
Its essential image consists of those colimit-preserving, symmetric monoidal functors
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
which factor over
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\xrightarrow{\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
.
If
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
admit small coproducts, then
(\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+})^{*}
is an equivalence.

In
1.3.35
, we describe a natural spectral enrichment of the category of spectrum objects
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
in a big presentable category
\mathcal{X}
. We use the spectrum-valued mapping functors
\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(-,-)
to define cohomology as

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{\mathcal{X}}}(-,-)\coloneqq\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}-,-)\colon\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}.

This notion enjoys the expected properties, including a Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence (
1.5.13
) for the cohomology groups
\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(-,-)\coloneqq\pi_{-*}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,-)
. Since every adjunction between stable, big presentable categories is spectrally enriched (
1.3.40
), every geometric morphism
L\colon\mathcal{X}\leftrightarrows\mathcal{Y}\colon R
(
Definition

1.5.6
) between big topoi induces an equivalence

(0.1)

\displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,R_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{Y}}(L-,-),

where
R_{\operatorname{Sp}}
denotes the
stabilization
(
Definition

1.3.3
) of
R
. In particular, cohomology in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
can always be computed in a subcategory
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
which is a topos.

In
Section

1.4
we record structural properties of module categories in big presentably monoidal categories which we will use in our discussion of group cohomology in big topoi.
We show that for an algebra
{R}
in a big presentably monoidal category
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
, the category of left
{R}
-modules
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is itself big presentable (
Lemma

1.4.9
).
Moreover, if
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is big presentably symmetric monoidal, for a commutative algebra
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C})
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
inherits the structure of a big presentably symmetric monoidal category (
1.4.13
).
Under mild conditions on
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
, this monoidal structure is closed:

Lemma G

(
Lemma

1.4.5
)
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a potentially large, closed symmetric monoidal category which has all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and all
\Delta
-indexed limits.
For
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C})
, the induced symmetric monoidal structure (
1.4.2
) on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is closed.

For a big presentably monoidal category
\mathcal{X}
and an algebra
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\geq 0})
, the category of left
R
-modules in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
inherits a
t
-structure (
1.4.21
).
If
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos, the heart of this
t
-structure is equivalent to the 1-category
\operatorname{LMod}_{\pi_{0}{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})
of underived
\pi_{0}{R}
-modules in
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
.
(Un)derived module categories in big topoi behave different than in ordinary topoi. For instance, the category of discrete abelian group objects
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
in a topos
\mathcal{X}
is Grothendieck abelian (
[
AGV71
, Exposé 2, 6.7]
) and in particular has functorial injective embeddings (
[
Sta22
,
Tag 079H
]
), whereas the category of condensed abelian groups has no non-zero injectives (
[
Sch22
]
).
Adapting
[
Lur18a
, Theorem 2.1.2.2]
, we describe conditions on a big topos
\mathcal{X}
under which

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\pi_{0}{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\pi_{0}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}),

see
Lemma

1.4.32
. This applies in particular to
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
:

Lemma H

(
2.6.7
)
.

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})}).

Such an equivalence is instructive as we have better control about the categorical properties of the right-hand side. It also allows to identify our definition of cohomology with more classical definitions in terms of Ext-groups:
If
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos satisfying
Lemma

1.4.32
, for
X\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
and
A\in\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\heartsuit}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(X,A)=\operatorname{Ext}_{\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}^{*}(\mathbb{Z}[X],\mathbb{Z}).

II Condensed mathematics

In the second chapter, we review cornerstones of condensed mathematics from
[
CS19a
, Lectures 1-6]
, paying special attention to set-theoretic size issues and using the language of
\infty
-categories.
As preparation, we recall the notion of
weight
of topological spaces and related categorical properties of the categories of compact Hausdorff spaces and profinite sets.
A condensed anima is roughly a hypersheaf on the site of profinite sets with finite, jointly surjective covers.
There are different ways to deal with the fact that profinite sets are a large category:

•

[
BH19
]
fix universes
\mathcal{U}\in\mathcal{V}
and work with hypersheaves of
\mathcal{V}
-small animae on the category
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\mathcal{U}}
of
\mathcal{U}
-small profinite sets. This yields the category of pyknotic animae
\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}}^{\mathcal{V}}
(with respect to
\mathcal{U}\in\mathcal{V}
).

•

More generally, one can consider sheaves on the small category of
\kappa
-light profinite sets (
Definition

2.1.4
) for a fixed small, uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, this yields the category of
\kappa
-condensed animae
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
.
[
CS23
]
work with
\operatorname{Cond}_{\aleph_{1}}(\operatorname{An})
for
\aleph_{1}
the smallest uncountable regular cardinal, and call this the category of light condensed animae.

•

[
CS19a
]
work with accessible, condensed hypersheaves
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}
(
Proposition

1.1.5
,
Definition

2.4.2
). This yields the category of condensed animae
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.

Remark
.

Suppose we work internal to a universe
\mathcal{U}_{0}
.
If
\kappa\in\mathcal{U}_{0}
is a small regular strong limit cardinal and
\mathcal{U}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{U}_{0}
is the universe associated to
{\kappa}
, i.e. the set of
\kappa
-small sets, then

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})=\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}^{\mathcal{U}_{1}}

is the category of pyknotic animae corresponding to
\mathcal{U}_{\kappa}\in\mathcal{U}_{0}
. If
\mathcal{U}_{0}\in\mathcal{U}_{1}\in\mathcal{U}_{2}
are further universes, there are fully faithful left adjoints

\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}^{\mathcal{U}_{1}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{1}},

where
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{i}}
refers to the categories of condensed animae computed in
\mathcal{U}_{i}
, see
2.4.4
.

The category of condensed animae is not presentable and in particular not a topos; however our discussion from the first chapter implies that it retains many topos-like properties, making it a reasonable category to work in.
More precisely, the category of condensed animae is a big topos and can be expressed as large filtered colimit of the categories
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
along fully faithful, left-exact left adjoints, where
\kappa
runs over all small uncountable regular cardinals, or alternatively all small strong limit cardinals (
2.4.9
).
The latter was the original definition of
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
given in
[
CS19a
]
and is instructive as for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\cong\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
enjoys particularly favorable properties (
2.3.7
). For instance,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
has enough projectives for all strong limit cardinals
\kappa
, which implies that the same holds for
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
(
2.6.5
). It follows from these colimit-descriptions of
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
that many computations such as small limits, colimits, and cohomology can be carried out within a topos
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
for a sufficiently large regular/strong limit cardinal
\kappa
.
We recall that (
\kappa
-)condensed sets are a good approximation to topological spaces:

Proposition

(
[
CS19a
]
,
Proposition

2.2.7
,
Section

2.4.2
)
.

(i)

For every uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, there is a right adjoint

\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set}).

This functor is fully faithful on
\kappa
-compactly generated (
Definition

2.1.15
) spaces. Its left adjoint sends a
\kappa
-condensed set
X
to a
\kappa
-compactly generated topological space with set of points
X(*)
.

(ii)

There is a functor

\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})

which is fully faithful on compactly generated topological spaces and admits a partially defined left adjoint.

In
Section

2.3
, we apply the functor
\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}
to describe
\kappa
-condensed animae as hypersheaves on the category of all
\lambda
-small topological spaces (for
\lambda\geq\kappa
), which we apply to generalize comparison results between condensed and sheaf cohomology from
[
CS19a
]
.

Comparison of condensed with sheaf cohomology and proof of
C
and
D

[
CS19a
]
constructed a comparison map from sheaf to condensed cohomology for compact Hausdorff spaces. Our description of
\kappa
-condensed animae as hypersheaves on the category of all
\lambda
-small topological spaces allows to extend this comparison map to arbitrary topological spaces.
More concretely, for
\lambda\geq\kappa
we construct a left-exact left adjoint

{j}^{*}\colon\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})

from the gros topos of
\lambda
-small topological spaces (
Definition

2.5.12
), which sends a
\lambda
-small topological space
X
to the associated
\kappa
-condensed set
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
.
For a
\lambda
-small topological space
X
, gros topos cohomology recovers sheaf cohomology (see
2.5.17
for a precise statement).
Using the geometric morphism
{j}^{*}\dashv{j}_{*}
and (
0.1
), we obtain for a
\kappa
-condensed abelian group
A
a comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A_{\kappa})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(X,\pi_{0}j_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(X,j_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A),

where
A_{\kappa}
denotes the sheaf

\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}\ni U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A).

This comparison map is by construction natural in the
\lambda
-small topological space
X
. If
X
is
\operatorname{T1}
, for regular cardinals
\kappa>|X|
,
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}{}(\underline{X},A)
(
2.5.4
).
We then apply descent of gros topos and condensed cohomology along
local section covers
(

) and results from

]
on the condensed cohomology of compact Hausdorff spaces and the solidification of free condensed abelian groups on topological spaces to prove

and
D
.

Solid modules

In the second half of the second chapter, we review the notion of solidity, the condensed analogue of (non-archimedean) completeness for abelian groups. In preparation for that, we recall basic properties of derived and underived condensed module categories (
Section

2.6
) and some compactness properties of condensed abelian groups (
Section

2.7
).
For a condensed ring
{R}
, we define the category of solid
{R}
-modules
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
as the full subcategory of condensed
{R}
-modules whose underlying condensed abelian group is solid (
Definition

2.8.1
).
This enjoys excellent formal properties:

(i)

\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is an abelian subcategory closed under small limits, colimits and extensions (
Lemmas

2.8.15
and
2.8.30
), and has enough projectives (
2.8.18
and
2.8.45
).

(ii)

The forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
, called solidification. (
2.8.16
and
2.8.30
). For a commutative condensed ring
{R}
,
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is a symmetric monoidal localisation, i.e. there exists a symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
such that
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor (
Lemma

2.8.44
).

(iii)

In many cases, the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
, for instance for
\kappa=\aleph_{1}
, for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
, for
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
, as well as for
{R}=\mathbb{Z}
and more generally for
{R}=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]
for a Hausdorff topological group
G
(
2.8.61
,
2.8.58
,
2.8.59
,
2.8.23
,
2.8.33
and
2.8.27
). We call the left-adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
derived solidification. It agrees with the derived functor of solidification at points where the latter is defined (
2.8.35
).

(iv)

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a local subcategory and the left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
is a symmetric monoidal localisation. The induced symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
is closed (
2.8.40
).

To prove these statements, we slightly adapt the arguments from
[
CS19a
]
, who proved the above results for
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
and
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
.
We review computations of the derived and underived solidification of free condensed abelian groups on compact Hausdorff spaces and CW-complexes (
2.8.51
and
2.8.53
). These computations imply that condensed cohomology with solid coefficients is homotopy invariant (
2.9.2
) and serve as the essential ingredient for the proofs of
D
and
B
.

We moreover characterize (
\kappa
-)condensed rings for which the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}))

factors over an equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}))})

(
Proposition

2.8.56
) and call them (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat. Condensed rings represented by (
\kappa
-light) profinite topological rings (
2.8.60
), as well as group rings
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]
for Hausdorff topological groups

are (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat (
Lemma

2.8.59
). All light condensed rings are
\aleph_{1}
-
s
-flat (
2.8.58
).

(
\kappa
-)
s
-flatness implies that the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
(
2.8.61
). For commutative (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat condensed rings, there is a closed symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
such that
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor (

).

III Group Cohomology

In the third chapter, we finally discuss group cohomology.
We first review the category of
G
-objects in a big topos. This category is itself a big topos (
3.1.4
), and we define group cohomology as cohomology of its terminal object.
4
4

4

If
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos as in
Lemma

1.4.32
and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits, for a discrete group
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
and
A\in\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})
,

H_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(G,A)=\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}(\mathbb{Z},A),

see
3.2.3
. This in particular applies to
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
.

Under mild assumptions on a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, there exists a
derived fixed-point functor

(-)^{G}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})

refining group cohomology (
Lemma

3.2.12
). We discuss this very briefly before specializing to (
\kappa
-)condensed group cohomology. For the purpose of readability, we focus on condensed group cohomology in this introduction, but we will also prove
\kappa
-condensed analogues of all results below.

Comparison to the cohomology of classifying spaces and proof of
A

By
[
NSS15
]
, for a group object
G
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, the homotopy orbit functor (
Definition

3.1.8
)

-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}

exhibits the category of
G
-objects in
\mathcal{X}
as classifying topos for principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles and factors over an equivalence
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
, where
\mathbb{B}G\coloneqq*//G
denotes the classifying space of principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles in
\mathcal{X}
(
3.1.19
).
In particular, group cohomology with coefficients in a
G
-module
M
with trivial
G
-action is isomorphic to the cohomology of
\mathbb{B}G
with coefficients in
M
(
Proposition

3.2.7
).

For a Hausdorff topological group
G
, every principal
G
-bundle
E\to B
(with
B
T1) defines a principal
\infty
-
\underline{G}
-bundle
\underline{E}\to\underline{B}
in condensed animae which is classified by a map
\underline{B}\to\mathbb{B}G
(
Lemma

3.4.2
). Pullback along this map yields a comparison map

H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\operatorname{triv}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\mathbb{B}\underline{G},-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{B},-)

from condensed group cohomology of
G
with coefficients in modules with trivial
G
-action to condensed cohomology of
B
.
If
0\neq G
, the map
\underline{BG}\to\mathbb{B}G
classifying a universal numerable principal
G
-bundle
EG\to BG
is not an equivalence as
\underline{BG}\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
whereas
\pi_{1}\mathbb{B}G=\underline{G}
. However, homotopy invariance of condensed cohomology with coefficients in solid abelian groups implies the following:

Theorem I

(
3.4.3
)
.

Suppose that
G
is a Hausdorff topological group and
BG
is a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles which is
\operatorname{T1}
.
5
5

5

This exists by
Lemma

3.4.1
.

For a solid abelian group
M
,

H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\operatorname{triv}M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{BG},M).

For many topological groups, the condensed cohomology of a classifying space
BG
of numerable principal
G
-bundles with coefficients in a discrete abelian group can be identified with its singular and sheaf cohomology, see
Section

3.4.1
. This then implies

.

Solid group cohomology and proof of
B

When restricted to solid coefficients,
\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{Solid}(\mathbb{Z}[G])}(\mathbb{Z},-)
is a natural alternative to condensed group cohomology. We refer to this as solid group cohomology. As we show in
Section

2.8
, solid
\mathbb{Z}[G]
-modules admit plenty projectives, which makes solid group cohomology more computationally accessible than condensed group cohomology.
Projective solid abelian groups are stable under solid tensor products (
2.8.46
). This implies the following:

Lemma J

(
3.5.15
)
.

Suppose that
G
is a Hausdorff topological group such that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}
.
Then
k
-continuous (
Definition

3.3.4
) group cohomology is isomorphic to solid group cohomology,

H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}}(\mathbb{Z},\underline{(-)}).

Our computations from
Section

2.8
moreover show that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}]^{{\square}}
is projective for large classes of topological groups (
3.5.9
), which then implies

.

Notation and conventions

This article is written in the language of
\infty
-categories as set down in
[
Lur17
]
,
[
Lur09
]
, and so by a category, we always mean an
(\infty,1)
-category unless stated explicitly otherwise. Analogously, topos means
\infty
-topos.
We need to assume the existence of Grothendieck universes
\mathcal{U}_{0}\in\mathcal{U}_{1}\in\mathcal{U}_{2}
to prove structural results on condensed animae and more generally big topoi/big presentable categories. We fix these universes once and for all and refer to categories in
\mathcal{U}_{0}
as small, categories in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
as large and categories in
\mathcal{U}_{2}
as very large. We denote by
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
the very large category of large categories.

We moreover use the following notation:

•

We write
\operatorname{An}
for the category of small animae/
\infty
-groupoids/spaces/(weak) homotopy types.

•

\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
denotes the category of presentable categories (in
\mathcal{U}_{0}
) and left adjoint functors.

•

Unless stated otherwise, all cardinals are assumed to be small. If
\kappa
and
\lambda
are regular cardinals, we write
\lambda\ll\kappa
if for all cardinals
\lambda_{0}<\lambda
and
\kappa_{0}<\kappa
,
\kappa_{0}^{\lambda_{0}}<\kappa
, see the discussion around
[
Lur09
, Definition 5.4.2.8]
for examples.

•

For a symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
, we denote by
\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C})\coloneqq\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathbb{E}_{\infty}}(\mathcal{C})
its category of commutative algebra objects.

•

If
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}
is a monoidal category, we denote by
\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})\coloneqq\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathbb{A}_{\infty}}(\mathcal{C})
the category of associative algebras in
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
.

•

For a topos
\mathcal{X}
, we denote by
\operatorname{hyp}\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
the subcategory on hypercomplete objects (
[
Lur09
, page 666]
).

•

For a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
and an uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, we denote by
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})
the category of
\kappa
-condensed objects in
\mathcal{C}
(

2.2.1
) and by
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
the category of condensed objects (
Definition

2.4.2
). We use
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathcal{C})
as placeholder for any of the two categories.

•

We denote by

\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})

and

\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})

the functors defined in

and

, respectively. We will always view
(\operatorname{T1})

\kappa
-)condensed sets via those functors, and drop the
\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)}
occasionally.

•

We denote by

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,-)\colon\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}

the cohomology functor (
Definition

1.5.1
) of a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, and by
\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(-,-)\coloneqq\pi_{-*}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,-)
the underlying cohomology groups.
If it exists, internal cohomology in
\mathcal{X}
(
Definition

1.5.1
) is denoted

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,-)\colon\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}).

We denote by

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,-)\coloneqq\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}(-,-)\text{ and }\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,-)\coloneqq\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})cond}}(-,-)

the cohomology and internal cohomology in

, respectively.

•

For a group object
G
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}

denotes the group cohomology functor of

(

(
Definition

3.2.1
). For a (

its group cohomology and internal group cohomology, respectively.

•

We call totally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces profinite. This is justified by
Lemma

2.1.1
. Locally profinite means locally compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected.

Our main motivation to work with
\infty
-categories is that it makes the comparison of condensed group cohomology with cohomology of classifying spaces conceptually transparent.

Relation to other work

1
Accessible sheaves and Higher Algebra in big presentable categories

In the definition of sites, the underlying category is usually required to be small to guarantee the existence of a (hyper)sheafification functor and that the associated categories of (hyper)sheaves form a topos. However, there are many situations where this smallness assumption fails and no general sheafification functor exists, for example the fpqc topology on affine schemes, cf.
[
Wat75
]
.
Following
[
Wat75
]
and
[
BH19
, Section 1.4]
, we formulate accessibility conditions on an
explicit covering site
(
Definition

1.1.1
) under which accessible presheaves can be sheafified.
The accessibility conditions ensure that the resulting categories of (hyper)accessible sheaves are, despite typically not presentable, reasonably well-behaved and retain many topos-like properties. For instance, they satisfy all of Giraud’s axioms except accessibility. Moreover, their categories of spectrum objects as well as module categories therein behave very similar to those of presentable categories (
Section

1.3
,
Section

1.4
).
To prove this, it is convenient to work with a class of so-called
big presentable categories
(
Definition

1.2.1
), which encompasses categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves, presentable categories, as well as module categories therein.
The notion of big presentable category is arranged so that their categories of spectrum objects closely resemble those of presentable categories.
This chapter is structured as follows: We first discuss accessibility conditions of explicit covering sites and basic properties of the associated categories of (hyper)complete sheaves.
Then we show that spectrum objects in big presentable categories behave similar as for presentable categories (
Section

1.3
).
In
Section

1.4
, we record structural properties of module categories, in particular the existence of (closed) symmetric monoidal structures. We also briefly review derived categories.
There is a natural notion of spectrum-valued cohomology in a
big topos
which we discuss in
Section

1.5
.

1.1
Sheaves on (hyper)accessible explicit covering sites

We now recall from
[
Lur18a
, section A.3.2]
a construction of Grothendieck topologies which allows a very explicit characterization of (hyper)complete sheaves. This will lead us to conditions on a site under which the category of accessible (hyper)sheaves retains many properties of a topos and accessible presheaves can be (hyper)sheafified.

Definition 1.1.1
.

[
Man22
, Definition A.3.12]
,
[
Lur18a
, section A.3.2]

An
explicit covering site

(\mathcal{C},S)
consists of a (possibly large) category
\mathcal{C}
and a wide subcategory
S\subseteq\mathcal{C}
satisfying the following conditions:

(i)

\mathcal{C}
has finite coproducts and pullbacks.

(ii)

Finite coproducts in
\mathcal{C}
are universal, i.e. given a diagram
\coprod_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}\to d\leftarrow e
, the canonical map
\coprod_{i=1}^{n}(c_{i}\times_{d}e)\to(\coprod_{i=1}^{n}c_{i})\times_{d}e
is an equivalence.

(iii)

Coproducts in
\mathcal{C}
are disjoint, i.e. for
c,d\in\mathcal{C},c\times_{c\sqcup d}d
is an initial object of
\mathcal{C}
.

(iv)

S
contains all equivalences and
f\circ g\in S\Rightarrow f\in S
.

(v)

S
is stable under pullbacks, i.e. for
s\colon A\to B\in S
and
Y\to B\in\mathcal{C}
,
A\times_{B}Y\to Y\in S
.

(vi)

S
is stable under finite coproducts, i.e. for
\{s_{i}\colon x_{i}\to y_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}\subseteq S
,

\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}s_{i}\colon\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}\to\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}y_{i}\in S.

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a small explicit covering site (i.e.
\mathcal{C}
is a small category), the sieves
\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
for which there exists a finite subset
F\subseteq I
with
\sqcup_{i\in F}c_{i}\to c\in S
constitute a Grothendieck topology on
\mathcal{C}
by
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.2.1]
.

Example 1.1.2
.

(\text{Affine schemes},\text{faithfully flat morphisms})
is an explicit covering site. The associated site is the fpqc topology on affine schemes.

(Hyper)sheaves in the Grothendieck topology associated to an explicit covering site admit a very explicit description which we recall now.

Definition 1.1.3

(Hypercovers,
[
Lur18a
, Definition A.5.7.1]
)
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is an explicit covering site.
Denote by
\Delta_{s,+}
the category with objects the linearly ordered sets

[n]\coloneqq\{0\leq\ldots\leq n\},n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq-1}

and morphisms the strictly increasing maps.
A functor
U\colon\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
is called an
augmented semi-simplicial object
in
\mathcal{C}
.
For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, denote by
\Delta_{s,+,<n}\subseteq\Delta_{s,+}
the full subcategory on linearly ordered sets
[k]
,
k<n
and by

M_{n}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{i^{*}}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta_{s,+,<n}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{i_{*}}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})

the composition of restriction and right Kan extension along
i\colon\Delta_{s,+,<n}\subseteq\Delta_{s,+}
.
The right Kan extension exists since
\mathcal{C}
has finite limits and
{\Delta_{s,+,<n}}_{/k}
is finite for all
k\in\Delta_{s,+}
.

An augmented semi-simplicial object
U_{*}\colon\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
is an
S
-
hypercover
if for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the unit
U\to M_{n}U
evaluates to a morphism
U([n])\to M_{n}U([n])
in
S
.
Denote by
\Delta_{s}\subseteq\Delta_{s,+}
the full subcategory on objects
[n],n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.

Definition 1.1.4

(Sheaves on explicit covering sites)
.

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},S)
is an explicit covering site and
\mathcal{D}
is a category.

(i)

The category of
\mathcal{D}
-valued
S
-sheaves

{\operatorname{Shv}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

is the full subcategory of finite products-preserving functors
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
such that
for all
s\colon x\to y\in S
,

\Delta_{+}\xrightarrow{\check{C}(s)}\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\xrightarrow{F}\mathcal{D}

is a limit diagram, where
\check{C}(s)\colon\Delta_{+}\to\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
denotes the (opposite of) the Čech nerve of
s
.

(ii)

The category of
\mathcal{D}
-valued hypercomplete
S
-sheaves

\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

is the full subcategory of finite products-preserving functors
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
such that for all
S
-hypercovers
U_{*}\colon\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
,

\Delta_{s,+}\xrightarrow{U_{*}}\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\xrightarrow{F}\mathcal{D}

is a limit diagram.

This terminology is compatible with
[
Lur09
, Notation 6.3.5.16]
:

Proposition 1.1.5

(
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.3.1, Proposition A.5.7.2]
)
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a small explicit covering site (i.e.
\mathcal{C}
is small), denote by
\tau_{S}
the associated Grothendieck topology on
\mathcal{C}
(
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.2.1]
), and by
\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})
the topoi of (hypercomplete,
[
Lur09
, p. 666]
)
\tau_{S}
-sheaves.
Suppose that
\mathcal{D}
is a category with small limits.

(i)

Restriction along the sheafified Yoneda embedding
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}
induces an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).

(ii)

Restriction along the hypersheafified Yoneda embedding
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}
is an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).

Proof.

By
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.3.1]
, a functor
F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
is in
\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
if and only if for all covering sieves
S\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
,
F
exhibits
F(c)
as limit of the diagram
F|_{S}
.
Since
\mathcal{D}
has all small colimits and
\mathcal{C}
is small,
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
.
As
\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is the localization of
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
at the maps
S\to h_{c}
for covering sieves
S\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
, this implies that the above equivalence restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).

By
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.5.7.2]
, a functor
F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
is in
\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
if and only if for all
d\in\mathcal{D}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,F-)\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}

is a hypercomplete
\tau_{S}
-sheaf, i.e. local with respect to
\infty
-connective morphisms in
\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})
.
As the functors
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,-),d\in\mathcal{D}
are jointly conservative and
\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})
is the localization at the
\infty
-connective morphisms, it follows that the above equivalence restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).\qed

Remark 1.1.6
.

If in the situation of the above lemma,
\mathcal{D}
is presentable, then

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}

is the tensor product of presentable categories (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
):
By
[
Lur09
, Theorem 6.1.0.6]
, the topos
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})
is presentable and by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.17]
and
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.2.6.2, Remark 5.5.2.10]
, for presentable categories
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D}
,

\mathcal{X}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{R}(\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{op}})^{\operatorname{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{op}})^{\operatorname{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}).

The above description of (hyper)sheaves on explicit covering sites leads to conditions on an explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
under which its category of accessible (hyper)sheaves retains many properties of a topos and accessible presheaves can be (hyper)sheafified:

Definition 1.1.7
.

Suppose
\kappa
is a regular cardinal.
6
6

6

A cardinal
\kappa
is regular if
\kappa
-small colimits of
\kappa
-small sets are
\kappa
-small. A set
S
is
\kappa
-small if it has cardinality less than
\kappa
.

(i)

An explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)

\kappa
-
accessible
if
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-coaccessible and for all
s\colon X\to Y\in S
, there exists a
\kappa
-cofiltered diagram

s_{*}\colon I\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})\cap S

such that
s={\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}s_{i}
, where
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
denotes the full subcategory of
\kappa
-cocompact objects.
7
7

7

As
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-coaccessible, it has
\kappa
-filtered limits. In particular, for every small category
K
,
\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal{C})
has
\kappa
-filtered limits and they can be computed pointwise.

An explicit covering site is
accessible
if for all small regular cardinals
\kappa
, there exists a small regular cardinal
\lambda\geq\kappa
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-accessible.
If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is an accessible explicit covering site, denote by

\operatorname{Shv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\coloneqq\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\cap\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

the full subcategory on accessible
S
-sheaves
F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
.

(ii)

An explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-
hyperaccessible
if
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-coaccessible and for all
S
-hypercoverings
X_{*}\colon\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}_{+}\to\mathcal{C}
, there exists a
\kappa
-cofiltered diagram of
S
-hypercoverings

s_{*}\colon I\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta_{+}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})

with
{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}(s_{i}\colon X_{*}^{i}\to X^{i})=(X_{*}\to X)
. Again,
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
denotes the category of
\kappa
-cocompact objects.

An explicit covering site is
hyperaccessible
if for all small regular cardinals
\kappa
there exists a small regular cardinal
\lambda\geq\kappa
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-hyperaccessible.
If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a hyperaccessible explicit covering site, denote by

\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\coloneqq\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\cap\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

the full subcategory on accessible, hypercomplete
S
-sheaves.

For a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
, we denote by

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\coloneqq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})

the category of
\operatorname{An}
-valued accessible (hyper)sheaves.

Remarks 1.1.8
.

1.

It is natural to consider accessible presheaves on a coaccessible, locally small category since this is its free cocompletion under small colimits, see
[
HP24
, Proposition A.2]
.
More generally, if
\mathcal{C}
is small and
i\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{idem}}
is an idempotent completion (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.18]
), then
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{idem}}
is small (
[
Lur09
, Lemma 5.4.2.4]
), and left Kan extension along
i
is an equivalence

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\cong\mathcal{P}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{idem}}).

In particular, every presheaf category arises as category of accessible presheaves. If
\mathcal{C}
is coaccessible and small, then every functor
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}
is accessible by
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.4.3.6]
.

2.

(Hyper)accessibility of an explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
implies that

(1.1.8.1)

\displaystyle{\underset{\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\subseteq C}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}),

where the colimit on the left is over the large poset of all small subcategories of
\mathcal{C}
which are closed under finite limits, and the transition maps are the left adjoints of restriction, see
1.1.22
below. The colimit is computed in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
.
In particular, a (hyper)sheaf on a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site is accessible if and only if it is left Kan extended from a sheaf on a small subcategory.

3.

(Hyper)accessibility of an explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
ensures that there exists a (hyper)sheafification functor for accessible presheaves, i.e.

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})

has a left-exact left adjoint, see
1.1.23
below. This follows from the colimit-description
1.1.8.1
.

4.

Note that in general, (hyper)accessibility is a stronger condition than being
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible for some cardinal
\kappa
. However, if
(\mathcal{C},S)
is an explicit covering site such that the collection of
S
-(hyper)covers is closed under
\kappa
-filtered limits, then
\kappa
-(hyper)accessibility implies (hyper)accessibility, see
Lemma

1.1.26
below.

5.

[
BH19
]
call
\kappa
-accessible explicit covering sites
\kappa
-accessible presites. They define accessible explicit covering sites as explicit covering sites which are accessible for some regular cardinal
\kappa
, but our stronger condition seems to be necessary to obtain the colimit-description of accessible sheaves (
1.1.21
), which ensures that this retains many properties of a topos and accessible presheaves can be sheafified.

Example 1.1.9
.

The explicit covering site
(\text{Affine schemes},\text{faithfully flat morphisms})
is
\kappa
-accessible for every uncountable cardinal by
[
Wat75
, Theorem 3.3]
.

Notation 1.1.10
.

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible explicit covering site, denote by
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
the full subcategory on
\kappa
-cocompact objects. Then
(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},S\cap\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}))
is an explicit covering site.
For a category
\mathcal{D}
denote by
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
the associated category of
\mathcal{D}
-valued (hypercomplete) sheaves on
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
.

The definition of
\kappa
-(hyper)accessibility is tailored so that the following holds:

Theorem 1.1.11

(
[
BH19
, Proposition 1.4.3]
,
[
Man22
, Lemma A.2.8]
)
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a
\kappa
-accessible explicit covering site and
\mathcal{D}
is a category with small limits and colimits and
\Delta
-indexed limits commute with
\kappa
-filtered colimits in
\mathcal{D}
.
Denote by
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
the full subcategory of
\kappa
-cocompact objects and by
\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}{\underset{}{\operatorname{colim}}}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
the full subcategory on functors which preserve
\kappa
-filtered colimits.

(i)

The restriction
r^{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
has a fully faithful left adjoint
i_{\kappa}
which factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}).

(ii)

This restricts to an adjunction

r^{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\colon i_{\kappa},

and
i_{\kappa}
factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}{\underset{}{\operatorname{colim}}}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cap\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).

(iii)

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-hyperaccessible, then the adjunction
r^{\kappa}\vdash i_{\kappa}
restricts to an adjoint pair

r^{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\colon i_{\kappa},

and
i_{\kappa}
factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}{\underset{}{\operatorname{colim}}}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cap\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).

Remark 1.1.12
.

If
\mathcal{D}
is a
\mu
-accessible category, then
\mu
-small limits commute with
\mu
-filtered colimits in
\mathcal{D}
, see e.g.
[
Man22
, Lemma A.2.8]
.
In particular, for uncountable cardinals
\mu\leq\kappa
,
\mu
-accessible categories satisfy the condition of the above theorem.

Proof.

This is a very straightforward generalization of
[
BH19
, Proposition 1.4.3]
or
[
Man22
, Proposition 2.1.8]
.
We first explain that restriction has a left adjoint.
As
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-coaccessible, for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
{c\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
is essentially small (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
).
Since
\mathcal{D}
has all small colimits, this implies that for all
F\colon\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
, the left Kan extension along
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
exists, i.e. the restriction

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})

has a left adjoint
i_{\kappa}
. This is fully faithful.
As
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-coaccessible,
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}})
(
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
), whence the essential image of the left Kan extension

i_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

consists precisely of the
\kappa
-filtered colimits preserving functors
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
.

The restriction
r^{\kappa}
obviously restricts to a functor
\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
. We claim that its left adjoint
i_{\kappa}
also preserves
S
-sheaves. Suppose that
F\in\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
and
s\colon X\to Y
is a morphism in
S
. By
\kappa
-accessibility of
(\mathcal{C},S)
there exists a
\kappa
-filtered diagram
s_{*}\colon I\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})
with
s={\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}(s_{i}\colon X_{i}\to Y_{i})
.
As
I
is filtered,
\check{C}(s)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\check{C}(s_{i})
, and since finite limits of
\kappa
-cocompact objects are
\kappa
-cocompact, for all
i\in I
and
[n]\in\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
,
\check{C}(s_{i})([n])\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
.
As
i_{\kappa}F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
commutes with
\kappa
-filtered colimits, this implies that

(i_{\kappa}F)(\check{C}(s))\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}\left(i_{\kappa}F(\check{C}(s_{i}))\right)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(\check{C}(s_{i}))

and
i_{\kappa}F(y)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(y_{i})
. Since
F
is an
S
-sheaf,
{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}F(\check{C}(s_{*}))\cong F(y_{*})\in\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal{D})
.
As
I
is
\kappa
-filtered and
\Delta
-indexed limits commute with
\kappa
-filtered colimits in
\mathcal{C}
, it now follows that

F(y)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(y_{i})\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}F(\check{C}(s_{i}))\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(\check{C}(s_{i}))\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}F(\check{C}(s)),

which shows that
i_{\kappa}F
is an
S
-sheaf.
This proves that
r^{\kappa}\vdash i_{\kappa}
restricts to an adjoint pair

r^{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\colon i_{\kappa}.

By the above and fully faithfulness of
i_{\kappa}
, a functor
F\colon\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
is an
S
-sheaf if and only if its left Kan extension
i_{\kappa}F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
is. It follows that
i_{\kappa}
factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}{\underset{}{\operatorname{colim}}}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cap\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).

The same arguments show that if
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-hyperaccessible, restriction and left Kan extension restrict to an adjunction

r^{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\colon i_{\kappa}

and
i_{\kappa}
factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}{\underset{}{\operatorname{colim}}}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cap\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).\qed

Corollary 1.1.13
.

Suppose that
\lambda\geq\kappa
are regular cardinals and
(\mathcal{C},S)
is an explicit covering site which is
\kappa
- and
\lambda
-(hyper)accessible.
Suppose that
\mathcal{D}
is a category with small limits and colimits, and
\Delta
-indexed limits commute with
\kappa
-filtered colimits in
\mathcal{D}
. Then the restriction

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})

has a fully faithful left adjoint.

Proof.

By
1.1.11
, for
\tau=\kappa,\lambda
,

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\tau},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\tau}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

via the left adjoint
i_{\tau}
of the restriction.
This implies that
i_{\kappa}
factors over a fully faithful functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})
which is left adjoint to the restriction.
∎

The proof of
1.1.11
shows that
\kappa
-and
\lambda
-(hyper)accessibility implies that left Kan extension along
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}
restricts to a functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})
.

We now apply
1.1.13
to prove basic categorical properties of categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves on (hyper)accessible explicit covering sites.
If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site and
\mathcal{C}
is not small, then
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is typically not accessible:

Corollary 1.1.14
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible
covering site and
S
is subcanonical, i.e.
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)
is an
S
-(hyper)sheaf for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
.
Then
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is accessible if and only if
\mathcal{C}
is essentially small.

Proof.

If
\mathcal{C}
is small and
\tilde{\mathcal{C}}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
is a small subcategory such that the inclusion is an equivalence, then
(\tilde{C},\tilde{C}\cap S)
is an explicit covering site and

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S\cap\tilde{\mathcal{C}}}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}})

via restriction. By
[
HP24
, Proposition A.2]
and
Proposition

1.1.5
,

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S\cap\tilde{\mathcal{C}}}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S\cap\tilde{\mathcal{C}}}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{\tau_{S\cap\tilde{\mathcal{C}}}}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}})

is a topos and in particular accessible (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7]
).

Conversely, if
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is accessible, there exists a small subcategory
G\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
which generates
\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
under small colimits.
Choose a regular cardinal
\kappa
such that
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-coaccessible and all elements in
G
preserve
\kappa
-filtered colimits.

1.1.11
implies that the restriction

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})

is conservative.
As the restriction has a fully faithful left adjoint (
1.1.11
), this implies that the restriction is an equivalence. (It follows from the triangle identities that the unit and counit are equivalences).
Hence by
1.1.11
, every element in
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is
\kappa
-accessible.
In particular, since
S
is subcanonical,
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)
is
\kappa
-accessible for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
, i.e.
\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
. The category
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
is essentially small by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
.
∎

1.1.11
moreover implies:

Corollary 1.1.15
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{D}
is a
\mu
-accessible category with small limits and colimits and
\kappa\geq\mu
is a regular cardinal.

(i)

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible explicit covering site, then

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

is closed under
\mu
-small limits and small colimits.

(ii)

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is (hyper)accessible, then
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
has all small limits and colimits.

Proof.

As
\mathcal{D}
has all small limits, small limits in
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
are computed pointwise (
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.1.2.3]
) and hence
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
is closed under small limits. Since
\mathcal{D}
is
\mu
-accessible,
\mu
-filtered colimits commute with
\mu
-small limits in
\mathcal{C}
(see e.g.
[
Man22
, Lemma A.2.8]
). This implies that for
\kappa\geq\mu
,

i_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

preserves
\mu
-small limits.
Being a left adjoint,
i_{\kappa}
also preserves small colimits.

Suppose now that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is (hyper)accessible and
F\colon I\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is a small diagram. Choose an uncountable regular cardinal
\mu_{F}\geq\mu
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\mu_{F}
-(hyper)accessible and

F(i)\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\mu_{F}}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

for all
i\in I
. Choose a regular cardinal
\tilde{\mu}\gg\mu
with
\tilde{\mu}>\max\{|I|,\mu_{F}\}
and a regular cardinal
\tilde{\kappa}\geq\tilde{\mu}
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\tilde{\kappa}
-accessible. By
[
Lur09
, Lemma 5.4.2.10]
,
\mathcal{D}
is
\tilde{\mu}
-accessible, whence

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\tilde{\kappa}}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

is closed under
\tilde{\mu}
-small limits and small colimits by the above. In particular,
F
admits a limit and colimit and both can be computed in
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\tilde{\kappa}}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
.
∎

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site. For all
\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
,
\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}
is essentially small since
\mathcal{C}
is
\lambda
-coaccessible (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
).
1.1.11
therefore implies:

Corollary 1.1.16
.

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible explicit covering site, then
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is a topos.

Proof.

By
1.1.11
,

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}).

As
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-coaccessible,
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
is essentially small (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
). Choose a small category
\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\kappa}
with an equivalence
f\colon\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\kappa}\cong\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
and denote by
f^{*}S\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\kappa})
the full subcategory on morphisms
s
with
f(s)\in S
.
It is straightforward to check that
(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\kappa},f^{*}S)
is an explicit covering site and that the pullback
f^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{f^{*}S}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\kappa}).

By
Proposition

1.1.5
and
[
Lur09
, Propositions 6.2.2.7, 6.5.1.16, 6.2.1.1]
),
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{f^{*}S}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\kappa})
is a topos.
∎

Together with
1.1.15
, this implies that small limits and colimits in
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
behave like in a topos:

Corollary 1.1.17

(Giraud’s axioms)
.

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site.
The category of accessible, (hypercomplete)
S
-sheaves
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is a locally small category and satisfies all of Giraud’s axioms (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.1.3.19]
) except accessibility, i.e.

(i)

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
has all small limits and colimits.

(ii)

Small colimits in
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
are universal.

(iii)

Small coproducts in
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
are disjoint.

(iv)

Every groupoid object in
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is effective.

Proof.

The category
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
is locally small as every accessible functor is a small colimit of representables, cf.
[
HP24
, Proposition A.9]
.
By
1.1.15
,
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
has all small limits and colimits.
By
1.1.16
and
[
Lur09
, Theorem 6.1.0.6]
, for all uncountable regular cardinals
\kappa
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible,
(ii)
,
(iii)
, and
(iv)
hold in
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
.
For every small diagram
F\colon S\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
, there exists a regular cardinal
\kappa
such that
F
factors over

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})

and
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-accessible. As
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
is closed under small colimits and finite limits (
1.1.15
), this implies
(ii)
,
(iii)
, and
(iv)
.
∎

By
1.1.14
, categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves are typically not presentable and in particular not topoi (
[
Lur09
, Theorem 6.1.0.6]
). We now explain that they can be
exhausted
by topoi, from which we will deduce that accessible presheaves can be sheafified.

Notation 1.1.18
.

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site, denote by
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
the large poset of small regular cardinals
\kappa
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible, ordered by
\leq
.

The poset
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
depends on
S
and on whether we consider
(\mathcal{C},S)
as a hyperaccessible or as an accessible explicit covering site.

Construction 1.1.19
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{D}
is a category with small colimits and
\mu
is a small regular cardinal such that
\mu
-filtered colimits commute with
\mu
-small limits in
\mathcal{D}
.
For a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
denote by
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}\subseteq\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
the full subcategory on cardinals
\geq\mu
and by
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}^{\triangleright}\coloneqq\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}\cup\{\infty\}
its cone.
The restrictions

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D}),\,\lambda\geq\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}

assemble into a functor

\displaystyle\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})\colon(\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}^{\triangleright})^{\operatorname{op}}

\displaystyle\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty},

\displaystyle\lambda

\displaystyle\mapsto\begin{cases}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})&\lambda\neq\infty\\
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})&\lambda=\infty.\end{cases}

By
1.1.13
, this enhances to a functor

(\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}^{\triangleright})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{R}

to the very large category of large categories and right adjoint functors.
Taking opposites yields a functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})\colon\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}^{\triangleright}\to{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L}}

to the very large category of large categories and left adjoint functors.
We used that
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L}\cong(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{R})^{\operatorname{op}}
, see e.g.
[
Hau+23
, Theorem B]
in the large universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
.

Remark 1.1.20
.

If
\mathcal{D}
is presentable, then
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})
factors over
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\subseteq\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L}
and the equivalence from
1.1.6
yields an equivalence

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{An})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu},\operatorname{Pr}^{L}).

Corollary 1.1.21
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{D}
is a category with small colimits and there exists a small regular cardinal
\mu
such that
\mu
-filtered colimits commute with
\mu
-small limits in
\mathcal{D}
.
