Then

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})\colon\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}^{\triangleright}\to{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L}}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}

is a colimit diagram.

Proof of
1.1.21
.

By
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2]
(in the large universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
), the colimit

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})

exists in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
.
Since
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
is filtered,
Lemma

A.1.3
,
1.1.13
, and
1.1.11
imply that the functor

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

is fully faithful.
By
1.1.11
, it is essentially surjective.
∎

Remark 1.1.22
.

1.1.21
implies that if
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site, the category of accessible (hyper)sheaves is the colimit (in the category of large categories) of all categories of (hyper)sheaves on an essentially small subsite:

If
\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
is a subcategory closed under finite limits and colimits, then
(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}},S\cap\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}})
is an explicit covering site, and if
\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\subseteq\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime\prime}}
are two such subcategories which are essentially small, then the inclusion
i\colon\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\subseteq\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime\prime}}
defines a morphism of sites, whence restriction
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime\prime}})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}})
restricts to a functor
i^{*}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime\prime}})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}})
.
This admits a left adjoint given by (hyper)sheafification after left Kan extension along
i
, which is left-exact by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.3.20]
.
Denote by
\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}
the poset of essentially small subcategories of
\mathcal{C}
which are closed under finite limits and colimits.
The left adjoints of restriction assemble into a diagram

\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L},\,\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\mapsto\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}).

As
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-accessible, for all regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa
,
\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}
is essentially small (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
), and every small subcategory is contained in
\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}
for some small regular cardinal
\lambda
(
Lemma

A.1.5
).
It therefore follows from the above corollary that for a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
and a presentable category
\mathcal{D}
,

{\underset{\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).

More generally, for an arbitrary, not necessarily accessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
, one has a functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(-)\colon\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L},\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\mapsto\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}),

and one can show that its colimit in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
satisfies Giraud’s axioms except accessibility, see
[
BDL25
, section 2.1]
. If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is not (hyper)accessible, then the colimit
{\underset{\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\subseteq\mathcal{C}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}})
(in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
) seems to be better behaved than the category
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C})
of (hyper)accessible sheaves. However, this has the drawback that in general there need not exist a forget functor to the category of presheaves
{\underset{\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}}\subseteq\mathcal{C}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}^{{}^{\prime}})
.

The above corollary (
1.1.21
) implies that accessible presheaves can be (hyper)-sheafified:

Corollary 1.1.23
.

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site and
\mathcal{D}
is a presentable category, the
\tau_{S}
-(hyper)sheafifications
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{S}}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})
assemble into a left adjoint

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

of the forget functor.

Remark 1.1.24
.

This was observed for fpqc-sheaves on affine schemes by
[
Wat75
]
and stated for sheaves in
[
BH19
]
.

Proof.

We will deduce this from
Lemma

A.2.3
.
We first recall that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
, the forget functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

admits a left adjoint.
As
\mathcal{C}
is
\lambda
-coaccessible,
\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}
is essentially small. Choose a small category
\tilde{\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}}
with an equivalence
f\colon\tilde{\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}}\cong\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}
and denote by
f^{*}S\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\tilde{\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}})
the full subcategory on morphisms
s
with
f(s)\in S
.
It is straightforward to check that
(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\lambda},f^{*}S)
is an explicit covering site and that the pullback
f^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{f^{*}S}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D}).

The forget functor
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{f^{*}S}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\tilde{\mathcal{C}}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
admits a left adjoint by e.g.
[
Man22
, Proposition A.3.7, Proposition A.3.14, Proposition A.3.16]
.
This implies that

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

admits a left adjoint
L_{\lambda}
.

For
\kappa\leq\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
denote by

i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\colon r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}

the adjunction induced by restriction and left Kan extension (
1.1.13
).
Under the identification of
1.1.21
, the colimit of

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})\xhookrightarrow{f_{*}}\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{*}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}^{\operatorname{op}},\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})

over
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
is the forget functor
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
.
The Beck-Chevalley transformation
f_{\kappa}r^{\kappa}\Rightarrow r^{\kappa}f_{\lambda}
associated to the commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{\lambda}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}}

is obviously an equivalence, whence so is its opposite
L_{\lambda}i_{\kappa}\Rightarrow i_{\kappa}L_{\kappa}
by
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.7.4.14]
.
It now follows from
Lemma

A.1.2
(applied to the opposite categories
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})^{\operatorname{op}}
and
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\mathcal{D})^{\operatorname{op}}
), that there exists a left adjoint

L\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
,
L|_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}
factors as

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{L_{\lambda}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\xhookrightarrow{i_{\lambda}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}).\qed

Corollary 1.1.25
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site.
The left adjoint of the forget functor
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
is left-exact.

Proof.

Since finite limits commute with filtered colimits in
\operatorname{An}
, for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
is closed under finite limits which are computed pointwise, cf.
[
HP24
, Proposition A.9]
. This implies that

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})

is closed under finite limits as well.
Suppose that
F\colon I\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{acc}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
is a finite diagram, and choose a regular cardinal
\kappa
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible and
F(i)\in\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
for all
i\in I
.
By construction, the left adjoint
L
of the forget functor restricts to a functor

\operatorname{Fun}^{\kappa\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C}),

which is left adjoint to the forget functor. We recall below that this functor is left-exact, then it follows from the above that
L({\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}F)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}L(F_{i})
.

As
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
is essentially small, we can argue as in the proof of
1.1.23
to reduce to the case where
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
is small. The identification of
Proposition

1.1.5
and
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7]
imply that the left adjoint

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})

is left-exact. Since
\infty
-connective morphisms are stable under pullbacks (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.5.1.16]
), the hypersheafification

\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})

is left-exact as well by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.1.1]
.
∎

The definition of (hyper)accessible explicit covering sites is rigged so that
1.1.21
holds. Alternatively, one could require
\kappa
-accessibility for some regular
\kappa
and that the collection of (hyper)covers is closed under
\kappa
-filtered limits:

Lemma 1.1.26
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is an explicit covering site.

(i)

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-accessible and
S\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C})
is closed under
\kappa
-filtered limits, then
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-accessible for all regular cardinals
\lambda\gg\kappa
.

(ii)

Denote by
S_{\Delta}\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta_{+}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})
the full subcategory on
S
-hypercovers.
If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-hyperaccessible and
S_{\Delta}\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})
is closed under
\kappa
-filtered limits, then
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-hyperaccessible for all regular cardinals
\lambda\gg\kappa
.

Proof.

We only show the statement about accessibility, the hyperaccessibility statement can be proven completely analogously.
Fix a regular cardinal
\lambda\gg\kappa
.
By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.11]
,
\mathcal{C}
is
\lambda
-coaccessible. The proof of
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.4.3]
shows that for every small category
I
,

\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}})

is
\kappa
-accessible, and the left Kan extension

\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})^{\operatorname{op}})\xhookrightarrow{i_{\kappa}}\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}})

along
\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})^{\operatorname{op}}\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}
restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})^{\operatorname{op}})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}},

where we identified the right-hand side with its Yoneda image.
It follows that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-accessible if and only if (the Yoneda image of)
S^{\operatorname{op}}\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}
is contained in the image of the composite

\operatorname{Ind}_{\lambda}\left((\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})\cap S)^{\operatorname{op}}\right)\to\operatorname{Ind}_{\lambda}\left(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}}\right)\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}})\xrightarrow{i_{\lambda}}\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}).

The left Kan extension
\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})^{\operatorname{op}})\xhookrightarrow{i_{\kappa}}\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}})
factors into left adjoints

\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})^{\operatorname{op}})\xhookrightarrow{i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}}\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}})\xhookrightarrow{i_{\lambda}}\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}),

and by
[
Lur09
, Lemma 5.4.2.10]
,
i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}
restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})^{\operatorname{op}})\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}}).

Since
S\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C})
is closed under
\kappa
-filtered limits,
[
Lur09
, Lemma 5.4.2.10]
implies that

\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa}\left((\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})\cap S)^{\operatorname{op}}\right)\to\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})^{\operatorname{op}})\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{\lambda}\left((\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}))^{\operatorname{op}}\right)

factors over
\operatorname{Ind}_{\lambda}\left((\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})\cap S)^{\operatorname{op}}\right)
, which shows that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-accessible.
∎

We now deduce from
1.1.21
that for a presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
,
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure:

Construction 1.1.27
.

Endow
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
with the Lurie tensor product (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
).
For all cardinals
\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
, the cartesian monoidal structure on the topos
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})
is cocontinuous (
[
Lur09
, Theorem 6.1.0.6.3]
) and for
\kappa\leq\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
, the left adjoint

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})

is left-exact by
1.1.15
and
1.1.11
.

[
Lur17
, Corollary 2.4.1.9]
now implies that
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*})
enhances to a functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*})^{\times}\colon\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L}).

By
[
Lur17
, Example 3.2.4.4]
,
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
admits a symmetric monoidal structure and the forget functor
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor. In particular, if
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
are two presentably symmetric monoidal categories, then
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
is a presentably symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}
.
Let

\displaystyle\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},-)^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}\times\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L}),

\displaystyle(\lambda,\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})

\displaystyle\mapsto\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda})^{\times}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}.

By
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2]
in the universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
, the category
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
has all
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small colimits, and the tensor product on
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is compatible with
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small colimits (
[
Lur17
, Definition 3.1.1.18]
).
Hence by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.3.1]
(in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
),
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
has all large sifted colimits and

\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}

preserves large sifted colimits.
Together with
1.1.21
and
1.1.20
, this implies that by taking the colimit of
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},-)^{\otimes}
over
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
in
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
, we obtain a functor

\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}),\,\,\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\mapsto{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})^{\otimes}

which sends a presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{D}
to a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
.

Theorem 1.1.28
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site.
For a presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
described above is closed.

This is a straightforward adaptation of
[
Man22
, Proposition 2.1.11]
and relies on the following observation.

Lemma 1.1.29
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site and
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal category.
Suppose that
\kappa
is a regular cardinal such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible.
For
c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
, the functor

\operatorname{ev}_{c}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{D},\,F\mapsto F(c)

admits a left adjoint
(-)[c]
.
This has the following properties:

(i)

For
d\in\mathcal{D}
,
d[c]\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
.

(ii)

Suppose that
G\subseteq\mathcal{D}
is a small generating set for
\mathcal{D}
.
Then
\{d[c],c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},d\in G\}
generates
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\kappa\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
under small colimits.

(iii)

For
c,\tilde{c}\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
and
d,\tilde{d}\in\mathcal{D}
,

d[c]\otimes\tilde{d}[\tilde{c}]\cong(d\otimes_{\mathcal{D}}\tilde{d})[c\times\tilde{c}]

naturally.

Proof.

We first explain that
\operatorname{ev}_{c}
admits a left adjoint for all
c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
.
As
\operatorname{ev}_{c}
factors as

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{c}}\mathcal{D}

and the restriction
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
has a left adjoint
i_{\kappa}
(
1.1.11
), it suffices to show that

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{c}}\mathcal{D}

admits a left adjoint.
We showed in the proof of
1.1.14
that the forget functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

has a left adjoint
L_{\kappa}
for all
\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
.
The category
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
is presentable by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.4.3]
.
As
\mathcal{D}
has small limits and colimits (
[
Lur09
, Theorem 5.5.1.1, Corollary 5.5.2.4]
),

\operatorname{ev}_{c}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{D}

preserves small limits and colimits by
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.1.2.3]
and in particular admits a left adjoint
p_{c}
by the adjoint functor theorem (
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
).
This shows that

(-)[c]\coloneqq i_{\kappa}\circ L_{\kappa}\circ p_{c}

is left adjoint to
\operatorname{ev}_{c}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{D}
, and in particular,
d[c]\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\kappa\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
for all
d\in\mathcal{D}
.

Suppose now that
G
is a small generating set for
\mathcal{D}
. This exists since
\mathcal{D}
is presentable. Then the functors

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}(c[g],-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}(g,\operatorname{ev}_{c}-),\,c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},g\in G

are jointly conservative.
As
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
is essentially small (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
) and the category
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
is accessible (
1.1.16
), by
Lemma

A.1.5
there exists a regular cardinal
\mu
such that
c[g]
is
\mu
-compact for all
c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},g\in G
. It now follows from
[
Man22
, Lemma A.2.1]
that
c[g],c\in\mathcal{C},g\in G
generate

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\kappa\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

under colimits.

It remains to prove the relation

d[c]\otimes\tilde{d}[\tilde{c}]\cong(d\otimes\tilde{d})[c\otimes\tilde{c}].

Denote by
l\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})
the
S
-(hyper)sheafification. The proof of
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
and
Proposition

1.1.5
imply that

l\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{D}}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})

is the left adjoint of the inclusion, i.e. equivalent to
L_{\kappa}
.
Since
l
is cartesian,
l
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})^{\times}\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})^{\times}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L}),

cf.
[
Lur17
, Corollary 2.4.1.9]
. Hence by construction of the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
,
L_{\kappa}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor.
By construction of the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
,
i_{\kappa}
is symmetric monoidal as well.
It therefore suffices to show that for
c,\tilde{c}\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},d,\tilde{d}\in\mathcal{D}
,

p_{c}(d)\otimes p_{\tilde{c}}(\tilde{d})\cong p_{c\otimes\tilde{c}}(d\otimes\tilde{d}).

For
t\in\mathcal{C},x\in\mathcal{D}
,
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}(p_{t}(x),F)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(x,F(t))
, whence
p_{t}(x)\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
is the left Kan extension of
\{x\}\to\mathcal{D}
along
\{t\}\to\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
.
As the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
is cocartesian, this implies that
p_{c\otimes\tilde{c}}(d\otimes\tilde{d})
is the left Kan extension of

\displaystyle p_{c}(d)\otimes^{ptw}p_{d}(\tilde{d})\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}

\displaystyle\to\mathcal{D},

\displaystyle(x,y)

\displaystyle\mapsto p_{c}(d)(x)\otimes_{\mathcal{D}}p_{\tilde{c}}(\tilde{d})(y)

along
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\xrightarrow{-\otimes-}\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
, which shows that
p_{c\otimes\tilde{c}}(d\otimes\tilde{d})\cong p_{c}(d)\otimes p_{\tilde{c}}(\tilde{d}),
cf.
Lemma

A.3.6
.
∎

Proof of
1.1.28
.

Since small colimits can always be computed on some stage

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{{\kappa}\text{-}\operatorname{colim}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

(
1.1.15
), the tensor product on
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
preserves small colimits in both variables. As
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
has small limits and colimits, it follows from
Lemma

A.1.1
that

\{M\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\,|\,M\otimes-\text{ admits right adjoint}\}\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

is closed under small colimits.

Fix a regular cardinal
\mu
such that
\mathcal{D}
is
\mu
-accessible.
For
\lambda\geq\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}
, denote by

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{i^{\lambda}}\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})

the left adjoints of the restriction, cf.
1.1.13
,

1.1.11
.
Lemmas

1.1.29
and
1.1.11
imply that

i_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mu},\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu}

generates
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
under small colimits, where
(-)_{\kappa}[c]
denotes the left adjoint of

\operatorname{ev}_{c}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{D}.

It therefore suffices to show that
i_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-
is a left adjoint for all
\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\mu},c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mu}
.
Fix
d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mu}
and choose a regular cardinal
\eta\geq\mu
such that
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,-)\colon\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{D}
preserves
\eta
-filtered colimits. This exists by the adjoint functor theorem (
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
).
Choose
\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq\eta}
, and
c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}
. We first show that for all
\lambda\geq\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
and

N\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}d_{\kappa}[c],i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}N)\colon C_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}

preserves
\kappa
-filtered colimits. For
e\in\mathcal{D}
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(e,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}d_{\kappa}[c],i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}N)(-))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(e_{\lambda}[-],\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(e_{\lambda}[-]\otimes i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N),

and since
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\cong d_{\lambda}[c]
,

e_{\lambda}[-]\otimes i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\cong(e\otimes d)_{\lambda}[-\times c]

by
Lemma

1.1.29
.
This implies that

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(e,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}d_{\kappa}[c],i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}N)(-))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}((e\otimes d)_{\lambda}[-\times c],i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(e\otimes d,i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N(-\times c))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(e,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N(-\times c))),

which shows that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}d_{\kappa}[c],i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}N)=(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni x\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N(x\times c)).

Since
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N\colon\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}
preserves
\kappa
-filtered colimits and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}
is cartesian, this functor commutes with
\kappa
-filtered colimits by choice of
\eta
.
The symmetric monoidal enhancement of
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
from
1.1.27
provides a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-}

We claim that the associated Beck-Chevalley transformation

\beta\colon i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}(d_{\kappa}[c],-)\Rightarrow\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}-)

is an equivalence, then it follows from
Lemma

A.1.2
that
i_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})}-
admits a right adjoint.
Since for all
N\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}N)\colon\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}

preserves
\kappa
-filtered colimits (see above), by
1.1.11
it suffices to show that
r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}(\beta)
is an equivalence.
As right adjoint of a symmetric monoidal functor,
r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
enhances to a lax symmetric monoidal functor (
Lemma

A.2.3
).
The lax monoidal structure yields a
2
-cell
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-}

Denote by

\gamma\colon r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],-)\Rightarrow\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}(r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],-)\circ r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}

the associated Beck-Chevalley transformation.
By fully faithfulness of
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
(
1.1.11
), the unit for
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\dashv r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
induces an equivalence

\eta^{*}\colon\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}(r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c],-)\circ r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}(d_{\kappa}[c],-)\circ r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}.

As
\eta^{*}\circ\gamma
is the total mate (
[
Cno24
, Definition F.7]
) of the equivalence
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-\cong i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}(d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-)
, it is an equivalence.
This shows that
\gamma
is an equivalence.
By the pasting law for mates (
[
CSY22
, Lemma 2.2.4]
),
\gamma\circ\beta
is the Beck-Chevalley transformation induced by
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\mathcal{D}),}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}i_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}i_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}d_{\kappa}[c]\otimes-}

where the 2-cell comes from the lax monoidal structure on
r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}
. By fully faithfulness of
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
(
1.1.13
), the 2-cell and the vertical arrows are equivalences, which implies that
\gamma\circ\beta
is an equivalence.
This shows that
r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\beta
is an equivalence.
∎

Remark 1.1.30
.

The above proof also shows that for
M,N\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
, there exists a regular cardinal
\kappa
such that for all
\kappa\leq\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
,

i_{\lambda}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(M,N)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})}(M,N).

Indeed, for
M,N\in\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
, choose a regular cardinal
\kappa_{0}
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa_{0}
-(hyper)accessible,
M
and
N
preserve
\kappa_{0}
-filtered colimits, and there exists an uncountable regular cardinal
\mu\leq\kappa_{0}
such that
\mathcal{D}
is
\mu
-accessible.
By
1.1.11
and
Lemma

1.1.29
,
M
is a small colimit of elements of the form
i_{\kappa_{0}}d_{\kappa_{0}}[c],c\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa_{0}},d\in\mathcal{D}
.
Choose a small regular cardinal
\kappa_{1}\geq\kappa_{0}
such that
M={\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{colim}}}i_{\kappa_{1}}d^{j}_{\kappa_{1}}[c^{j}]
is a
\kappa_{1}
-small colimit of such elements and
\mathcal{D}
is
\kappa_{1}
-accessible.
Choose a regular cardinal
\kappa\geq\kappa_{1}
such that
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}}(d^{j},-)
preserves
\kappa
-filtered colimits for all
j\in J
.
We showed in the proof of
1.1.28
that for
\lambda\geq\kappa\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
,

i_{\lambda}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}d^{j}_{\kappa}[c^{j}],N)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})}(i_{\kappa}d^{j}_{\kappa}[c^{j}],N).

Since
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
is closed under
\kappa
-small limits (
1.1.15
), it follows that

i_{\lambda}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\mathcal{D})}(M,N)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})}(M,N)

for
\kappa\leq\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
.

1.2
Big presentable categories

Categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves on a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site are in general not accessible (
1.1.14
) and therefore not topoi, cf.
[
Lur09
, Theorem 6.1.0.6]
.
Our next goal is to show that however, their category of spectrum objects behaves like the stabilization of a presentably symmetric monoidal category in many aspects.
We chose to work with the following more general setup to also include the category of
G
-objects in a category of accessible (hyper)sheaves for a group object
G
in our discussion.

Definition 1.2.1
.

(i)

A
chain of presentable

categories
is a functor

\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
from a possibly large filtered set
\Lambda
such that for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
is a fully faithful, left-exact left adjoint.
A possibly large category
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is
big presentable
if there exists a chain of presentable categories
\mathcal{B}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
with
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}={\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{*}
, where the colimit is computed in the very large category
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
of large categories.
We call such a chain an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
(by presentable categories).

(ii)

A
chain of

topoi
is a chain of presentable categories
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
is a topos. A
big topos
is a possibly large category
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
such that there exists a chain of topoi
\mathcal{B}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
with
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}={\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{*}
, where the colimit is computed in the very large category of large categories.
We call such a chain an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
(by topoi).

Remark 1.2.2
.

The definitions of big topoi/big presentable categories are rigged so that their categories of spectrum objects behave much like for presentable categories.
The left-exactness of the transition functors may seem unnatural, however it is crucial in several arguments, for example to ensure that the stabilization of a big presentable category is stable and big presentable. We also used it to
glue
left adjoints which exist on the level of presentable categories, for instance in the proofs of
Lemmas

1.2.5
and
1.3.10
.
The fully faithfulness (and left-exactness) of the transition functors seems necessary to obtain a corresponding colimit-description of the category of spectrum objects (
Lemma

1.3.5
).

Our discussion of monoidal structures in big presentable categories and module categories therein could be streamlined by restricting to those big presentable categories which admit small colimits (or at least countable colimits). While this condition is satisfied in all examples relevant to this article, simply adding it to the definition would be inconvenient as it is generally not preserved by passing to categories of spectrum objects. A more suitable alternative would be to work with chains of presentable categories indexed on diagrams which are
\lambda
-filtered for every small regular cardinal
\lambda
(or at least
\omega_{1}
-filtered), rather than merely filtered. By
Lemma

1.2.4
, this implies that the resulting big presentable categories admit all small (respectively
\omega_{1}
-small) colimits, while still encompassing all examples we care about. However, we did not adopt this convention to keep the general framework as flexible as possible.

Lemma 1.2.3
.

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site, the category of accessible
S
-(hyper)sheaves on
\mathcal{C}
is a big topos.

Proof.

Denote by
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
the poset of regular cardinals
\lambda
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-(hyper)accessible.
In
1.1.19
, we described a functor

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{An})\colon\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L},\,\lambda\mapsto\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{An}).

For all
\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
,
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{An})
is a topos by
1.1.16
, and by
1.1.13
, for all
\kappa\leq\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
,

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{An})
is a fully faithful left adjoint.

1.1.11
and
1.1.15
imply that it is also left-exact.
It now follows from
1.1.21
that
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{An})
is an exhaustion for
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})
by topoi.
∎

More generally,
macrotopoi

[
BH19
, Definition 1.4.10]
, i.e. left-exact accessible localizations of categories of accessible presheaves are big topoi by
[
BH19
, Example 1.4.11]
.
Macrotopoi are arguably a more natural generalization of topoi than big topoi, but the definition of big topoi/big presentable categories captures the essential structure needed to generalize results from presentable categories.

Before turning to spectrum objects in big presentable categories, we record some basic categorical properties of big presentable categories.

Lemma 1.2.4
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion for a big presentable category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
.

(i)

For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, the canonical functor
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a fully faithful, left-exact left adjoint.
In particular,
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is locally small.

(ii)

If
I
is a category such that for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
preserves
I
-indexed limits, then
\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
preserves
I
-indexed limits. In particular,
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
has all finite limits.

(iii)

If
I
is a category such that for all diagrams
\phi\colon I\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
, there exists
\lambda\in\Lambda
such that
\phi
factors over
I\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
, then
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
has all
I
-indexed colimits.
If in addition, for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
preserves
I
-indexed limits, then
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
also has all
I
-indexed limits.

Proof.

This is an immediate consequence of
Lemma

A.1.3
.
∎

Lemma 1.2.5
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentable category.

(i)

The full subcategory
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
of
n
-truncated objects (
[
Lur09
, Definition 5.5.6.1]
) is a big presentable category. The inclusion
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
admits a left adjoint
\tau_{\leq n}
.

(ii)

More concretely, if
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion for
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories, then
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{*}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{*}
defines a subfunctor which is an exhaustion for
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories and for
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\cong\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}.

For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, the functor
\tau_{\leq n}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
restricts to the truncation functor
\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories.
By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.16]
, for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
, the left-exact functor
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
restricts to a functor
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
.
We therefore obtain a functor

\Lambda\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty},\lambda\mapsto\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}.

By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.18]
, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
admits a left adjoint
\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
, and by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.28]
, the Beck-Chevalley transformation

\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\circ\mathcal{B}(\kappa\to\lambda)\to(\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B})(\kappa\to\lambda)\circ\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}

coming from the commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}

is an equivalence for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
.
It now follows from
Lemma

A.1.2
that
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
admits a left adjoint
\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}={\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
.
By
Lemma

A.1.3
, the functor
c\colon{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is fully faithful.
As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is left-exact (
Lemma

1.2.4
),

\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.15]
.
As
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a fully faithful left adjoint (
Lemma

1.2.4
),

(\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\cap\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},

which shows that

\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\cong\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}.

It follows that
c
factors over an equivalence

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\cong\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}.

It remains to show that
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{*}
is a chain of presentable categories.
As localization of the presentable category
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
,
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is presentable for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
For all
\kappa\leq\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is fully faithful as restriction of a fully faithful functor. As for all
\mu\in\Lambda
, colimits in
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
can be computed by applying
\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\mu}}
to the corresponding colimit in
\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
and for
\kappa\leq\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\circ\mathcal{B}(\kappa\to\lambda)\cong\mathcal{B}(\kappa\to\lambda)\tau_{\leq n}^{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}

(see above), cocontinuity of
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
implies that
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
preserve small colimits for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
.
As for all
\mu\in\Lambda
,
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\mu}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
is closed under small limits, and for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is left-exact, the functors
\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
are left-exact for all
\kappa\leq\lambda
.
∎

1.3
Spectrum objects in big presentable categories

Definition 1.3.1

(Spectrum objects)
.

[
Lur17
, Definition 1.4.2.8]

For a category
\mathcal{C}
, the category of
spectrum objects
in
\mathcal{C}
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},\mathcal{C})

is the full subcategory on reduced, excisive functors
\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}\to\mathcal{C}
, i.e. functors
F\colon\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}\to\mathcal{C}
which send pushouts to pullbacks and satisfy
F(*)=*
.

Evaluation at
S^{0}\in\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}
,

\displaystyle\Omega^{\infty}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})

\displaystyle\to\mathcal{C}

\displaystyle F

\displaystyle\mapsto F(S^{0})

is called
infinite loop space functor
.

In this section, we show that the category of spectrum objects of a big presentable category behaves in many aspects similar to the stabilization of a presentable category. This leads to well-behaved notions of (group) cohomology in big topoi which we will discuss in
Sections

1.5
,
3.2
and
3.2
.
This section is structured as follows:
We first show that the category of spectrum objects in a big presentable category is stable
(
Lemma

1.3.2
) and big presentable (
Lemma

1.3.5
).
Then we show that the infinite loop space functor admits a left adjoint which factors over the categories of (grouplike) commutative monoids (
Lemma

1.3.10
). We use the left adjoint to define a
t
-structure on the category of spectrum objects (
Lemma

1.3.12
).

For a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
, the left adjoint
\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
of the infinite loop space functor exhibits
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
as the initial stable category in
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
over
\mathcal{C}
. We establish a similar universal property for big presentable categories (
1.3.20
,
1.3.21
).
In
Section

1.3.1
, we describe conditions on a (symmetric) monoidal structure on a big presentable category
\mathcal{C}
under which the left adjoint
\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
of
\Omega^{\infty}
inherits a (symmetric) monoidal structure. We establish a universal property of this (symmetric) monoidal structure and show that it is compatible with the
t
-structure from
Lemma

1.3.12
.
In
Section

1.3.2
, we show that the category of spectrum objects in a big presentable category is naturally spectrally enriched (
1.3.35
), and that every adjunction between stable, big presentable categories enhances to an adjunction of spectrally enriched categories (
1.3.40
).
We conclude with basic properties of the
constant sheaf functor
into a big presentable category.

Lemma 1.3.2
.

If
\mathcal{B}
is a big presentable category, its category of spectrum objects
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})
is stable.

Proof.

By
Lemma

1.2.4
,
\mathcal{B}
has all finite limits and hence
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})
is stable by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.2.17]
.
∎

Definition 1.3.3
.

If
f\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is a finite limits preserving functor, then pushforward along

f_{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},\mathcal{D})

restricts to a functor
\operatorname{Sp}(f)\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{D})
.
We call
\operatorname{Sp}(f)
the
stabilization
of
f
.

If
f
is fully faithful, so is
f_{*}
and hence
\operatorname{Sp}(f)
.

Example 1.3.4
.

Suppose
L\colon\mathcal{X}\rightleftarrows\mathcal{Y}\colon R
is an adjunction and
L
preserves finite limits.
Then pushforward along
L
and
R
restricts to functors

L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})\text{ and }R_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}).

An adjunction datum
(\eta\colon\operatorname{id}\to RL,\epsilon\colon LR\to\operatorname{id})
yields natural transformations

\operatorname{id}\to R_{\operatorname{Sp}}L_{\operatorname{Sp}},\,\,L_{\operatorname{Sp}}R_{\operatorname{Sp}}\to\operatorname{id}

which exhibit
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}
as left adjoint to
R_{\operatorname{Sp}}
.
By construction,

(1.3.4.1)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Y}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{\operatorname{Sp}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}

commutes, and by construction of the adjunction datum for
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv R_{\operatorname{Sp}}
, its mate

(1.3.4.2)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Y}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R_{\operatorname{Sp}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}

commutes as well.

Lemma 1.3.5
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion for a big presentable category
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
.
Then
\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},\mathcal{B}_{*})\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}
has

\displaystyle\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\colon\Lambda

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty},

\displaystyle\lambda

\displaystyle\mapsto\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

as a subfunctor. This functor enhances to a functor
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
which is an exhaustion for
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
In particular,
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a big presentable category.

Proof.

Since for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
preserves finite limits,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},\mathcal{B}_{*})
is a subfunctor.
We explained above that for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is a fully faithful left adjoint. Since its source and target are stable, it is also left-exact.
By
[
Lur17
, Example 4.8.1.23]
, for every presentable category
\mathcal{X}
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\cong\mathcal{X}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\operatorname{Sp}
is presentable, whence
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})
lifts to a functor
\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
.

As for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
, the functors
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})
and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
are fully faithful,

{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})

is fully faithful by
Lemma

A.1.3
. Its essential image consists of the reduced, excisive functors
\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
which factor over
\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\subseteq\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
for some
\kappa\in\Lambda
. Suppose
E\colon\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a reduced and excisive functor and choose
\kappa\in\Lambda
with
E(S^{0})\in\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\subseteq\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
. Since
E
is excisive and
\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\subseteq\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is closed under finite limits,

\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}(E,\kappa)\coloneqq\{X\in\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}\,|\,E(X)\in\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\}

is closed under pushouts. As
E
is reduced,
*\in\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}(E,\kappa)
. As
\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}
is generated under pushouts by
S^{0}
and
*
, this implies that

\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*}(E,\kappa)=\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},

i.e.
E\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
.
∎

For a presentable category
\mathcal{B}
, the infinite loop space functor has a left adjoint
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})
which exhibits
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})
as the initial stable category over
\mathcal{B}
in
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
. This implies the following:

Lemma 1.3.6
.

If
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is a chain of presentable categories, there is an equivalence

\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{B}_{*}\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, the functor

\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\cong\operatorname{An}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

induced by
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\operatorname{An}\to\operatorname{Sp}\in\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is left adjoint to

\Omega^{\infty}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\,F\mapsto F(S^{0}).

Proof.

Evaluation at
S^{0}
induces a natural transformation

\Omega^{\infty}_{*}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\to\mathcal{B}_{*}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
, cf.
1.3.4
.
For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\Omega^{\infty}_{\lambda}
has a left adjoint
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\lambda}
by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.4.4.4]
and for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
, the mate
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}(\kappa\to\lambda)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\lambda}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})(\kappa\to\lambda)}

of
1.3.4.1
commutes as its opposite
1.3.4.2
is commutative, cf.
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.7.4.14]
.
Whence by
Lemma

A.1.2
, the left adjoints assemble into a natural transformation

\mathcal{B}_{*}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\operatorname{Pr}^{L}).

Since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is presentable and stable for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.2.18]
, this factors uniquely over a natural transformation
\mathcal{B}_{*}\to\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{B}_{*}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})
and by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.4.5]
,
\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is an equivalence for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
∎

Corollary 1.3.7
.

For a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An}))\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp}).

Proof.

Denote by
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
the poset of regular cardinals
\kappa
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-(hyper)accessible and by

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{An}),\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{Sp})\colon\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}

the functors described in
1.1.19
.
By
1.1.20
,

\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{An})}\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{Sp})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}},\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}),

and by
Lemma

1.3.6
,

\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}{\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{An})}\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*},\operatorname{An}))\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}},\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}).

The statement now follows from
1.1.21
and
Lemma

1.3.5
.
∎

Corollary 1.3.8
.

(i)

If
\mathcal{X}
is a topos, then

\Omega^{\infty-i}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathcal{X}

preserves filtered colimits for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.

(ii)

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site.
For all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\Omega^{\infty-i}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An}))\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})

preserves filtered colimits.

Proof.

By
[
Lur09
, Example 7.3.4.7]
, for a topos
\mathcal{X}
,

\Omega\colon\mathcal{X}_{*}\to\mathcal{X}_{*}

preserves filtered colimits. By
[
Lur17
, Remark 1.4.2.25]
, this implies that
\Omega^{\infty-i}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathcal{X}
preserves filtered colimits for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
It now follows from
1.3.7
,
1.1.11
,
1.1.16
and
1.1.15
that for a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
,

\Omega^{\infty-i}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An}))\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})

preserves filtered colimits for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
∎

We now show that for every big presentable category
\mathcal{C}
, the infinite loop space functor has a left adjoint which factors over the categories of (grouplike) commutative monoids in
\mathcal{C}
. We will apply this below to describe a
t
-structure on spectrum objects and to prove a recognition principle for big topoi.

Definition 1.3.9

(
[
GGN13
, Definition 1.2]
)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a cartesian monoidal category.
A commutative monoid
A\in\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{C})
is grouplike if the underlying commutative monoid in the homotopy category
\operatorname{ho}(\mathcal{C})
is a group, i.e. the shear map
A\times A\to A\times A
is an isomorphism.
Denote by
\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{C})
the full subcategory of
\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{C})
on grouplike commutative monoids.

See
[
GGN13
, Proposition 1.1]
for other characterizations of grouplike commutative monoids.

Lemma 1.3.10
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentable category.
The functor
\Omega^{\infty}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
admits a left adjoint
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B_{\infty}}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
which factors into left adjoints

\mathcal{B_{\infty}}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}}),

where

\mathcal{B_{\infty}}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}}),\text{ and }\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})

are left adjoint to the forget functors.

Proof.

This is a straightforward consequence of
[
GGN13
, Corollary 4.10]
and
Lemma

A.1.2
.
Recall from
[
GGN13
, Corollary 4.7]
that for a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
,

\mathcal{C}\cong\operatorname{An}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{C},\,\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{CMon}(\operatorname{An})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{C},\text{ and }\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{C}.

Under these identifications, the functors

(\operatorname{An}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\operatorname{An}))\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}}\colon\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\operatorname{An})

and

(\operatorname{CMon}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\operatorname{An}))\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}}\colon\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{C})

are left adjoint to the forget functors
\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{C}
. This follows from
[
GGN13
, Corollary 4.10, Corollary 4.8]
.
By
[
GGN13
, Corollary 4.10]
,
\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}-\colon\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
factors as

\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{CMon}(\operatorname{An})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}-}\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}-}\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}-}\operatorname{Pr}^{L}.

By
Lemma

1.3.6
, we now obtain natural transformations

\mathcal{B}_{*}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})

is left adjoint to
\Omega^{\infty}
and
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
are left adjoint to the forget functors.
For
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda
, this yields commutative diagrams
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B_{\mu}}}

We claim that their mates
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B_{\mu}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma}

commute as well, where the two right horizontal arrows are the forget functors.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
preserves finite limits,

[
GGN13
, Lemma 6.1]
implies that
\beta
and
\gamma
are equivalences, so it remains to show that
\alpha
is an equivalence.
As the forget functor
f_{\mu}\colon\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
is conservative, it suffices to show that
f_{\mu}\alpha
is an equivalence.
By the pasting law for mates (
[
CSY22
, Lemma 2.2.4]
) and since
\beta,\gamma
are equivalences,
f_{\mu}\alpha
is equivalent to the Beck-Chevalley transformation
\alpha\beta\gamma
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{B}}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\mu},}

which is an equivalence by
1.3.4.1
since
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
preserves finite limits.
It now follows from
Lemma

A.1.2
that after taking the colimit over
\Lambda
in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
, we obtain left adjoints

\mathcal{B_{\infty}}\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})\to{\underset{\lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}).

By
Lemma

1.3.5
,
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
Since for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\times}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\times}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory and
\Lambda
is filtered,
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})\cong\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
As for
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\operatorname{ho}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{ho}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a full cartesian subcategory, this restricts to an equivalence
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}).

We have therefore constructed left adjoints

\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}).

Their composition is left adjoint to
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\Omega^{\infty}_{\lambda}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})=\Omega^{\infty}_{B_{\infty}}
.
The functors

\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

are left adjoint to the
\Lambda
-indexed colimits of the forget functors

\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\operatorname{CMon}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},

which equal the forget functors.
∎

Remark 1.3.11
.

The above proof and
1.1.21
imply that if
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site, then

\operatorname{CMon}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An}))\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{CMon}(\operatorname{An}))

and

\operatorname{CGrp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C}))\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})).

Lemma 1.3.12
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{\mathcal{}}{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentable category.
Then

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})_{\leq-1}\coloneqq\{X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\,|\,\Omega^{\infty}X=0\}

determines a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
.
Its connective part is generated by the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
under small colimits and extensions, and its coconnective part equals

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0}=\{X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\,|\,\Omega^{\infty}(X)\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\}.

If
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\text{ and }\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\leq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0}.

Proof.

Denote by
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
the subcategory generated by the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
under small colimits and extensions.
As for
X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
,

L_{X}\coloneqq\{T\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\,|\,\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})}(T,X)=0\}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

is closed under small colimits and extensions, for
X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq-1}
and
T\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
,

(1.3.12.1)

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(T,X)=0.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories.
As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\Omega^{\infty}
restricts to
\Omega^{\infty}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\leq-1}\coloneqq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq-1}\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

is the
(-1)
-coconnective part of a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.4.3.4]
.
We claim that its connective part
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
equals
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
. As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a full subcategory,
1.3.12.1
implies that

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
. The proof of
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.4.3.4]
shows that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
is generated under small colimits and extensions by the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
.
By construction,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
contains the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
. Since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits, it is also closed under extensions, which implies that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
.

We now deduce from this the statement of the lemma.
As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is closed under small colimits and extensions, the category

\{X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\,|\,\Sigma X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\}

is closed under small colimits and extensions. It contains the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
, which implies that

\Sigma(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}.

Clearly,
\Omega(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0}
.
For
x\in\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
x\in\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
and a fiber sequence
x_{+}\to x\to x_{-}\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
with
x_{+}\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0},x_{-}\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\leq-1}
.
Since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is exact,
x_{+}\to x\to x_{-}
is a fiber sequence in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, and by the above,
x_{+}\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0},x_{-}\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq-1}
. This shows that
(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq-1})
constitutes a
t
-structure.
We have shown above that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\text{ and }\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\leq-1}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq-1}.

As

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda/\infty})_{\leq 0}=\{X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda/\infty})\,|\,\Omega X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda/\infty})_{\leq-1}\}

and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a stable subcategory, this implies that

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\leq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0}.

For
X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
,

\mathcal{L}_{X}^{+}\coloneqq\{B\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\,|\,\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(B,X)\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{An}\}

is closed under small colimits and extensions, whence
X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0}
if and only if
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\subseteq\mathcal{L}_{X}^{+}
.
As
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\dashv\Omega^{\infty}
, it follows that

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0}=\{X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\,|\,\Omega^{\infty}(X)\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\}.\qed

Corollary 1.3.13
.

If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big topos, the left adjoint
\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
from
Lemma

1.3.10
factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}.

This restricts to an equivalence
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\heartsuit}
between the 1-category of abelian group objects in
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
and the heart of the
t
-structure.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by topoi.
By
[
HPT25
, Proposition 3.8]
, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
the left adjoint
\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is fully faithful with essential image
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
. We thank Lucas Piessevaux for pointing out this reference to us.
It now follows from
Lemma

A.1.3
and the construction of the left adjoint
\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
that it is fully faithful.
Since for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
, its essential image equals
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
.

As

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit}=\{X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\,|\,\Omega^{\infty}(X)\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\},

the equivalence
\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit},

and since
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under limits,
