\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\cong\operatorname{CGrp}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}).\qed

Definition 1.3.14
.

For a big topos
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
, the functor

H\colon\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\heartsuit}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})

is called
Eilenberg-Mac Lane functor
.

In addition to
1.3.4
, stabilization also commutes with left-exact left adjoints:

Corollary 1.3.15
.

Suppose that
L\colon\mathcal{X}\rightleftarrows\mathcal{Y}\colon R
,
L\dashv R
is an adjunction between big presentable categories such that
L
preserves finite limits.
Then
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}L\cong L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
via the Beck-Chevalley transformation of the commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Y}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{\operatorname{Sp}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}

.

Proof.

By
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.7.4.14]
, the Beck-Chevalley transformation is an equivalence if and only if the opposite Beck-Chevalley transformation

\Omega^{\infty}R_{\operatorname{Sp}}\to R\Omega^{\infty}
is, which holds by construction of the adjunction
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv R_{\operatorname{Sp}}
.
∎

Lemma 1.3.16
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}
are big presentable categories.

(i)

If
F\colon\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}
is a finite limits preserving functor, its stabilization
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})
is left t-exact, i.e.
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is exact and
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq 0})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})_{\leq 0}
.

(ii)

If
L\colon\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}
is a left-exact left adjoint, its stabilization
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})
is t-exact.

Proof.

By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.16]
, a finite limits preserving functor
F\colon\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}
preserves
0
-truncated objects.
By definition of the stabilization
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}
,
F\circ\Omega^{\infty}=\Omega^{\infty}F_{\operatorname{Sp}}
. The characterization of the coconnective part of the
t
-structure from
Lemma

1.3.12
now implies that

F_{\operatorname{Sp}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq 0})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})_{\leq 0}.

Since finite limits in

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},\mathcal{X})\text{ and }\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An}^{\operatorname{fin}}_{*},\mathcal{Y})

are computed pointwise,
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}
preserves finite limits. As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})
are stable (
Lemma

1.3.2
), it follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.1.4.1]
that
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is exact.

Suppose now that
L\colon\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}
is a left-exact left adjoint.
Since
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is a left adjoint (
1.3.4
) and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})
is closed under small colimits and extensions,

\mathcal{L}_{\geq 0}\coloneqq\{X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\,|\,L_{\operatorname{Sp}}(X)\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})_{\geq 0}\}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})

is closed under small colimits and extensions. As
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}L
(
1.3.15
),
\mathcal{L}_{\geq 0}
contains the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{X}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
, which implies that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{L}_{\geq 0}
.
It now follows from the above that
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact.
∎

For a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
, the stabilization functor
\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
is the initial cocontinuous functor into a presentable stable category.
Our next goal is to show that for a big presentable category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
, the
stabilization

\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

has a similar universal property, see
1.3.20
,
1.3.21
.

An object
b
in a stable category
\mathcal{B}
is a generator if
\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B}}(b,T)=0
implies that
T=0
. By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.4.2]
, every stable, presentable category admits a generator.

Lemma 1.3.17
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}
is a presentable, stable category and
b\in\mathcal{B}
is a generator.
If
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}
is a stable, full subcategory closed under small colimits with
b\in\mathcal{C}
, then the inclusion
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}
is an equivalence.

Proof.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}
is a stable, full subcategory closed under small colimits and
b\in\mathcal{C}
.
Then
\mathcal{C}
is presentable by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.4.2]
, whence by the adjoint functor theorem
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
,
l\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
admits a right adjoint
r
.
Since
l\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is fully faithful, the unit is an equivalence.
For
x\in\mathcal{D}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(lb,lrx)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(b,rx)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(lb,x),

whence

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(lb,\operatorname{Fib}(lrx\to x))=0
.
As
lb
is a generator, this implies that
\operatorname{Fib}(lrx\to x)=0
, which shows that the counit
lr\to\operatorname{id}
is an equivalence.
∎

Corollary 1.3.18
.

Suppose that
T
is a stable, presentable category,
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentable category, and
F\colon T\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a cocontinuous, left-exact functor.
If
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories, there exists
\lambda\in\Lambda
such that
F
factors over
T\to{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\subseteq{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}
.

Proof.

For
\lambda\in\Lambda
denote by
\overline{{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}}
the essential image of
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
. Choose a generator
t\in T
and
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
F(t)\in\overline{{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}}
.
Since
\overline{{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}}\subseteq{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}
is closed under small colimits and finite limits and
F
preserves finite limits and small colimits,

\{x\in T\,|\,F(x)\in\overline{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\}\subseteq T

is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits.

Lemma

1.3.17
now implies that
F
factors over
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
.
∎

Lemma

1.3.17
also implies that the category of spectrum objects
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
of a big presentable category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is as a stable category generated by the image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
under small colimits:

Corollary 1.3.19
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentable category.
If
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits and equivalences such that
\operatorname{ess.im}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})\subseteq\mathcal{C}
, then

\mathcal{C}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}).

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
, and for
\lambda\in\Lambda
denote by
i_{\lambda}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
the canonical functor.
As
i_{\lambda}
is a left adjoint and
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits,

\tilde{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\coloneqq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\times_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}\mathcal{C}\cong\{b\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\,|\,i_{\lambda}(b)\in\mathcal{C}\}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits.
Since
\operatorname{ess.im}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})\subseteq\mathcal{C}
, the proof of
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.4.2]
implies that
\tilde{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
contains a generator of
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
. Hence by
Lemma

1.3.17
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\times_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is an equivalence for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, which by
Lemma

1.3.5
implies that the inclusion
\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is an equivalence.
As
\mathcal{C}
is closed under equivalences, it follows that
\mathcal{C}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
∎

For potentially large categories
\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}
denote by
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
the full subcategory of small colimits preserving functors.
The above implies that the
stabilization

\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

of a big presentable category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
almost has a universal property:

Corollary 1.3.20
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
are two big presentable categories and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is stable.

Pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
defines a fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}).

If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
admit small coproducts, then this is an equivalence.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
are closed under small colimits for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
(
Lemma

1.3.5
and
Lemma

1.2.4
),

Lemma

1.3.5
and the construction of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}

Lemma

1.3.10
imply that

(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

factors as

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\hookrightarrow{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

where the left functor is induced by the restrictions along
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, the middle functor is induced by pullback along the functors
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
, and the right functor is induced by the inclusions
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})
.
The left and right functor are fully faithful:
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})
is equivalent to the full subcategory of functors
F\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is cocontinuous, and
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})
is equivalent to the full subcategory of functors
F\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
F|_{{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}}
is cocontinuous, cf.
Lemma

A.1.4
.
We claim that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

is fully faithful.
Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{C}_{*}\colon F\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
.
Since for all
f\in F
,
\mathcal{C}_{f}\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is a presentable category closed under finite limits and colimits, it is a stable presentable category.
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.4.5]
implies that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
induces an equivalence

{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{f})\cong{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{f}).

Since for all
f\to g\in F
,
\mathcal{C}_{f}\to\mathcal{C}_{g}
is fully faithful and cocontinuous,

{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{f})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

and

{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{f})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

are fully faithful by
Lemma

A.1.3
.
By
1.3.18
,

{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{f})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

is essentially surjective and hence an equivalence, which shows that

(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

is fully faithful for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
This proves that

(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

is fully faithful and factors as

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\hookrightarrow{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{f})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}},\mathcal{C}_{f})

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}).

Suppose now that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
admit small coproducts.
We first want to show that

(1.3.20.1)

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty}),

i.e. that a functor
G\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is cocontinuous if for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
G|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
is cocontinuous.
Suppose that
T\colon I\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a small diagram and choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with

\sqcup_{i\in I}T(i)\in\operatorname{ess.im}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})).

Since
\operatorname{ess.im}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits, for all
i\in I
,

T(i)=\operatorname{Cofib}(\sqcup_{\begin{subarray}{c}j\in I\\
j\neq i\end{subarray}}T(i)\to\sqcup_{{j\in I}}T(j))\in\operatorname{ess.im}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})),

i.e.
T
factors over
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
and we can compute
{\underset{}{\operatorname{colim}}}^{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})}T
in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, which shows
1.3.20.1
.
As a consequence,

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{f})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C_{\infty}})

factors over a fully faithful functor
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{f})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C_{\infty}}).

We claim that this functor is essentially surjective, i.e. for every small colimits preserving functor
G\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
and
\lambda\in\Lambda
, there exists
f(\lambda)\in F
such that
F|_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
factors over
\mathcal{C}_{f}\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is presentable, there exists a regular cardinal
\kappa
and a small set of
\kappa
-compact objects
(b_{i})_{i\in I}
which generates
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
under small colimits (
[
Lur09
, Theorem 5.5.1.1]
).
Choose
f\in F
with
\sqcup_{i\in I}G(b_{i})\in\operatorname{ess.im}(\mathcal{C}_{f}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty})
. Since
\operatorname{ess.im}(\mathcal{C}_{f}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is a stable subcategory closed under colimits, by the same argument as above, if follows that

\{b\in\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\,|\,G(b)\in\operatorname{ess.im}(\mathcal{C}_{f}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\}

is closed under small colimits and contains
b_{i}
for all
i\in I
, i.e.
G
factors over
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{C}_{f}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
.
∎

Remark 1.3.21
.

The above proof also shows a universal property of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
:
For big presentable categories
\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
denote by

\operatorname{Fun}^{p\operatorname{-colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

the full subcategory of functors
F\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
such that for all presentable categories
P
and all small colimits preserving, left-exact functors
p\colon P\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
,
F\circ p
preserves small colimits.
The above proof and
1.3.18
show that if
\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
are big presentable categories and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is stable, pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
induces a fully faithful functor

(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{p\operatorname{-colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}).

Its essential image consists of those functors
F\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
such that there exists an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}^{F}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by topoi such that
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{F}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\xrightarrow{F}\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
preserves small colimits for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.

1.3.1
Symmetric monoidal structure

We now formulate conditions under which a (symmetric) monoidal structure on a big presentable category induces a (symmetric) monoidal category on its category of spectrum objects.

Definition 1.3.22
.

A
chain
of presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories is a functor

\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

from a large filtered set
\Lambda
such that for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
, the underlying functor of categories
\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
is a fully faithful, left-exact left adjoint.

The forget functor
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is lax symmetric monoidal (
[
Lur17
, Propositions 4.8.1.15, 4.8.1.4]
), and therefore lifts to a functor

\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}).

A
big presentably (symmetric) monoidal category
is a (symmetric) monoidal category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
such that there exists a chain of presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
with colimit
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
in
\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
.

Lemma 1.3.23
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
is a chain of presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories. The colimit
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\coloneqq{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}
in
\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
exists and is a (symmetric) monoidal enhancement of
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
.

Proof.

The category
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
has all
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small colimits, and the tensor product on
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is compatible with
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small colimits (
[
Lur17
, Definition 3.1.1.18]
) by
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2]
in the universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
.
Since
\Lambda
is
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small and filtered,
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.3.1]
(in
\mathcal{U}_{1})
now implies that the colimit of
\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes}
in
\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
exists and is a (symmetric) monoidal enhancement of
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
.
∎

Definition 1.3.24
.

Suppose
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a possibly large (symmetric) monoidal category.
A subcategory
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{D}
is a (symmetric) monoidal subcategory if it contains the unit and for
b,c\in\mathcal{C}
,
b\otimes_{\mathcal{D}}c\in\mathcal{C}
.
By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 2.2.1.1]
, this implies that there exists an operad
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
which exhibits
\mathcal{C}
as a (symmetric) monoidal category.

If
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a presentably (symmetric) monoidal category, a
presentably (symmetric) monoidal subcategory

\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{D}
is a (symmetric) monoidal subcategory which is presentable, closed under small colimits and finite limits, and such that the induced tensor product on
\mathcal{C}
preserves small colimits in both variables.

By
Lemma

1.3.23
, a (symmetric) monoidal category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably (symmetric) monoidal category if and only if its underlying category is a big presentable category and admits an exhaustion by presentably (symmetric) monoidal subcategories.

Example 1.3.25
.

If
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos, the cartesian monoidal structure on
\mathcal{X}
exhibits it a big presentably symmetric monoidal category:
If
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion for
\mathcal{X}
by topoi, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under finite limits (
Lemma

1.2.4
), whence
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}^{\times}\subseteq\mathcal{X}^{\times}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory. By universality of colimits in the topos
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
,
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}^{\times}
is presentably symmetric monoidal.

The main result of this section is the following:

Proposition 1.3.26
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably (symmetric) monoidal category.
There exists a (symmetric) monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
such that

\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B_{\infty}}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})

promotes to a (symmetric) monoidal functor and for all presentably (symmetric) monoidal subcategories
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a presentably (symmetric) monoidal subcategory.
This is unique in the following sense: If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\tilde{\otimes}}
are two (symmetric) monoidal enhancements as above, there is an essentially unique (symmetric) monoidal equivalence
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\tilde{\otimes}}
of (symmetric) monoidal categories over
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
, and this is a (symmetric) monoidal enhancement of the identity
\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}
.

We will prove this below. If
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
has small colimits, the above (symmetric) monoidal structure has a handier characterization:

Corollary 1.3.27
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably (symmetric) monoidal category and denote by
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
its underlying category. Suppose that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
has small coproducts.

The (symmetric) monoidal enhancement
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}
from
Proposition

1.3.26
is the unique one so that the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
preserves small colimits in both variables.

Proof of
Proposition

1.3.26
.

We only prove the statement for symmetric monoidal structures here, the statement for monoidal structures can be shown completely analogously. We first prove existence of the symmetric monoidal structure.
The symmetric monoidal localization

-\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\operatorname{Sp}\colon\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}

(
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.8.2.18]
) enhances to a localization

\operatorname{Sp}(-)^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L}),

cf.
A.2.6
.
Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories.
The adjunction unit for
\operatorname{Sp}(-)^{\otimes}
yields an enhancement

\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}^{\otimes})^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L}))

of
\mathcal{B}_{*}\to\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{B}_{*}
, cf.
A.2.6
or
[
GGN13
, Theorem 5.1/Corollary 5.5.(ii)]
.
Composing with the forget functor
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
yields a natural transformation

\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{*}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes})^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})).

By
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2]
in the large universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
,
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
has all large colimits and the symmetric monoidal structure is compatible with large colimits. Hence, by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.2.3.2]
(in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
), the colimit

{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{*}\to{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{*})^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})

exists and is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
. By construction,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Suppose that
\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal subcategory.
Since
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under small colimits,
\mathcal{C}
is presentable and
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is locally small (
Lemma

1.2.4
),
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a left adjoint by
[
Lur09
, Remark 5.5.2.10]
.
As
\mathcal{C}\subseteq{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}
is closed under finite limits, the induced functor
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a fully faithful left adjoint and

\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\xrightarrow{\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

factors over

\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

by
1.3.15
.
As
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\xrightarrow{\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is symmetric monoidal, this implies that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
contains the unit of
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
By
1.3.18
, there exists
\lambda\in\Lambda
such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
.
For
x\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{\mathcal{C}})
denote by
\mathcal{G}_{x}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
the full subcategory on objects
g\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
such that
x\otimes g,g\otimes x\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
.
Since

x\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}-,-\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})_{\lambda}}x\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

are exact, cocontinuous functors and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits,
\mathcal{\mathcal{}}G_{x}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits.
It therefore suffices to show that for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}c\in\mathcal{G}_{x}
, then it follows from
1.3.19
that
\mathcal{G}_{x}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
. If
x=\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}d,d\in\mathcal{C}
, this holds by monoidality of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\circ(\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
By the same argument as above,

\mathcal{G}\coloneqq\{x\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\,|\,\mathcal{G}_{x}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})

is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits. Since it contains the image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
,
\mathcal{G}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{\mathcal{C}})
by
1.3.19
, which proves that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.
As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
preserves small colimits, the induced tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
is cocontinuous in both variables.
This proves the existence of a symmetric monoidal structure with the claimed properties.

It remains to show the uniqueness statement.
Suppose that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\tilde{\otimes}}
is another symmetric monoidal structure and
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\tilde{\otimes}}
is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\tilde{\otimes}}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal subcategory.
Denote by

\operatorname{Map}^{c,\Lambda}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\subseteq\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))

the full subspace on functors
F\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

F|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
preserves small colimits, and by
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{c}\subseteq\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
the wide subcategory on small colimits preserving functors.
Then

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}^{\otimes}}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\tilde{\otimes}})\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))}\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}^{c,\Lambda}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(\operatorname{Map}_{{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\kappa}^{\otimes}}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\tilde{\otimes}})\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))}\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{c}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\right)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(\operatorname{Map}_{{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\kappa}^{\otimes}}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\tilde{\otimes}})\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}))}\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{c}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}))\right),

where we used in the last step that every cocontinuous functor
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
factors over
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
for some
\mu\geq\kappa
(
1.3.18
), and that
\Lambda
is filtered.
By assumption,
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\otimes},\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\tilde{\otimes}|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})}}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
, whence the right-hand side is equivalent to

\displaystyle{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\kappa}^{\otimes}}}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\tilde{\otimes}}).

As
\operatorname{Sp}(-)^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
is a localization,
\operatorname{Map}_{{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\kappa}^{\otimes}}}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})^{\tilde{\otimes}|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})}})
is contractible for all
\kappa\in\Lambda
.
This shows that

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}^{\otimes}}}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\tilde{\otimes}})\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))}\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}^{c,\Lambda}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\cong{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}*

is contractible, i.e. there exists an essentially unique symmetric monoidal functor

F^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\tilde{\otimes}}

over
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
such that
F|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
is cocontinuous for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
As

\operatorname{Sp}(-)^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

is a lift of the localization
\operatorname{Sp}(-)\colon\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
, for all
\kappa\in\Lambda
, the essentially unique cocontinuous symmetric monoidal functor

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})^{\tilde{\otimes}}\in{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\kappa}^{\otimes}}}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}

is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of the identity for all
\kappa\in\Lambda
.
As
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
preserves large sifted colimits (
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2, Corollary 3.2.3.2]
), this implies that

F\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\tilde{\otimes}}

is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of the identity and in particular an equivalence.
As every equivalence has to preserve small colimits and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is closed under small colimits, the space of symmetric monoidal equivalences

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\tilde{\otimes}}

in
\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}^{\otimes}}}
is a subspace of

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}^{\otimes}}}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\tilde{\otimes}})\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))}\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}^{c,\Lambda}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))

and hence contractible. (It is non-empty by the above).
∎

Proof of
1.3.27
.

We only prove the statement for symmetric monoidal structures here, the statement for monoidal structures can be shown completely analogously.
We first show that the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is cocontinuous in both variables.
Suppose that
S
is a small category and
F\colon S\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
Choose an essentially surjective functor
i\colon T\to S
from a set
T
and
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
\oplus_{t\in T}F(it)\in\operatorname{ess.im}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))=:\overline{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
.
Since
\overline{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is closed under colimits, for all
t\in T
,

F(it)=\operatorname{Cofib}(\oplus_{s\in T}F(is)\to\oplus_{\begin{subarray}{c}s\in T\\
s\neq t\end{subarray}}F(it)\hookrightarrow\oplus_{s\in T}F(is))\in\overline{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}.

This implies that
F
factors over
S\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
. In particular,
{\underset{S}{\operatorname{colim}}}F
exists in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
and can be computed in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
For
b\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
choose
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda
such that
b\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a presentably symmetric monoidal subcategory, it follows that

{\underset{S}{\operatorname{colim}}}(F\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}b)\cong{\underset{S}{\operatorname{colim}}}(F\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}b)\cong({\underset{S}{\operatorname{colim}}}F)\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})}b\cong({\underset{S}{\operatorname{colim}}}F)\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}b,

which shows that the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is cocontinuous in both variables.

Suppose now that
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\tilde{\otimes}}
is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
such that the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is cocontinuous in both variables, and
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal subcategory.
Since the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is cocontinuous, one can argue as in the proof of
Proposition

1.3.26
that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory. As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is closed under finite limits and small colimits, it is a presentably symmetric monoidal subcategory.
∎

For categories of accessible (hyper)sheaves on (hyper)accessible explicit covering sites, the above recovers the symmetric monoidal structure constructed in
1.1.27
:

Lemma 1.3.28
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site.
The equivalence from
1.3.7
enhances to a symmetric monoidal equivalence

\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})^{\times})^{\otimes}\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})^{\otimes},

where the left-hand side is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure from
Proposition

1.3.26
and the right-hand side with the symmetric monoidal structure induced from
\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes}
via
1.1.27
.
In particular, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An}))
is closed.

Proof.

By
1.1.27
,
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\operatorname{An}^{\times}\to\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes}
induces a symmetric monoidal functor

\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An})^{\times}\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})^{\otimes}.

Under the identification
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C}))
of
1.3.7
, the functor underlying
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}
is left adjoint to
\Omega^{\infty}
.
As the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})
is closed (
1.1.28
) and
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})
has all small colimits (
1.1.15
), the statement now follows from
1.3.27
.
∎

Remark 1.3.29
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a big presentable symmetric monoidal category such that the induced symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is closed.
The internal Hom

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

has the following properties:

(i)

If
I
is a small category such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
has
I
-indexed colimits and
I^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed limits, then
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(-,-)
preserves
I
-indexed limits in the first variable by
Lemma

A.1.1
and
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.2.6.2]
.

(ii)

Since
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(-,-)
preserves limits in the second variable, stability implies that for
i\in\mathbb{Z}
,
\Sigma^{i}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(-,-)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(-,\Sigma^{i}-)
.

(iii)

As
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}
is symmetric monoidal, for
b\in\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
,

\Omega^{\infty}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}b,-)

is right adjoint to
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(b\otimes-)
.
In particular, if the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed with internal mapping functors
\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,-)
, then

\Omega^{\infty}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}-,-)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,\Omega^{\infty}-).

The universal property of the stabilization functor (
1.3.20
) has a (symmetric) monoidal analogue:
For potentially large (symmetric) monoidal categories
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
denote by
\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})
the category of (symmetric) monoidal functors and by

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})

the full subcategory on (symmetric) monoidal functors whose underlying functor preserves small colimits.

Corollary 1.3.30
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
are two big presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is stable.
Then pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}
defines a fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})

with essential image

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}).

In particular, if
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
admit small coproducts, then

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}).

Proof.

We first prove fully faithfulness.
Choose exhaustions

\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L}),\mathcal{C}_{*}^{\otimes}\colon F\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
by presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories.
Since for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under colimits and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes}
,

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\hookrightarrow{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})

is fully faithful.
Since
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is stable,
1.3.18
and
A.1.3
imply that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}).

For all
f\in F
,
\mathcal{C}_{f}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
is closed under finite limits and colimits and hence stable.
As
\operatorname{Sp}\in\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is idempotent, this implies that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
and
f\in F
,

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes})

via pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+,\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes}
, cf.
[
GGN13
, Proposition 5.4]
.
By
Lemma

A.1.3
,
{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})
is fully faithful.
By construction (see the proof of
Proposition

1.3.26
),

(1.3.30.1)

\displaystyle\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+,\lambda}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}))\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})).

This implies that pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}
factors as

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\hookrightarrow{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{f\in F}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes})

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}),

and is in particular fully faithful.
Pullback along
\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}
also factors over

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\xrightarrow{i}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

\displaystyle\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}).

By
1.3.20
, the right functor is fully faithful, hence so is
i
by the above.
We claim that
i
is an equivalence.
Suppose that
G\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is a cocontinuous functor and there exists a cocontinuous (symmetric) monoidal functor
H^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
with
H\cong G\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
.

1.3.30.1
implies that

\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})}\{H^{\otimes}\}\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\bigl(\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}^{\otimes}},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})}\{H^{\otimes}|_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}}\}\bigr).

For
\lambda\in\Lambda
, choose
f\in F
such that
G(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{f}
. This is possible by
1.3.18
. Then
H^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes}
, and hence

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}^{\otimes}},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})}\{H^{\otimes}|_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}}\}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{f}^{\otimes})}\{H^{\otimes}|_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}}\}.

The right-hand side is contractible since
\operatorname{Sp}
is an idempotent in
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
, cf.
[
GGN13
, Proposition 5.4]
.
This implies that

*\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}*\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}^{\otimes}},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})}\{H^{\otimes}|_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}}\},

i.e. there exists an essentially unique (symmetric) monoidal functor
\tilde{G}^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C}_{\infty})
with
\tilde{G}^{\otimes}\circ\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}=H^{\otimes}
such that
\tilde{G}^{\otimes}|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}
is cocontinuous for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
We have shown in the proof of
1.3.20
that

(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})^{*}\colon{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda},\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

is fully faithful.
As
\tilde{G}\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\cong H\cong G\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
, this shows that
\tilde{G}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
G
, which proves that

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\xrightarrow{i}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}),\mathcal{C}_{\infty})

is an equivalence.

1.3.20
now implies that if
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
and
\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
admit small coproducts, then

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}).\qed

Corollary 1.3.31
.

Suppose that
F^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a (symmetric) monoidal functor between big presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories such that the underlying functor
F\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\mathcal{C}_{\infty}
is a left-exact left adjoint.
There exists an essentially unique filler

F_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C}_{\infty})^{\otimes}

for the diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C}_{\infty}^{\otimes}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C}_{\infty})^{\otimes}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{\otimes}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\exists!}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}}

The functor
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
is a (symmetric) monoidal enhancement of
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}
.

Proof.

This follows from
1.3.30
since
F_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\circ F
by
1.3.15
.
∎

Lemma 1.3.32
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
is a chain of presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories.
The induced (symmetric) monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is compatible with the
t
-structure from
Lemma

1.3.12
, i.e.

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})

is a (symmetric) monoidal subcategory (
Definition

1.3.24
).

Proof.

Since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
contains the unit, it suffices to show that for all
x,y\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
,

x\otimes y,y\otimes x\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
for
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
by presentably (symmetric) monoidal subcategories.
For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\otimes}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}
is a (symmetric) monoidal subcategory by
Proposition

1.3.26
, and by
Lemma

1.3.12
, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}.

As
\Lambda
is filtered, it therefore suffices to show that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
is closed under
-\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}-
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Fix
\lambda\in\Lambda
and for
x\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
let

\mathcal{G}_{x}\coloneqq\{y\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}\,|\,x\otimes y\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}\}.

As the (symmetric) monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
is cocontinuous and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is closed under small colimits and extensions,
\mathcal{G}_{x}
is closed under small colimits and extensions.

Since
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
enhances to a (symmetric) monoidal functor, this implies that for
x=\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}x_{0}
,
\mathcal{G}_{x}
contains the essential image of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
and hence
\mathcal{G}_{x}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
by
1.3.19
.
By the same reasoning as above,

\mathcal{G}\coloneqq\{x\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}\,|\,\mathcal{G}_{x}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}\}

is closed under small colimits and extensions, whence
\mathcal{G}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}
by
1.3.19
.
∎

In particular, if
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentably symmetric monoidal category, then
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit}
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure such that
\tau_{\leq 0}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit}
enhances to a (symmetric) monoidal functor
\tau_{\leq 0}^{\otimes}
by
[
Lur17
, Example 2.2.1.10]
.
Being right adjoint to the (symmetric) monoidal functor
\tau_{\leq 0}^{\otimes}
, the inclusion
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}
enhances to fully faithful right adjoints

\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}),

cf.
A.2.6
.

Notation 1.3.33
.

If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big topos, endow

\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit}\text{ (\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{recognitionprinciplebigtopoi})}

with the induced symmetric monoidal structure. The Eilenberg-Mac Lane functor (
Definition

1.3.14
) induces fully faithful functors

\displaystyle H\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0})\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\text{ and }

\displaystyle H\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0})\subseteq\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})).

We will in the sequel freely identify (commutative) algebras in
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
with their images under these functors.

Remark 1.3.34
.

If
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
is an chain of presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories exhausting
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
, then
\tau_{\leq 0}^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}^{\otimes}\to(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit})^{\otimes}
is the colimit of the functor

\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{B}_{*}}\otimes_{\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\tau_{\leq 0}\colon\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\times}\otimes_{\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\operatorname{Sp}_{\geq 0}\to\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\times}\otimes_{\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\operatorname{Ab}^{\otimes}

in
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
.
In particular, for a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
, there is a symmetric monoidal equivalence

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})^{\heartsuit}\cong\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab}),

where the right-hand side is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure from
1.1.27
.

1.3.2
Spectral enrichment

In this section, we explain that every big presentable, stable category is naturally spectrally enriched and record some basic properties of this spectral enrichment.
The main result is that every adjunction between big presentable, stable categories enhances to an adjunction of spectrally enriched categories.
We will use the spectral enrichment described below to define cohomology in big topoi.

Construction 1.3.35
.

By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.8.2.18]
, the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is fully faithful with essential image the category
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}_{\operatorname{st}}
of stable, presentable categories. A chain of stable, presentable categories
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
therefore enhances essentially uniquely to a functor
\mathcal{B}^{\operatorname{Sp}}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})
.
By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15, Remark 4.8.1.8]
, the forget functor
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
enhances to a lax symmetric monoidal functor (where the left-hand side is endowed with the Lurie tensor product
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
and the right-hand side with the cartesian monoidal structure). This induces a functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})
.
Since
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
has all large colimits and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is compatible with large colimits (
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2]
in the large universe),
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})
has all large colimits and the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
reflects large colimits by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.5]
in the very large universe. In particular,
{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\operatorname{Sp}}
exhibits the colimit
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
as a left
\operatorname{Sp}
-module.

If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentable category which is stable and
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion for
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories, then
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under finite limits and colimits for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
and in particular stable.
The above construction therefore yields a
\operatorname{Sp}
-module structure on
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
.

Lemma 1.3.36
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a stable, big presentable category. The
\operatorname{Sp}
-module structure of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
constructed above is independent of the chosen exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories.

Proof.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}_{\operatorname{st}},\mathcal{Y}_{*}\colon M\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}_{\operatorname{st}}
are two exhaustion for
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable stable categories.
By
1.3.18
, for
m\in M
, there exists
\kappa(m)\in\Lambda
such that
\mathcal{Y}_{m}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
factors over
\mathcal{X}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
.
For
(\lambda,m)\in\Lambda\times M
choose
\kappa\in\Lambda
with maps
\lambda\to\kappa,\kappa(m)\to\kappa
. Then

\mathcal{X}_{m}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{Y}_{\lambda}\cong\mathcal{X}_{m}\times_{\mathcal{Y}_{\kappa}}\mathcal{Y}_{\lambda}

is presentable.
As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under small colimits and finite limits (
Lemma

1.2.4
),
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{Y}_{m}\subseteq\mathcal{Y}_{m}
is closed under small colimits and finite limits, and analogously for
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{Y}_{m}\subseteq\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
It follows that the functor

M\times\Lambda\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty},(\lambda,m)\mapsto\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{Y}_{m}

enhances to a functor
\mathcal{X}_{*}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{Y}_{*}\colon M\times\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}_{\operatorname{st}}
which is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories.
Let

\pi_{\Lambda}^{*}\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon M\times\Lambda\to\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}_{\operatorname{st}}

and

\pi_{M}^{*}\mathcal{C}_{*}\colon M\times\Lambda\to M\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}_{\operatorname{st}}.

As
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})\cong\operatorname{Pr}^{L}_{\operatorname{st}}
(
[
Lur09
, Corollary 4.8.2.18]
), we obtain natural transformations

\pi_{M}^{*}\mathcal{C}_{*}\leftarrow\mathcal{B}_{*}\times_{\mathcal{B}}\mathcal{C}_{*}\to\pi^{*}\mathcal{B}_{*}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda\times M,\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})).

Taking the colimit in
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{\times}})
yields functors

{\underset{M}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{Sp}}_{*}\leftarrow{\underset{\Lambda\times M}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\mathcal{B}_{*}\times_{\mathcal{B}}\mathcal{C}_{*})\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{Sp}}.

By
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2, Corollary 4.2.3.5]
, the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is conservative and preserves large colimits. This implies that

{\underset{M}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{Y}_{*}\cong{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{X}_{*}\in\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}).\qed

Lemma 1.3.37
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a stable, big presentable category.
The left
\operatorname{Sp}
-module structure on
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
described above exhibits
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
as enriched (
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.2.1.28]
) over
\operatorname{Sp}
.
Denote by

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,-)\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}

the associated mapping spectrum functor (
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.2.1.31]
).
Then

\Omega^{\infty}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,-).

Proof.

For
M\in\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
M\in\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
.
Since
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\subseteq\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a
\operatorname{Sp}
-module map,

-\otimes M\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}

factors as
-\otimes M\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
, where
-\otimes M\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is induced by the left
\operatorname{Sp}
-tensoring of
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
. As
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{Sp}}
is in the image of the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})
,

-\otimes M\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}

is a left adjoint functor. By
Lemma

1.2.4
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a left adjoint, which implies that

-\otimes M\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}

is a left adjoint.
This shows that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is enriched in
\operatorname{Sp}
.
By definition of the mapping spectrum functor (
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.2.1.31]
),

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(\mathbb{S},\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(-_{1},-_{2}))\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(\mathbb{S}\otimes-_{1},-_{2})\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(-_{1},-_{2})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\operatorname{An}).

The left-hand side is equivalent to
\Omega^{\infty}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-_{1},-_{2})
.
∎

Corollary 1.3.38
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a stable, big presentable category.
The mapping spectrum functor

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(-,-)\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}

preserves small limits in both variables.

Proof.

For
b\in\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
,
\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(b,-)\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{Sp}
is a right adjoint and in particular preserves small limits.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
and
\operatorname{Sp}
are stable, this implies that

\Sigma^{n}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,\Sigma^{n}-)

for all
n\in\mathbb{Z}
.
Suppose
F\colon I\to B_{\infty}
is some small diagram and denote by
{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F
its colimit in
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
.
For
b\in\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
, the canonical map

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}({\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F,b)\to{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(F,b)

is an equivalence since for all
n\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\displaystyle\Omega^{\infty-n}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}({\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F,b)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}({\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F,\Sigma^{n}b)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(F,\Sigma^{n}b)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\Omega^{\infty-n}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(F,b)

\displaystyle\cong\Omega^{\infty-n}{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(F,b)

and the functors
\Omega^{\infty-n}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{An},n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
are jointly conservative.
∎

Next, we show that every adjunction between stable, big presentable categories is spectrally enriched.
For a category
\mathcal{T}
with small limits denote by
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{T})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{T})
the full subcategory on small limits-preserving functors.

Lemma 1.3.39
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a stable, big presentable category.
Pushforward along
\Omega^{\infty}
defines a fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Sp})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}).

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentable categories.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}}={\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}
and for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under small colimits, for a category
\mathcal{T}
, we have a fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{T})\hookrightarrow{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{T}).

For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under finite limits and colimits and in particular stable. Hence
\Omega^{\infty}
induces an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Sp})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}),

by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.4.2.21]
.
This shows that pushforward along
\Omega^{\infty}
defines a fully faithful functor

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Sp})\hookrightarrow{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Sp})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}).

Since
\Omega^{\infty}
preserves small limits, this factors over
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
.
∎

Corollary 1.3.40
.

Every adjunction
L\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}\colon R
between big presentable, stable categories is spectrally enriched, i.e. every adjunction datum

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(L-,-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,R-)\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}\to\operatorname{An}

lifts essentially uniquely to an equivalence of functors

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}}(L-,-)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,R-)\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}\to\operatorname{Sp}.

Proof.

For
\mathcal{T}=\operatorname{An},\operatorname{Sp}
denote by
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim},v}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D},\mathcal{T})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D},\mathcal{T})
the category of functors which preserve small limits in both variables.
By
Lemma

1.3.39
, pushforward along
\Omega^{\infty}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{An}
induces a fully faithful functor

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim},v}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D},\operatorname{Sp})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{D},\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Sp}))\hookrightarrow

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{D},\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim},v}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D},\operatorname{An}).

By
1.3.38
and
Lemma

1.3.37
, this implies that every equivalence

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(L-,-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(-,R-)

lifts essentially uniquely to an equivalence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}}(L-,-)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}}(-,R-)
.
∎

1.3.3
Constant sheaves

Lemma 1.3.41
.

For a big presentable category
\mathcal{B}
, there exists a unique small colimits preserving functor
c\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{B}
with
c(*)=*
.
This is a left adjoint.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{B}
by presentable categories and
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}
is closed under small colimits and
*\in\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
, every small colimits preserving functor
c\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{B}
with
c(*)=*
factors over a colimits preserving functor
\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
. Since
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
is cocomplete, there exists a unique such functor. This proves uniqueness and existence.
Since
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
is presentable, the cocontinuous functor
\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
admits a right adjoint
\Gamma_{\lambda}
.
By
Lemma

1.2.4
, the inclusion
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B}
admits a right adjoint
r^{\lambda}
.
The composite
\Gamma_{\lambda}\circ r^{\lambda}
is right adjoint to
c
.
∎

Definition 1.3.42
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}
is a big presentable category. The unique small colimits preserving functor
c\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{B}
with
c(*)=*
is called
constant sheaf functor
. Its right adjoint
\Gamma
is called
global sections functor
.

Corollary 1.3.43
.

If
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos, the constant sheaf functor
c\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{X}
is left-exact.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi and fix
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Choose a small category
\mathcal{C}
with a left-exact localisation
L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
As
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under finite limits and small colimits,
Lemma

1.3.41
implies that the constant sheaf functor factors as
