\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{c_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{L}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{X},

where
c_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}
denotes the constant sheaf functor of
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
.
The functor
c_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
is given by
X\mapsto(c\mapsto X)
and in particular left-exact as limits in
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
are computed pointwise.
∎

In particular, for a big topos
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
, the constant sheaf functor enhances essentially uniquely to a symmetric monoidal functor
c^{\times}\colon\operatorname{An}^{\times}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
(
[
Lur17
, Corollary 2.4.1.9]
).
1.3.31
implies:

Corollary 1.3.44
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big topos.

There is an essentially unique filler
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
for the diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{An}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B_{\infty}}^{\otimes}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\otimes}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c^{\times}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\exists!}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}}

of (symmetric) monoidal categories such that the underlying functor
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
is cocontinuous. The functor
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
is a (symmetric) monoidal enhancement of the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor.

For many big topoi, the constant sheaf functor commutes with totalizations of bounded above cosimplicial objects:

Lemma 1.3.45
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
admits countable products and denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor.
If
A\colon\Delta\to\operatorname{Sp}_{\leq N}
is a bounded above cosimplicial spectrum,
the canonical map

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}A)\to{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}(A)

is an equivalence.

Proof.

Since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is stable and admits countable products, it admits
\Delta
-indexed limits by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.6]
.
As
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is exact, for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A\cong{\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A
, whence it suffices to show that the canonical map
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}A)\to{\underset{p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}(A))
is an equivalence.
By
[
Lur17
, Remark 1.2.4.3]
, for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
,
\operatorname{Fib}({\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A\to{\underset{\Delta_{\leq p-1}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A)=\Omega^{p}A(p-1)
.
Choose
N\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
A\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta,\operatorname{Sp}_{\leq N})
.
Then

\Omega^{p}A(p-1)\in\operatorname{Sp}_{\leq N-p},

whence

\tau_{>N-p}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A\cong\tau_{>N-p}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq p-1}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A.

As
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact, this implies that

\tau_{>N-p}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A\cong\tau_{>N-p}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq p-1}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A.

Using
t
-exactness of
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
again, it follows that for all
m\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\tau_{\geq m}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}A\cong c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\tau_{\geq m}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}A\cong c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{k}{\operatorname{lim}}}^{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\geq m}}\tau_{\geq m}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq k}}{\operatorname{lim}}}(A))\cong c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\tau_{\geq m}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq N-m}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A

and

\tau_{\geq m}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong{\underset{k}{\operatorname{lim}}}^{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\geq m}}\tau_{\geq m}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq k}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A\cong\tau_{\geq m}{\underset{\Delta_{\leq N-m}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A,

which shows that

\tau_{\geq m}\operatorname{Fib}(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}A)\to{\underset{p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A))=0

for all
m\in\mathbb{Z}
.
Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi and
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
F\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
.
As for all
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq m}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})_{\leq m}
, the above implies that

F\coloneqq\operatorname{Fib}(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}A)\to{\underset{p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A))\in\bigcap_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}\tau_{<m}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}).

Since the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
is right-separated (
[
Lur18a
, Proposition 1.3.2.7]
), it follows that
F=0
, i.e.

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}A)\cong{\underset{p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}A).\qed

Lemma 1.3.46
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos. The monoidal functor
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\otimes}
provided by
1.3.44
exhibits
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
as left
\operatorname{Sp}
-module in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
.
This
\operatorname{Sp}
-module structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
agrees with the
\operatorname{Sp}
-module structure described in
1.3.35
.

Proof.

If
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{X}_{\infty}
by topoi,
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
factors over a symmetric monoidal functor
\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})^{\otimes}
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
This implies that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{*})^{\otimes}
enhances to a functor
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{*})^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\phantom{}_{\operatorname{Sp}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
. By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.1.5, Corollary 4.5.1.6]
,

\phantom{}{}_{\operatorname{Sp}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))\text{ and }\phantom{}_{\operatorname{Sp}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})).

Denote by

u\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})

the forget functor.
As
u
factors as

\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))\xrightarrow{v}\phantom{}_{\operatorname{Sp}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}}))\xrightarrow{w}\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}})

(where
v
,
w
are the forget functors), and
w
preserves large filtered colimits (
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.2.3.1, Lemma 4.8.4.2]
),

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}u\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})^{\otimes}
is the
\operatorname{Sp}
-module structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\infty})
provided by the symmetric monoidal functor
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
.
As every presentable stable category admits an essentially unique
\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes}
-module structure (
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.8.2.18]
),

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}u\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{*})^{\otimes}
is the
\operatorname{Sp}
-module constructed in
1.3.35
.
∎

Denote by
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{Sp}
the stabilization of the global sections functor, which is right adjoint to
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
.

Corollary 1.3.47
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big topos such that the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
induced by the cartesian monoidal structure on
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed and denote by

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{Sp}

the internal Hom.
Then
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})}(-,-)
recovers the
\operatorname{Sp}
-enrichment of
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
from
Lemma

1.3.37
.

1.4
Module categories

In this section, we record fundamental structural results on module categories (in big presentable categories).
Throughout, we freely use the notation of
[
Lur17
, section 4.2.1]
.
We begin by recalling conditions on a symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
under which the category of left
A
-modules
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
inherits a (closed) symmetric monoidal structure for all commutative algebras
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C})
.
Then we establish analogues of the following two results for big presentable categories:

(i)

If
A
is an algebra in a presentably monoidal category
\mathcal{C}
, the category of left
A
-modules is again presentable. (
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
)

(ii)

If
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is presentably symmetric monoidal, for a commutative algebra
A
in
\mathcal{C}
, the category of left
A
-modules
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
inherits the structure of a presentably symmetric monoidal category. (
[
Lur17
, Theorem 3.4.4.2]
)

Next, we show that if
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably monoidal category, for
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})_{\geq 0})
, the category of left
A
-modules
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})})
inherits a
t
-structure such that the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
is
t
-exact.
Here
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
is endowed with the
t
-structure and the monoidal structure described in
Propositions

1.3.26
and
1.3.12
, respectively.
In
Section

1.4.1
, we recall basic facts on derived categories and, adapting
[
Lur18a
, Proposition 2.1.2.2]
, describe conditions on a big topos
\mathcal{X}
under which

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

for all
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))
.
Such an equivalence is instructive since the right-hand side has more tractable categorical properties.
Finally, we record some basic properties of module categories over constant rings in big topoi.

Proposition 1.4.1

(
[
Lur17
, Chapter 4]
)
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
is a monoidal category and
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})
is an associative algebra.

(i)

The forget functor

f\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathcal{C}
is conservative and reflects limits.

(ii)

If
K
is a category such that
\mathcal{C}
has
K
-indexed colimits and the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-
preserves
K
-indexed colimits in both variables, then the forget functor preserves all
K
-indexed colimits.

(iii)

The forget functor has a left adjoint
A[-]
with
f\circ A[-]=A\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-
.

Proof.

The forget functor is conservative by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.5.8]
(in the universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
).
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.3]
(in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
), it preserves limits.
The preservation of
K
-indexed colimits is
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.5]
(in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
).
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.4.8]
(in the universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
), the forget functor has a left adjoint
A[-]
with
f\circ A[-]=A\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-
.
∎

Recollection 1.4.2
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
is a symmetric monoidal category such that
\mathcal{C}
has
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
For a commutative algebra
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})
denote by
\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}\to N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
the operad defined in
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.5.1.1]
. By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.5.2.1]
, this is a symmetric monoidal category and by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.5.1.6]
, the category underlying
\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}
is equivalent to
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
. We endow
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
with the induced symmetric monoidal structure.

By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.5.3.1/Remark 4.5.3.2]
, a morphism
A\to B\in\operatorname{CAlg}(A)
induces a strong symmetric monoidal functor
\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{B}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}
.
The symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Mod}_{-}({-})
is moreover natural with respect to symmetric monoidal functors:
Suppose
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is another symmetric monoidal category with
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}}-
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
A lax symmetric monoidal functor
\phi\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
induces a functor
\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})
.
For
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C})
,
\phi
induces a functor
\phi^{A,\otimes}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})^{\otimes}
of categories over
N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
. This is immediate from the definition of
\operatorname{Mod}_{-}({-})^{\otimes}
.
It follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.3.3.10]
, that

\phi^{A,\otimes}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})^{\otimes}

is lax symmetric monoidal (i.e. preserves inert morphisms).
By construction of
\phi^{A,\otimes}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
, the underlying functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})
is pushforward along the lax
\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}
-monoidal functor

\phi\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}.

Lemma 1.4.3
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
are symmetric monoidal categories whose underlying categories admit
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor products
-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-
and
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}}-
preserve
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
If
\phi\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal functor such that the underlying functor
\phi\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits, then the induced functor

\phi^{A,\otimes}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})^{\otimes}

is symmetric monoidal.

Proof.

Since
\phi^{A,\otimes}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})^{\otimes}
is lax symmetric monoidal, it suffices to show that for
M,N\in\operatorname{Mod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
, the map

\phi_{N,M}\colon\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(M\otimes_{A}N)\to\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(M)\otimes_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(N)

provided by the lax symmetric monoidal structure is an equivalence.
By construction of
\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
and symmetric monoidality of
\phi
, this holds if
M
and
N
are free modules.

As the forget functors
f_{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathcal{C},f_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})\to\mathcal{D}
reflect colimits, (
Proposition

1.4.1
) and

\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\circ f_{A}\cong f_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}},

\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits.
By
Lemma

1.4.4
below, the tensor products on
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
and
\operatorname{LMod}_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})
preserve
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
Since every module is a
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimit of free
A
-modules (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.7.3.14]
), it now follows that

\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(M\otimes_{A}N)\to\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(M)\otimes_{\phi^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}\phi^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(N)

is an equivalence for all
M,N\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
.
∎

Lemma 1.4.4
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal category such that
\mathcal{C}
has
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and
-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-

preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
If
K
is a category such that
\mathcal{C}
admits
K
-indexed colimits and the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-
preserves
K
-indexed colimits in both variables, then
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
has
K
-indexed colimits and
-\otimes_{A}-
preserves
K
-indexed colimits in both variables.

Proof.

The category
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
has
K
-indexed colimits by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.5]
.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.4.2.15, Theorem 4.5.2.1.(ii)]
, the tensor product preserves
K
-indexed colimits in both variables.
∎

Lemma 1.4.5
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a potentially large, closed symmetric monoidal category which has all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and all
\Delta
-indexed limits.

For every commutative algebra
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C})
, the induced symmetric monoidal structure (
1.4.2
) on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is closed.
Denote by
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}(-,-)
the internal Hom and by
f\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathcal{C}
the forget functor.
Then

f\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}({R}[-],-)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,f-).

Proof.

We first show that the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is closed.
Choose a universe
\mathcal{U}
in which
\mathcal{C}
is small and denote by
\operatorname{An}_{+}
the category of
\mathcal{U}
-small animae. Denote by
\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}_{+})
the full subcategory of functors which preserve
\Delta
-indexed limits and by
y\colon\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}_{+})
the Yoneda embedding.
As

S\coloneqq\{{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,yF\to y({\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}F)\,|\,F\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})\}

is
\mathcal{U}
-small and
\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}_{+})
is the category of
S
-local objects, it is presentable (in
\mathcal{U}
) by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.4.15]
in the universe
\mathcal{U}
.
By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.10]
(in the universe
\mathcal{U}
), there exists a symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})
which is compatible with
\mathcal{U}
-small colimits, such that the Yoneda embedding enhances to a strong symmetric monoidal functor

y^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})^{\otimes}.

This induces a fully faithful functor
y_{LM}^{{R}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
.

By naturality of the symmetric monoidal structure on module categories (
Lemma

1.4.3
),
y_{LM}^{{R}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})^{\otimes}
.
In particular, for
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
, we obtain a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y_{LM}^{{R}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M\otimes_{{R}}-}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y_{LM}^{{R}}M\otimes_{y{R}}-}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y_{LM}^{{R}}}

Since
\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{U})
is a presentable category in
\mathcal{U}
and its symmetric monoidal structure is compatible with all
\mathcal{U}
-small colimits, the same holds for
\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
in the universe
\mathcal{U}
, i.e.
\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
is presentably symmetric monoidal in
\mathcal{U}
.
In particular, the right vertical functor has a right adjoint
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})}(yM,-)
.
We claim that
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})}(yM,-)\circ y
factors over
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
, then the induced functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is right adjoint to
M\otimes_{{R}}-
.
Denote by

\mathcal{L}\coloneqq\{M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\,|\,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}_{+}^{\Delta}(\mathcal{C})})}(yM,-)\circ y\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}}),\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}}))\}

the full subcategory on
{R}
-modules for which this holds.
Since
\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
has all
\mathcal{U}
-small limits and colimits,

\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}),\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}),\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}))

and

\operatorname{Fun}^{R}(\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}),\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}),\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}))

are closed under
\mathcal{U}
-small colimits and they can be computed pointwise by
Lemma

A.1.1
in
\mathcal{U}
.

Denote by

f_{y{R}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})\to\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})

the forget functor.
As
\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
is the full subcategory on objects
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
with
f_{y{R}}M\in\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})
, by
Proposition

1.4.1
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})
is closed under small limits and
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits. This implies that
\mathcal{L}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is closed under
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits.
By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.7.3.14]
, every
{R}
-module
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is a
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimit of free modules, so it suffices to show that for
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
{R}[c]\in\mathcal{L}
, then it follows that
\mathcal{L}=\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
. Note that

\mathcal{L}=\{M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\,|\,f_{y{R}}\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})}(M,-)\circ y\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}}),\mathcal{C})\}.

For
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
y_{LM}^{{R}}{R}[c]=y{R}[yc]
is the free
y{R}
-module on
yc
, whence

f_{y{R}}\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})}(y_{LM}^{{R}}{R}[c],-)\vdash(y{R}[yc]\otimes_{y{R}}-)\circ y{R}[-].

The symmetric monoidal enhancement of the free
y{R}
-module functor

y{R}[-]\colon\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})

yields an equivalence

(y{R}[yc]\otimes_{y{R}}-)\circ y{R}[-]\cong y{R}[-]\circ(yc\otimes_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}-)\dashv\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(c,-)\circ f_{y{R}},

whence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(c,-)\circ f_{y{R}}\cong f_{y{R}}\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{y{R}}({\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})})}(y_{LM}^{{R}}{R}[c],-).

Since
f_{y{R}}\circ y=y\circ f_{{R}}
, we are reduced to showing that for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(yc,-)\circ y\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})).

By fully faithfulness and symmetric monoidality of the Yoneda embedding
y
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(-,y\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,-))\circ y

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,-))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-\otimes c,-)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(y(-)\otimes yc,y-)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(y-,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(yc,-)\circ y),

which implies that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})}(yc,-)\circ y\cong y\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,-)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{P}^{\Delta}_{+}(\mathcal{C})).

This shows that the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is closed.

The symmetric monoidal structure of the free
{R}
-module functor
{R}[-]
provides an equivalence

{R}[-]\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}{R}[-]\cong{R}[-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-],

which defines an equivalence

f\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}({R}[-],-)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,f-).\qed

If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site and
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal category, then
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
has all small limits and colimits by
1.1.15
.
By
1.1.28
,
\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
inherits a closed symmetric monoidal structure.

Lemma

1.4.5
therefore implies:

Corollary 1.4.6
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site and
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal category. For
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}))
, the symmetric monoidal structure on

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})})

is closed.

We now recall that under mild assumptions on a closed symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{C}
, for an algebra
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
, the category of left
{R}
-modules is naturally enriched in
\mathcal{C}
.

Recollection 1.4.7
.

If
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a monoidal category, for
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})
, the category of left
{R}
-modules
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is right-tensored over
\mathcal{C}
by
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.3.3.7, Example 4.3.1.15]
.
By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.6.3.15, Corollary 4.3.2.8]
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{C}_{\operatorname{rev}}}({\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}})\cong\operatorname{RMod}_{\mathcal{C}}({\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}}),

so we can consider
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
as left tensored over the reverse
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}_{\operatorname{rev}}
(
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.1.1.7]
).

Lemma 1.4.8
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a closed symmetric monoidal category which has all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and all
\Delta
-indexed limits. For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
, the left-tensoring of
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
over
\mathcal{C}_{\operatorname{rev}}^{\otimes}\cong\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
exhibits
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
as enriched (
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.2.1.28]
) in
\mathcal{C}
.

Proof.

By
Proposition

1.4.1
,
\mathcal{C}
and
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
admit all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and all
\Delta
-indexed limits.
In particular,
\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}}))
is closed under
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and they can be computed pointwise by
Lemma

A.1.1
.
By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.5.8]
, the action map

-\otimes-\colon\mathcal{C}\times\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})

preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
As every left
{R}
-module is a
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimit of free
{R}
-modules (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.7.3.14]
), it therefore suffices to show that for all free
{R}
-modules
{R}[c],c\in\mathcal{C}
,

-\otimes{R}[c]\colon\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})

is a left adjoint.
By
[
Lur17
, Construction 4.8.3.24]
, the algebra map
1_{\mathcal{C}}\to{R}
determines a
\mathcal{C}_{\operatorname{rev}}
-linear enhancement of the free
{R}
-module functor
{R}[-]
.
This yields an equivalence of
-\otimes{R}[c]
with

\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}c}\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{{R}[-]}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
. This functor is a left adjoint as the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{C}
is closed.
∎

We now show that module categories in big presentably monoidal categories behave similar as for presentable categories. More concretely, we prove analogues of the statements listed on page
1.4
.
Suppose
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
is a chain of presentably (symmetric) monoidal categories. By
Lemma

1.3.23
, this has a colimit in
\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
.
The (symmetric) monoidal functors
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
induce an equivalence

{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}^{\otimes}})\cong\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}^{\otimes}}).

Lemma 1.4.9
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a big presentably monoidal category.

(i)

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
is a big presentable category.

(ii)

If
\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
is an exhaustion by presentably monoidal categories and
\mu\in\Lambda
is such that
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})
, then

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({{\mathcal{B}_{*}}})\colon\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}

is an exhaustion for
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
by presentable categories and for
\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
by presentably monoidal categories and
\mu\in\Lambda
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
As for all
\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a monoidal subcategory, we obtain a functor

\phantom{}{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda

\displaystyle\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty/\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})}

\displaystyle\mu\to\kappa

\displaystyle\mapsto\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}),

cf.
Lemma

A.2.7
. By
Lemmas

A.2.7
and
A.2.8
and
Proposition

1.4.1
, for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})

are fully faithful left adjoints and left-exact.

A.2.8
moreover implies that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mu\backslash}
, the essential image of
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
is equivalent to
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
.

It now follows from

Lemma

A.1.3
that

{\underset{\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})

is an equivalence.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}})
is presentable for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
∎

Recollection 1.4.10
.

Suppose
A
is an algebra in a presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
and

\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories. Choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
.
As
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure by
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.8.1.24]
and
1.4.2
.
Recall from
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.1.5, Corollary 4.5.1.6]
that

\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\backslash}.

This implies that
\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes}
enhances to a diagram

\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})).

By
[
Lur17
, section 4]
/
A.2.8

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})
is left-tensored over
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
, i.e. enhances to an element in
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})
.
We therefore obtain a diagram

\mathcal{B_{*}}\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash},\operatorname{Pr}^{L}).

Corollary 1.4.11
.

In the above situation,

{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\mathcal{B_{*}}\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})),

where the colimit on the left-hand side is computed in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
.

Proof.

[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.8.4.6]
yields an equivalence

\displaystyle\mathcal{B}_{*}\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{*}})

in
\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash},\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
, note that the construction of the equivalence (
[
Lur17
, Construction 4.8.4.4]
) is natural in the presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}
.
The statement now follows from
Lemma

1.4.9
.
∎

[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.6.2.17]
implies:

Corollary 1.4.12
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably monoidal category.
For an algebra morphism
\phi\colon R\to S\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, restriction of scalars
\phi^{*}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
admits a left adjoint.

In case
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
admits
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}-
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables, this is
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.6.2.17]
.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentably monoidal categories such that
R,S\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
. (This can be achieved by passing to a suitable slice
{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda
).
For
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
, the symmetric monoidal functor
i\colon\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
yields a commutative diagram

(1.4.12.1)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}),}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{LM}^{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{LM}^{R}}

where
i_{LM}^{S,R}
denotes the functors induced by the symmetric monoidal functor
\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}^{\otimes}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}
.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is presentably symmetric monoidal,
Proposition

1.4.1
implies that

\phi^{*}_{\lambda}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})

preserves small colimits and limits for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
As
\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}),\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})
are presentable (
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
),
\phi^{*}_{\lambda}
admits a left adjoint
L_{\lambda}
by the adjoint functor theorem.
We claim that for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
, the mate

(1.4.12.2)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({B_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({B_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{LM}^{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{LM}^{R}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{\lambda}}

of the above diagram commutes, then it follows from
Lemma

A.1.2
that
{\underset{\lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,L_{\lambda}
is left adjoint to
\phi^{*}={\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,\phi^{*}_{\lambda}
.
The functors
i_{LM}^{R,S}
are left adjoints, cf.
Lemma

A.2.7
.
Denote by
r_{LM}^{R,S}
their right adjoints.
By
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.7.4.14]
, it is enough to show that the opposite mate of
1.4.12.2
, that is
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({B_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({B_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\phi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r_{LM}^{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r_{LM}^{R}}

commutes.
Suppose first that
R=1
. By construction of the adjunction
i_{LM}^{S}\dashv r_{LM}^{S}
,
r\phi^{*}\cong\phi^{*}r_{LM}^{S}
and the composition of this equivalence with the Beck-Chevalley transformation
\beta_{\phi}
is

\phi^{*}_{\kappa}(r_{LM}^{S}\xrightarrow{\eta r_{LM}^{S}}r_{LM}^{S}i_{LM}^{S}r_{LM}^{S}\xrightarrow{r_{LM}^{S}\epsilon^{S}}r_{LM}^{S})=\phi^{*}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{id}_{r_{LM}^{S}}),

which shows that
\beta_{\phi}
is an equivalence if

. As the forget functor
f_{R}^{\lambda}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is conservative,
\beta_{\phi}
is an equivalence if and only if
{f_{R}^{\lambda}}_{*}(\beta_{\phi})
is an equivalence, and since
\beta_{1\to R}
is an equivalence,
{f_{R}^{\lambda}}_{*}(\beta_{\phi})\cong\beta_{1\to R}\circ\beta_{\phi}
.
By the pasting law for mates (
[
CSY22
, Lemma 2.2.4]
),
\beta_{1\to R}\circ\beta_{\phi}=\beta_{1\to R\xrightarrow{\phi}S}
which is an equivalence by the above.
∎

We now deduce from
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.5.1.1, Theorem 4.5.2.1]
/
1.4.2
that for a commutative algebra
{R}
in a big presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
enhances to a big presentably symmetric monoidal category. We can not apply
1.4.2
respectively
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.5.1.1, Theorem 4.5.2.1]
directly since big presentably monoidal categories need not admit
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and their tensor product need not preserve them.

Construction 1.4.13
.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories such that
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.8.5.16]
(in the large universe), we obtain a functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{*}})^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})

such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}
is the symmetric monoidal enhancement described in
1.4.2
. This is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})
and a presentably symmetric monoidal category by
[
Lur17
, Theorem 3.4.4.2]
.
For all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})

is a fully faithful, left-exact left adjoint by
Lemma

1.4.9
.
This shows that the colimit

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}

in
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
is a big presentably symmetric monoidal category. Since
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
preserves large sifted colimits (
[
Lur17
, Lemma 4.8.4.2, Corollary 3.2.3.2]
),
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
by
Lemma

1.4.9
and
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.5.1.6]
.

Lemma 1.4.14
.

The symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
constructed above is independent of the chosen exhaustion by presentably symmetric monoidal categories.

Proof.

Suppose
\mathcal{A}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L}),\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon J\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
are two exhaustions of
\mathcal{B_{\infty}^{\otimes}}
by presentably symmetric monoidal subcategories such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, and for all
j\in J
,
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{j})\subseteq\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
.
For
(\lambda,j)\in\Lambda\times J
let
C_{\lambda,j}\coloneqq\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\mathcal{B}_{j}
.
Since
\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty},\mathcal{B}_{j}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
are fully faithful, symmetric monoidal functors which preserve small colimits,
C_{\lambda,j}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory closed under small colimits. As
\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}
is presentably symmetric monoidal, this implies that
C_{\lambda,j}
has all small colimits and the symmetric monoidal structure on
C_{\lambda,j}
is cocontinuous in both variables.
Since
C_{\lambda,j}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory,

\operatorname{CAlg}(C_{\lambda,j})\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes})\times_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}^{\otimes}}}C_{\lambda,j},

so in particular
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(C_{\lambda,j})\subseteq\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
for all
(\lambda,j)\in\Lambda\times J
.
Equip
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({C_{\lambda,j}})
with the symmetric monoidal structure described in
1.4.2
.
By naturality of the symmetric monoidal structure on module categories (
Lemma

1.4.3
),
\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({C_{\lambda,j}})^{\otimes}\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}
and
\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({C_{\lambda,j}})^{\otimes}\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{j}})^{\otimes}
are symmetric monoidal subcategories.
This implies that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}\cong{\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({C_{\lambda,j}})^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})

and analogously for
\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({{\mathcal{B}}_{j}})^{\otimes}
, which shows that

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}\cong{\underset{(\lambda,j)\in\Lambda\times J}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({C_{\lambda,j}})^{\otimes}\cong{\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{j}})^{\otimes}.\qed

Remark 1.4.15
.

If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big presentably symmetric monoidal category which admits
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor product on
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables, then the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
constructed above agrees with the symmetric monoidal structure described in
1.4.2
.
Indeed: Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories such that
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
. The symmetric monoidal functor
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is cocontinuous for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, and hence induces a symmetric monoidal functor
\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})^{\otimes}
by
Lemma

1.4.3
. These functors induce a symmetric monoidal functor
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
which is an equivalence by
Lemma

1.4.9
.

Corollary 1.4.16
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably symmetric monoidal category,
T^{\otimes}
is a stable, presentably symmetric monoidal category, and
F^{\otimes}\colon T^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a cocontinuous, symmetric monoidal functor.
For
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(T)
,

F^{\otimes}
induces a symmetric monoidal functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({T})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{F^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})^{\otimes}.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories.
By
1.3.18
, there exists
\lambda\in\Lambda
such that
F\colon T\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
factors over
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
.
Since
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory,
F^{\otimes}
defines a symmetric monoidal functor
T^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}
.
As
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is closed under small colimits and has all small colimits and
F
is cocontinuous,
Lemma

1.4.3
implies that
F^{\otimes}
induces a symmetric monoidal functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({T})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{F^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}.

By
Lemma

1.4.14
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{F^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{F^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.
The composite

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({T})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{F^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{F^{\operatorname{CAlg}}A}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})^{\otimes}

is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
F
.
As
\Lambda
is filtered, this enhancement does not depend on the choice of
\lambda\in\Lambda
.

1.3.18
and the argument from the proof of
Lemma

1.4.14
imply that it also does not depend on the chosen exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
by presentably symmetric monoidal subcategories.
∎

Corollary 1.4.17
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a big presentably symmetric monoidal category and

\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories. For
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
. Then the equivalence from
1.4.11
enhances to an an equivalence of symmetric monoidal categories

{\underset{\mu\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\mathcal{B_{\mu}}^{\otimes}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))^{\otimes},

where the colimit is computed in
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
, and the right-hand side and
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})
are endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure from
1.4.13
.

Proof.

By construction of the symmetric monoidal structure on the right-hand side,

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))^{\otimes}\cong{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}))^{\otimes},

where the colimit is computed in
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.4.2, Theorem 4.8.5.16]
, the free
A
-module functors enhance to a symmetric monoidal natural transformation

A^{\otimes}[-]_{*}\colon\mathcal{B}_{*}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{*}})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash},\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))),

and by
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.8.5.16, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{*}})
enhances to a functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{*}})\colon\Lambda_{\mu\backslash}\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\mu}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})).

As the tensor product on
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))
is cocartesian (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.4.7]
),
A^{\otimes}[-]_{*}
and the canonical functor

\operatorname{const}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\mu}})}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B_{*}}})

determine a natural transformation

c_{*}^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}{\mathcal{B}_{*}}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({{\mathcal{B}_{*}}})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash},\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))).

For
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}
, the functor
c_{\mu}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of the equivalence from
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.8.4.6]
, i.e. the one used in the identification of
1.4.11
.
As the forget functor
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
preserves filtered colimits (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.3.1]
), this implies the statement.
∎

Corollary 1.4.18
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably monoidal category.
For a map of commutative algebras
\phi\colon R\to S\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, restriction of scalars
\phi^{*}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
admits a symmetric monoidal left adjoint.

In particular, for a commutative algebra
R\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, the free
{R}
-module functor enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor
{R}[-]^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})
.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories and
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
{R},{S}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
.
By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.5.3.1]
,
\phi
determines a symmetric monoidal functor
\phi_{!,\lambda}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{S}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})
which is left adjoint to restriction of scalars.
Tensoring with
\mathcal{B}_{*}
in
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))
yields a natural transformation

\phi_{!,*}^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{B}_{*}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\to\mathcal{B}_{*}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{LMod}_{{S}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})

in
\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash},\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})).

By
1.4.17
, taking the colimit over
\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}
in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
yields a symmetric monoidal functor

\phi^{\otimes}_{!}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})^{\otimes}.

Since
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
preserves filtered colimits (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.3.1]
), it follows from the proof of
1.4.12
that
\phi^{\otimes}_{!}
is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of the left adjoint of restriction of scalars.

We claim that the symmetric monoidal enhancement is independent of choices.
We first show that it is independent of the choice of
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
{R},{S}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
.
Fix
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
such that
{R},{S}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})
and denote by

c_{\lambda}({R}/{S})^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R/S}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R/S}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})

the equivalences chosen in the proof of
1.4.17
.
We will show that

(1.4.18.1)

\displaystyle c_{\lambda}(S)^{\otimes}\circ(\phi^{\otimes}_{!,\kappa}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})=\phi^{\otimes}_{!,\lambda}\circ c_{\lambda}({R})^{\otimes}.

As
\Lambda
is filtered, it then follows that
\phi^{\otimes}_{!}
is independent of the choice of
\lambda
with
{R},{S}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
.

For
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})
, the composite
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\otimes\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\xrightarrow{c_{\lambda}(A)^{\otimes}}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})
is by construction of
c_{\lambda}(A)^{\otimes}
the free
A
-module functor (with the symmetric monoidal structure induced from the unique map
1\to A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
via
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.5.3.1]
).
This determines an enhancement of
c_{\lambda}(A)^{\otimes}\circ(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
to a functor in
{}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))
.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.1.5]
,

{}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}))

and by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.1.9]
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}})
as symmetric monoidal categories, whence

{}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})).

In particular,

c_{\lambda}(S)^{\otimes}\circ(\phi^{\otimes}_{!,\kappa}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\circ(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

and

\phi^{\otimes}_{!,\lambda}\circ c_{\lambda}({R})^{\otimes}\circ(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

enhance to functors in

{}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}^{\otimes}\backslash}\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}))\cong\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})).

As
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
is the initial object of
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))
, it follows that

\displaystyle c_{\lambda}(S)^{\otimes}\circ(\phi^{\otimes}_{!,\kappa}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\circ(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})

\displaystyle=\phi^{\otimes}_{!,\lambda}\circ c_{\lambda}({R})^{\otimes}\circ(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}).

For
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})
, the symmetric monoidal functor
i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
induces a symmetric monoidal left adjoint

i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}(A)^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})\,\,\text{(\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{higheralgebra}{}{}, Theorem 4.8.5.16]})},

and by construction of
c_{\lambda}({A})^{\otimes}
, the composite

\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\to\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})\xrightarrow{c_{\lambda}(A)^{\otimes}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})

is
i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}(A)^{\otimes}
.
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.8.5.16]
now implies that
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{S}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{LMod}_{{S}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{S}}({\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{\otimes}_{!,\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c_{\kappa}({R})^{\otimes}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\phi}^{\otimes}_{!,\lambda}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c_{\kappa}({S})^{\otimes}}

commutes.
As the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))
is cocartesian, this implies (
1.4.18.1
).
The same argument as in the proof of
Lemma

1.4.14
shows that the symmetric monoidal enhancement
\phi^{\otimes}_{!}
of
\phi_{!}
is also independent of the chosen exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories.
∎

Corollary 1.4.19
.

Suppose
\phi\colon A\to B\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{X})
is a morphism of commutative algebras in a big presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{X}
.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.1.5, Corollary 4.5.1.6]
, this exhibits
B\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{X}}))
.
The forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{X}})\to\mathcal{X}
induces a symmetric monoidal equivalence

\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{X}})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\mathcal{X}}).

Proof.

The symmetric monoidal structure on the free
A
-module functor (
1.4.18
) determines a lax symmetric monoidal structure of the forget functor

f\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{X}})\to\mathcal{X},

cf.
Lemma

A.2.3
.
By construction of the symmetric monoidal structure (
1.4.2
/
[
Lur17
, Definition 3.3.8]
) on module categories, this induces a lax symmetric monoidal functor

f^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}).

We claim that
f^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal equivalence. Choose an exhaustion of
\mathcal{X}
by presentably symmetric monoidal subcategories
\mathcal{X}_{*}
such that
A,B\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
. For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
f^{\otimes}
restricts to

f^{\otimes}_{\lambda}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}),

the functor induced by the lax monoidal structure of the forget functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}})\to\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}.

This is immediate from the construction (
Lemma

A.2.3
).
By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 3.4.1.9]
,
f^{\otimes}_{\lambda}
is strong symmetric monoidal and an equivalence.
The statement now follows from
1.4.13
.
∎

Next, we show that if
\mathcal{B}
is a big presentably monoidal category, for
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})_{\geq 0})
, the category of left
{R}
-modules in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})
inherits a
t
-structure from
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B})
(with the
t
-structure described in
Lemma

1.3.12
).

Lemma 1.4.20
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a stable, presentably symmetric monoidal category with an accessible
t
-structure
(\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0},\mathcal{C}_{\leq 0})
which is compatible with the symmetric monoidal structure, i.e.
\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory and presentable.

(i)

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0})
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}

\displaystyle\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\times_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0},

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\leq 0}

\displaystyle\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\times_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{C}_{\leq 0}

define a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
.

(ii)

If
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0})
is a commutative algebra, then this is compatible with the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
described in
1.4.2
, i.e.
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.

Proof.

The proof is completely analogous to
[
Lur18a
, Proposition 2.1.1.1]
.
Since
\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}
. As
\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}
and
\mathcal{C}
are presentable, so are
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
and
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}})
by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
.
Since the forget functor

f\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathcal{C}

is exact and creates colimits (
Proposition

1.4.1
),
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}
is the connective part of a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.4.4.11]
. Denote by
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\tilde{\leq}0}
the coconnective part of this
t
-structure. For
T\in\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}
,
{R}[T]\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}
since
f{R}[T]={R}\otimes T\in\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}
. This implies that for
B\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\tilde{\leq 0}}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}({R}[T],B)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(T,fB)\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{An},

i.e.
fB\in\mathcal{C}_{\leq 0}
, which shows that
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\tilde{\leq}0}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\leq 0}
. Conversely, for
B\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\leq 0}
, denote by
\mathcal{G}_{B}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}
the full subcategory on objects
G
such that

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})}(G,B)\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{An}.

Since
\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{An}
is closed under limits,
\mathcal{G}_{B}
is closed under colimits. By definition,
\mathcal{G}_{B}
contains all free modules
{R}[T],T\in\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}
. As those generate
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}})
under
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.7.3.14]
), it follows that
\mathcal{G}_{B}=\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}
, which proves that

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\leq 0}=\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\tilde{\leq}0}
.

Suppose now that
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0})
is a commutative algebra.
As the symmetric monoidal functor
\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}^{\otimes}\subseteq\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
preserves colimits, it induces a symmetric monoidal functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})^{\otimes}

by
Lemma

1.4.3
.
The underlying functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is fully faithful with essential image
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{C}})_{\geq 0}
, which shows that the latter is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.
∎

Corollary 1.4.21
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{\infty}
is a big presentably symmetric monoidal category and endow
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})
with the induced symmetric monoidal structure (
Proposition

1.3.26
) and the
t
-structure described in
Lemma

1.3.12
.
For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})_{\geq 0})
, the subcategories

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\geq 0}

\displaystyle\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\times_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})_{\geq 0},

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\leq 0}

\displaystyle\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\times_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})_{\leq 0}

constitute a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))
.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by presentably monoidal categories such that
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
. Since for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is accessible (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.4.3.4]
) and compatible with the monoidal structure (
Lemma

1.3.32
),

(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))_{\geq 0},\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))_{\leq 0})

defines a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))
by
Lemma

1.4.20
.

By
Lemma

1.3.12
, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\text{ and }\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})_{\leq 0}=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\cap\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\leq 0},

whence

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))\cap\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\geq 0}=\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))_{\geq 0}

and

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))\cap\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\leq 0}=\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}))_{\leq 0}.

Using
Lemma

1.4.9
and
Lemma

1.2.4
, it is now straightforward to check that

(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\geq 0},\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\leq 0})

defines a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})).

∎

Corollary 1.4.22
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\otimes}
is a big presentably symmetric monoidal category.
For a connective ring spectrum object
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})_{\geq 0})
, the
t
-structure from
1.4.21
is compatible with the symmetric monoidal structure from
1.4.13
, i.e.

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))

is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
of
\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}_{\infty}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories.
Since
{R}\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}})_{\geq 0}
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\geq 0}
contains the unit of the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))
.
For
M,N\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\geq 0}
choose
\kappa\in\Lambda
with

{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}))\subseteq\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\infty}}))

and
M,N\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}))\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))
.
Then
M,N\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}))_{\geq 0}
. Hence by
Lemma

1.4.20
,
M\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}})}N\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}))_{\geq 0}
.
Since

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}))\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))

is symmetric monoidal and
t
-exact, this implies that

M\otimes_{{R}}N\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))_{\geq 0}.\qed

If
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big topos and
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))
, the Eilenberg-Mac Lane functor is symmetric monoidal (
1.3.33
) and therefore induces a functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}).

Lemma 1.4.23
.

This factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})^{\heartsuit}.

Proof.

By definition of the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})
, the Eilenberg-Mac Lane functor factors over
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})^{\heartsuit}
.
The symmetric monoidal functor

\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})^{\heartsuit}\cong\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})

induces a functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})^{\heartsuit}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})_{\geq 0}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})_{\geq 0}})\xrightarrow{\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})

which is inverse to the functor induced by the Eilenberg-Mac Lane functor.
∎

1.4.1
Derived categories

We now review derived categories of abelian categories.
Adapting
[
Lur18a
, Theorem 2.1.2.2]
, we formulate conditions on a big topos
\mathcal{X}
under which
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
for all discrete rings
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))
, see
Lemma

1.4.32
. Such an equivalence is instructive as, by our above discussion, the right-hand side enjoys good categorical properties.

Definition 1.4.24
.

Consider
\mathbb{Z}
as poset via
\geq
.
For a possibly large abelian category
\mathcal{A}
denote by
\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{Z},\mathcal{A})
the (large) category of chain complexes in
\mathcal{A}
.

A chain map
f\colon C_{*}\to D_{*}\in\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})
is a homology equivalence if
H_{i}(f)
is an isomorphism in
\mathcal{A}
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.

Define the
derived category
of
\mathcal{A}
as

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\coloneqq\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})[W^{-1}]

the localization of
\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})
at the homology equivalences in the (very large) category
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
of large categories.

Remark 1.4.25
.

If
\mathcal{U}_{1}\in\tilde{\mathcal{U}}_{1}
are universes, the inclusion
\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}({\mathcal{U}}_{1})\subseteq\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}({\tilde{\mathcal{U}}_{1}})
of
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small categories into
\tilde{\mathcal{U}}_{1}
-small categories preserves
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small colimits.
In particular, for a
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small abelian category
A
, it sends the derived category of
A
(computed in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
) to the derived category of
A
(computed in
\mathcal{U}_{2}
).
Indeed: For a universe
\mathcal{V}
and a
\mathcal{V}
-small abelian category
A
, the derived category
\mathcal{D}(A)
computed in
\mathcal{V}
is the pushout of
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces W}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Ch}(A)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mid W\mid}

in
\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}(\mathcal{V})
, where
W\subseteq\operatorname{Ch}(A)
denotes the wide subcategory on weak equivalences and
|W|
is its
geometric realization
, i.e. the image of
W
under the left adjoint of the inclusion
\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal{V}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}(\mathcal{V})
of
\mathcal{V}
-small animae into
\mathcal{V}
-small categories.
Denote by
J
the nerve of the 1-category with two objects
\{0,1\}
and a unique isomorphism between them.
There is a canonical map
\Delta^{1}\to J
, and
|W|
is the pushout
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sqcup_{w\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},W)}\Delta^{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces W}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sqcup_{w\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},W)}J}

in
\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}(\mathcal{V})
, see e.g.
[
Lan21
, Lemma 2.4.6]
.

The following is again folklore, but we could not find a reference.

Lemma 1.4.26
.
