Suppose
\mathcal{A}
is a (large) abelian category.
The (large) category
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
is stable and cofibers can be computed using the mapping cone construction on the level of chain complexes.

Proof.

We thank Stefan Schwede for suggesting the following argument.
By
[
Lur17
, Definition 1.3.2.1]
(in the large universe), the category
\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})
is a differential graded category and by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.4.5]
,

\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})[\text{(chain homotopy equivalences)}^{-1}]\cong\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))

is the
differential graded nerve
(
[
Lur17
, Construction 1.3.1.6]
) of
\operatorname{Ch}(A)
.
Since chain homotopy equivalences are homology equivalences, the homology functors descend to functors

H_{i}\colon\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))\to\mathcal{A}

and in particular,

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\cong\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))[(\text{homology equivalences})^{-1}].

The category
\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))
is stable by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.2.10]
(in the large universe), and by
[
Lur17
, Remark 1.3.2.17]
(in the large universe): if
a\to b\in\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))
is a map represented by a map of chain complexes
f\colon A\to B\in\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})
, then the mapping cone
\operatorname{Cone}(f)
(computed in the category of chain complexes) represents the cofiber
\operatorname{Cofib}(f)
.
In particular, a map
f\colon A\to B
in
\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))
is a homology equivalence if and only if
H_{i}(\operatorname{Cofib}(f))=0
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
This implies that

\mathcal{N}\coloneqq\{N\in\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(A))\,|\,H_{i}(N)=0\text{ for all }i\in\mathbb{Z}\}\subseteq\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(A))

is a stable subcategory (
[
NS18
, Definition I.3.2]
).
Indeed, for
N\in\mathcal{N}
, the cofiber sequence
\Omega N\to*\to N
implies that
\Omega N\to*
is a homology equivalence, i.e.
\Omega N\in\mathcal{N}
.
Suppose that
A\xrightarrow{f}B\to C\in\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\mathcal{A})
is a cofiber sequence.
If
A,B\in\mathcal{N}
, then
f
is a homology equivalence and hence
C=\operatorname{Cofib}(f)\in\mathcal{N}
, and if
B,C\in\mathcal{N}
, the (co)fiber sequence
\Omega B\to\Omega C\to A
implies that
A\in\mathcal{N}
.
It now follows from
[
NS18
, Theorem I.3.3]
(in the large universe) that

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\cong\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))[\text{(homology equivalences)}^{-1}]

is a stable category and that the functor
\operatorname{N}_{\operatorname{dg}}(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}))\to\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
is exact.
In particular, cofibers can be computed using the mapping cone construction.
∎

Corollary 1.4.27

(
[
GM96
, section IV.4, Proposition 3]
)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{A}
is a (large) abelian category.
Then

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0}\coloneqq\{X\in\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\,|\,H_{i}(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\},

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\leq 0}\coloneqq\{X\in\mathcal{D}(A)\,|\,H_{i}(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}

defines a
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(A)
.

Corollary 1.4.28
.

Suppose that
\phi\colon\mathcal{A}_{1}\to\mathcal{A}_{2}
is an exact (i.e. finite limits and finite colimits preserving) functor between (large) abelian categories.
Then
\phi_{*}\colon\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{1})\to\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{2})
descends to a functor
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{1})\to\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{2})
which is
t
-exact.

Proof.

As
\mathcal{A}_{1}\to\mathcal{A}_{2}
is exact,
H_{i}^{\mathcal{A}_{2}}\circ\phi_{*}=\phi_{*}\circ H_{i}^{\mathcal{A}_{1}}
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
In particular,
\phi_{*}
descends to a functor

\mathcal{D}(\phi)\colon\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{1})\to\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{2})
with

H_{i}^{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{2})}\circ\mathcal{D}(\phi)=\mathcal{D}(\phi)\circ H_{i}^{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{1})}

for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
Since finite coproducts in abelian categories are exact, for a finite set
I
,

\oplus_{I}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(I,\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{k}))\to\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{k})\to\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})

descends to a functor

\oplus_{I}^{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k}))\to\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})

for
k=1,2
. The unit and counit for the adjunction

\oplus_{I}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(I,\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{k}))\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{k})\colon\operatorname{diag}

induce natural transformations

\oplus_{I}^{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})}\operatorname{diag}\to\operatorname{id},\,\operatorname{id}\to\operatorname{diag}\oplus_{I}^{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})}

which exhibit
\oplus_{I}^{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})}
as left adjoint to the diagonal functor

\operatorname{diag}\colon\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})\to\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})),

i.e. finite coproducts can be computed on the level of chain complexes in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{k})
. This implies that
\mathcal{D}(\phi)
preserves finite coproducts. Since
\phi_{*}\colon\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{1})\to\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{2})
preserves mapping cones,
\mathcal{D}(\phi)
preserves cofibers by
Lemma

1.4.26
and hence finite colimits. Since
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{1})
and
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{2})
are stable, this shows that
f
is exact.
∎

Notation 1.4.29
.

A chain of abelian categories is a functor
\mathcal{A}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
from a possibly large filtered set
\Lambda
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}
is an abelian category, and
\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}
is a fully faithful, left-exact left adjoint.

Lemma 1.4.30
.

If
\mathcal{A}\colon\Lambda\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is a chain of abelian categories, its colimit
{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}
in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is an abelian category.

Proof.

This holds as by
Lemma

A.1.3
, finite limits and finite colimits in
\mathcal{A}_{\infty}
can always be computed in some stage
\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}
.
∎

Lemma 1.4.31
.

Suppose
\mathcal{A}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is a chain of abelian categories whose colimit
\mathcal{A}_{\infty}
has countable coproducts.
Then

{\underset{\lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})\cong\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\infty})\in\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}.

Proof.

As for
\lambda\geq\kappa
,
\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})
is fully faithful,

c\colon{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\infty})

is fully faithful by
Lemma

A.1.3
.
For a countable family
(C_{i})_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{\infty}
and
j\in\mathbb{Z}
there exists
\kappa\in\Lambda
with
\oplus_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}C_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{\infty}
.
For
j\in I
let

\pi_{j}\colon\oplus_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}C_{i}\to\oplus_{\begin{subarray}{c}i\in I\\
i\neq j\end{subarray}}C_{i}\hookrightarrow\oplus_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}C_{i}.

Since
\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{\infty}
is closed under colimits (
Lemma

A.1.3
),

C_{j}=\operatorname{Coker}(\pi_{j})\in\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}
for all
j\in\mathbb{Z}
.
This implies that
c
is an equivalence.
Denote by
W_{\infty/\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\infty/\kappa})
the wide subcategories on homology equivalences. As for all
\kappa\in\Lambda
,

\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{A}_{\infty}
preserves finite limits and colimits and is conservative,

W_{\infty}\cap\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa})=W_{\kappa}.

In particular,
{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,W_{\kappa}\cong W_{\infty}
as wide subcategories of
\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})
.
As left adjoint to the forget functor,
|-|\colon\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}\to\widehat{\operatorname{An}}
commutes with large colimits.
This shows that
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})=\operatorname{Ch}(A)[W^{-1}]
is the pushout of
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,W_{\kappa}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,\mid W_{\kappa}\mid}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa})}

in the very large category
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
of large categories, and hence

{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa})\cong{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,(\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa})\cup_{W_{\kappa}}|W_{\kappa}|)\cong\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal{A})\cup_{W}|W|=\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}).

∎

Lemma 1.4.32
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{B}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is a chain of hypercomplete, 1-localic topoi with colimit
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}\in\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
such that
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
has countable coproducts.
For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))
, the inclusion

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))^{\heartsuit}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))

extends to a
t
-exact equivalence

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})),

where we view
{R}
as an algebra in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
via the Eilenberg-Mac Lane functor (
1.3.33
).

Proof.

Choose
\mu\in\Lambda
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{B_{\mu}}))\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}({\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}))
. Since
\Lambda
is filtered,
\Lambda_{\mu\backslash}\to\Lambda
is cofinal, so we can assume that
\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mu\backslash}
and for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}({\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}}))
.
Fix
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
By
[
Lur18a
, Proposition 2.1.1.1(c)]
, the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})
is right-complete (the proof there does not use commutativity of the ring
{R}
, hence also applies in our situation).
By
1.3.13
,

\Omega^{\infty}|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})_{\geq 0}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})_{\geq 0}\cong\operatorname{CGrp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}

is conservative. As
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
is hypercomplete, this implies that the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
is left-separated. Since the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})
is conservative and
t
-exact, it follows that the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})})
is left-separated.
Since
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})
is Grothendieck abelian, the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}))
is right-complete by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.5.21]
.
It now follows from
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
that for all
\kappa,\lambda\in\Lambda
, restriction to hearts defines an equivalence

(1.4.32.1)

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{L,\operatorname{t-ex}}

\displaystyle(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})),\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({B_{\kappa}})}))

(1.4.32.2)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}),\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})})^{\heartsuit}),

see also
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
.
In particular, for
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
there exists an essentially unique
t
-exact left adjoint

c_{\kappa,\lambda}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})}))\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})})

extending the functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})^{\heartsuit}
induced by

\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})^{\heartsuit}\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})^{\heartsuit}.

For
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
1.4.32.1
yields a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\lambda}})})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c_{{\kappa,\kappa}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c_{{\lambda,\lambda}}}

where the left vertical functor is induced by the fully faithful, exact left adjoint

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})

(cf.
1.4.28
) and the right vertical morphism is induced by the fully faithful, symmetric monoidal left adjoint
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\kappa})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
.
The proof of
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.4.5.7]
shows that every 1-localic topos is a left-exact localisation of a presheaf category
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
for a 1-category
\mathcal{C}
. This implies that for every
\lambda\in\Lambda
and
b\in\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
, there exists
c\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
with an effective epimorphism
c\to b
.
8
8

8

By
[
Lur18a
, Proposition 20.4.5.1, Remark 20.4.5.2]
,
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.4.5.9]
this condition is satisfied for hypercomplete topoi if and only if they are 1-localic.

Hence by
[
Lur18a
, Theorem 2.1.2.2]
, the maps
c_{\lambda,\lambda}
are equivalences for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
(the proof there also works for associative algebras),
which shows that the induced functor

\displaystyle{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}))\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})

is an equivalence.

Lemma

1.4.31
and
Lemma

1.4.9
now imply that

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})}).

As
c_{\lambda,\lambda}
is
t
-exact for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, this equivalence is
t
-exact.
∎

Remark 1.4.33
.

For a topos
\mathcal{X}
and an algebra
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))
,
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
/
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
yield a
t
-exact functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\widehat{\mathcal{X}})})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}),

where
\widehat{\mathcal{X}}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
denotes the full subcategory on hypercomplete objects. But the author is unaware of a construction of a
t
-exact functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

for general big which extends the inclusion of the heart.

If
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is a chain of
\infty
-topoi, the transition functors
i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}\colon\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{X}_{\kappa}
preserve
\infty
-connective morphisms.
We therefore obtain a functor
\widehat{\mathcal{X}}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
, where for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\widehat{\mathcal{X}}_{\kappa}\to\widehat{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}
is the composition of hypersheafification (in
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
with
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
and in particular a left-exact left adjoint.
The argument from the above proof shows that there exists a
t
-exact functor

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})}))\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\widehat{\mathcal{X}}_{\lambda})}).

If
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
admits countable coproducts, then the left-hand side is equivalent to
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))
, but since
\widehat{\mathcal{X}}_{*}
is not a subfunctor of
\mathcal{X}
, there is no obvious way to compare the right-hand side to
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
.

This is not an issue for categories of (hyper)accessible sheaves on hyperaccessible explicit covering sites:
If
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a hyperaccessible explicit covering site, denote by
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
the poset of regular cardinals
\kappa
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\kappa
-hyperaccessible.
Then

\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*})\subseteq\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{*})\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}

is a subfunctor and
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C}))=\operatorname{Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab})
has small colimits.
We therefore obtain
t
-exact functors

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab})}))\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})}).

By the above lemma, the left functor is an equivalence if
\mathcal{C}
is a 1-category.

1.4.2
Modules over constant rings

If
\mathcal{X}^{\otimes}
is a big topos, the (symmetric) monoidal enhancement
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
of the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor (
1.3.44
) induces a functor

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})).

We now record some basic observations about module categories over constant rings.

1.4.11
and
1.4.17
imply the following:

Lemma 1.4.34
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
is a big topos and
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
by topoi.

(i)

For a ring spectrum
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp})
,

{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\mathcal{B_{*}}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})),

where the colimit is computed in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
.

(ii)

For a commutative ring spectrum
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})
, this enhances to an an equivalence of symmetric monoidal categories

{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\mathcal{B_{*}}^{\times}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))^{\otimes},

where the colimit is computed in
\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
, and the right-hand side is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure from
Propositions

1.3.26
and
1.4.13
.

Proof.

We first prove the first statement.
Choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
. As the constant sheaf functor factors over
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
, by
1.4.11
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))\cong{\underset{\mu\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}).

By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.8.4.6]
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
, and by
Lemma

1.3.6
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})\cong\operatorname{Sp}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{B}_{*}
. It now follows that

\displaystyle{\underset{\mu\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\mu\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})\otimes_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}})}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\mu\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{\mu}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}}).

Suppose now that
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})
.
By
1.4.17
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))^{\otimes}\cong{\underset{\mu\in\Lambda_{\lambda\backslash}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{*}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})),

and by
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.8.4.6]
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})
, whence

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\lambda})}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}))}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\mu})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{B}_{\mu}

naturally in
\mu
, where we used that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{*})^{\otimes}\cong\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\otimes}
(
[
GGN13
, Proposition 5.4]
).
∎

Corollary 1.4.35
.

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site and denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp}))
the functor induced by the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor.

(i)

For
{A}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp})
,

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\operatorname{Sp}}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{A}}({\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})}).

(ii)

For
{A}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})
, this enhances to a symmetric monoidal equivalence

\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{LMod}_{{A}}({\operatorname{Sp}})^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{A}}({\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})}),

where the left-hand side is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure induced from
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})^{\otimes}
via
1.1.27
, and the right-hand side with the symmetric monoidal structure from
1.4.13
.

Proof.

The first statement holds by
Lemmas

1.4.34
,
1.1.21
and
1.1.6
, the second statement follows from
Lemmas

1.4.34
and
1.1.27
.
∎

Recall from
[
Lur18a
, Theorem 2.1.2.2]
or
Lemma

1.4.32
that if
A=\pi_{0}A
is a discrete ring spectrum, then
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\cong\mathcal{D}(A)
is the
\infty
-derived category of
A
-modules.

If
\mathcal{X}^{\otimes}
is a big topos, for
A\in\operatorname{Sp}
, the symmetric monoidal enhancement
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
of the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor (
1.3.44
) induces a left adjoint

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\text{ (\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{localisationinduceslocalisationonmodulecategories})}.

We will use the following elementary observation to construct simplicial resolutions (
Lemma

1.5.17
) and to compare internal (group) cohomology with (group) cohomology:

Lemma 1.4.36
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
the functor induced by the constant sheaf functor.
If
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{\heartsuit})\cong\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab})
is a discrete ring, for
X\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X]\in\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})^{\heartsuit}
.

Proof.

By definition of the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
, we have to show that

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A\otimes\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\heartsuit}.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi.
As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X_{\lambda}})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is
t
-exact, it suffices to prove the statement for
\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}
, so we can assume that
\mathcal{X}
is a topos, i.e. there exists a small category
\mathcal{C}
with a left-exact, accessible localization
L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{X}
.
Since
L
is cartesian,
c^{\times}
factors as
\operatorname{An}^{\times}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{const}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\times}\xrightarrow{L}\mathcal{C}^{\times}
, where
\operatorname{const}
sends an anima to the associated constant presheaf.
This implies that

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X]=L_{\operatorname{Sp}}(c\mapsto A\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X(c)).

As for
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
X(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(Ly(c),X)\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{An}
(where
y
denotes the Yoneda embedding),

\mathcal{C}\ni c\mapsto A\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X(c)\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}))^{\heartsuit}.

t
-exactness of
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}
(
Lemma

1.3.16
) now implies that
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X]\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\heartsuit}
.
∎

We now explain that for a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, the category of left
A
-modules
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
over a a commutative algebra
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
is naturally enriched in
\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})
.

Notation 1.4.37
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos.
The symmetric monoidal enhancement of the constant sheaf/global sections-adjunction (
1.3.44
and
A.2.3
) induces an adjunction

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))\colon\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\text{ (\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{adjuncttioninducesadjunctiononalgebraobjects})}.

For
{A}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
, the counit
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A\to A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
determines a symmetric monoidal enhancement of the free
A
-module functor

A[-]\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})})

(
1.4.18
), and by
1.4.19
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

as symmetric monoidal categories.

By
1.4.16
, the constant sheaf functor induces a symmetric monoidal functor

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}).

Denote by

c_{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

the composition

\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\xrightarrow{c^{A}_{\operatorname{Sp}}}\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\xrightarrow{A[-]}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}).

Lemma 1.4.38
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos. For
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
, the functor

c_{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

exhibits
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
as enriched (
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.2.1.28]
) over
\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})^{\otimes}
.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion

\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

of
{\mathcal{X}}^{\otimes}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories with
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}))
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
. As
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
factors over
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{A,\otimes}
factors as

\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})})^{\otimes}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})^{\otimes}

for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
The construction of the free
A
-module functor (
1.4.18
) and the identification of
1.4.19
imply that
c_{A}
factors as

\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\xrightarrow{c^{\lambda}_{A}}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}),

where

c^{\lambda}_{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})})

is the symmetric monoidal functor induced by the constant sheaf functor for
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.

For
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})})
. By the above,

-\otimes M\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

factors as

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\xrightarrow{-\otimes_{\lambda}M}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}),

where
-\otimes_{\lambda}M
is induced by the left-tensoring of
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})})
over
\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})
induced by the constant sheaf functor for
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.3.1.33]
,
-\otimes_{\lambda}M
is a left adjoint, and since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is a symmetric monoidal left adjoint,
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
is a left adjoint by
Lemma

A.2.7
.
∎

Corollary 1.4.39
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is a big topos such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
has all small limits and colimits. For
A\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})
, the
\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})
-enriched mapping functor (
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.2.1.31]
)

\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{B}_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})

preserves small limits in both variables.

Proof.

As for all
b\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})
,
\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})}(b,-)
is a right adjoint,
\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})}(-,-)
preserves small limits in the second variable.
By
1.3.27
and
Lemma

1.4.4
, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})
is cocontinuous.
As the left-tensoring

\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\times\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})

is induced by the symmetric monoidal left adjoint
\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})
, this implies that the left-tensoring

\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}A}({\operatorname{Sp}})\times\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})

preserves small colimits in both variables.
It now follows from
Lemma

A.1.1
and
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.2.6.2]
that
\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty})})}(-,-)
preserves small limits in the first variable.
∎

1.5
Cohomology in big topoi

Our discussion from
Section

1.3
leads a robust notion of cohomology in big topoi. In this section, we record some elementary observations about it. In particular, we show that cohomology is invariant under geometric morphisms (
Lemma

1.5.7
), and admits a Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence (
1.5.13
).

Definition 1.5.1
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and denote by
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{X}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
the stabilization functor (
Lemma

1.3.10
).

(i)

Denote by
\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(-,-)
the spectrally enriched mapping functor of
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
(
Lemma

1.3.37
,
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.2.1.31]
). For
X\in\mathcal{X}
and
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
, the
cohomology spectrum
of
A
at
X
is

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\coloneqq\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X,A).

For
i\in\mathbb{Z}
, the ith cohomology group of
X
with coefficients in
A
is

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{i}(X,A)\coloneqq\pi_{-i}(\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)).

(ii)

If the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
provided by
Proposition

1.3.26
is closed, denote by
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(-,-)
the internal Hom in
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
and define
internal cohomology
by

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\coloneqq\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X,A)\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}).

For
i\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\underline{\mathbb{H}}^{i}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\coloneqq\pi_{-i}^{\mathcal{X}}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X,A)\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\heartsuit}\cong\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}).

Remarks 1.5.2
.

1.

Recall that if
\mathcal{X}
is a topos or the category of accessible (hyper)sheaves on a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site, then the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is closed by
Lemma

1.3.28
, whence internal cohomology in
\mathcal{X}
exists.

2.

Denote by
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Ab}}\colon\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Ab}
,
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}
the functors induced by the global sections geometric morphism
\Gamma\colon\mathcal{X}\to\operatorname{An}
(
Definition

1.3.42
).
By
1.3.47
,

\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)

(provided that internal cohomology in
\mathcal{X}
exists).
If
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact (equivalently, if
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Ab}}
is exact), this implies that

\Gamma_{\operatorname{Ab}}\circ\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{q}(X,A)=\mathbb{H}^{q}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\text{ for all }q\in\mathbb{Z}.

This holds for example for
\mathcal{X}=\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
(
Definition

2.2.1
,
Definition

2.4.2
), see
2.4.27
.

Example 1.5.3
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and denote by

c\colon\operatorname{An}\rightleftarrows\mathcal{X}\colon\Gamma

the global sections geometric morphism.

1.3.15
, and
Lemma

1.3.46
imply that for
A\in\operatorname{Sp}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(cA,-)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}A,-)

is right adjoint to

\operatorname{Sp}\xrightarrow{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}A\otimes c_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}).

The symmetric monoidal structure of
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
(
1.3.44
) yields an equivalence of this functor with
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}A\otimes-)
, whence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(cA,-)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}A,-)\circ\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}.

Remarks 1.5.4
.

It is natural to consider the following enhancements of cohomology in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
:

1.

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
, denote by
\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})}(-,-)
the
\operatorname{Sp}
-enrichment of the stable, big presentable category
\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
(
Lemma

1.3.37
,
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.2.1.31]
).

The free-forget adjunction

{R}[-]\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\colon f

is spectrally enriched by
1.3.40
, whence

(1.5.4.1)

\displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,f-)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})}({R}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}-],-).

In particular, if
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos as in
Lemma

1.4.32
, for
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))

(1.5.4.2)

\displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(-,fi-)|_{\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))}\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}({R}[-],-),

where

i\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

is the equivalence provided by
Lemma

1.4.32
and
{R}[-]\colon\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})
denotes the free
{R}
-module functor.

2.

Denote by
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})
the functor induced by the global sections functor. For
R\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
is enriched in
\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}})
by
Lemma

1.4.38
. In particular, cohomology with coefficients in
{R}
-modules refines to a functor

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,-)_{R}\colon\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}}).

3.

If
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is cartesian closed and has
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and all
\Delta
-indexed limits, then for all commutative algebras
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
, internal cohomology with coefficients in
{R}
-modules refines to a functor

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,-)_{{R}}\colon\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

by
Lemma

1.4.5
.

Lemma 1.5.5
.

For
i\in\mathbb{Z}
,
\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{i}(-,-)\cong\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,\Omega^{\infty}\Sigma^{i}-).

In particular, the counit
\tau_{\geq-i}\to\operatorname{id}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{i}(-,-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{i}(-,\tau_{\geq-i}-).

Proof.

For
i\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{i}(-,-)=\pi_{-i}\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}-,-)=\pi_{0}\Sigma^{i}\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}-,-)

\displaystyle=\pi_{0}\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}-,\Sigma^{i}-)

\displaystyle=\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(-,\Omega^{\infty}\Sigma^{i}-).

This implies the second statement since
\Omega^{\infty}\Sigma^{i}=\Omega^{\infty}\tau_{\geq 0}\Sigma^{i}=\Omega^{\infty}\Sigma^{i}\tau_{\geq-i}.

∎

Definition 1.5.6
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}
are big topoi.
A geometric morphism
L\colon\mathcal{X}\rightleftarrows\mathcal{Y}\colon R
is an adjoint pair
L\dashv R
such that the left adjoint
L
preserves finite limits.

By
1.3.4
and
1.3.15
, a geometric morphism stabilizes to an adjunction

L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})\colon R_{\operatorname{Sp}}

with
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{Y}}\circ L
.

Lemma 1.5.7
.

Suppose
L\colon\mathcal{X}\rightleftarrows\mathcal{Y}\colon R
is a geometric morphism between big topoi.
The adjunction
L\dashv R
induces an equivalence of functors

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{Y}}(L-,-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,R_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)\colon\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})\to\operatorname{Sp}.

Proof.

By
1.3.40
, the adjunction
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv R_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is spectrally enriched,
whence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,R_{\operatorname{Sp}}A)=\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X,R_{\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\underbrace{L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X}_{\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}LX},A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(LX,A).\qed

Remark 1.5.8
.

If
R\colon\mathcal{Y}\to\mathcal{X}
is a right adjoint between presentable categories with left adjoint
L
, the stabilization
R_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{Y})
(
Definition

1.3.3
) admits a left adjoint
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}
by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.4.4]
.
This satisfies
L_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}}\circ L
since both functors are left adjoint to
\Omega^{\infty}\circ R_{\operatorname{Sp}}=R\circ\Omega^{\infty}
. In particular,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(L,-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{Y}}(-,R_{\operatorname{Sp}}-).

However, for big topoi the functor
R_{\operatorname{Sp}}
need not admit a left adjoint if its left adjoint
L
is not left-exact.

Corollary 1.5.9
.

Suppose
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is a chain of topoi.
For all
\kappa\in\Lambda
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,-)|_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B_{\kappa}})}\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}(-,-).

Proof.

Denote by
r^{\kappa}\colon\mathcal{B_{\infty}}\to\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}
the right adjoint of the canonical functor
i_{\kappa}\colon\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
. This exists by
Lemma

1.2.4
.
For
x\in\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\subseteq\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(i_{\kappa}x,-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}}(x,r^{\kappa}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)

by
Lemma

1.5.7
.
As
\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}\xhookrightarrow{i_{\kappa}}\mathcal{B_{\infty}}\xrightarrow{r^{\kappa}}\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}
is the identity (
Lemma

1.2.4
), this implies the statement.
∎

For the convenience of the reader, we spell out a version of a Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence in a big topos that arises as an application of
[
Lur17
, section 1.2.4]
.

Proposition 1.5.10

(
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.4.5, Variant 1.2.4.9]
)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a stable category with countable products and
(\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0},\mathcal{C}_{\leq 0})
is a
t
-structure.

(i)

If
X_{*}\colon\Delta\to\mathcal{C}
is a cosimplicial object in
\mathcal{C}
,
there exists a spectral sequence
BKSS(X_{*})

with
E_{1}^{p,q}=\pi_{-q}(X_{p})
and
d_{1}
-differential

d_{1}\colon E_{1}^{p,*}=\pi_{-*}(X_{p})\to E_{1}^{p+1,*}=\pi_{-*}(X_{p+1})

the alternating sum

d_{1}^{p,*}\coloneqq\sum_{i=0}^{p}(-1)^{i}\pi_{-*}(s_{i})

of the degeneracies

s_{i}\colon X_{p}\to X_{p+1}.

(ii)

If there exists
N\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
X_{*}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta,\mathcal{C}_{\leq N})
, then the above spectral sequence converges to
\pi_{-(p+q)}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X)
, filtered by

\{F^{p}\pi_{*}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X)\coloneqq\ker(\pi_{*}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X)\to\pi_{*}({\underset{\Delta_{\leq p}}{\operatorname{lim}}}X))\}_{p\geq 0}.

This filtration is bounded, for
k\in\mathbb{Z}
:

0=F^{k+N-1}\pi_{-k}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X\subseteq\ldots\subseteq F^{0}\pi_{-k}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X\subseteq F^{-1}\pi_{-k}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X=\pi_{-k}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X.

(iii)

This is natural in the cosimplicial object
X_{*}
:
A map of cosimplicial objects

c_{*}\colon X_{*}\to Y_{*}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta,\mathcal{C})

induces

–

A map of spectral sequences

BKSS(c)\colon BKSS(X_{*})\to BKSS(Y_{*})

which is on the
E_{1}
-page given by pushforward
\pi_{-q}X_{p}\to\pi_{-q}Y_{p}
.

–

A map of filtered graded abelian groups
\pi_{*}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}(c)\colon\pi_{*}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X)\to\pi_{*}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}Y)
.

If
X_{*}
and
Y_{*}
are bounded above, then
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E_{\infty}^{p,q}(X)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{gr}^{p}\pi_{-(p+q)}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}X)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E_{\infty}^{p,q}(Y)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{gr}^{p}\pi_{-(p+q)}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}Y)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces BKSS(c)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{*}{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}(c)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

commutes for all
p,q\in\mathbb{Z}
.

Proof.

The existence of the spectral sequence is
[
Lur17
, Variant 1.2.4.9]
in the category
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
with the opposite
t
-structure.
The convergence statement is
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.4.5]
in the category
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
with opposite
t
-structure, shifted by degree
-N
.
Naturality follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.4.5, Variant 1.2.4.9]
in the stable category
\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}
with the pointwise
t
-structure (shifted by degree
-N
).
∎

Definition 1.5.11
.

A
simplicial cover
of an object
X
in a category
\mathcal{C}
is an augmented simplicial object
X_{*}\to X\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}_{+},\mathcal{C})
which exhibits
X
as
{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}X_{*}=X
.
A morphism
p\colon Y\to X
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
is an
effective epimorphism
if its Čech nerve
\check{C}(p)
is a simplicial cover of
X
.

Remark 1.5.12
.

By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 7.2.1.14]
, the Čech nerve of a map
p\colon Y\to X
in a topos
\mathcal{X}
is a simplicial cover if and only if
\tau_{\leq 0}f\colon\tau_{\leq 0}Y\to\tau_{\leq 0}X
is an epimorphism in the
1
-topos
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
.
Since for a chain of topoi
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
,
\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under small colimits and finite limits (
Lemma

1.2.4
) and the left adjoint
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\to\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
preserves epimorphisms, the same statement holds for big topoi.

Corollary 1.5.13

(Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence)
.

Suppose
X_{*}\to X
is a simplicial cover in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
.

(i)

Then

{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X_{*},-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X_{*},-).

(ii)

For
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
, there is a spectral sequence
BKSS(X_{*},A)

with

E^{1}_{p,q}\coloneqq\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{q}(X_{p},A),

and
d_{1}
-differential

d_{1}^{p,q}\coloneqq\sum_{i=0}^{p}(-1)^{i}(\partial_{i})^{*}\colon H^{q}(X_{p},A)\to H^{q}(X_{p+1},A)

the alternating sum of the pullback along the face maps
\partial_{i}\colon X_{p+1}\to X_{p}.

(iii)

If
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq N}
is a bounded above spectrum object, the spectral sequence
BKSS(X_{*},A)
converges to
\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(X,A)
, filtered by

\{F^{n}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(X,A)\coloneqq\ker(\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(X,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(X_{n},A))\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}.

This filtration is bounded: for
k\in\mathbb{Z}
,

0=F^{k+N-1}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{k}(X,A)\subseteq\ldots\subseteq F^{0}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{k}(X,A)\subseteq F^{-1}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{k}(X,A)=\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{k}(X,A).

(iv)

This is natural in the simplicial cover
X_{*}\to X
and the spectrum object
A
:

–

A map
A\to B
of bounded above spectrum objects induces a map of spectral sequences

BKSS(X_{*},A)\to BKSS(X_{*},B)

and a map of filtered graded abelian groups

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(X,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(X,B),

and
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E^{p,q}_{\infty}(BKSS(X_{*},A))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{gr}^{p}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(X,A)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E^{p,q}_{\infty}(BKSS(X_{*},B))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{gr}^{p}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(X,B).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

commutes.

–

A map
f\colon(X_{*}\to X)\to(Y_{*}\to Y)
of simplicial covers in
\mathcal{X}
(i.e. of the underlying augmented simplicial objects) induces a map of spectral sequences

BKSS(Y_{*},A)\to BKSS(X_{*},A)

and a map of filtered graded abelian groups

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(Y,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(X,A),

and
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E^{p,q}_{\infty}(BKSS(Y_{*},A))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{gr}^{p}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(Y,A)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E^{p,q}_{\infty}(BKSS(X_{*},A))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{gr}^{p}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(X,A)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

commutes.

Proof.

The functor
\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}
preserves small limits in the first variable by
1.3.38
.
In particular, if
X_{*}\to X\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\cup\{-1\},\mathcal{X})
is a simplicial cover, then
\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,-)
is the totalization of the cosimplicial object

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X_{*},-)\colon\Delta\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}).

For
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq N}
and
X\in\mathcal{X}
,
\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\in\operatorname{Sp}_{\leq N}
since for
k\geq N+1
,

\Omega^{\infty-k}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\cong\Omega^{\infty}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,\Sigma^{k}A)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,\Omega^{\infty-k}A)=0.

The statement is now an immediate consequence of
Proposition

1.5.10
.
∎

In case
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is closed symmetric monoidal and admits countable products, we also obtain spectral sequences for internal cohomology:

Corollary 1.5.14
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos such that the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is closed and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and
\Delta
-indexed limits.
If
X_{*}\to X
is a simplicial cover in
\mathcal{X}
, there is a spectral sequence with
E_{1}
-page

E_{1}^{p,q}=\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}^{q}(X_{p},A),

which converges to
\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}^{q}(X,A)
if
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is bounded above.
This is natural in the coefficient object
A
and the simplicial cover
X_{*}\to X
.

The above corollary in particular applies to the category of accessible (hyper)sheaves on a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site by
Lemma

1.3.28
.

Proof.

Since the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is closed, the tensor product preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables. Since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has
\Delta
-indexed limits and
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits,
Lemma

A.1.1
and
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.2.6.2]
imply that
\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,-)\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(X_{*},-)
.
Suppose that
N\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
such that
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq N}
. By
Lemma

1.3.32
, for
T\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{>N}
and
Y\in\mathcal{X}
,
T\otimes\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}Y\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{>N}
.
This implies that

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(T,\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(Y,A))\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(T\otimes\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}Y,A)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\tau_{\leq N}(Y\otimes\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X),A)=0,

i.e.
\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(Y,A)\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq N}
for all
Y\in\mathcal{X}
.
The statement now follows from
Proposition

1.5.10
.
∎

Lemma

1.3.45
implies the following:

Corollary 1.5.15
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
admits countable products and denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor.
If
X_{*}\to X
is a simplicial cover in
\mathcal{X}
, for bounded above spectrum objects
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{<\infty}
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X_{*},A))

via the canonical map.

Proof.

For
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\leq N}
and
X\in\mathcal{X}
,
\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\in\operatorname{Sp}_{\leq N}
since for
k\geq N+1
,

\Omega^{\infty-k}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)=\Omega^{\infty}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,\Sigma^{k}A)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,\Omega^{\infty-k}A)=0.

Hence by
1.3.38
and
1.3.45
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)\cong c_{\operatorname{Sp}}({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X_{*},A))\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X_{*},A)).\qed

We will apply the following construction to compare continuous and condensed/solid group cohomology.

Definition 1.5.16

(Simplicial resolution)
.

For a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, denote by
\mathbb{Z}[-]\colon\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}\to\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
the free functor.
If
\pi\colon A\to B\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
is an epimorphism, denote by

\mathbb{Z}[\check{C}(\pi)]\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))

the free simplicial abelian group on the Čech nerve of
\pi
.
By
Lemma

1.5.17
below, its unnormalized Moore complex (
[
Lur17
, Definition 1.2.3.8]
)
S_{*}^{\pi}\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))
augments to a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}[B]
via
\mathbb{Z}[\pi]\colon S_{0}^{\pi}=\mathbb{Z}[A]\to\mathbb{Z}[B]
.
We call this the
simplicial resolution
of
\mathbb{Z}[B]
along
\pi
.
Explicitly,
S_{*}^{\pi}
is given by

S_{n}^{\pi}\coloneqq\mathbb{Z}[\check{C}(p)_{n}]=\mathbb{Z}[\underbrace{A\times_{B}\times\ldots\times_{B}A}_{n+1\text{ times}}]\,\text{ and boundaries }\partial_{n}\coloneqq\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^{i}d_{i}\colon S_{n}^{\pi}\to S_{n-1}^{\pi}

the alternating sum of the face maps. If
B=*
, we write
S_{*}^{A}\coloneqq S_{*}^{A\to*}
for the corresponding resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
.

Lemma 1.5.17
.

The unnormalized Moore complex
S_{*}^{\pi}
augments to a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}[B]
via
\mathbb{Z}[\pi]\colon S_{0}^{\pi}=\mathbb{Z}[A]\to\mathbb{Z}[B]
.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi and
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
A,B\in\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
.
Since
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under finite limits, we can compute
\check{C}(\pi)
in
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
Since
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}\to\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
restricts to a functor
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
and
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
is exact, it follows that the simplicial resolution of
\pi
in
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
is the simplicial resolution of
\pi
in
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
. By exactness of
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
we may therefore assume that
\mathcal{X}=\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
is a topos. Denote by

H\mathbb{Z}[-]\colon\mathcal{X}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

the composition of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
with the free
H\mathbb{Z}
-module functor.
Since
H\mathbb{Z}[-]
is a left adjoint,

{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}H\mathbb{Z}[\check{C}(\pi)]\cong H\mathbb{Z}[{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\check{C}(\pi)]\cong H\mathbb{Z}[B].

The second equivalence holds since
\pi
is an effective epimorphism, cf.
1.5.12
.
By
Proposition

1.5.10
in the category
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\operatorname{op}}
with the opposite
t
-structure/
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.4.5, Variant 1.2.4.9]
, we have a spectral sequence with
E_{1}
-page
E_{1}^{p,q}=\pi_{q}(H\mathbb{Z}[\check{C}(\pi)_{p}])
which converges completely to
\pi_{p+q}H\mathbb{Z}[B]
.
By
Lemma

1.4.36
,

\pi_{q}H\mathbb{Z}[B]=\begin{cases}\mathbb{Z}[B]&q=0\\
0&\text{ else }\end{cases},

and

E_{1}^{*,q}=\begin{cases}0&q\neq 0\\
S_{*}^{\pi}&q=0\end{cases}.

This implies that

E_{\infty}^{p,q}=E_{2}^{p,q}=\begin{cases}0&q\neq 0\\
H_{p}(S_{*}^{\pi})&q=0\end{cases},

and hence

E_{\infty}^{p,0}=\operatorname{gr}^{p}\pi_{p}(H\mathbb{Z}[B])=\pi_{p}(H\mathbb{Z}[B])=\begin{cases}0&p\neq 0\\
\mathbb{Z}[B]&p=0.\end{cases}\qed

The following spectral sequence is central for proving compactness properties of certain condensed abelian groups in
Section

2.7
and for computations of derived internal Homs which enter our discussion of solid modules.

Lemma 1.5.18

(
[
CS19a
, Corollary 4.8]
, Breen-Deligne spectral sequence)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a 1-topos.
There is a spectral sequence of functors

\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))\times\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab}

with
E_{1}^{p,q}(A,B,T)=\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\operatorname{Ext}^{q}_{\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})}(\mathbb{Z}[A^{i_{k,p}}\times T],B)
,
b_{p},i_{k,p}\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.

On
\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))_{<\infty}
, this converges to

(A,B,T)\mapsto\operatorname{Ext}^{p+q}_{\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})}(\mathbb{Z}[T]\otimes A,B).

Proof.

Choose a small 1-category
\mathcal{C}
and a left-exact localization
L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Set})\to\mathcal{X}
.
By
[
CS19a
, Theorem 4.5]
, every abelian group
A
admits a resolution
S_{*}(A)\to A
with terms

S_{n}=\oplus_{k=1}^{b_{n}}\mathbb{Z}[A^{i_{k}}],i_{k},b_{n}\in\mathbb{N}_{0},n\in\mathbb{N}_{0},

and this is functorial in the abelian group
A
. (
[
CS19a
]
attributes this to Eilenberg, MacLane, Breen and Deligne).
Since
L
induces a left-exact localization
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})
, for
A\in\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})
, the degreewise sheafification of

\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni c\mapsto S_{*}(A(c))
is a resolution of
A
with terms

S_{n}=\oplus_{k=1}^{b_{n}}\mathbb{Z}[A^{i_{k}}]
. We denote this resolution by
S_{*}(A)
, it obviously depends functorially on
A
.

For
T\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
,

\mathbb{Z}[T]
is the sheafification of

\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni c\mapsto\mathbb{Z}[T(c)].

Since
\mathbb{Z}[T(c)]
is flat for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
\mathbb{Z}[T]
is flat in
\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})
by
[
Sta22
,
Tag 03ET, Tag 03ES
]
. In particular,
C_{*}(A,T)\coloneqq S_{*}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T]
is a resolution of
A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T]
for all
T\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
.
For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
denote by
C_{*}^{\leq n}(A,T)
the stupid truncation of this resolution.
By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.4.5.7]
, there exists a hypercomplete 1-localic topos
\widehat{\mathcal{Y}}
with
\tau_{\leq 0}\widehat{\mathcal{Y}}\cong\mathcal{X}
.
Lemma

1.4.32
and
Lemma

1.4.38
provide a
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
-enrichment of
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\widehat{\mathcal{Y}})})
. The
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
-enriched mapping functor

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(-,-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))

preserves small limits in both variables (
1.4.39
), and in particular,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(-,-)(C_{*}(-,-),-)\cong{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}^{\leq n}(-,-),-).

The long exact homology sequence implies that the canonical chain map

\operatorname{Cone}(C_{*}^{\leq n}(-,-)\to C_{*}^{\leq n+1}(-,-))\to C_{n+1}(-,-)[n+1]

is a quasi-isomorphism for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
We therefore obtain fiber sequences

\displaystyle\Omega^{n+1}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{n+1}(-_{1},-_{3}),-_{2})

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}^{\leq n+1}(-_{1},-_{3}),-_{2})

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}^{\leq n}(-_{1},-_{3}),-_{2})

in
\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))\times\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})).

By
[
Lur17
, Definition 1.2.2.9]
, the cofiltered object

\ldots\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}^{\leq n}(-,-),-)\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}^{\leq n+1}(-,-),-)\to\ldots

yields a spectral sequence with
E_{1}
-page

\displaystyle E_{1}^{p,q}(A,B,T)

\displaystyle=\pi_{-(p+q)}(\operatorname{Fib}\bigl(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C^{\leq p}(A,T),B)\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}^{\leq p-1}(A,T),B)\bigr))

\displaystyle=\operatorname{Ext}^{q}_{\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})}(\oplus_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\mathbb{Z}[A^{i_{k,p}}\times T],B)

in
\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))\times\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
If
B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))_{\leq N}
is bounded above, then

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}^{\leq n}(A,T),B)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})_{\leq N}

for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, whence by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.4.5]
the spectral sequence converges to

\pi_{-(p+q)}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X}))}(C_{*}(A,T),B)=\operatorname{Ext}^{p+q}_{\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal{X})}(A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T],B)

with filtration

\{F^{s}\coloneqq\ker(\operatorname{Ext}^{*}(C_{*}(A,T),B)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{*}(C_{*}^{\leq s}(A,T),B))\}_{s\geq-1}.

This filtration is bounded, for
m\in\mathbb{Z}
:

F^{m+N-1}\operatorname{Ext}^{m}(A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T],B)=0,\text{ and }F^{-1}\operatorname{Ext}^{m}(A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T],B)=\operatorname{Ext}^{m}(A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T],B).\qed

2
Condensed Mathematics

In this chapter, we review cornerstones of condensed mathematics from
[
CS19a
, Lectures 1-6]
, paying particular attention to set-theoretic size issues.
We begin by recalling basic results on the
weight
(
Definition

2.1.4
) of topological spaces and related categorical properties of the categories of compact Hausdorff spaces and profinite sets. A key fact is that the category of profinite sets is cocompactly generated and for every uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, the
\kappa
-cocompact objects are the
\kappa
-light profinite sets (
Lemma

2.1.14
). This implies that
(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}),\text{surjections})
forms a hyperaccessible explicit covering site (
Definition

1.1.7
,
Lemma

2.4.1
). The associated category of accessible hypersheaves is called condensed animae and denoted
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.
By our discussion from the first chapter, the category of condensed animae is not presentable and in particular not a topos; however it retains many topos-like properties. We review this in
Section

2.4
, it relies on the following description of condensed animae:
For an uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, denote by
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
the category of condensed hypersheaves (
Definition

2.2.1
) on the category of
\kappa
-light (
Definition

2.1.4
) profinite sets
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.
Via sheafification of left Kan extension, these categories form a large filtered system with
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})\cong{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
(
2.4.8
).
Restricted to the poset of regular/strong limit cardinals, this is an exhaustion of
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
by topoi (
Definition

1.2.1
,
2.4.13
). This description allows many statements about condensed categories to be deduced from their
\kappa
-condensed analogues. In particular, for a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
, many computations in
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
, such as small limits and colimits, can be carried out in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
for some sufficiently large strong limit/regular cardinal
\kappa
.
Some sources (e.g.
[
CS23
]
,
[
BH19
]
) work with
\kappa
-condensed instead of condensed categories. We therefore chose to formulate all results for both the condensed and the
\kappa
-condensed setting.

The first part of this chapter is structured as follows: After recalling basic properties of the weight of topological spaces, we review
\kappa
-condensed categories and show that large classes of topological spaces embed fully faithfully into
\kappa
-condensed sets in
Section

2.2
. We apply this embedding to model
\kappa
-condensed animae as hypersheaves on other categories of topological spaces in
Section

2.3
.
In
Section

2.4
we specialize our discussion from the first chapter to establish basic structural properties of condensed categories and their relation to
\kappa
-condensed categories. This uses the results from
Section

2.1
.
We then recall that there is a fully faithful functor from T1 compactly generated topological spaces to condensed sets which has a partially defined right adjoint. In
Section

2.5
, we compare condensed cohomology of topological spaces with their sheaf cohomology.

[
CS19a
]
constructed a comparison map from sheaf to condensed cohomology for compact Hausdorff spaces. We use the description of
\kappa
-condensed animae as hypersheaves on the category of all
\lambda
-small topological spaces to extend this to general (
\operatorname{T1}
) topological spaces. Descent for condensed and sheaf cohomology along local-section covers then yields generalizations of the identifications between sheaf and condensed cohomology obtained in
[
CS19a
]
.

In the second part of this chapter, we study the notion of solidity, the condensed analogue of non-archimedean completeness. As preparation, we record basic structural properties of derived and underived condensed module categories in
Section

2.6
, and establish some compactness properties of condensed abelian groups in
Section

2.7
.
In
Section

2.8
, we discuss the category of solid modules over a condensed ring
{R}
. We show that the category of solid
R
-modules is closed under limits, colimits and extensions and has enough projectives, and construct a (derived) solidification functor and a (derived) solid tensor product.
To do so, we slightly adapt the discussion from
[
CS19a
]
to obtain arguments that work for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
for arbitrary uncountable cutoff cardinals
\kappa
.
We compute the (derived and underived) solidification of free condensed abelian groups on compact Hausdorff spaces and CW-complexes. These computations imply that condensed cohomology with solid coefficients is homotopy invariant and lead to identifications of singular/sheaf and condensed cohomology with solid coefficients for large classes of topological spaces, see
Section

2.9
.

2.1
Some point-set topology

In this section, we record some basic results on the
weight
of topological spaces and related categorical properties of the categories of compact Hausdorff spaces and profinite sets. We will use this to relate condensed sets with topological spaces and to compare
\kappa
-condensed with condensed categories.

Lemma 2.1.1

(
[
Sta22
,
Lemma 08ZY
]
)
.

The functor
\lim\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})\to\operatorname{Top}
is fully faithful with essential image the totally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces.

We freely identify totally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces with profinite sets in the sequel.

Definition 2.1.2
.

A compact Hausdorff space
P
is
extremally disconnected
if it is projective in the category of compact Hausdorff spaces, i.e. if all continuous surjections
X\to P
from a compact Hausdorff space
X
admit a section.
Denote by
\operatorname{edCH}
the (large) category of extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces and continuous maps.

Recall that the forget functor from compact Hausdorff spaces to all topological spaces admits a left adjoint, called Stone-Čech compactification.

Lemma 2.1.3

(
[
Gle58
]
)
.

(i)

A compact Hausdorff space is extremally disconnected if and only if the closure of every open subset is open.

(ii)

The Stone-Čech-compactification of a discrete topological space is extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff.

(iii)

Extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces are totally disconnected.

(iv)

Every compact Hausdorff space is a quotient of the Stone-Čech-compactification of its set of points. In particular, every extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space is a retract of the Stone-Čech-compactification of its set of points.

Proof.

The first statement is
[
Gle58
, Definition 1.1, Theorem 2.5]
.
Together with
[
Gle58
, Theorem 4.1]
, this implies that Stone-Čech-compactifications of discrete topological spaces are extremally disconnected.

Suppose that
X
is extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff and
x,y\in X
are distinct points. Choose disjoint open neighborhoods
x\in U_{x},y\in U_{y}\subseteq X,U_{x}\cap U_{y}=\emptyset
. The closures
\overline{U_{x}},\overline{U_{y}}
are clopen by the first statement, and disjoint by
[
Gle58
, Lemma 2.2]
. In particular,
x
and
y
lie in different connected components of
X
, which shows that
X
is totally disconnected.

By definition of the Stone-Čech-compactification, for a compact Hausdorff space
K
, the
identity

K^{\delta}\to K
from the underlying set of
K
to
K
factors over a map
q\colon\beta(K^{\delta})\to K
which is surjective.
If
K
is extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff,
q
admits a section which exhibits
K
as a retract of
\beta(K^{\delta})
.
∎

The following definition will be central to us as it characterizes
\kappa
-cocompact profinite sets/compact Hausdorff spaces, see
Lemma

2.1.14
.

Definition 2.1.4
.

The
weight

\operatorname{wt}(X)
of a topological space
X
is the smallest infinite cardinal such that
X
admits a basis of cardinality
<\kappa
, i.e. a
\kappa
-small collection
\mathcal{B}
of open subsets of
X
such that every open subset of
X
is a union of elements in
\mathcal{B}
.
We say that a topological space
X
is
\kappa
-
light
if
\operatorname{wt}(X)<\kappa
.

A topological space is
light
if it admits a countable basis, i.e. is
\aleph_{1}
-light for
\aleph_{1}
the smallest uncountable cardinal.

For an uncountable cardinal
\kappa
denote by

\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{CH},\,\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}),\text{ and }\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{edCH}

the full subcategories on
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff/profinite/extremally disconnected spaces, respectively.

Remark 2.1.5
.

For a compact Hausdorff space
X
,
\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\max\{|X|,\aleph_{0}\}
by
[
Eng89
, Theorem 3.1.21]
. In particular, the categories
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
are small for all small cardinals
\kappa
.

Lemma 2.1.6
.

(i)

For a subspace
A\subseteq X
,
\operatorname{wt}(A)\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
.

(ii)

For a set of topological spaces
(X_{i})_{i\in I}
,

\operatorname{wt}(\prod_{i\in I}X_{i})\leq\max\{|I|,\operatorname{wt}(X_{i}),i\in I\}.

Proof.

This is immediate from the definition of the subspace and product topology.
∎

Lemma 2.1.7

(
[
Eng89
, Theorem 3.1.22]
)
.

If
X
is a compact Hausdorff space and
Y\to X
is a quotient map, then
\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\operatorname{wt}(Y)
.

Lemma 2.1.8

(
[
Aok24a
, Lemma 2.5]
)
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal.
A compact Hausdorff space
X
has
\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\kappa
if and only if there exists a continuous injection
X\hookrightarrow\prod_{\kappa}[0,1]
.

Proof.

Suppose that
X
is a compact Hausdorff space.
If
X\hookrightarrow\prod_{\kappa}[0,1]
is a continuous injection, then
X
is homeomorphic to its image, and hence every basis on
\prod_{\kappa}[0,1]
pulls back to a basis on
X
, which shows that
\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\operatorname{wt}(\prod_{\kappa}[0,1])=\kappa
.
Conversely, suppose that
\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\kappa
.
For
f\in\mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])
let
\mathcal{U}_{f}\coloneqq f^{-1}((0,1])\subseteq X
. We claim that these sets form a basis of the topology on
X
.
If
U\subsetneq X
is open, choose
x\in U
. By Urysohn’s lemma, there exists a continuous map
f_{x}\colon X\to[0,1]
with
f_{x}(x)=1
and
f_{x}|_{X\setminus U}=0
. Hence
U=\bigcup_{x\in X}U_{f_{x}}
, which shows that

\mathcal{B}\coloneqq\{U_{f}\,|\,f\in\mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])\}

forms a basis of the topology on
X
. By
[
Eng89
, Theorem 1.1.15]
,
\mathcal{B}
has a subbasis of cardinality
\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
, i.e. there exists a
\kappa
-small collection
\{f_{i}\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])
such that
(U_{f_{i}})_{i\in I}
is a basis of the topology on
X
. It follows that

\prod_{i\in I}f_{i}\colon X\to\prod_{i\in I}[0,1]

is injective.
Indeed: Since
X
is
\operatorname{T1}
, for
x,y\in X
with
x\neq y
there exists an open neighborhood
x\in U_{x}
such that
y\notin U_{x}
. Choose
i\in I
with
x\in U_{f_{i}}\subseteq U_{x}
. Then
f_{i}(x)\neq f_{i}(y)
.
∎

Lemma 2.1.9
.

For a profinite set
X
, the canonical map
X\to\prod_{f\in\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})}\{0,1\}
is injective.

Proof.

Suppose that
x,y\in X
with
x\neq y
.
Then
X\setminus\{x\},X\setminus\{y\}
form an open cover of
X
. As
X
is profinite, there exists a refinement to an open cover
X=\bigsqcup_{i\in I}U_{i}
with

U_{i}\subseteq X\setminus\{x\}\text{ or }U_{i}\subseteq X\setminus\{y\}\text{ for all }i\in I,

see e.g.
[
Sta22
,
Lemma 08ZZ
]
.
Choose
i_{x}\in I
with
x\in U_{i}
.
Then

\displaystyle 1_{U_{i_{x}}}\colon X

\displaystyle\to\{0,1\}

\displaystyle t

\displaystyle\mapsto\begin{cases}1&t\in U_{i_{x}}\\
0&\text{ else }\end{cases}

is continuous,
1_{U_{i_{x}}}(x)=1
and
1_{U_{i_{x}}}(y)=0
.
This shows that

X\to\prod_{f\in\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})}\{0,1\}

is injective.
∎

Corollary 2.1.10
.

For a profinite set
X
, the following hold:

(i)

\operatorname{wt}(X)=\max\{|\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})|,\aleph_{0}\}
.

(ii)

There exists a continuous injection

X\hookrightarrow\prod_{\operatorname{wt}(X)}\{0,1\}.

In particular,
|X|\leq 2^{\operatorname{wt}(X)}
and
