\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\max\{2^{|X|},\aleph_{0}\}
.

Proof.

We first show
i)
. By
Lemma

2.1.9
,
X\hookrightarrow\prod_{\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})}\{0,1\}
is injective.
Since
X
is compact and
\prod_{\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})}\{0,1\}
is Hausdorff, this is a homeomorphism onto its image, so in particular

\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\operatorname{wt}(\prod_{\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})}\{0,1\})\leq\max\{\aleph_{0},|\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})|\}.

We now show that
|\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})|\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
.
Suppose that
\mathcal{B}
is a basis of the topology on
X
with
|\mathcal{B}|\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
and
f\in\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})
. Since
f^{-1}(\{0\})
is open in
X
, there exist a subset
\mathcal{B}_{f}\subseteq\mathcal{B}
with
f^{-1}(\{0\})=\cup_{U\in\mathcal{B}_{f}}U
.
The closed subspace
f^{-1}(\{0\})\subseteq X
is compact, so we can choose
\mathcal{B}_{f}
to be finite.
This determines an injection

\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})\hookrightarrow\{F\subseteq\mathcal{B}\,|\,F\text{ finite }\}

to the set of finite subsets of
\mathcal{B}
.
In particular,

|\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})|\leq|\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\mathcal{B}^{n}|\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)\times\aleph_{0}\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)^{2}=\operatorname{wt}(X)

since
\operatorname{wt}(X)
is infinite.
The second statement follows from the first and
Lemma

2.1.9
.

Lemma

2.1.9
also implies that
|X|\leq 2^{|\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})|}
and obviously,
|\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})|\leq 2^{|X|}
.
∎

Corollary 2.1.11
.

Suppose that
\kappa
is an uncountable regular cardinal.
A profinite set
X
is
\kappa
-light if and only if it can be realized as a
\kappa
-small filtered limit of finite sets.

Proof.

If
I
is a
\kappa
-small filtered category, for
F\colon I\to\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}
,

{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}F\hookrightarrow\prod_{i\in I}F(i)
, whence

\operatorname{wt}({\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}F)\leq\operatorname{wt}(\prod_{i\in I}F)\leq|I|\times\aleph_{0}<\kappa.

Conversely, if
X
is a
\kappa
-light profinite set, for
F\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})
finite let

X_{F}\coloneqq\operatorname{Im}(\prod_{f\in F}f\colon X\to\prod_{f\in F}\{0,1\}).

By
Lemma

2.1.9
, the canonical map
l\colon X\to{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{F}
is injective.
As for
G\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})
finite,

X\xrightarrow{l}{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,\{0,1\})\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{F}\xrightarrow{\pi_{G}}X_{G}

is surjective, it follows that
l
is surjective and hence a homeomorphism since both sides are compact Hausdorff.
This exhibits
X
as
\kappa
-small filtered limit of finite sets.
∎

Lemma 2.1.12
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal. A compact Hausdorff space is
\kappa
-light if and only if it is the quotient of a
\kappa
-light profinite set.
A compact Hausdorff space is light if and only if it is metrizable.

Proof.

Suppose
X
is a
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff space. By
Lemma

2.1.8
, there exists a continuous injection
X\hookrightarrow\prod_{\operatorname{wt}(X)}[0,1]
.
Since
[0,1]
is compact metrizable, by the Hausdorff-Alexandroff theorem there exists a quotient map
\prod_{\mathbb{N}}\{0,1\}\to[0,1]
from the Cantor set.
Let
S\coloneqq\prod_{\operatorname{wt}(X)}\prod_{\mathbb{N}}\{0,1\}
.
Then
\operatorname{wt}(S)\leq\max\{\aleph_{0},\operatorname{wt}(X)\}<\kappa
.
Let
T\coloneqq S\times_{\prod_{\operatorname{wt}(X)}[0,1]}X
.
This is a closed subspace of
S
and in particular profinite of
\operatorname{wt}(T)\leq\operatorname{wt}(S)<\kappa
.
The surjection
S\to\prod_{\kappa}[0,1]
pulls back to a surjection
T\to X
which is a quotient map since
T
and
X
are compact Hausdorff. The converse implication is
Lemma

2.1.7
.

By
Lemma

2.1.9
and
2.1.10
, every light profinite set
X
is homeomorphic to a subspace of the Cantor set
\prod_{\mathbb{N}}\{0,1\}
and in particular metrizable.
Conversely, by the Hausdorff-Alexandroff theorem, every (non-empty) compact metrizable space is a quotient of the Cantor set
\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}
which is light profinite.

Lemma

2.1.7
now implies that compact metrizable spaces are light.
∎

Lemma 2.1.13
.

Suppose
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal.
9
9

9

This means that
\lambda<\kappa\Rightarrow 2^{\lambda}<\kappa
.

For a compact Hausdorff space
X
, the following are equivalent:

(i)

X
is
\kappa
-light, i.e.
\operatorname{wt}(X)<\kappa
.

(ii)

X
is
\kappa
-small, i.e.
|X|<\kappa
.

(iii)

X
is the quotient of a
\kappa
-light extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space.

Proof.

Suppose that
\operatorname{wt}(X)<\kappa
. Then
X
is the quotient of a
\kappa
-light profinite set
T
by
Lemma

2.1.12
and in particular,
|X|\leq|T|
.
By
2.1.10
,
|T|\leq 2^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}
and since
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal,
2^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}<\kappa
. This shows that
\ref{wtsmallerkappa}\Rightarrow\ref{sizesmallerkappa}
.
As the collection of all open subsets of
X
is a basis,
\operatorname{wt}(X)\leq\max\{2^{|X|},\aleph_{0}\}
, which shows
\ref{sizesmallerkappa}\Rightarrow\ref{wtsmallerkappa}
.

The implication
\ref{quotientedchkappa}\Rightarrow\ref{wtsmallerkappa}
holds by
Lemma

2.1.7
.
Suppose now that
|X|<\kappa
.
By
Lemma

2.1.3
,
X
is the quotient of
\beta(X^{\delta})
, the Stone-Čech compactification of its set of points.
By construction of the Stone-Čech-compactification,

|\beta(X^{\delta})|\leq 2^{|X|}<\kappa
(since
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal), whence
\beta(X^{\delta})
is
\kappa
-light by the equivalence of
(ii)
and
(i)
. This proves
\ref{sizesmallerkappa}\Rightarrow\ref{quotientedchkappa}
.
∎

The following result will be central for our discussion of condensed categories and motivated our discussion of weight of topological spaces.

Lemma 2.1.14

(
[
Man22
, Lemma 2.1.5]
,
[
Aok24a
, Proposition 2.11]
)
.

(i)

The category
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}
is compactly generated.
For an uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa
, the
\kappa
-compact objects of
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}
are precisely the
\kappa
-light profinite sets.

(ii)

The category
\operatorname{CH}^{\operatorname{op}}
is
\aleph_{1}
-compactly generated.
For an uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa
, the
\kappa
-compact objects are precisely the
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff spaces.

Proof.

The first statement is essentially
[
Man22
, Lemma 2.1.5]
.
The category

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}=\operatorname{Ind}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}^{\operatorname{op}})=\operatorname{Ind}_{\aleph_{0}}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}^{\operatorname{op}})

is
\aleph_{0}
-compactly generated by the objects of
\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}^{\operatorname{op}}
.
By
[
Man22
, Lemma 2.1.5]
,
X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
is
\kappa
-cocompact if and only if it is a
\kappa
-small filtered limit of finite sets, which is equivalent to being
\kappa
-light by
2.1.11
.

By

GU71
, 4.7, 6.5c]
,
\operatorname{CH}^{\operatorname{op}}
is
\aleph_{1}
-compactly generated by
[0,1]
and by

, Proposition 2.11]
, the
\kappa
-compact objects are precisely the

∎

We will use the following variants of continuity to compare topological spaces with (
\kappa
-)condensed sets.

Definition 2.1.15
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and
X,Y
are topological spaces.

(i)

A map
X\to Y
is
\kappa
-
continuous
if for all
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff spaces
K
and all continuous maps
K\to X
, the composition
K\to X\to Y
is continuous.
Denote by
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,Y)
the set of
\kappa
-continuous functions
X\to Y
and by
\operatorname{Top}^{\kappa\text{-}c}
the large category of all topological spaces and
\kappa
-continuous maps.

(ii)

A map
X\to Y
is
k
-
continuous
if for all compact Hausdorff spaces
K
and all continuous maps
K\to X
, the composition
K\to X\to Y
is continuous. Denote by
\mathcal{C}_{k}(X,Y)
the set of
k
-continuous maps
X\to Y
.

(iii)

A topological space
X
is
\kappa
-
compactly generated
if every
\kappa
-continuous map
X\to Y
to a topological space
Y
is continuous, i.e.
\mathcal{C}(X,-)=\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,-)
.

A topological space is
compactly generated
if every
k
-continuous map
X\to Y
to a topological space
Y
is continuous, i.e.
\mathcal{C}(X,-)=\mathcal{C}_{k}(X,-)
.

For cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa
, we have inclusion

\mathcal{C}(-,-)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{k}(-,-)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}(-,-)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,-).

Lemma 2.1.16
.

A continuous map is
\aleph_{1}
-continuous if and only if it is sequentially continuous.

Proof.

Suppose that
f\colon X\to Y
is sequentially continuous. If
K\to X
is a continuous map, the composite
K\to X\to Y
is sequentially continuous as continuous maps are sequentially continuous and compositions of sequentially continuous maps are sequentially continuous. Since all light profinite sets are metrizable (
2.1.10
), this implies that
f
is
\aleph_{1}
-continuous. Conversely, denote by
\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}
the one-point compactification of the natural numbers (with discrete topology). This is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected, hence profinite and

\{\{k\}\,|\,k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}\}\cup\{\mathbb{N}_{0}\setminus\{1,\ldots,k\}\cup\{\infty\},k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}\}

is a countable basis for its topology. If
(a_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}
is a convergent sequence in
X
with limit
a_{\infty}
, then

\displaystyle a_{*}\colon\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}

\displaystyle\to X

\displaystyle n

\displaystyle\mapsto a_{n}

defines a continuous map. By definition of the one-point compactification,
f\circ a_{*}\colon\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}\to Y
is continuous if and only if
f(a_{n})_{n}
converges to
f(a_{\infty})
. This shows that every
\aleph_{1}
-continuous map is sequentially continuous.
∎

Example 2.1.17
.

If
X
is Hausdorff and compactly generated, then
X
is
\kappa
-compactly generated for all cardinals
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(X)
since

X\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\to X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}K\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}K\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}K\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\to X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}K.

The first equivalence holds since
X
is compactly generated, the second since the compact subspaces of
X
form a cofinal subcategory of
\operatorname{CH}{}_{/X}
, the third since all subspaces of
X
are
\kappa
-light, and the last since the compact subspaces form a cofinal subcategory of
{\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}}_{/X}
.

We end this section with two results on the space of connected components of a compact Hausdorff space/topological group which we will use in our comparison of continuous and solid group cohomology in
Section

3.5.2
.
The following is a consequence of
[
Eng89
, Theorem 6.1.23]
.

Lemma 2.1.18
.

For a compact Hausdorff space
X
, the space of connected components
\pi_{0}X
, endowed with the quotient topology from the projection
X\to\pi_{0}X
, is profinite.

Proof.

As quotient of a compact space,
\pi_{0}X
is compact.
Next, we show that
\pi_{0}X
is Hausdorff.

By
[
Eng89
, Theorem 6.1.23]
, the connected component of a point
x\in X
is the intersection of all clopen subsets of
X
containing
x
. In particular, if
x_{1},x_{2}\in X
lie in distinct connected components, there exist clopen subsets
x_{1}\in C_{1}\subseteq X,x_{2}\in C_{2}\subseteq X
with
x_{1}\notin C_{2},x_{2}\notin C_{1}
.
Denote by
q\colon X\to\pi_{0}X
the quotient map. For
i=1,2
: As
C_{i}
is clopen, for a connected component
K\subseteq X
,
C_{i}\cap K=\emptyset
or
K\subseteq C_{i}
, whence
q^{-1}(q(C_{i}))=C_{i}
. In particular,
q(C_{i}),q(C_{2})\subseteq\pi_{0}X
are clopen and disjoint, which shows that
\pi_{0}X
is Hausdorff.
It follows from
[
Eng89
, Theorem 6.1.23]
that
X
is also totally disconnected.
∎

Corollary 2.1.19
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group, and endow its set of connected components
\pi_{0}G
with the quotient topology induced by
G\to\pi_{0}G
.
This is a totally disconnected and Hausdorff topological group.
If
\pi_{0}G
is locally compact, then
\operatorname{wt}(\pi_{0}G)\leq\operatorname{wt}(G)
.

Proof.

By continuity of the group operation, the connected component of the identity in a topological group is a normal subgroup, whence
\pi_{0}G
with quotient topology is a topological group. As the connected component of the identity is closed,
\pi_{0}G
is
\operatorname{T1}
and hence Hausdorff.
\pi_{0}G
is totally disconnected by e.g.
[
Str06
, Lemma 2.9]
.

Suppose now that
\pi_{0}G
is locally compact. By van Dantzig’s theorem,
\pi_{0}G
is a coproduct of profinite sets
\pi_{0}G=\sqcup_{i\in I}S_{i}
. Choose
I
such that
S_{i}\neq\emptyset
for all
i\in I
and denote by
q\colon G\to\pi_{0}G
the quotient map.
Then
G=\sqcup_{i\in I}q^{-1}(S_{i})
.
Since
q^{-1}(S_{i})\neq\emptyset
for all
i\in I
,
|I|\leq\operatorname{wt}(G)
.
As
q^{-1}(S_{i})\to S_{i}
is a quotient map for all
i\in I
, it follows from
Lemma

2.1.7
that

\operatorname{wt}(\pi_{0}G)\leq\sum_{i\in I}\operatorname{wt}(S_{i})\leq\sum_{i\in I}\operatorname{wt}(q^{-1}(S_{i}))\leq|I|\operatorname{wt}(G)\leq\operatorname{wt}(G).\qed

2.2
\kappa
-condensed categories

Definition 2.2.1
.

For an uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, the condensed topology on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
is the Grothendieck topology generated by finite, jointly surjective covering families, i.e.

S\subseteq{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}

is a covering sieve if and only if there exists a finite set
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i=1}^{n}\subseteq S
such that
\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\to X
is onto. This defines a Grothendieck topology by
Lemma

A.4.19
.

The category of
\kappa
-
condensed animae

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\coloneqq\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})

is the topos of hypercomplete
[
Lur09
, p. 666]
condensed sheaves on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.

For a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
, define the category of
\kappa
-condensed objects in
\mathcal{C}
by

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\coloneqq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{C},

where
\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}
denotes the tensor product of presentable categories (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
).

For
\kappa=\aleph_{1}
the smallest uncountable cardinal,

\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{light}}(\mathcal{C})\coloneqq\operatorname{Cond}_{\aleph_{1}}(\mathcal{C})

is called category of light condensed objects in
\mathcal{C}
.

Remark 2.2.2
.

\kappa
-condensed categories for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
were introduced in
[
CS19a
]
. Our definition is equivalent to theirs by
Lemma

2.1.13
.

[
CS23
]
discussed light condensed categories and

[
Man22
]
worked with
\kappa
-condensed categories for uncountable regular cardinals.
\kappa
-condensed categories for arbitrary uncountable cardinals
\kappa
were introduced in
[
Aok24a
]
.
By
1.1.6
, for a presentable category
\mathcal{D}
,

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}).

One can more generally define
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D})\coloneqq\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
for categories
\mathcal{D}
with small limits.

Example 2.2.3
.

A functor
F\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}\subseteq\operatorname{An}
is a
\kappa
-condensed set/anima if and only if the following hold:

(i)

F
preserves finite products, i.e.
F(\emptyset)=*
and for
A_{1},A_{2}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, the canonical maps
F(A_{1}\sqcup A_{2})\to F(A_{k})
exhibit
F(A_{1}\sqcup A_{2})=F(A_{1})\times F(A_{2})
.

(ii)

For all continuous surjections
q\colon X\to Y\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

F(Y)\cong\operatorname{Eq}(F(X)\rightrightarrows F(X\times_{Y}X)).

This follows from
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.5.7.2]
since
\operatorname{Set}\subseteq\operatorname{An}
is closed under limits and
\Delta_{s,\leq 1}\subseteq\Delta_{s}
is left 1-cofinal, see
[
Du23
, Example 6.14]
.
In particular, for a topological space
X
,

\underline{X}_{\kappa}\coloneqq\mathcal{C}(-,X)\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}

defines a condensed functor as every continuous surjection between compact Hausdorff spaces is a quotient map.

More generally,
Proposition

1.1.5
implies that
\kappa
-condensed objects in a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
can be identified with functors
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
satisfying a descent condition for
condensed hypercovers
:

Definition 2.2.4
.

An augmented semi-simplicial object
U_{*}\colon\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
is a
condensed hypercover
if for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the map

U([n])\to M_{n}U([n])\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
induced by the unit of
i^{*}\dashv i_{*}
is surjective.

If
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable category, denote by

\operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})

the full subcategory on finite products-preserving functors
F\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
such that for all condensed hypercovers
U_{*}\colon\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, the canonical map

F(U_{-1})\to{\underset{\Delta_{s}}{\operatorname{lim}}}F(U_{*})
is an equivalence. We call such functors
condensed functors
.

Corollary 2.2.5

(
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.2.1, Proposition A.5.7.2]
)
.

For a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
, restriction along the Yoneda embedding

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}

defines a fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C}).

Its essential image consists of the condensed functors.

Proof.

Denote by
S\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
the wide subcategory on continuous surjections
X\to Y
.
As
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
has finite coproducts and pullbacks and the forget functor
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{CH}\to\operatorname{Set}
preserves coproducts and pullbacks and is conservative, it is straightforward to check that
(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa},S)
is an explicit covering site and the associated Grothendieck topology (
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.2.1]
) is the condensed topology on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.

Proposition

1.1.5
now implies that pullback along the
hypersheafified Yoneda embedding

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})

is fully faithful with essential image the condensed functors.
By
2.2.3
, the Yoneda embedding
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
factors over

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}),

i.e. no hypersheafification is necessary. ∎

Lemma 2.2.6
.

The global sections functor
\Gamma\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{An}
is a left adjoint.

Proof.

By the adjoint functor theorem (
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
), it suffices to show that the global sections functor preserves small colimits.
Denote by
\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\xrightarrow{L_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
the left adjoint of the inclusion.
We will show that the global sections functor

\Gamma_{0}\colon\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{An}

of
\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})
factors over
\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\xrightarrow{L_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{An}
. Then the induced functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{An}
preserves small colimits and is the global section functor:
It is left adjoint to the composite

\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{c}\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\xrightarrow{L_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})

which equals the constant sheaf functor since it is cocontinuous and preserves the terminal object.

We first show that
\Gamma_{0}
factors over the category
\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})
of not necessarily hypercomplete sheaves. As
\Gamma_{0}
is evaluation at
*
and for
X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\mathcal{C}(-,X)
is a condensed sheaf (
2.2.3
), the composite

j\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\xrightarrow{\Gamma_{0}}\operatorname{An}

of
\Gamma_{0}
with the (hypersheafified) Yoneda embedding factors as
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\xrightarrow{f}\operatorname{Set}\subseteq\operatorname{An}
, where
f\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})\subseteq\operatorname{CH}\to\operatorname{Set}
denotes the forget functor. In particular,
j
preserves finite limits.
If
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
is a condensed cover, there exists a finite subset
F
such that
\sqcup_{i\in F}X_{i}\to X
is surjective. This implies that
\sqcup_{i\in I}j(F_{i})\to j(X)
is a surjection, i.e. an epimorphism in
\operatorname{Set}
and hence an effective epimorphism in
\operatorname{An}
. It now follows from
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.3.20]
that
\Gamma_{0}
factors over
\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})
.
The induced functor
\Gamma_{1}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{An}
preserves small limits and colimits. Hence by
[
Lur09
, Propositions 5.5.6.28, 6.5.1.12]
,
\Gamma_{1}
preserves
\infty
-connective morphisms.
As
\operatorname{An}
is hypercomplete, this implies that
\Gamma_{1}
factors over a functor
\Gamma\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})=\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{An}
.
∎

We now recall that
\kappa
-condensed sets are a good approximation of (
\kappa
-compactly generated) topological spaces.
For an uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, denote by
\operatorname{Top}^{\kappa\text{-}c}
the category of topological spaces and
\kappa
-continuous maps (
Definition

2.1.15
).

Proposition 2.2.7

(
[
CS19a
, Proposition 1.7]
)
.

The functor

\displaystyle\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Top}^{\kappa\text{-}c}

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})

\displaystyle X

\displaystyle\mapsto\mathcal{C}(-,X)\colon{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}_{\kappa}}\to\operatorname{Set}

is fully faithful.
It admits a left adjoint which sends a
\kappa
-condensed set
X
to the topological space

X(*)_{\kappa}\coloneqq{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/X}}{\operatorname{colim}}}S,

where the colimit is computed in the category of all topological spaces with continuous maps.
For a
\kappa
-condensed set
X
, the space
X(*)_{\kappa}
is
\kappa
-compactly generated with set of points
X(*)
.

Remark 2.2.8
.

Denote by
\operatorname{Top}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}^{\kappa\text{-}c}
the wide subcategory on topological spaces and continuous maps.
As the right adjoint
(*)_{\kappa}
takes values in
\kappa
-compactly generated spaces,
the adjunction
\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\dashv(*)_{\kappa}
induces an adjoint pair

\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Top}\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\colon(*)_{\kappa}.

Proof.

This is essentially
[
CS19a
, Proposition 1.7]
. By
2.2.3
, for all topological spaces
X
,
\underline{X}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
.
As every
\kappa
-condensed set is a colimit of representables, for every
X\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
and
Y\in\operatorname{Top}^{\kappa\text{-}c}
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(X,\underline{Y}_{\kappa})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{S\in(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/X})^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{S}_{\kappa},\underline{Y}_{\kappa})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{S\in(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/X})^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}(S,Y)

\displaystyle\cong\mathcal{C}({\underset{S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/X}}{\operatorname{colim}}}S,Y)

where the colimit
X(*)_{\kappa}\coloneqq{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/X}}{\operatorname{colim}}}S
is computed in the category
\operatorname{Top}
of topological spaces with continuous maps.
This space is
\kappa
-compactly generated by
Lemma

2.1.12
, so in particular,
\mathcal{C}(X(*)_{\kappa},Y)\cong\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X(*)_{\kappa},Y)
. As all the above identifications are natural in
X
and
Y
, this shows that

X\mapsto{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/X}}{\operatorname{colim}}}S

is left adjoint to
\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}
.

Lemma

2.2.6
and
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.28]
imply that the global section functor

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Set},\,F\mapsto F(*)

preserves colimits, whence

X(*)_{\kappa}={\underset{S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/X}}{\operatorname{colim}}}S\to X(*)

is a bijection of sets.
It remains to show that
\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}
is fully faithful. Fix a topological space
T
.
For a profinite set
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\underline{T}_{\kappa}(S)=\mathcal{C}(S,T)\subseteq\prod_{s\in S}T
is the subset on elements
(t_{s})_{s\in S}
such that
S\to T,s\mapsto t_{s}
is continuous. If
X\to\underline{T}_{\kappa}
is a map of
\kappa
-condensed sets, for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
s\in S
, the inclusion
\{i_{s}\}\hookrightarrow S
induces a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X(S)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T(S)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{s\in S}T}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X(\{s\})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{s}^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{s}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f(*)}

A map of
\kappa
-condensed sets
X\to\underline{T}_{\kappa}
is therefore the same data as a map of sets
f(*)\colon X(*)\to T
such that for all profinite sets
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, and all
x\in X(S)
, the composition

S\to X(*)\to T,\,s\mapsto f(*)(i_{s}^{*}(x))

is continuous. Since
X(S)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{S}_{\kappa},X)
, this is equivalent to requiring that for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and all maps
\underline{S}_{\kappa}\xrightarrow{t}X\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
, the composition
S\xrightarrow{t(*)}X(*)\xrightarrow{f(*)}T
is continuous.
In particular, if
X=\underline{Y}_{\kappa}
for a topological space
Y
, then
\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{Y}_{\kappa},\underline{T}_{\kappa})
is the set of maps
Y\to T
such that for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and all

t\in\mathcal{C}(S,Y)=\underline{Y}_{\kappa}(S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{S}_{\kappa},\underline{Y}_{\kappa}),

the composition
S\xrightarrow{t}Y\to T
is continuous.
By
Lemma

2.1.12
, these are precisely the
\kappa
-continuous maps, which shows that
\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}
is fully faithful.
∎

Lemma 2.2.9

(
[
Man22
, Proposition 2.1.8]
,
[
Aok24
, Proposition 2.5]
)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable category.
For uncountable cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa
, the restriction

r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})

has a left adjoint.

Suppose in addition that one of the following holds:

(i)

\lambda
and
\kappa
are uncountable regular cardinals and
\kappa
-filtered colimits commute with
\Delta
-indexed limits in
\mathcal{C}
.

(ii)

\lambda,\kappa
are strong limit cardinals and
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)
-filtered colimits commute with finite products in
\mathcal{C}
.

Then the left adjoint of restriction is fully faithful and given by left Kan extension along

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}.

Proof.

By construction of the restriction,
the composition

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{i_{\kappa,!}^{\lambda}}\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{L_{\operatorname{\lambda-cond}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})

of left Kan extension along
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}
followed by
\lambda
-condensed hypersheafification is left adjoint to the restriction.
The left Kan extension is fully faithful since
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\lambda}^{\operatorname{op}}
is.
By
[
Man22
, Proposition 2.1.8]
or
1.1.11
in the first and by
[
Aok24
, Proposition 2.5]
in the second case,
left Kan extension
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa,!}
restricts to a functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})
which is hence left adjoint to the restriction.
∎

2.3
Other models for
\kappa
-condensed animae

In this section, we model
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
as hypercomplete sheaves on other classes of topological spaces. This will be central for our comparison of condensed with sheaf cohomology.

Definition 2.3.1
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and
\mathbb{T}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a small full subcategory. Denote by
\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
the restriction of the functor from
Proposition

2.2.7
to the wide subcategory
\operatorname{Top}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}^{\kappa\text{-}c}
.
A collection of maps
\{T^{i}\to T\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\mathbb{T}
is a
\kappa
-
condensed cover
if

p\colon\bigsqcup_{i\in I}\underline{T^{i}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{T}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
.

The main result of this section is the following:

Proposition 2.3.2
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and
\mathbb{T}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a small full subcategory.

(i)

If
\mathbb{T}
contains all
\kappa
-light profinite sets, then the
\kappa
-condensed covers form a coverage (
Definition

A.4.3
) on
\mathbb{T}
and right Kan extension yields an equivalence

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T},\operatorname{An})

between hypercomplete,
\kappa
-condensed sheaves on
\mathbb{T}
(
Definition

A.4.8
) and
\kappa
-condensed animae.

(ii)

If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal and
\mathbb{T}
contains all
\kappa
-light extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces, then the
\kappa
-condensed covers constitute a coverage on
\mathbb{T}
and right Kan extension yields equivalences

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\cong\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T},\operatorname{An})

between hypercomplete sheaves in the
\kappa
-condensed topology on
\mathbb{T}
and
\kappa
-condensed animae.

In both cases, the hypersheafified Yoneda embedding

\mathbb{T}\xhookrightarrow{Y}\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{T})\xrightarrow{L}\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T},\operatorname{An})

sends a topological space
X
to
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,X)
.

Before giving the proof, we make some preliminary observations about
\kappa
-condensed covers.

Lemma 2.3.3
.

If
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover, the map
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X
is surjective.

Proof.

Suppose
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover and let
Y\coloneqq\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{X^{i}}_{\kappa}
.
As epimorphisms in the 1-topos
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
are effective and
(*)_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Top}
is a left adjoint,

\underline{X}_{\kappa}(*)_{\kappa}=\operatorname{Coeq}(Y(*)_{\kappa}\times_{\underline{X}_{\kappa}(*)_{\kappa}}Y(*)_{\kappa}\rightrightarrows Y(*)_{\kappa})

in
\operatorname{Top}
. As
\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Set}
reflects colimits, this implies that
\sqcup_{i\in I}(\underline{X^{i}}_{\kappa}(*)_{\kappa})=Y(*)_{\kappa}\to\underline{X}_{\kappa}(*)_{\kappa}
is surjective, whence
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X
is surjective by
Proposition

2.2.7
.
∎

Lemma 2.3.4
.

(i)

A family
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover if and only if for all
K\to X\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}
, there exists a finite family
\{K^{j}\to K\}_{j=1}^{n}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
such that
\sqcup_{j=1}^{n}K^{j}\to K
is surjective, and for all
j\in J
there is
i(j)\in I
such that
K_{j}\to K\to X
factors over
K_{j}\to X^{i(j)}\to X
.

(ii)

If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, a family
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover if and only if for all
K\to X\in{{{\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}
, there exists a finite family
\{K^{j}\to K\}_{j=1}^{n}\subseteq\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
such that
\sqcup_{j=1}^{n}K^{j}\to K
is surjective and for all
j\in J
there is
i(j)\in I
such that
K_{j}\to K\to X
factors over
K_{j}\to X^{i(j)}\to X
.

Proof.

We first show the following:

(*)

Suppose
K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
. A map
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
is an epimorphism if and only if there exists a finite family
\{K^{j}\to K\}_{j=1}^{n}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
such that
\sqcup_{j=1}^{n}K^{j}\to K
is surjective and for all
j\in J
there is
i(j)\in I
such that
\underline{K^{j}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}
factors over a map
\underline{K^{j}}_{\kappa}\to X^{i(j)}
.

The if-statement holds since
\sqcup_{j=1}^{n}\underline{K^{j}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets by definition of the condensed topology on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
(see also
[
Lur09
, Propositions 6.2.3.20 and 7.2.1.14]
).
Conversely, if
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets, then

\sqcup_{i\in I}\sqcup_{Y\in{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}_{/X^{i}}}}\underline{Y}_{\kappa}\to\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism. As the condensed topology on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
is finitary, there exist a finite subset
F\subseteq I
and for all
f\in F
a finite subset
P_{f}\subseteq{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X^{f}}}
such that

\sqcup_{f\in F}\sqcup_{Y\in{P_{f}}}\underline{Y}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets, cf.
[
Sta22
,
Lemma 0D06
]
.
By
Proposition

2.2.7
, the maps
\underline{Y}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}
are induced by continuous maps
Y\to K
and by
Lemma

2.3.3
,

\sqcup_{f\in F}\sqcup_{Y\in P_{f}}Y\to K

is surjective. This shows (*).

We now prove
(i)
.
As colimits in the 1-topos
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
are universal, epimorphisms are effective and every
\kappa
-condensed set is a colimit of representables
\underline{K}_{\kappa},K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, a map
A\to B\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
is an epimorphism if and only if for all
\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to B
,
K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

A\times_{B}\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets.
In particular, a family of continuous maps

\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}

is a
\kappa
-condensed cover if and only if for all
K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to\underline{X}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
,

\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{X^{i}\times_{X}K}_{\kappa}=\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{X^{i}}_{\kappa}\times_{\underline{X}_{\kappa}}\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets.
By (*), this holds if and only if for all
\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to X
,
K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, there exists a finite family
\{K^{j}\to K\}_{j\in J}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
such that

(i)

\sqcup_{j\in J}K^{j}\to K
is onto, and

(ii)

for all
j\in J
there is
i(j)\in I
such that

K^{j}\to K
factors as
\underline{K^{j}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{X^{i(j)}\times_{X}K}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}
.

By
Proposition

2.2.7
,
(ii)
holds if and only if for all
j\in J
,
K^{j}\to K
factors over a
\kappa
-continuous (and hence continuous) map
K^{j}\to X^{i(j)}\times_{X}K
.
This proves the first statement.

Suppose now that
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal.
By
Lemma

2.1.13
, every
\kappa
-light profinite space is a quotient of a
\kappa
-light extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space.
For
X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
choose a quotient map
Y\to X,X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
.
As
Y\times_{X}Y\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, there exists a quotient map
Z\to Y\times_{X}Y
with
Z\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
.
By definition of the condensed topology on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{Coeq}(\underline{Z}_{\kappa}\to\underline{Y\times_{X}Y}_{\kappa}\rightrightarrows\underline{Y}_{\kappa})=\underline{X}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set}).

This shows that
\underline{X}_{\kappa},X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
generates
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
under colimits.
As epimorphisms in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
are effective and colimits are universal, this implies that a map
A\to B\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
is an epimorphism if and only if for all
\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to B,K\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
,
A\times_{B}\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
.
The characterization of
\kappa
-condensed covers now follows from
Lemma

2.1.13
and the above.
∎

Lemma 2.3.5
.

Suppose
\mathbb{T}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a small full subcategory.

(i)

If
\mathbb{T}
contains all
\kappa
-light profinite sets, then the
\kappa
-condensed covers form a coverage on
\mathbb{T}
.

(ii)

If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal and
\mathbb{T}
contains all
\kappa
-light extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces, then the
\kappa
-condensed covers form a coverage on
\mathbb{T}
.

Proof.

Suppose first that
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathbb{T}
.
Suppose that
\{T^{i}\to T\}_{i\in I}
is a condensed cover and
S\to T\in\mathbb{T}
is a continuous map.
Since epimorphisms are effective and colimits are universal, epimorphisms in a 1-topos are stable under pullback. In particular,

\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{T^{i}\times_{T}S}_{\kappa}\cong(\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{T^{i}}_{\kappa})\times_{\underline{T}_{\kappa}}\underline{S}_{\kappa}\to\underline{S}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets.
As for
i\in I
,

\bigsqcup_{{X\in{{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/T^{i}\times_{T}S}}}}}\underline{X}_{\kappa}\to\underline{T^{i}\times_{T}S}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets, this implies that

\{X\to T^{i}\times_{T}S\to S\}_{X\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/T^{i}\times_{T}S}},i\in I}\subseteq\mathbb{T}

is a
\kappa
-condensed cover of
S
, which shows that
\kappa
-condensed covers define a coverage on
\mathbb{T}
.

Suppose now that
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal and
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathbb{T}
.
Suppose that
\{T_{i}\to T\}_{i\in I}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover and
S\to T\in\mathbb{T}
.
Above, we constructed a family of continuous maps
\{X_{j}\to S\}_{j\in J}
such that

(i)

for all
j\in J
,
X_{j}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

(ii)

\sqcup_{j\in J}\underline{X_{j}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{S}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets, and

(iii)

for all
j\in J
, there exists
i(j)\in I
such that
X_{j}\to S\to T
factors as
X_{j}\to T_{i(j)}\to T
.

Since
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, for all
j\in J
,
X_{j}
is the quotient of a
\kappa
-light extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space
\tilde{X_{j}}
(
Lemma

2.1.13
), and by definition of the condensed topology, the quotient map
\underline{\tilde{X}_{j}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{X_{j}}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets for all
j\in J
. This implies that
\{\tilde{X}_{j}\to X_{j}\to S\}_{j\in J}\subseteq\mathbb{T}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover, which shows that
\kappa
-condensed covers define a coverage on
\mathbb{T}
.
∎

Corollary 2.3.6
.

Suppose that
\mathbb{T}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}
is a small full subcategory and
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal such that the
\kappa
-condensed coverings form a coverage on
\mathbb{T}
.
For a topological space
S
,

\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,S)\colon\mathbb{T}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}\subseteq\operatorname{An}

defines is a
\kappa
-condensed sheaf, i.e.
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,S)\in\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T})
.

Proof.

Suppose
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\in\mathbb{T}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover. As
\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\to X
is surjective (
Lemma

2.3.3
), for every topological space
S
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Set}}(X,S)\cong\operatorname{Eq}(\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Set}}(X^{i},S)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Set}}(X^{i}\times_{X}X^{j},S)).

We claim that this isomorphism restricts to an isomorphism

\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,S)\cong\operatorname{Eq}(\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X^{i},S)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j\in I}\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X^{i}\times_{X}X^{j},S)),

i.e. that a map of sets
X\to S
is
\kappa
-continuous if and only if the composite
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X\to S
is
\kappa
-continuous. The only-if statement holds by continuity of
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X
.
Suppose now that
X\to S
is a map of sets such that
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X\to S
is
\kappa
-continuous.
By
Lemma

2.1.12
, it suffices to show that for all
K\to X\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}
, the composite
K\to X\to S
is continuous.
Fix
K\to X\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}
.
By
Lemma

2.3.4
, there exists a
\kappa
-light profinite space
\tilde{K}
with a continuous surjection
\tilde{K}\to K
and a continuous map
\tilde{K}\to\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}
such that
\tilde{K}\to K\to X
factors as
\tilde{K}\to\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X
.
In particular,
\tilde{K}\to K\to X
is continuous.
As
\tilde{K}
and
K
are
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff,
K\to\tilde{K}
is a quotient map, whence
K\to X\to S
is continuous.
∎

Proposition

2.3.2
is now a straightforward consequence:

Proof of
Proposition

2.3.2
.

By
Lemma

2.3.5
, the
\kappa
-condensed covers form a coverage
\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}
on
\mathbb{T}
in both cases.
Suppose first that
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathbb{T}
and denote by
\tau_{\operatorname{cond}}
the coverage on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
given be finite, jointly surjective covering families.

By
[
Lur09
, Propositions 6.2.3.20 and 7.2.1.14]
, the inclusion
(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa},\tau_{\operatorname{cond}})\to(\mathbb{T},\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}})
is a continuous functor, and for
T\in\mathbb{T}
,

\{X\to T\}_{X\to T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa/T}}\subseteq\mathbb{T}

is a
\kappa
-condensed cover in
\mathbb{T}
.
By
Lemma

2.3.4
,
(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa},\tau_{\operatorname{cond}})\to(\mathbb{T},\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}})
has the covering lifting property (
Definition

A.4.14
).
It now follows from

A.4.18
that

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T})

via right Kan extension and restriction.
By
2.3.6
, for
T\in\mathbb{T}
:
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,T)\colon\mathbb{T}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}
is a
\kappa
-condensed sheaf.
The inclusion
\mathcal{C}(-,T)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,T)
therefore induces a monomorphism

L_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathcal{C}(-,T))\to\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,T)\in\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T}),

where
L_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{T}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T})
denotes condensed hypersheafification which is left-exact by
[
Lur09
, Propositions 6.2.2.7, 6.2.1.1 and 6.5.1.16]
.
As the restriction

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})

is an equivalence and for
X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\mathcal{C}(X,T)=\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,T),

it follows that
L_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathcal{C}(-,T))\cong\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,T)
.

Suppose now that
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathbb{T}
and equip both sides with the
\kappa
-condensed coverages
\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}
. The inclusion
(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa},\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}})\subseteq(\mathbb{T},\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}})
is continuous and by
Lemma

2.3.4
, it has the covering lifting property.
Since
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal,
Lemma

2.1.13
implies that for
T\in\mathbb{T}
,

\{X\to T\}_{X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}/T}\subseteq\mathbb{T}

is a
\kappa
-condensed cover.
It now follows from
A.4.18
that right Kan extension induces an equivalence

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathbb{T}).

By setting
\mathbb{T}=\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, we obtain that

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An}),

where the right equivalence is the first statement of the proposition for
\mathbb{T}=\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.

It remains to show that
\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
. As for
X^{0},X^{1}\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
,

\{X^{i}\to X^{0}\sqcup X^{1}\}_{i=0,1}

is a
\kappa
-condensed cover, and the empty cover of the empty set is a
\kappa
-condensed cover,

{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}).

Suppose that
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
is such that
\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets.
Since
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
is representable and the condensed topology is finitary, there exists a finite subset
F\subseteq I
such that
\sqcup_{i\in F}\underline{X^{i}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{X}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism of condensed sets (
[
Sta22
,
Lemma 0D06
]
).
By
Lemma

2.3.3
,

q\colon\sqcup_{i\in F}X^{i}\to X

is surjective, and hence admits a section since
X
is extremally disconnected. This implies that every presheaf

F\colon\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}

is
\{\sqcup_{i\in F}X^{i}\to X\}
-descendable, and hence every additive sheaf
F\in\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
is
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
-descendable, which shows that

{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})=\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}).

By
[
Lur09
, Lemma 6.5.1.2]
, the homotopy group functors
\pi_{n}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
restrict to functors

\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\to\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}),

which implies that
\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
is hypercomplete.
The same argument as above shows that for
T\in\mathbb{T}
,
L_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\mathcal{C}(-,T))\cong\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,T)
.
∎

In particular, we obtain the following models for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
:

Corollary 2.3.7

(
[
CS19a
, Proposition 2.3, Proposition 2.7]
)
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal.

(i)

The finite, jointly surjective covers form a coverage
\tau
on the category
\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
of
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff spaces which generates (
Definition

A.4.4
) the
\kappa
-condensed topology on
\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
. In particular, restriction along
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
is an equivalence

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau}(\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An}).

(ii)

The restriction
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
has a fully faithful right adjoint given by right Kan extension.
If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, then this is an equivalence.

Proof.

We first prove the first statement.
If
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i=1}^{n}\subseteq\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
is such that
\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\to X
is onto, for all
Y\to X\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
:
\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}Y\times_{X}X_{i}\to X
is onto. Since
X
is Hausdorff,
Y\times_{X}X_{i}
is a closed subspace of
Y\times X
and in particular
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff.
This shows that finite, jointly surjective covers form a coverage on
\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
.
By
Lemma

2.1.12
, every
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff space is the quotient of a
\kappa
-light profinite set. Together with
Lemma

2.3.4
, this implies that a family
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
is a
\kappa
-condensed cover if and only if there exists a finite subset
F\subseteq I
such that
\sqcup_{i\in F}X^{i}\to X
is onto.
This shows that
\kappa
-condensed covers and finite, jointly surjective maps generate the same Grothendieck topology on
\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
.

Proposition

2.3.2
now implies that

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau}(\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa},\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})

via restriction.

Equip
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
with the coverage given by covers of the form
\{X_{j}\to\sqcup_{j=1}^{n}X^{j}\}_{j=1,\ldots,n}
and the empty cover of the empty set, and
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
with the coverage defined by finite, jointly surjective covers. We claim that
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
has the covering lifting property. Suppose that

\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i=1}^{n}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}

is such that
q\colon\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\to X
is onto and
X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
.
Since
\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}
is compact Hausdorff, the map
q
has a section
s\colon X\to\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}
. As
X=\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}s^{-1}(X_{i})
,

\{s^{-1}(X_{i})\to X\}_{i=1}^{n}\subseteq\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}

is a cover for
X
, which shows that
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
has the covering lifting property.
By
[
Lur09
, Lemma 6.5.1.2]
, the homotopy group functors
\pi_{n}\colon\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\to\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
restrict to functors

\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\to\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}),

which implies that
\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
is hypercomplete. It now follows from
Lemma

A.4.16
that right Kan extension
\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})
restricts to a functor

\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
which is fully faithful since right Kan extension is.
By
Proposition

2.3.2
, it is an equivalence if
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal.
∎

Recall that an object
c
in a category
\mathcal{C}
is compact if
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,-)\colon\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{An}
preserves filtered colimits and compact projective if

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,-)
preserves sifted colimits.

2.3.7
implies that the following families of
representables
are compact respectively projective in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
and
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
:

Corollary 2.3.8
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal.

(i)

For a
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff space
X\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
,
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
is compact in
\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and in particular in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})=\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
.

(ii)

For a
\kappa
-light extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space
X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
,
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
is compact projective in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
. If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, then

\underline{X}_{\kappa},\,X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}

generate
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
under colimits.

Proof.

By
2.3.7
, the
\kappa
-condensed topology on
\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
is finitary (i.e. every cover can be refined by a finite cover). Hence the representable sheaves
\underline{X}_{\kappa},X\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
in the associated hypercomplete topos
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
are coherent by
[
Lur18a
, Corollary A.2.3.2, Proposition A.2.2.2]
. By
[
Lur18a
, Corollary A.2.3.2]
, this implies that for all
X\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
,
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
is compact in
\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.

By
2.3.7
, the restriction
i^{*}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
has a right adjoint given by right Kan extension. In particular,
i^{*}
preserves colimits. Since colimits in
\operatorname{An}
are universal, sifted colimits in
\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
are computed pointwise, i.e. for representables
h_{X}\in\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}),X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})}(h_{X},-)\colon\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{An}

preserves sifted colimits, which implies that

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})}(h_{X},-)\circ i^{*}

does as well.
If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, then

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\cong\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})

and hence the represented condensed sets
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
, for
X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
generate
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
under colimits.
∎

Corollary 2.3.9
.

The Cantor set
\underline{\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}}_{\kappa}
generates
\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{light}}(\operatorname{An})
under colimits.

Proof.

By the Hausdorff-Alexandroff theorem, every non-empty metrizable compact Hausdorff space is the quotient of the Cantor set
\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}
.
It follows from
[
Lur18a
, Proposition 20.4.5.1]
that
\underline{\{0,1\}}^{\mathbb{N}}_{\kappa}
generates
\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{light}}(\operatorname{An})
under small colimits. ∎

2.4
Condensed categories

We now review condensed categories and record basic categorical properties thereof which follow from our discussion in the first chapter and
Section

2.1
.

Lemma 2.4.1
.

(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}),\text{surjective maps})
is an explicit covering site which is
\kappa
-hyperaccessible for every uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa
.

Proof.

As the forget functor
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})\subseteq\operatorname{CH}\to\operatorname{Set}
reflects limits and finite colimits, it is straightforward to check that

(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}),\text{surjective maps})
is an explicit covering site.
The category
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
is
\kappa
-coaccessible for all uncountable regular cardinals
\kappa
by
[
Lur09
, Lemma 5.4.2.10, Remark 5.4.2.9]
.
It now follows from
[
Man22
, Lemma 2.1.7]
that

(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}),\text{surjective maps})
is a
\kappa
-hyperaccessible explicit covering site for all uncountable regular cardinals
\kappa
.
∎

Definition 2.4.2
.

Denote by
S\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
the wide subcategory on surjections.
For a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
denote by

\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})\coloneqq\operatorname{hypShv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}),\mathcal{C})

the category of hypercomplete, accessible
S
-sheaves valued in
\mathcal{C}
(
Definition

1.1.7
).

This is equivalent to the definition of
[
CS19a
]
, see
2.4.9
below.

More concretely, a functor
F\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
is a condensed object in
\mathcal{C}
if and only if the following are satisfied:

(i)

F
is accessible,

(ii)

F
preserves finite products, and

(iii)

for every condensed hypercover
U_{*}\colon\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
(
Definition

2.2.4
),

F(U_{-1})={\underset{\Delta_{s}}{\operatorname{lim}}}F(U_{*}).

Example 2.4.3
.

A functor
F\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}
is a condensed set if and only if

(i)

F
is accessible,

(ii)

F
preserves finite products, and

(iii)

for all continuous surjections
q\colon X\to Y\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

F(Y)\cong\operatorname{Eq}(F(X)\rightrightarrows F(X\times_{Y}X)).

This holds since
\operatorname{Set}\subseteq\operatorname{An}
reflects filtered colimits and small limits and
\Delta_{s,\leq 1}\subseteq\Delta_{s}
is left 1-cofinal, see
[
Du23
, Example 6.14]
.

Remark 2.4.4

(Pyknotic versus condensed)
.

If
\kappa
is an uncountable, small strong limit regular cardinal and
\mathcal{U}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{U}_{0}
is the universe associated to
{\kappa}
, i.e. the set of
\kappa
-small sets, then
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
is the category of pyknotic animae corresponding to
\mathcal{U}_{\kappa}\in\mathcal{U}_{0}
.
As the inclusion
i\colon\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal{U}_{1}}
from
\mathcal{U}_{0}
-small animae into
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small animae preserves
\mathcal{U}_{0}
-small limits, the functor

i_{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal{U}_{0}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal{U}_{1}})

restricts to a fully faithful functor
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}^{\mathcal{U}_{1}}
from condensed anima (defined in
\mathcal{U}_{0}
) to pyknotic animae (defined with respect to
\mathcal{U}_{0}\in\mathcal{U}_{1}
). Here
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}
denotes the category of
\mathcal{U}_{0}
-small profinite sets. By
Lemma

2.1.13
, these are precisely the
\mathcal{U}_{0}
-light profinite sets.
As
(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\mathcal{U}_{2}},\text{ epimorphisms})
is
\mathcal{U}_{0}
- and
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-hyperaccessible (
Lemma

2.4.1
), left Kan extension along

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\mathcal{U}_{1}}
restricts to a functor

\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}^{\mathcal{U}_{2}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{1}}^{\mathcal{U}_{2}}

(
1.1.11
in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
). By definition of condensed anima (in
\mathcal{U}_{1}
), this factors over

\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{1}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{1}},

so we obtain fully faithful functors

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{0}}^{\mathcal{U}_{1}}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{1}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pyk}(\operatorname{An})_{\mathcal{U}_{1}}^{\mathcal{U}_{2}}.

As
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
is not an essentially small category and the condensed topology is subcanonical,
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is not an accessible category by
1.1.14
, and in particular not a topos (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.1.3.19]
).
We recall here from the first chapter that
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
however resembles a topos in many ways.
1.1.17
implies:

Corollary 2.4.5

(Giraud’s axioms)
.

Condensed animae are a locally small category and satisfy all of Giraud’s axioms except accessibility, i.e.

(i)

All small colimits and all small limits exist.

(ii)

Small colimits are universal.

(iii)

Small coproducts are disjoint.

(iv)

Every groupoid object of
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is effective.

1.1.28
implies:

Corollary 2.4.6

(
[
Man22
, Proposition 2.1.11]
)
.

If
\mathcal{C}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal category,
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
inherits the structure of a closed monoidal category such that for all regular cardinals
\kappa
such that
\mathcal{C}
is
\kappa
-accessible,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.

We have also shown that the category of spectrum objects in
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
behaves like the stabilization of a presentable category in many
aspects:

(i)

\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An}))\cong\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
is a stable category
(
Lemma

1.3.2
,
1.3.7
).

(ii)

The functor
\Omega^{\infty}\colon\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})

admits a left adjoint
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
, which factors as a composite of left adjoints

\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{CGrp}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An}))\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})

(
Lemma

1.3.10
).

(iii)

The essential image of
\operatorname{CGrp}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An}))\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
is
the connective part of a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
with

\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})^{\heartsuit}\cong\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
(
Lemma

1.3.12
)

(iv)

There exists an essentially unique cocontinuous symmetric
monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
with a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
(
1.3.27
).
This symmetric monoidal structure is closed (
Lemma

1.3.28
).

(v)

The symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
is compatible
with the
t
-structure, i.e.
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory
(
Lemma

1.3.32
).

2.4.1
Condensed and
\kappa
-condensed categories

We now recall that for a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
,
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
can be exhausted by
\kappa
-condensed categories
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})
, as
\kappa
ranges over a suitable family of uncountable cardinals. We will apply this to deduce statements on condensed categories from the corresponding
\kappa
-condensed statements for sufficiently large
\kappa
.
The identification from
2.2.5
, yields for every uncountable cardinal
\kappa
a restriction functor

\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C}).

Lemma 2.4.7
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable category.
For every uncountable cardinal
\kappa
, the restriction

\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})
has a left adjoint.

Proof.

Chose a regular cardinal
\mu
such that
\mathcal{C}
is
\mu
-accessible.
Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and choose a regular cardinal
\lambda\geq\kappa,\lambda\gg\mu
.
Then the restriction
r^{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})
factors as

\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{r^{\lambda}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C}).

By
Lemma

2.1.14
and
1.1.11
,
r^{\lambda}
has a left adjoint.
The functor
r^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
has a left adjoint by
Lemma

2.2.9
.
∎

Denote by
\Lambda
the poset of all small uncountable cardinals and by
\Lambda^{\triangleright}\coloneqq\Lambda\cup\{\infty\}
its cone.
The
restrictions
yield a functor

\displaystyle(\Lambda^{\triangleright})^{\operatorname{op}}

\displaystyle\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}

\displaystyle\lambda

\displaystyle\mapsto\begin{cases}\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})&\lambda\neq\infty\\
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})&\lambda=\infty.\end{cases}

By
Lemma

2.4.7
and
Lemma

2.2.9
, this enhances to a functor

(\Lambda^{\triangleright})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{R}.

Denote by
\operatorname{Cond}_{*}(\mathcal{C})\colon\Lambda^{\triangleright}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L}
its opposite. (Recall that
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L}\cong(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{R})^{\operatorname{op}}
, see e.g.
[
Hau+23
, Theorem B]
.)

1.1.11
implies:

Corollary 2.4.8
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable category.
Then

\operatorname{Cond}_{*}(\mathcal{C})\colon\Lambda^{\triangleright}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}^{L}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}

is a colimit diagram.

Proof.

Choose a regular cardinal
\mu
such that
\mathcal{C}
is
\mu
-accessible. Since the uncountable regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
form a cofinal subcategory of
\Lambda
, the statement follows from
1.1.21
and
Lemma

2.1.14
.
∎

Corollary 2.4.9
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable category.
Denote by
\Lambda^{r},\Lambda^{s}
the large posets of small regular/strong limit cardinals, respectively.
Then

{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda^{r}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\cong{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda^{s}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})

where the colimits are computed in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
and the transition maps are the left adjoints of the restriction.

Proof.

This follows from
2.4.8
as the regular/strong limit cardinals form a cofinal system in the poset of all small cardinals.
∎

Remark 2.4.10
.

[
CS19a
]
defined
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
as
{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda^{s}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})
.
The identification

\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})\cong{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda^{s}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})

is instructive as for all strong limit cardinals
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\cong\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa})
is a particularly nice category. For example,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
has enough compact projectives for all strong limit cardinals
\kappa
, which implies that the same holds for
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
, see
2.6.5
.

Corollary 2.4.11
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable category such that filtered colimits commute with finite products in
\mathcal{C}
(e.g.
\mathcal{C}
is compactly generated or stable).
Then the left adjoint

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})

of restriction is fully faithful for all strong limit cardinals
\kappa
.

Proof.

By
Lemma

2.2.9
, for all strong limit cardinals
\kappa\leq\lambda
, the left adjoint
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})
of restriction is fully faithful.

Lemma

A.1.3
now implies that

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\to{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\lambda\\
\lambda\text{ str. limit}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})

is fully faithful for all strong limit cardinals
\kappa
.
∎

1.1.11
and
1.1.15
imply:

Corollary 2.4.12
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable category and
\mu
is a regular cardinal such that
\mathcal{C}
is
\mu
-accessible and
\kappa\geq\mu
is an uncountable regular cardinal.

(i)

The left adjoint
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
of restriction is fully faithful. Its essential image consists of the condensed hypersheaves
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
which preserve
\kappa
-filtered colimits.

(ii)

In particular,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
is closed under
\mu
-small limits and small colimits.

(iii)

If
\kappa>>\mu
, then
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
is closed under
\kappa
-small limits.

(iv)

The category
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
has small limits and colimits and small limits and colimits can always be computed in some stage
\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\mathcal{C})
for an uncountable regular cardinal
\lambda\geq\mu
.

Proof.

This is a special case of
1.1.11
and
1.1.15
, note that
\mathcal{C}
is
\lambda
-accessible for all
\lambda\gg\mu
by
[
Lur09
, Lemma 5.4.2.10]
.
∎

Corollary 2.4.13
.

Denote by
\Lambda^{r/s}
the posets of small regular/strong limit cardinals, respectively.
The functor

\operatorname{Cond}_{*}(\operatorname{An})\colon\Lambda^{r/s}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L},\lambda\mapsto\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{An})

with transition maps given by the left adjoints of the restriction is an exhaustion of
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
by topoi (
Definition

1.2.1
).

Proof.

By
2.4.9
,
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is the colimit of both functors in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
, and by
Lemma

2.2.9
, the transition functors
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{An})
are fully faithful left adjoints for all pairs of regular or strong limit cardinals
\kappa\leq\lambda
, respectively.
As for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})

is closed under finite limits, the left adjoint
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{An})
preserves finite limits by
Lemma

A.4.11
.
∎

As the condensed topology is finitary, the following holds:

Lemma 2.4.14
.

If
\mathcal{C}
is a presentable
(n,1)
-category so that filtered colimits commute with finite limits in
\mathcal{C}
, then filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})
can be computed pointwise.

Proof.

Suppose that
F\colon I\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})
is a filtered diagram and denote by
{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F
its colimit in
\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{C})
. As
\mathcal{C}
has filtered colimits, this colimit is computed pointwise.
Since finite limits commute with filtered colimits in
\mathcal{C}
,
{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F
preserves finite products.
Suppose that
U_{*}\colon\Delta_{s,+}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
is a condensed hypercover.
As
\Delta_{s,\leq n}\subseteq\Delta_{s}
is left
n
-cofinal (
[
Du23
, Example 6.14]
), for a functor
G\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
,

{\underset{\Delta_{s}}{\operatorname{lim}}}G(U_{*})\cong{\underset{\Delta_{s,\leq n}}{\operatorname{lim}}}G(U_{*}).

As
\Delta_{s,\leq n}
is finite and filtered colimits commute with finite limits in
\mathcal{C}
,
2.2.5
/
Definition

2.4.2
imply that

{\underset{\Delta_{s}}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(U_{*})\cong{\underset{\Delta_{s,\leq n}}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(U_{*})\cong{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}{\underset{\Delta_{s,\leq n}}{\operatorname{lim}}}F(U_{*})\cong{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(U_{-1}),

whence
{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F\in\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathcal{C})
by
2.2.5
/
Definition

2.4.2
.
∎

2.4.2
Condensed sets and topological spaces

In this section, we recall how
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces embed into condensed sets.

Proposition 2.4.15

(
[
CS19a
, Proposition 2.15]
)
.

Suppose
X
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space.
If
\kappa>|X|
is an uncountable regular cardinal, then
\mathcal{C}(-,X)\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}
is
\kappa
-accessible.
In particular,

\underline{X}\coloneqq\mathcal{C}(-,X)\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}

defines a condensed set.

Remark 2.4.16
.

If
X
is a topological space which is not
\operatorname{T1}
, then
\mathcal{C}(-,X)
is not accessible and in particular not a condensed set, see
[
CS19a
, Warning 2.14]
.

The proof of
Proposition

2.4.15
uses the following observation.

Lemma 2.4.17

(
[
Sto79
, Theorem 3]
)
.

Suppose that
F\colon I\to\operatorname{CH}
is a cofiltered diagram with
{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}F=\emptyset
.
Then there exists
i\in I
such that
F(i)=\emptyset
.

Proof of
Proposition

2.4.15
.

We follow the proof of
[
CS19a
, Proposition 2.15]
.
As every continuous surjection between totally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces is a quotient map, for every topological space
X
,

\mathcal{C}(-,X)\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}\subseteq\operatorname{An}

is a condensed hypersheaf.
Suppose now that
X
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space and
\kappa>|X|
is an uncountable regular cardinal. By
Lemma

2.1.14
, we have to show that for
Y\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
, the canonical map

c\colon{\underset{K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(K,X)\to\mathcal{C}(Y,X)

is a bijection.
Fix
Y\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
and suppose that
(f_{i}\colon K_{i}\to X,t_{i}\colon Y\to K_{i})_{i=1,2}
are continuous maps with
