K_{i}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
such that
f_{1}\circ t_{1}=f_{2}\circ t_{2}
.
Since
Y
is compact,

\tilde{K}\coloneqq t_{1}(Y)\times t_{2}(Y)\subseteq K_{1}\times K_{2}

is a compact subspace, and hence profinite of weight
<\kappa
.
By construction, the two maps

f_{i}\circ\pi_{i}\colon K_{1}\times K_{2}\to X,i=1,2

restrict to the same map
\tilde{K}\to K_{i}\to X
, whence
c
is injective.
We now show surjectivity. Fix
f\colon Y\to X\in\mathcal{C}(Y,X)
.
Below, we will construct
K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}
such that the two maps

Y\times_{K}Y\rightrightarrows Y\xrightarrow{f}X

agree.
If such
K
is found, denote by
\tilde{K}\subseteq K
the image of the map
Y\to K
.
As
Y
is compact,
\tilde{K}
is profinite (as closed subspace of the profinite space
K
). It has
\operatorname{wt}(\tilde{K})\leq\operatorname{wt}(K)<\kappa
.
Since
Y\times_{K}Y\rightrightarrows Y\to\tilde{K}
is a coequalizer diagram,
f
factors over
\tilde{f}\colon\tilde{K}\to X
, which then proves surjectivity of the map
c
.
We now construct a space
K
as above.
The diagonal induces an injective continuous map

l\colon Y\to{\underset{K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}Y\times_{K}Y.

Lemma

2.1.9
implies that
l
is surjective: Suppose
x,y\in Y,x\neq y
.
By
Lemma

2.1.9
, there exists a continuous map
s\colon Y\to\{0,1\}
with
s(x)\neq s(y)
.
Fix
(f\colon Y\to K)\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}
and denote by

\pi_{f}\colon{\underset{K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}Y\times_{K}Y\to Y\times_{K}Y

the projection. Since
f
factors as

Y\xrightarrow{s\times f}\{0,1\}\times K\xrightarrow{\pi_{K}}K,

(x,y)\notin\operatorname{Im}(\pi_{f})
, which shows that
\operatorname{Im}(\pi_{f})=\Delta_{Y}
for all
f\colon Y\to K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}
.
As
{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}
is cofiltered, this shows that
l
is surjective, and hence a homeomorphism as its target and source are compact Hausdorff.
For
K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}
let

d_{K}\colon Y\times_{K}Y\to Y\times Y\to X\times X.

Suppose
x,y\in X
,
x\neq y
. Since
{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}
is cofiltered and

{\underset{K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}d_{K}^{-1}(x,y)={\underset{K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}Y\times_{K}Y\times_{X\times X}\{(x,y)\}\cong\Delta_{Y}\times_{X\times X}\{(x,y)\}=\emptyset,

by
Lemma

2.4.17
there exists
K_{(x,y)}\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}}}_{/Y}}
with
d_{K_{(x,y)}}^{-1}(x,y)=\emptyset
.
As
|X^{2}|<\kappa^{2}=\kappa
,

K_{\infty}\coloneqq\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}(x,y)\in X^{2}\\
x\neq y\end{subarray}}K_{(x,y)}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}

(
Lemma

2.1.6
). Since for all
(x,y)\in X\times X,x\neq y
,

t\colon Y\times_{K_{\infty}}Y\to Y\times Y\xrightarrow{f\times f}X\times X

factors as

Y\times_{K_{\infty}}Y\to Y\times_{K_{(x,y)}}Y\to Y\times Y\to X\times X,

\operatorname{Im}(t)\subseteq\Delta_{X}
, i.e. the two maps
Y\times_{K}Y\rightrightarrows Y\xrightarrow{f}X
agree.
This shows that
c
is an isomorphism, i.e.

\underline{X}\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}

preserves
\kappa
-filtered colimits.
∎

Corollary 2.4.18

(
[
CS19a
, Proposition 1.7]
)
.

Denote by
\operatorname{T1Top}_{k}
the category of
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces with
k
-continuous maps (
Definition

2.1.15
).
The assignment
X\mapsto\underline{X}
defines a fully faithful functor

\displaystyle\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{T1Top}_{k}\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set}).

Proof.

For
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces
X,Y
, choose an uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa>|X|+|Y|
.
Then
\underline{X},\underline{Y}
are
\kappa
-accessible by
Proposition

2.4.15
, whence

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{X},\underline{Y})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{Y}_{\kappa})

by
1.1.11
.
By
Proposition

2.2.7
,

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{Y}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,Y)
.
The same holds for regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa
, which implies that
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,Y)=\mathcal{C}_{k}(X,Y)
. This shows that
\underline{(-)}
is fully faithful.
∎

We will show below (
Proposition

2.4.23
) that
\underline{(-)}
has a partially defined left adjoint.

Lemmas

2.1.14
and
2.4.15
imply the following:

Corollary 2.4.19
.

Suppose
X
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space and
\kappa
is a regular or strong limit cardinal such that one of the following is satisfied:

(i)

\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>|X|
.
10
10

10

The cofinality
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)
of a cardinal
\kappa
is the minimal cardinal
\lambda
with a cofinal functor
\beta\to\kappa
. A map
f\colon\beta\to\kappa
is cofinal if for
\alpha_{0}<\alpha
, there exists
\beta_{0}<\beta
with
\alpha_{0}<f(\beta_{0})
. More concretely,

\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)=\min\{|I|\,|\,\kappa=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_{i},\forall i\in I,|\lambda_{i}|<\kappa\}.

(ii)

X
is compact Hausdorff and
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(X)
.

Then the left adjoint

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
maps
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
to
\underline{X}
.

Proof.

By
2.4.13
and
Lemma

1.2.4
, for a regular and strong limit cardinals
\kappa
, the left adjoint
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
of the restriction is fully faithful.
As
\underline{X}
restricts to
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
, it therefore suffices to show that
\underline{X}
lies in the essential image of
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.
Since
\kappa\geq\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)
,

\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})

factors over left adjoints

\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})

of the restrictions, so it is enough to show that
\underline{X}
lies in the essential image of

\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An}),

i.e. that
\underline{X}
preserves
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)
-filtered colimits (
2.4.12
).
If
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>|X|
, this holds by
Proposition

2.4.15
.
If
X
is compact Hausdorff and
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(X)
, then

\mathcal{C}(-,X)\colon\operatorname{CH}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}

preserves
\kappa
-filtered colimits by
Lemma

2.1.14
.
As
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})\subseteq\operatorname{CH}
is closed under limits, this implies that
\underline{X}\colon\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}
preserves
\kappa
-filtered colimits.
∎

2.4.9
and
2.3.8
imply:

Corollary 2.4.20
.

(i)

For
X\in\operatorname{edCH}
,
\underline{X}
is a compact projective condensed anima.
Every condensed anima is a small colimit of representables
\underline{X},\,X\in\operatorname{edCH}
.

(ii)

If
K
is compact Hausdorff, then
\underline{K}
is compact in
\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.

Proof.

We first show that
\underline{X},X\in\operatorname{edCH}
generate
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
under small colimits.
For a condensed anima
T\in\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
choose a strong limit cardinal
\kappa
with
T\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.
By
2.3.8
, there exists a small diagram
X_{*}\colon I\to\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
such that
\underline{T}_{\kappa}\cong{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{X_{i}}_{\kappa}
.
As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is closed under small colimits (
2.4.13
and
1.2.4
) and maps
\underline{X}_{\kappa}
to
\underline{X}
for
X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
(
2.4.19
), this shows that
\underline{X},X\in\operatorname{edCH}
generates
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
under small colimits.

We now show that for
X
extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff,
\underline{X}
is compact projective in
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
. If
F\colon I\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is a small sifted diagram, choose a regular cardinal
\mu>\operatorname{wt}(X)
such that
F
factors over
\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
. As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is closed under small colimits (
2.4.12
) and
\underline{X}_{\mu}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})
is compact projective (
2.3.8
),
2.4.19
implies that

\displaystyle{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{X},F)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{X}_{\mu},F)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{X}_{\mu},{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{X},{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F),

which shows that
\underline{X}
is projective in
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.

Suppose now that
K
is a compact Hausdorff space and
F\colon I\to\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is a filtered diagram. Choose a regular cardinal
\mu>\operatorname{wt}(K)
such that
F
factors over
\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.
Since
\underline{K}_{\mu}\in\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})
is compact (
2.3.8
),

\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})

is closed under small colimits (
2.4.12
), and

\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})\cap\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})=\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})\text{ (\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{truncationbigtopos})},

it follows from
2.4.19
that

\displaystyle{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{K},F)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{K}_{\mu},F)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{K}_{\mu},{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{K},{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F),

which proves that
\underline{K}
is compact in
\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
∎

Definition 2.4.21
.

(i)

A condensed set
X
is
quasi-compact
if for every effective epimorphism
\sqcup_{i\in I}U_{i}\to P\in\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
, there exists a finite subset
F\subseteq I
such that
\sqcup_{i\in F}U_{i}\to P
is an effective epimorphism.

(ii)

A condensed set
X
is
\operatorname{T1}
if for all
*\to X
and
\underline{T}\to X\in{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})}_{/X}}
, the pullback
P\coloneqq*\times_{X}\underline{T}
is a quasi-compact condensed set.

(iii)

Denote by
\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
the full subcategory on
\operatorname{T1}
condensed sets.

2.4.20
implies:

Corollary 2.4.22
.

For a compact Hausdorff space
K
,
\underline{K}
is a quasi-compact condensed set.

Proof.

Suppose that
K
is a compact Hausdorff space and
\{X_{i}\to\underline{K}\}_{i\in I}
is a small collection of maps so that
\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\to\underline{K}
is an effective epimorphism.
Choose a regular cardinal
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(K)
such that
X_{i}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
for all
i\in I
.
By
2.4.19
,
\underline{K}=\underline{K}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.
As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is closed under small colimits and finite limits (
2.4.12
),
\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\to K
is an effective epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
, i.e.
\sqcup_{i\in I}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i}\to\underline{K}
is an epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
. By effectivity of epimorphisms and universality of colimits in the 1-topos
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
, this means that

\underline{K}=\underline{K}_{\kappa}\cong\operatorname{Coeq}(\sqcup_{i,j\in I}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i}\times_{\underline{K}}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{j}\rightrightarrows\sqcup_{i\in I}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i}).

The right-hand side is equivalent to

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Coeq}(\sqcup_{i,j\in F}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i}\times_{\underline{K}}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{j}\rightrightarrows\sqcup_{i\in F}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i}).

Hence by compactness of
\underline{K}=\underline{K}_{\kappa}
in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
(
2.3.8
), there exists
F\subseteq I
finite so that
\operatorname{id}_{\underline{K}_{\kappa}}
factors over

\operatorname{Coeq}(\sqcup_{i,j\in F}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i}\times_{K}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{j}\rightrightarrows\sqcup_{i\in I}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i})\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}.

This implies that
\sqcup_{i\in F}\tau_{\leq 0}X_{i}\to\underline{K}
is an epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
, i.e.
\sqcup_{i\in F}X_{i}\to\underline{K}_{\kappa}
is an effective epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
. As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
preserves finite limits and small colimits, it preserves effective epimorphisms, which proves that
\underline{K}
is quasi-compact.
∎

Proposition 2.4.23

(
[
CS19a
, Proposition 1.7, Proposition 2.15]
)
.

The functor

\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{T1Top}_{k}\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})

factors over
\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
.
The induced functor

\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{T1Top}_{k}\to\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})

admits a left adjoint which sends a
\operatorname{T1}
condensed set
X
to
X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}\coloneqq{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\underline{K}\to X\\
K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}K
. This is a compactly generated
\operatorname{T1}
topological space with set of points
X(*)
.

Proof.

Suppose
X
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space.
By fully faithfulness of
\underline{(-)}
, an element of
{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/\underline{X}}}
consists of a
\kappa
-light profinite set
T
and a
k
-continuous and hence continuous map
T\to X
. As
X
is
\operatorname{T1}
, the pullback
T\times_{X}*
in topological spaces is a closed subspace of
T
and in particular compact Hausdorff.
Since for all
K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{T\times_{X}*}(K)=\mathcal{C}(K,T\times_{X}*)\cong\mathcal{C}(K,T)\times_{\mathcal{C}(K,X)}\mathcal{C}(K,*)\cong(\underline{T}\times_{\underline{X}}*)(K),

\underline{T\times_{X}*}\cong\underline{T}\times_{\underline{X}}*.

By
2.4.22
,
\underline{T\times_{X}*}
is quasi-compact, which shows that
\underline{X}
is
\operatorname{T1}
.

We now show that
\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})\ni X\mapsto X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}
is well-defined. Suppose
X\in\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
and choose a regular cardinal such that
X
is
\kappa
-accessible, i.e.
X\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
. As
X
is left Kan extended from

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}},

the colimit

X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}={\underset{K\in{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})}_{/X}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}K={\underset{K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}K=X(*)_{\kappa}

exists. It is
\kappa
-compactly generated and the underlying set of points is
X(*)
by
Proposition

2.2.7
.
We now want to show that
X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}
is
\operatorname{T1}
.
As
X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}
is compactly generated, by
Lemma

2.1.12
it suffices to show that for all
x\in X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}
and all
K\in{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}
,
K\times_{X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}}\{x\}\subseteq K
is a closed subspace, i.e.
K\times_{X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}}\{x\}
is compact.
Fix
K\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
with a map
\underline{K}\to X
.
As

\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Set},\,F\mapsto F(*)

preserves limits, the canonical map

(\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\})(*)_{\operatorname{top}}\to K\times_{X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}}\{x\}

is a continuous bijection, hence it is enough to show that
(\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\})(*)_{\operatorname{top}}
is compact.
As
\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
,

q\colon\sqcup_{Y\in{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}_{/\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\}}}}\underline{Y}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\}

is an effective epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
and hence in
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
by
2.4.12
.
Since
X
is
\operatorname{T1}
,
\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\}
is quasi-compact, i.e. there exists a finite collection of
\kappa
-light profinite sets
(Y_{i})_{i=1}^{n}
with an effective epimorphism
\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}\underline{Y_{i}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\}
.
By
2.4.12
, this is also an effective epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
, i.e.

\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\}=\operatorname{Coeq}(\sqcup_{i,j=1}^{n}\underline{Y_{i}}_{\kappa}\times_{\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\}}\underline{Y_{j}}_{\kappa}\rightrightarrows\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}\underline{Y_{i}}_{\kappa})

by effectivity of epimorphisms and universality of colimits in the 1-topos
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
.
As
(-)(*)_{\kappa}
is a left adjoint, this implies that

\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}Y_{i}=(\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}\underline{Y_{i}}_{\kappa})(*)_{\kappa}\to(\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\})(*)_{\kappa}

is a continuous surjection, and in particular,
(\underline{K}\times_{X}\{x\})(*)_{\kappa}
is compact, which proves that
X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}
is
\operatorname{T1}
.
It follows from
Proposition

2.2.7
that
X\mapsto X(*)_{\operatorname{top}}
it is left adjoint to
\underline{(-)}
.
∎

2.3.7
implies the following which we will use in the proofs of
Lemmas

2.8.59
and
1.5.17
.

Corollary 2.4.24
.

For a Hausdorff space
X
,

\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\to X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}

where the colimit in the middle is over the category
{{\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}}_{/X}}
of (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff spaces with a continuous map to
X
, and the colimit on the right runs over all (
\kappa
-light) compact subspaces of
X
.

Proof.

By
2.3.7
and
2.2.7
,

\underline{X}_{\kappa}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\underline{K}_{\kappa}\to X\\
K\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}_{\kappa}\cong{{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\to X\\
K\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}}\underline{K}_{\kappa}.

The image of a continuous map
f\colon K\to X
map is a compact subspace of
X
. As
X
is Hausdorff,
\operatorname{Im}(f)
is compact Hausdorff, whence
K\to\operatorname{Im}(f)
is a quotient map and in particular,

\operatorname{wt}(\operatorname{Im}(f))\leq\operatorname{wt}(K)

by
Lemma

2.1.7
.
This shows that the
\kappa
-light compact subspaces of
X
are cofinal in
{{\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}}_{/X}}
and hence

\underline{X}_{\kappa}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}_{\kappa}

for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
.
Choose a regular cardinal
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(X)+|X|
.
As

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})

is closed under small colimits,
2.4.19
and the above imply that

\underline{X}={\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}.

By
Lemma

2.1.6
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}={\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\operatorname{CH}{}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}.

As the compact subspaces of
X
are cofinal in compact spaces with a continuous map to
X
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\operatorname{CH}{}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}{K}\to X\\
K\operatorname{CH}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}.\qed

We will need the following observation to prove
2.6.14
, which enters our discussion of solid modules.

Lemma 2.4.25
.

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
is Postnikov complete, i.e.
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})\cong{\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})\right)
.

Proof.

We first show that for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
is a replete topos (
[
BS13
, Definition 3.1.1]
), i.e. that the following holds: If
F\colon\mathbb{N}^{\geq}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
is a diagram such that for all
n\leq m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
F_{m}\to F_{n}
is an epimorphism, then the projection
\pi_{n}\colon{\underset{m}{\operatorname{lim}}}F_{m}\to F_{n}
is an epimorphism for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
Fix
X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
x\in F_{n}(X)
. We want to construct a sequence of quotient maps of profinite sets
(q_{k}\colon X_{k+1}\to X_{k}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa})_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}
and elements
(x_{k}\in F_{k+n}(X_{k}))_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}
such that
X_{0}=X,x_{0}=x
and for all
k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

(F_{k+1+n}(X_{k+1})\to F_{k+n}(X_{k+1})\to F_{k+n}(X_{k}))(x_{k+1})=(F_{k+n}(q_{k+1}))(x_{k}).

Suppose that we have constructed a finite such sequence
X_{k}\to X_{k-1}\to\ldots\to X
and
(x_{k},\ldots,x_{1},x)
.
By surjectivity of
F_{n+k+1}\to F_{n+k}
, there exists a cover

\{X^{i}\to X_{k}\}_{i\in I}
such that the image of
x_{k}
under
F_{n+k}(X)\hookrightarrow\prod_{I}F_{n+k}(X^{i})
lies in the image of
\prod_{I}F_{n+k+1}(X^{i})\to\prod_{I}F_{n+k}(X^{i})
.
Since the condensed topology is finitary, we can assume that
I
is finite and since
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
has finite coproducts and condensed sets send finite coproducts to products, we can reduce to the case that
I
consists of a single element
X_{k+1}\coloneqq\sqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}
. Denote by
q_{k+1}\colon X_{k+1}\to X_{k}
the induced map and choose
x_{k+1}\in F_{n+k+1}(X_{k+1})
with

(F_{n+k+1}(X_{k+1})\to F_{n+k}(X_{k+1}))(x_{k+1})=(F_{n+k}(q_{k+1}))(x_{k}).

By repeating this process we obtain a sequence with the claimed properties.
Let

X_{\infty}\coloneqq{\underset{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}.

As
\kappa
-small filtered limit of
\kappa
-light profinite sets,
X_{\infty}
is
\kappa
-light profinite.
For
k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
the projection
p_{k}\colon X_{\infty}\to X_{k}
is surjective since all transition maps are surjective.
By construction,

((F_{k+n}(p_{k}))(x_{k}))_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\in{\underset{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}F_{k+n}(X_{\infty})\subseteq\prod_{k}F_{k}(X_{\infty}).

This shows that

(F_{n}(q_{0}))(x)
lies in the image of the projection
{\underset{m}{\operatorname{lim}}}F_{m}(X_{\infty})\to F_{n}(X_{\infty})
, which proves that
{\underset{m}{\operatorname{lim}}}F_{m}\to F_{n}
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets, i.e.
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
is replete.

It now follows from
[
MR24
, Theorem A]
that the associated hypercomplete topos
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
is Postnikov complete.
As the large poset of small regular cardinals
\Lambda^{r}
is
\aleph_{1}
-filtered and for
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}_{(\operatorname{An})}\cong{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda^{r}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\text{ (\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{truncationbigtopos})},

{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda^{r}}{\operatorname{colim}}}{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})_{\leq n})\cong{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})_{\leq n},

see e.g.
[
Man22
, Corollary A.2.11]
in the large universe. Hence by the above,

\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})\cong{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n}\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An}).\qed

Notation 2.4.26
.

We will in the sequel prove results about condensed and
\kappa
-condensed categories in parallel and use
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathcal{C})
as a placeholder for the category of condensed (or
\kappa
-condensed) objects in a presentable category
\mathcal{C}
.

Lemma

2.2.6
implies:

Corollary 2.4.27
.

The global sections functor stabilizes to a
t
-exact, colimits preserving functor

\Gamma^{(\kappa)}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Sp}.

Proof.

By
Lemma

2.2.6
,
\Gamma^{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{An}
is a left adjoint for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
. Hence its stabilization
\Gamma^{k}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is a left adjoint and
t
-exact by
1.3.4
and
1.3.16
.
As for all regular cardinals
\kappa
,
i_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
is fully faithful,

\Gamma^{\kappa}=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}(*,-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})}(*,i_{\kappa}-)\cong\Gamma\circ i_{\kappa},

where
\Gamma\colon\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{An}
is the global sections functor for
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.
It now follows from
2.4.12
,
2.4.13
and
1.3.12
that

\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Sp}

is
t
-exact and preserves small colimits as well.
∎

2.5
Condensed and sheaf cohomology

In this section, we compare condensed and sheaf cohomology.
[
CS19a
]
constructed a comparison map
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{X},\underline{-})
from sheaf to condensed cohomology for compact Hausdorff spaces
X
. We apply the identification of
\kappa
-condensed animae with hypersheaves on the category of all
\kappa
-small topological spaces from
Section

2.3
to extend this comparison map to arbitrary topological spaces and then use descent of sheaf and condensed cohomology along
local section covers
to generalize comparison results from
[
CS19a
]
.

Definition 2.5.1
.

If
X
is a topological space, denote by
\operatorname{Op}(X)
the poset of open subsets of
X
, ordered by inclusion, and equip it with the Zariski topology, where a sieve
\{U_{i}\to U\}_{i\in I}\subseteq{{\operatorname{Op}(X)}_{/U}}
is a covering if and only if
U=\cup_{i\in I}U_{i}
.
Denote by
\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)
the topos of
\operatorname{An}
-valued Zariski sheaves on
\operatorname{Op}(X)
.
Sheaf cohomology of
X
is defined as

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,-)\coloneqq\mathbb{H}_{{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)}(X,-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\operatorname{Shv}}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X))\to\operatorname{Sp}.

Remark 2.5.2
.

By
Lemma

1.4.32
/
[
Lur18a
, Theorem 2.1.2.3]
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X,\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X))})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X))})

is equivalent to the category of hypercomplete
H\mathbb{Z}
-modules in
\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X))
which is a full subcategory of
\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X))})
.
In particular, the above definition of sheaf cohomology recovers more classical notions of sheaf cohomology (after taking homotopy groups).

Definition 2.5.3
.

We denote by

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,-)\coloneqq\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Sp}

the cohomology functor of
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
, and by

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,-)\coloneqq\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})

the internal cohomology, cf.
Definition

1.5.1
.

1.5.9
and
2.4.13
imply:

Corollary 2.5.4
.

For all strong limit/regular cardinals
\kappa
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(-,-)|_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})}\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(-,-).

Corollary 2.5.5
.

Suppose
X
is a T1 topological space.
For all strong limit/regular cardinals
\kappa
with
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>|X|
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},-)|_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})}\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},-).

In particular, if
M
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological abelian group, for all strong limit/regular cardinals
\kappa
with
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>|X|,|M|
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},\underline{M})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

Proof.

This follows from
2.5.4
and
2.4.19
.
∎

We now describe a comparison map from sheaf to condensed cohomology.

Construction 2.5.6
.

Suppose
X
is a topological space and
\lambda\geq\max\{\kappa,|X|\}
is an uncountable cardinal.
Denote by
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
the category of
\lambda
-small topological spaces and continuous maps.
By
[
Eng89
, Theorem 3.1.21]
,

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\lambda}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
, whence the
\kappa
-condensed topology
\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}
(
Definition

2.3.1
) defines a coverage on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
by
Proposition

2.3.2
.

Equip
{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
with the Grothendieck topology pulled back from the
\kappa
-condensed topology (
Definition

A.4.22
).
By
Lemma

A.4.24
and
Proposition

2.3.2
,

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}})\cong{{\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})}_{/\underline{X}_{\kappa}}}\cong{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}_{/\underline{X}_{\kappa}}}.

The inclusion
\operatorname{Op}(X)\to{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
preserves finite limits and is continuous and therefore defines a morphism of sites

i\colon(\operatorname{Op}(X),\operatorname{Zar})\to({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}},[\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}]),

cf.
Lemma

A.4.11
.
We obtain geometric morphisms

{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}_{/\underline{X}_{\kappa}}}\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}},\operatorname{An})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}},\operatorname{An})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X),

where the left adjoint pair is hypersheafification and forgetting, and the right adjoint pair is induced by the morphism of sites
i
(
A.4.12
). We denote by

{i}^{X}_{*}\colon{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}_{/\underline{X}_{\kappa}}}\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)\colon{i}^{*}_{X},{i}^{X}_{*}\vdash{i}^{*}_{X}

their composite.
Composition with the forget functor

{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}_{/\underline{X}_{\kappa}}}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An}),

which is left adjoint to
-\times\underline{X}_{\kappa}
, yields an adjoint pair

{i}^{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\colon{i}_{*},\,{i}^{*}\dashv{i}_{*}.

As the left-exact functor
\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)\to{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}_{/\underline{X}_{\kappa}}}
preserves the terminal object
X
,

{i}^{*}\mathcal{C}(-,X)=\underline{X}_{\kappa}.

The adjunction
{i}^{*}\dashv{i}_{*}
therefore induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X,{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},-)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp}),\operatorname{Sp}),

cf.
1.5.8
.
The functor
i_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X))
is left t-exact as stabilization of a right adjoint (
Lemma

1.3.16
), and hence the counit for
\tau_{\geq 0}\vdash(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp}))
yields a natural transformation

\pi_{0}i_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}|_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}\to i_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}|_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}.

This induces a comparison map

(2.5.6.1)

\displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},-)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}),\operatorname{Sp}).

By construction of the equivalence
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})
, for
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
,

{i}_{*}A\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An},U\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A).

This implies that for
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
,

\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab},U\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A).

We will denote this sheaf by
A|_{\operatorname{Op}(X)}\coloneqq\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A
in the sequel.
If
A
is a topological abelian group, then
\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa}=\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,A)
is the sheaf of
\kappa
-continuous functions into
A
(
Proposition

2.3.2
).

As
\mathcal{C}(-,A)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,A)=:A_{\kappa}
is a subsheaf, we obtain a map

(2.5.6.2)

\displaystyle c_{\kappa,A}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A_{\kappa})\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa}).

The above construction also yields a comparison map from sheaf to condensed cohomology for
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces:

Construction 2.5.7
.

Suppose that
X
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space. By
2.5.5
, for regular/strong limit cardinals
\kappa
with
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>|X|
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X},-)\circ(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})\xrightarrow{r^{\kappa}_{\operatorname{Sp}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})).

2.5.6.1
therefore induces a comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}j^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}r^{\kappa}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,j^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}r^{\kappa}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},-).

For
U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)
,
\underline{U}=\underline{U}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
by
Proposition

2.4.15
.
This implies that for
A\in\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
,

A|_{\operatorname{Op}(X)}\coloneqq\pi_{0}j^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}r^{\kappa}_{\operatorname{Sp}}A\in\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X,\operatorname{Ab})

equals

\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab},U\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})}(\underline{U},A).

In particular, if
A
is a Hausdorff topological group, then
\underline{A}|_{\operatorname{Op}(X)}=\mathcal{C}_{k}(-,A)
.

As
\mathcal{C}(-,A)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{k}(-,A)=:A_{k}
is a subsheaf, we obtain a map

(2.5.7.1)

\displaystyle c_{k,A}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A_{\kappa})\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},\underline{A}).

Theorem 2.5.8

(
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2, 3.3]
)
.

Suppose
X
is a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space.

If
A
is a product of a discrete abelian group and a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space, then

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{X}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})

via the comparison map described above.

Proof.

This is an immediate consequence of
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2, 3.3]
, we recall their proof and spell this out in
Section

A.6
.
∎

Remark 2.5.9
.

In general, condensed and sheaf cohomology are not isomorphic:
If
X
is a profinite topological space, for all
\mathcal{F}\in\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X,\operatorname{Ab})
sheaves of abelian groups on
X
,

H^{p}_{\operatorname{\operatorname{sheaf}}}(X,\mathcal{F})=0\text{ for }p>0,

see e.g.
[
Sta22
,
Tag 0A3F
]
.
In contrast, if
X
is profinite and
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}]
is not a projective condensed abelian group, e.g. if
X=Y^{2}
for a profinite but not discrete space
Y
, see
[
CS19
, Proposition 4.8]
, then there exists a condensed abelian group
M\in\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
such that
\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}],M)\neq 0
.

We now want to generalize
2.5.8
.

Notation 2.5.10
.

(i)

Suppose
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is a
\kappa
-condensed abelian group.
We say that a topological space
X
is
\kappa
-
A
-
exact
if the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A|_{\operatorname{Op}(X)})\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)

is an isomorphism.

(ii)

Suppose
A\in\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
. A
\operatorname{T1}
topological space
X
is
A
-
exact
if the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A|_{\operatorname{Op}(X)})\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},A)

is an isomorphism.

(iii)

A
local section cover
is a collection of continuous maps
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
such that the map
p\colon\bigsqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\to X
admits local sections, i.e. there exists an open cover
X=\bigcup_{j}U_{j}
and continuous maps
s_{j}\colon U_{j}\to\bigsqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}
such that
p\circ s_{j}\colon U_{j}\hookrightarrow X
is the inclusion for all
j\in J
.

(iv)

For
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
, a local section cover
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
of a topological space is
\kappa
-
A
-
exact
if for all
(i_{1},\ldots,i_{n})\in I^{n}
,
n\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
,

X_{i_{1}}\times_{X}\times\ldots\times_{X}X_{i_{n}}
is
\kappa
-
A
-exact.

(v)

For
A\in\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
, a local section cover
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
of
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces is
A
-
exact
if for all
(i_{1},\ldots,i_{n})\in I^{n}
,
n\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
,

X_{i_{1}}\times_{X}\times\ldots\times_{X}X_{i_{n}}
is
A
-exact.

Our next goal is to prove the following:

Proposition 2.5.11
.

(i)

For a
\kappa
-condensed abelian group
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
, a topological space is
\kappa
-
A
-exact if and only if it admits a
\kappa
-
A
-exact local section cover.

(ii)

For a condensed abelian group
A
, a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space is
A
-exact if and only if it admits an
A
-exact local section cover by
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces.

The only-if statement is trivial:
If
X
is (
\kappa
-)
A
-exact, then
\{id_{X}\colon X\to X\}
is an
A
-exact local section cover.
To prove the converse, we use the
gros topos
to interpolate between
\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)
and
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
, the proof will be completed on page
2.5
.

Definition 2.5.12
.

Fix an uncountable cardinal
\lambda
and denote
by
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
the category of
\lambda
-small topological spaces.
The local section covers constitute a coverage on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
(
Lemma

A.4.21
).
Denote by
(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},LS)
the associated site.
The corresponding topos
\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}\coloneqq{\operatorname{Shv}}_{LS}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})
is called the
gros topos
of (
\lambda
-small) topological spaces.

Remark 2.5.13
.

The local section topology is generated by open covers which form a coverage on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
.
The local section topology is subcanonical, i.e. for all
x\in\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
,
h_{x}\coloneqq\mathcal{C}(-,x)\colon\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Set}
is an
LS
-sheaf.

The category of topological spaces is not accessible. For example, the Sierpińsky space is not
\kappa
-compact for any regular cardinal
\kappa
, see e.g.
[
Hov99
, p. 49]
. We can therefore not apply the formalism from
Section

1.1
to study sheaves on the large category
\operatorname{Top}
.

Suppose
\lambda\geq\kappa
are uncountable cardinals.
For a
\lambda
-small topological space
X\in\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
equip
{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
with the topology pulled back from the local section topology (
Definition

A.4.22
). Then
{\operatorname{Shv}}_{LS}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}})\cong{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}_{/{h_{X}}}}
by
Lemma

A.4.24
.
The inclusion

t_{X}\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)\to{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}

obviously defines a continuous functor
(\operatorname{Op}(X),\operatorname{Zar})\to({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}},LS)
.
Since
\operatorname{Op}(X)
has finite limits and
t_{X}
preserves finite limits,
t_{X}
is a morphism of sites by
Lemma

A.4.11
.
Since the local section topology is coarser than the
\kappa
-condensed topology (
Lemma

A.4.21
), the identity defines morphisms of sites

(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},LS)\to(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},[\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}]).

({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}},LS)\to({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}},[\tau_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}]).

This yields a commutative diagram of left adjoint functors
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}_{/{h_{X}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}}_{/\underline{X}_{\kappa}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An}),}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{t}^{*}_{X}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{t}^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{j}^{*}_{X}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{j}^{*}}

where the horizontal arrows are induced by the corresponding morphisms of sites (
A.4.12
) and condensed hypersheafification, and the vertical arrows are the forget functors, which are left adjoint to
h_{X}\times-
and
\underline{X}_{\kappa}\times-
, respectively.
The composite
\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
is the functor
{i}^{*}
from above.

Lemma 2.5.14
.

For a
\lambda
-small topological space
X\in\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
,

{t}^{*}(\mathcal{C}(-,X))=h_{X}
and
{j}^{*}{{h_{X}}}=\underline{X}_{\kappa}
.

Proof.

This holds since
{t}^{*}_{X}
and
{j}^{*}_{X}
are left-exact and in particular preserve the terminal object.
∎

By
1.5.8
, this implies the following:

Corollary 2.5.15
.

For
X\in\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-),

and in particular,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)=\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-).

Lemma 2.5.16
.

The right adjoint
{t}_{*}\colon\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)
has a further right adjoint.

Proof.

Since
-\times h_{X}\colon\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}\to{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}_{/{h_{X}}}}
has a right adjoint, it suffices to show that the restriction

{t}^{X}_{*}\colon{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}_{/{h_{X}}}}\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)

has a right adjoint. The morphism of sites

(\operatorname{Op}(X),\operatorname{Zar})\to({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}},LS)

has the covering lifting property (
Definition

A.4.14
), hence right Kan extension restricts to a functor

{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(\operatorname{Op}(X))\to\operatorname{Shv}_{LS}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}})\cong{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/{h_{X}}}}

which is right adjoint to
{t}^{X}_{*}
by
Lemma

A.4.16
.
∎

Corollary 2.5.17
.

For
A\in\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})
and a
\lambda
-small topological space
X\in\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A|_{\operatorname{Op}(X)}),

where

A|_{\operatorname{Op}(X)}\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab},U\mapsto A(U)

is the restriction of
A
along
t\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)\to\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
.

Proof.

Lemmas

1.3.16
and
2.5.16
imply that
t_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact, whence
t_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A=\pi_{0}t_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A=A\circ t
. The statement now follows from
2.5.15
.
∎

Corollary 2.5.18
.

Suppose
X
is a
\lambda
-small topological space.

(i)

For
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})_{\leq 0}
, the counit
\pi_{0}A\to A
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},\pi_{0}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},A)

if and only if the counit

\pi_{0}{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A).

(ii)

In particular, for
\kappa\leq\lambda
and
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)

via the comparison map (
2.5.6.1
) if and only if
\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}(h_{X},\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}(h_{X},{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A).

Proof.

The second statement follows from the first since
{t}_{*}\circ{j}_{*}={i}_{*}
.
Since
{t}_{*}
has a left and a right adjoint,
{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact by
Lemma

1.3.16
.
As the adjunction
{t}^{*}\vdash{t}_{*}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}),\operatorname{Sp})

(
Lemma

1.5.7
), this implies the first statement.
∎

The remaining implication of
Proposition

2.5.11
is now straightforward:

Proof of
Proposition

2.5.11
.

Suppose first that
\{X_{i}\to X\}
is a
\kappa
-
A
-exact local section cover and choose a cardinal
\lambda\geq\kappa,|\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\sqcup X|
. By definition of the local section topology,
p\colon\sqcup_{i\in I}h_{X_{i}}\to h_{X}
is an effective epimorphism in
{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}
(
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.3.20]
), and hence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},-)={\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}(\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{\check{C}(p)},-))

by
1.3.38
.
For all
n\in\Delta
,

\check{C}(p)_{n}=\sqcup_{(i_{0},\ldots,i_{n})\in I^{n+1}}X_{i_{0}}\times_{X}\ldots\times_{X}X_{i_{n}}

is (

)-
A
-exact as coproduct of (
\kappa
-)
A
-exact spaces and
\lambda

|\sqcup_{(i_{0},\ldots,i_{n})\in I^{n+1}}X_{i_{0}}\times_{X}\ldots\times_{X}X_{i_{n}}|\leq|\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}|^{n+1}<\lambda^{n+1}=\lambda.

It now follows from

that the map

\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A

induces an isomorphism of cosimplicial spectra

In particular,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A),

whence

is
\kappa

-exact by

.

Suppose now that
A\in\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
and

A
-exact local section cover.
Choose a regular cardinal

such that

and

.
For a
\kappa

is

\kappa
-
A
-exact.
Since for all

,

\check{C}(p)_{n}=\sqcup_{(i_{0},\ldots,i_{n})\in I^{n+1}}X_{i_{0}}\times_{X}\ldots\times_{X}X_{i_{n}}\leq|\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}|^{n+1}<\kappa,

.

Corollary 2.5.19
.

Suppose
X
is a (
\kappa
-light), locally compact Hausdorff space.

(i)

For a topological abelian group
A
,
\mathcal{C}(-,A)=\mathcal{C}_{k}(-,A)=\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,A)\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab}
.

(ii)

If
A
is a product of a discrete abelian group and a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space, then

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{X}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})

via the comparison map (
2.5.6
/
2.5.7
).

Remark 2.5.20
.

The statement for discrete abelian groups (and more generally bounded above spectra) was obtained in
[
Hai22
, Corollary 4.12]
using shape theory.
[
Mai25
, Proposition 1.3.5, Corollary 1.3.6]
identified
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},A)
for a locally contractible or paracompact, compactly generated Hausdorff space

and a discrete abelian group
A
.
We give an alternative proof for locally contractible spaces below, see
Lemma

2.9.4
.

Proof.

Since
X
is locally compact and
\kappa
-light, every point of
x
has a neighborhood basis by
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff spaces.
This implies that the monomorphisms

\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,A)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{k}(-,A)\subseteq\mathcal{C}(-,A)

are isomorphisms on stalks and hence isomorphisms.
For
x\in X
choose a compact neighborhood
x\in K_{x}\subseteq X
. Then
\{K_{x}\to X\}_{x\in X}
is a local section cover and for
x\in X
,
\operatorname{wt}(K_{x})\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
.
For
(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})\in X^{n}
,
K_{x_{1}}\times_{X}\ldots\times_{X}K_{x_{n}}=\cap_{i=1}^{n}K_{x_{i}}
is compact Hausdorff, whence
\{K_{x}\to X\}_{x\in X}
is (
\kappa
-)
A
-exact for
A
a product of a discrete abelian group and a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space by
2.5.8
.
∎

We will use the following observation to identify sheaf and condensed cohomology of locally contractible spaces with coefficients in discrete abelian groups (
Lemma

2.9.4
):

Lemma 2.5.24
.

Suppose that
X
is a topological space,
\mathcal{B}\subseteq\operatorname{Op}(X)
is a basis for the topology on
X
, i.e. every open subset of
X
is a union of elements in
\mathcal{B}
.

(i)

If
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is such that for all
U\in\mathcal{B}
, the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A)

is an equivalence, then the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)

is an equivalence.

(ii)

If
A
is a topological abelian group such that for all
U\in\mathcal{B}
, the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

is an equivalence, then the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

is an equivalence.

(iii)

If
\phi\colon A\to B\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is such that for all
U\in\mathcal{B}
,

{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\phi)\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}B)

is an equivalence, then

{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\phi)\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},B)

is an equivalence.

Remark 2.5.25
.

By
2.5.4
, the corresponding results for condensed cohomology hold as well (for
\operatorname{T1}
topological spaces).

Proof.

Suppose first that
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is such that for all
U\in\mathcal{B}
, the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A)

is an equivalence, then the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)

is an equivalence.
We claim that
\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A
is an equivalence.
As right adjoint of a geometric morphism,
{i}_{*}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\to\operatorname{Shv}(X)
preserves hypercomplete objects, i.e. factors over
\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}}(X)
.
This implies that
{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
factors over a morphism
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}}(X))\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}(X))
.
It therefore suffices to show that
\epsilon\colon\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A
is an isomorphism on stalks (cf.
A.6.5
). By our assumption,

\eta(U)\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)=\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A)

is an equivalence for all
U\in\mathcal{B}
.
As
\mathcal{B}
forms a basis of the topology, for
x\in X
,
\{B\in\mathcal{B}\,|\,x\in B\}
is cofinal in the open neighbourhoods of
x
.
It now follows that
\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A
is an isomorphism on stalks and hence an isomorphism.
In particular,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A),

whence

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

via the comparison map.

The same argument shows that if
A
is a topological abelian group such that for all
U\in\mathcal{B}
, the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A)

is an equivalence, then
A\to\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A
is an equivalence on stalks and hence an equivalence and in particular,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa}),

i.e.

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

via the comparison map.

The same argument also shows that if
\phi\colon A\to B\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is such that for all
U\in\mathcal{B}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},B)

is an equivalence, then
{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\phi)\colon{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\to{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(B)
is an equivalence on stalks and hence an equivalence.
As
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)
, this implies that

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{Y}_{\kappa},B)

is an equivalence.
∎

We now deduce from
2.5.8
that internal condensed cohomology of a compact Hausdorff space with discrete coefficients has a trivial condensed structure (
2.5.27
). This will be central for the proof of
Lemma

2.8.50
.

Lemma 2.5.26
.

Suppose
X
is (
\kappa
-light) profinite set.
For all discrete abelian groups
A
,

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{X}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\cong\underline{\mathcal{C}(X,A)}_{(\kappa)}

is represented by the discrete abelian group
\mathcal{C}(X,A)
and concentrated in degree
0
.

Proof.

By
2.5.5
and
1.1.30
, it suffices to show the
\kappa
-condensed statement.
For
T\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
,

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\kappa\operatorname{-cond}}(T,\underline{A}_{\kappa})\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Sp})

is the small limits-preserving functor

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(T\times-,A)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Sp},

cf.
A.3.5
.
By
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2]
/
A.6.4
, for
X,S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa}\times\underline{S}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X\times S,A)\cong\mathcal{C}(X\times S,A)

is concentrated in degree
0
.
This shows that for
X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\kappa\operatorname{-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A)\cong\underline{\mathcal{C}(X,A)}_{\kappa},

where
\mathcal{C}(X,A)
is endowed with the compact open topology which is discrete since
X
is compact Hausdorff and
A
is discrete.
∎

Denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor.

Corollary 2.5.27
.

Suppose that
X
is a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space.
For all discrete abelian groups
A
, the counit

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(X,\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\to\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{X}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})

is an equivalence.

Proof.

Choose a quotient map
p\colon P\to X
from a (
\kappa
-light) profinite set
P
.
This exists by
Lemma

2.1.12
.
Then
\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}\cong{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{\check{C}(p)}_{(\kappa)}
(
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.3.20]
), and hence

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{\check{C}({p})}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)

and

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{X}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{\check{C}({p})}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)

by
1.3.38
and
1.5.14
.
By
1.5.15
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{X}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)\cong c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left({\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{\check{C}({p})}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{\check{C}({p})}_{(\kappa)},A)\right).

As the Čech nerve
\check{C}(p)
consists of (
\kappa
-light) profinite spaces, and
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact (
Lemma

1.3.16
),

Lemma

2.5.26
implies that for all discrete abelian groups
A
, the counit for
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}
induces an equivalence of cosimplicial spectra

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{\check{C}({p})}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)\cong\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{\check{C}({p})}_{(\kappa)},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)}).\qed

Remark 2.5.28
.

Internal condensed cohomology has a non-constant condensed structure in many cases: For a topological space
X
and a topological abelian group
A
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{0}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})
is the (
\kappa
-)condensed abelian group represented by the discrete abelian group
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{0}(X,A)=\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,A)
.
On the other hand,
\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\kappa\operatorname{-cond}}^{0}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})
is represented by the topological abelian group
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(X,A)
with compact open topology.
For example, if
X
is an infinite set and
A
is a compact abelian group, then

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\kappa\operatorname{-cond}}^{0}(X,A)\cong\prod_{X}\underline{A}_{(\kappa)}

is represented by the compact topological group
\prod_{X}A
, whereas
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{0}(X,A)
is represented by the discrete abelian group
(\prod_{X}A)^{\delta}
.

2.6
Condensed module categories

In this section, we record basic properties of derived and underived
(\kappa\text{-})
condensed module categories relevant to the discussion of solid modules in
Section

2.8
. Many of the statements below are special cases of the results established in
Section

1.4
, we spell them out here for the convenience of the reader.

Notation 2.6.1
.

Endow
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
with the symmetric monoidal structure arising from the tensor product of abelian groups via
1.1.27
.

For a
(\kappa\text{-})
condensed ring
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, denote by

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})})

the (underived) category of left
{R}
-modules.

Remarks 2.6.2
.

This has the following properties:

(i)

By
1.1.28
, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed.

As
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
has all small limits and colimits (
2.4.12
), this implies that for a (
\kappa
-)condensed ring
{R}
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
has small limits and colimits and the forget functor

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})

reflects small limits and colimits (
Proposition

1.4.1
).

(ii)

Moreover, if
{R}
is commutative, then
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
inherits a closed symmetric monoidal structure such that the free
{R}
-module functor enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor. (
Lemmas

1.4.14
and
1.4.5
).

(iii)

For uncountable cardinals
\kappa\leq\lambda
, the left-exact left adjoints

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})

induce symmetric monoidal left adjoints

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}).

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, these induce left adjoints

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}({R}),

which enhance to symmetric monoidal functors if
{R}
is commutative (
Lemmas

A.2.7
and
1.4.3
).
If
\kappa,\lambda
are regular or strong limit cardinals, then

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}({R})

are fully faithful. (
Lemmas

2.2.9
,
2.4.11
,
2.4.12
and
A.2.8
).
By
Lemmas

1.4.9
and
2.4.9
,

\operatorname{Cond}({R})\cong{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}),

where the colimit is computed in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
and runs over all small regular/strong limit cardinals
\kappa
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

(iv)

For a regular cardinal
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}({R})
is closed under small colimits and
\kappa
-small limits. This follows from
2.4.12
and
1.4.1
.

(v)

For a commutative, (
\kappa
-)condensed ring
{R}
, the tensor product on
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
can be described as follows:
Symmetric monoidality of the free functor

{R}[-]\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})

and cocontinuity of the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
imply that for
\kappa
-condensed
R
-modules
M,N
,
M\otimes_{{R}}N
is the
\kappa
-condensed sheafification of

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab},\,T\mapsto M(T)\otimes_{{R}(T)}N(T)

with the canonical condensed
{R}
-module structure.

If
\mu
is a regular cardinal with

{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})),

for regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
,

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}({R})

is symmetric monoidal with essential image

\operatorname{Cond}({R})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set}),

so we can always compute the tensor product of to condensed
R
-modules in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
for a sufficiently large regular/strong limit cardinal
\kappa
. This implies that for
M,N\in\operatorname{Cond}({R})
,

M\otimes_{{R}}N
is the condensed sheafification (
1.1.23
) of

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab},\,T\mapsto M(T)\otimes_{{R}(T)}N(T),

equipped with the canonical condensed
{R}
-module structure.

(vi)

Denote by
c\colon\operatorname{Ab}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
the constant sheaf functor. If
{R}=c{S}
for some ring
S
, then

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\operatorname{Ab}}))\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})

(
Lemma

1.4.34
). If
S
is commutative, this enhances to a symmetric monoidal equivalence where the right-hand side is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure induced from
\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\operatorname{Ab}})^{\otimes}
via
1.1.27
.

(vii)

The symmetric monoidal structure of
\operatorname{Sp}
induces a symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}{\operatorname{Sp}}
which is compatible with the
t
-structure (
Lemma

1.3.32
), whence
{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})}^{\heartsuit}
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure. The equivalence
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})\cong{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})}^{\heartsuit}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor by
1.3.34
.

Lemma 2.6.3

(
[
CS19a
, Theorem 1.10]
)
.

For a (
\kappa
-)condensed ring
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the category
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is abelian and satisfies Grothendieck’s axioms
AB3
,
AB3^{*}
,
AB4
,
AB5
and
AB6
, to wit:

(i)

All small limits (
AB3
) and small colimits (
AB3^{*}
) exist,

(ii)

Small coproducts (
AB4
) and small filtered colimits (
AB5
) are exact.

(iii)

(
AB6
): For any small index set
I
and
I
-indexed family of small filtered diagrams

(F_{i}\colon J_{i}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}))^{\heartsuit})_{i\in I},

{\underset{(j_{i}\in J_{i})_{i}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\prod_{i\in I}F_{i}(j_{i})\cong\prod_{i\in I}{\underset{J_{i}}{\operatorname{colim}}}F_{i}.

Moreover,
\kappa
-small products are exact in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
.
If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, then small products in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact. Small products in
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
are exact.

Proof.

Since the forget functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
is conservative and creates small limits and colimits, it suffices to prove the statements for
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
. We first do this for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
The category
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\cong\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa},\operatorname{Ab})
has all small limits and colimits, and limits and filtered colimits can be computed pointwise:
For limits this is clear, for filtered colimits this holds by
Lemma

2.4.14
. Since the category of abelian groups
\operatorname{Ab}
satisfies
AB3
,
AB3^{*}
,
AB4
,
AB5
and
AB6
, it follows that
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
does as well.
Next, we show that
\kappa
-small products are exact in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
Suppose that
(X_{i}\to Y_{i})_{i\in I}
is a family of epimorphisms in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
with
|I|<\kappa
.
Fix
T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
(y_{i})_{i\in I}\in\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}(T)
. For all
i\in I
: Since
X_{i}\to Y_{i}
is an epimorphism, there exists a cover

\{q_{j}\colon T_{j}^{i}\to T\}_{j\in J_{i}}
such that

q_{j}^{*}(y_{i})\in\operatorname{Im}(X_{i}(T_{j}^{i})\to Y_{i}(T_{j}^{i}))\text{ for all }j\in J_{i}.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{i}(T)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{j\in J_{i}}X_{i}(T_{j}^{i})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y_{i}(T)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{j\in J_{i}}Y_{i}(T_{j}^{i}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{j}q_{j}^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{j}q_{j}^{*}}

Since the condensed topology is finitary, we can assume that
J_{i}
is finite for all
i\in I
and by taking the coproduct
T_{i}\coloneqq\sqcup_{j\in J_{i}}T_{j_{i}}
that it consists of a single element
T_{i}
.
Let

T^{y}=\{(t_{i})_{i\in I}\in\prod_{i\in I}T_{i}\,|\,q_{i}(t_{i})=q_{k}(t_{k})\,\forall i,k\in I\}\subseteq\prod_{i\in I}T_{i}.

The space
T^{y}
is profinite as closed subspace of the profinite set
\prod_{i\in I}T_{i}
and since
|I|<\kappa
,

\operatorname{wt}(T^{y})\leq\max\{|I|,\operatorname{wt}(T_{i})\}<\kappa.

The induced map
q_{y}\colon T^{y}\to T
is onto as for all
i\in I
,
T_{i}\to T
is onto.
We obtain a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{i\in I}X_{i}(T)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{i\in I}X_{i}(T^{y})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}(T)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}(T^{y}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces q_{y}^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces q_{y}^{*}}

The pullbacks along
q_{y}
factor as

\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}(T)\hookrightarrow\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}(T_{i})\to\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}(T^{y}),

respectively

\prod_{i\in I}X_{i}(T_{i})\hookrightarrow\prod_{i\in i}X_{i}(T_{i})\to\prod_{i\in I}X_{i}(T^{y}),

whence

q_{y}^{*}((y_{i})_{i\in I})\in\operatorname{Im}(\prod_{i\in I}X_{i}(T^{y})\to\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}(T^{y})).

This shows that
\prod_{i\in I}X_{i}\to\prod_{i\in I}Y_{i}
is an epimorphism of condensed abelian groups, which proves that
\kappa
-small products are exact.

2.3.7
implies that if
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, then

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\cong\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An}))\cong\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa},\operatorname{Ab}).

As finite finite products commute with all limits and colimits in
\operatorname{Ab}
, small limits and colimits in
\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa},\operatorname{Ab})
can be computed pointwise, which implies that arbitrary products are exact in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
.

For every uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under
\kappa
-small limits by
2.4.12
.
As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
is also closed under small colimits and every small diagram
I\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
factors over
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
for some uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa
, it follows from the above that products in
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact and that
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
satisfies
AB3
,
AB3^{*}
,
AB4
,
AB5
and
AB6
.
∎

Notation 2.6.4
.

For a
(\kappa\text{-})
condensed ring
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, denote by

{R}[-]\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})

the left adjoint of the forget functor.

2.4.20
,
2.3.8
and
2.3.9
imply:

Corollary 2.6.5
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a
(\kappa)
-condensed ring.

(i)

For
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}
,
{R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]
is compact in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
.

(ii)

For
X\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
,
{R}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]
is compact projective in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
.

(iii)

If
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, then
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
has enough projectives.

(iv)

For every condensed
{R}
-module
M
, there exists a small family
(X_{i})_{i\in I}
of extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces with a quotient map
\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{X_{i}}]\to M
. In particular,
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
has enough projectives.

Proof.

As the forget functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set})
commutes with filtered colimits (
2.6.2
and
2.4.14
), its left adjoint
{R}[-]
preserves compact objects.
In particular, for a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space
K
,
{R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]
is compact in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
by
2.4.20
/
2.3.8
.

Next, we show that for a (
\kappa
-light) extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space
X
,
{R}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]
is projective in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
.
For a
\kappa
-light extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space
X
,

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})}(R[\underline{X}_{\kappa}],-)

factors as

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\xrightarrow{f}\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})\xrightarrow{r^{*}}\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma}(\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa},\operatorname{Ab})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{X}}\operatorname{Ab},

where
r^{*}
is the restriction along
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.
2.3.7
implies that
r^{*}
has a right adjoint given by right Kan extension, whence
r^{*}
preserves colimits.
As
f
and
\operatorname{ev}_{X}
are exact, it follows that
{R}[\underline{X}_{\kappa}]
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
.
Suppose now that
X
is extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff and
0\to A\to B\to C\to 0
is a short exact sequence of condensed
{R}
-modules. Choose a regular cardinal
\kappa
such that
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,
A,B,C\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
and
\operatorname{wt}(X)<\kappa
.
Denote by
r^{\kappa}
the right adjoint of
i_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}({R})
. As
i_{\kappa}
is fully faithful and exact,

0\to r^{\kappa}A\to r^{\kappa}B\to r^{\kappa}C\to 0

is exact.
By
2.4.19
,
i_{\kappa}{R}[\underline{X}_{\kappa}]={R}[\underline{X}]
. It now follows from the above that

0\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}({R})}({R}[\underline{X}],A)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}({R})}({R}[\underline{X}],B)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}({R})}({R}[\underline{X}],C)\to 0

is exact, which shows that
R[\underline{X}]
is projective.

Suppose now that
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal. As the forget functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})
is faithful,
2.3.8
implies that for every
\kappa
-condensed
{R}
-module
M
, the canonical map

\oplus_{S\in{\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}}{/M}}{R}[\underline{X}_{\kappa}]\to M

is an epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
, where we consider
M
as a
\kappa
-condensed set in the indexing category. As
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
is small and for all
