S\in\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}
,
M(S)
is small,
\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa/M}
is small.
This shows in particular that
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
has enough projectives for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
.

Suppose now that
M\in\operatorname{Cond}({R})
and choose a strong limit cardinal
\kappa
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
M\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}({R})
. As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}({R})
is a left adjoint, it follows from the above and
2.4.19
that
\oplus_{S\in{\operatorname{edCH}_{\kappa}}{/M}}{R}[\underline{X}]\to M
is an epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
. In particular,
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
has enough projectives.
∎

Remarks 2.6.6
.

1.

As the forget functor
\operatorname{Cond}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})
is conservative, for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,
\oplus_{X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}{R}[\underline{X}_{\kappa}]
is a generator for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
.
Together with
Lemma

2.6.3
, this implies that
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
is Grothendieck abelian for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
.

2.

The category
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
is not Grothendieck abelian (if
{R}\neq 0
) since it does not admit a generator.
The generating family
\{{R}[\underline{X}],X\in\operatorname{edCH}\}
is large and the direct sum

\oplus_{X\in\operatorname{edCH}}{R}[\underline{X}]
does NOT exist in
\operatorname{Cond}({{R}})
(unless
{R}=0
).

3.

The author is unaware whether for arbitrary uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
admits enough projectives, but expects that this is not the case.

4.

If
\mathcal{X}
is a topos, the category
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
of abelian group objects in the underlying 1-topos has enough injectives, cf.
[
Sta22
,
Tag 01DP
]
.
In contrast to that, the category of condensed abelian groups has no non-zero injectives, cf.
[
Sch22
]
.

We now collect some basic properties about derived/stable condensed module categories which follow from our discussion in
Section

1.4
.

Lemma

1.4.32
implies:

Corollary 2.6.7
.

If
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a
(\kappa\text{-})
condensed ring,

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))^{\heartsuit}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))

extends to a
t
-exact equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})}),

where on the right-hand side we consider
{R}
as an algebra in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
via the Eilenberg-Mac Lane functor (
1.3.33
).

This is instructive as by our discussion from
Section

1.4
, the right-hand side has good categorical properties.
In particular, we have shown the following:

Corollary 2.6.8
.

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the category
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is big presentable and has small limits and colimits.

Proof.

2.6.7
and
Lemma

1.4.9
imply that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is big presentable.
As
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
has small colimits and limits (
2.4.12
) and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
is closed (
Lemma

1.3.28
), (co)completeness follows from
Proposition

1.4.1
and the identification of
2.6.7
.
∎

Corollary 2.6.9
.

Denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))
the functor induced by the constant sheaf functor.

(i)

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp})
,

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})).

(ii)

In particular, for a ring
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab})
,

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathcal{D}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R})).

(iii)

For a commutative ring spectrum
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp})
, the above equivalence enhances to a symmetric monoidal equivalence

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{c_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})),

where the left-hand side is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure induced from
\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Sp}}({{R}})
via
1.1.27
, and the right-hand side with the symmetric monoidal structure provided by
1.4.13
.

Proof.

The first identification is
Lemma

1.4.34
, the second statement follows from the first and
Lemmas

1.4.32
and
2.6.7
, and third identification holds by
1.4.35
.
∎

1.4.6
implies:

Corollary 2.6.10
.

If
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))
is a commutative condensed ring spectrum, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}{(\operatorname{Sp})}})
described in
1.4.13
is closed.

Proof.

For
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
, this is
1.4.6
.
For
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})
, this follows from
[
Lur17
, Theorem 3.4.4.2]
.
∎

Notation 2.6.11
.

For a commutative condensed ring
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, endow
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
with the closed symmetric monoidal structure induced from the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})
from
2.6.10
via the equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})

from
2.6.7
. Denote by
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(-,-)
the internal Hom.
By
Lemma

1.4.38
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})

is enriched in
\mathcal{D}({R}(*))
. We denote by
\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(-,-)
the enriched mapping functor.

Remarks 2.6.12
.

1.

Denote by
c\colon\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
the functor induced by the constant sheaf functor. By
2.6.9
, for a ring
{R}
, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(c{R}))
from above is equivalent to the one induced by the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}({R})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}})
.
In particular, for
M,N\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
,

M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}N
is the (
\kappa
-)condensed sheafification of

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni K\mapsto M(K)\otimes_{\mathcal{D}({R})}N(K).

2.

By
Lemma

1.3.32
, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is compatible with the
t
-structure. The induced symmetric monoidal structure on the heart
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is the one induced by the tensor product of abelian groups, cf.
1.3.34
.

Recall from
2.6.7
that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})
.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.1.9, Corollary 4.5.1.6]
, this implies that for all algebras
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}{\operatorname{Sp}}}).

In particular,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})
inherits a
t
-structure via
1.4.21
.
2.6.7
now implies:

Corollary 2.6.13
.

For
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the inclusion

\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})^{\heartsuit}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})

extends to an equivalence

\mathcal{D}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{R}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}).

Lemma

2.4.25
implies the following:

Corollary 2.6.14
.

If
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\geq 0})
is a connective
(\kappa\text{-})
condensed ring, the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})
from
1.4.21
is left and right complete.

Proof.

[
Lur18a
, Proposition 1.3.2.7]
implies that for all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})

is closed under countable coproducts and that the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})
is right-separated. It follows from
Lemmas

1.3.12
,
2.4.12
and
1.3.12
that this also holds for
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})
.
As the forget functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})

is
t
-exact, conservative and reflects colimits (
Proposition

1.4.1
), it follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.1.19]
that the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})
is right-complete.

To show left-completeness, we proceed as in
[
MR24
, Corollary 3.26]
.
As
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})
has small limits, the functor

{\underset{n\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n}-\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})\to{\underset{n\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})_{\leq n}\right),X\mapsto(\tau_{\leq n}X)

has a right adjoint

{\underset{}{\operatorname{lim}}}\colon{\underset{n\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\left(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})_{\leq n}\right)\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})}),(X_{n})_{n}\mapsto{\underset{n\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{n}

by

[
Lan21
, Proposition 5.1.10]
.
The unit and counit of this adjunction are the canonical maps

\eta\colon X\to{\underset{n\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n}X\text{ and }(\epsilon_{n}\colon(\tau_{\leq n}{\underset{k\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}\to\tau_{\leq n}X_{n}=X_{n}))_{n\in\mathbb{Z}},

respectively.
So it remains to show that these maps are equivalences, then left-completeness follows.
By
1.4.21
and
1.4.1
it suffices to check this for
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
.
By right separatedness of the
t
-structure and
1.3.13
, the functors

\Omega^{\infty-m}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An}),m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}

are jointly conservative.
As
\Omega^{\infty-m}
preserves limits and
\Omega^{\infty-m}\tau_{\leq n}=\tau_{\leq n+m}\Omega^{\infty-m}
,

\Omega^{\infty-m}({\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n}X)\cong({\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}\Omega^{\infty-m}\tau_{\leq n}X)\cong{\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n+m}\Omega^{\infty-m}X\cong{\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n}\Omega^{\infty-m}X.

Since Postnikov towers in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
converge (
Lemma

2.4.25
), this implies that

\Omega^{\infty-m}\eta\colon\Omega^{\infty-m}X\to\Omega^{\infty-m}{\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n}X

is an equivalence for all
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
Suppose now that
(X_{k})_{k}\in{\underset{k\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq k}
. Then

(\Omega^{\infty-m}X_{k-m})_{k}\in{\underset{k\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})_{\leq k}.

As
\lim{}\colon{\underset{k\in\mathbb{Z}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})_{\leq k}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
is an equivalence (
Lemma

2.4.25
), for all
k\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\Omega^{\infty-m}X_{k-m}\cong\tau_{\leq k}{\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}(\Omega^{\infty-m}X_{n-m})\cong\Omega^{\infty-m}\tau_{\leq k-m}{\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{n}.

This shows that
\Omega^{\infty-m}\epsilon
is an equivalence for all
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
∎

2.7
Compact condensed abelian groups

In this section, we collect some compactness properties of condensed abelian groups from
[
CS19a
, Lecture 4]
which we will use in our discussion of solid abelian groups in the next section.
Throughout, we use
2.6.11
.

Lemma 2.7.1
.

Fix
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.

(i)

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal. For a
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff space
S
,

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\kappa\operatorname{-cond}}(\underline{S}_{\kappa},-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})

and

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{S}_{\kappa},-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{Sp}

commute with filtered colimits.

(ii)

For a compact Hausdorff space
S
,

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{S},-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})

and

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{S},-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{Sp}

commute with filtered colimits.

Proof.

It is enough to prove the statement for internal cohomology, then the statement for cohomology follows from
2.4.27
. By
1.3.8
,

\Omega^{\infty-i}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})

preserves filtered colimits for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
. As the functors
\Omega^{\infty-i},i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
are jointly conservative (
[
Lur17
, Remark 1.4.2.25]
),
it suffices to show that

\Omega^{\infty-i}\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{S}_{(\kappa)},-)|_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq n}}\cong\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{S}_{(\kappa)},\Omega^{\infty}\Sigma^{i}-)|_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq n}}

preserves filtered colimits for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
. The equivalence of these functors was explained in
1.3.29
.
By
2.4.12
and
1.3.12
, it suffices to show this for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})
.
As
\Omega^{\infty}\Sigma^{i}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})_{\leq i+n}
preserves filtered colimits and

\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{S}_{\kappa},-)=(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni T\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}(\underline{S}_{\kappa}\times\underline{T}_{\kappa},-))

(
A.3.5
), the statement now follows from
2.4.20
and
2.4.14
.
∎

Corollary 2.7.2
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and
R\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp}))
is a commutative condensed ring spectrum.
For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and
S\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))}({R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],-)\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))

commutes with filtered colimits.

Proof.

Since the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
is compatible with small colimits, the forget functor
f\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
reflects colimits by
Proposition

1.4.1
.
As

f\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))}({R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}],-)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\underline{K}_{(\kappa)},-)\circ f

(both are right adjoint to
{R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]\otimes_{{R}}{R}[-]\cong{R}[-]\circ(\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}\times-)
) and
f
is
t
-exact,

f\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))}({R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}],-)\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})

preserves filtered colimits for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
by

Lemma

2.7.1
, which implies that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))}({R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}],-)\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))_{\leq n}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp}))

does as well.
∎

Some computations using Breen-Deligne resolutions

We end this section with a recollection of computations using Breen-Deligne resolutions from
[
CS19a
, Lecture 4]
.

Corollary 2.7.3
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
For all
S\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}
and
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\leq n}\to\mathcal{D}({R}(*))

commutes with filtered colimits.

Proof.

By
2.4.27
and
Proposition

1.4.1
, the global sections functor

\Gamma_{{R}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R}(*)))

preserves small colimits.
As

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}],-)=\Gamma_{{R}}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}],-),

the statement now follows from
2.7.2
.∎

Together with
Lemma

1.5.18
, this implies:

Corollary 2.7.4
.

Suppose
A
is a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff topological abelian group and
n\in\mathbb{Z}
. The internal Hom (
2.6.11
)

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{(\kappa)},-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))

and the
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
-enriched mapping functor (
2.6.11
)

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{(\kappa)},-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})

commute with filtered colimits.

Proof.

We first prove the
\kappa
-condensed statement. Under the equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}))

provided by
2.6.9
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{(\kappa)},-)=(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni T\mapsto\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],-)),

cf.
A.3.5
. Here
A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}]
denotes the tensor product in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
, which agrees with the tensor product in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
since
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}]
is flat.
It therefore suffices to show prove the statement for
\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{\kappa},-)
, then the statement for
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{\kappa},-)
follows.

Lemma

1.5.18
provides a convergent spectral sequence of functors

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq N}\times\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}),

E_{1}^{p,q}(B,T)=\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\pi_{-q}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{A^{i_{k}}\times T}_{\kappa}],B)\Rightarrow\pi_{-(p+q)}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],B).

As for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
\sqcup_{k=1}^{b_{n}}A^{i_{k},n}\times T\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
,
2.7.3
implies that the
E_{1}
-page preserves filtered colimits in the variable from
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq N}
, hence the limit

\pi_{-i}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq N}\to\operatorname{Ab}

of the spectral sequence commutes with filtered colimits for all
T\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
and all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
As the functors

\pi_{-i}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Ab},i\in\mathbb{Z}

are jointly conservative and commute with filtered colimits, this implies the statement for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.

We now deduce the statement for
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
from this. Fix
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and suppose that

F\colon I\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}

is a small filtered diagram. Choose a regular cardinal
\kappa\geq|A|
such that
F
factors over

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}.

By
1.1.30
, there exists a regular cardinal
\lambda\geq\kappa
such that for all
i\in I
,

\displaystyle\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,F(i))

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,F(i)),

\displaystyle\text{ and }\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F)

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F)

in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under small colimits, it follows from the above that

{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}\,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,F)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,{\underset{I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F).

By
2.4.27
and
Proposition

1.4.1
, the global sections functor
\Gamma\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
preserves colimits.
It now follows that

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,-)|_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}}=\Gamma\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,-)|_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}}

preserves filtered colimits for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
∎

Lemma 2.7.5
.

Suppose
M
is a discrete abelian group.
For
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})=0.

Proof.

As
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})
has small limits and colimits (
2.6.8
),
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(-,\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)})
commutes with small limits in the first variable (
Lemma

A.1.1
).
As the free
\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}
-modules generate
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}))
under small colimits (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.7.3.14]
), it suffices to show that for
T\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}[T],\underline{M}_{\kappa})=0.

For
T\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}[T],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(T,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{\kappa}))

(
Proposition

1.4.1
). It is therefore enough to show that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{\kappa})=0.

By
1.1.30
, it suffices to show this for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
Under the identification

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})),

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})
becomes

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni T\mapsto\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa}),

cf.
A.3.5
.
It therefore suffices to show that
\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})=0
for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.

For a
\kappa
-condensed abelian group
A
denote by
S_{*}(A)\to A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
its Breen-Deligne resolution (
[
CS19a
, Theorem 4.5]
). As filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
),

A\cong S_{*}(A)={\underset{n\to\infty}{\operatorname{colim}}}S_{*}(A)^{\leq n}

is the colimit over its stupid truncations. This implies that for
T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\cong{\underset{n\to\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{*}(A)^{\leq n}\otimes\mathbb{\mathbb{}}Z[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}).

For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, we have cofiber sequences
S_{*}(A)^{\leq n}\to S_{*}(A)^{\leq n+1}\to S_{n+1}(A)[n+1]=\oplus_{k=1}^{b_{n+1}}\mathbb{Z}[A^{i_{k,n+1}}]
.
By
2.5.19
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{n+1}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\cong\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n+1}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(\mathbb{R}^{i_{k,n+1}}\times T,M)

and

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{n+1}(0)\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\cong\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n+1}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(T,M).

By
[
Bre97
, Proposition 11.13]
, sheaf cohomology with constant coefficients is a homotopy invariant, see also
A.5.6
.
This implies that the chain map
\pi_{*}\colon S_{*}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\to S_{*}(0)
induced by
\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\to 0
(
[
CS19a
, Theorem 4.10]
) defines an equivalence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{n+1}(0)\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{n+1}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

It follows inductively that

\pi^{*}\colon\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{*}(0)_{\leq n}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{*}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})_{\leq n}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],M)

is an equivalence for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, and hence

\displaystyle 0

\displaystyle=\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{*}(0)\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(S_{*}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T],\underline{M}_{\kappa}).\qed

Lemma 2.7.6

(
[
CS19a
, Theorem 4.3]
)
.

If
A
is a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff abelian topological group, then

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{(\kappa)},\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)})=0
.

Proof.

By
1.1.30
, it suffices to show this for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
Under the identification

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})),

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))}(A,\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})
becomes

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni T\mapsto\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{\kappa}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}),

cf.
A.3.5
.
By
Lemma

1.5.18
, we have a spectral sequence

E_{1}^{p,q}=\oplus_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\operatorname{Ext}^{q}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{A^{n_{k}}\times T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\Rightarrow\pi_{-(p+q)}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{A}_{\kappa}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}).

By
2.5.19
and
2.5.21
,

E_{1}^{*,q}(T)=\begin{cases}0&q\neq 0\\
\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S_{*}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})&q=0,\end{cases}

where
S_{*}(A)
denotes the Breen-Deligne resolution of
A
.
We are therefore reduced to showing that

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S_{*}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})
is exact.

A.3.5
and
2.2.7
imply that for
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S_{n}(A),\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\cong\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\underline{\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,p}},\mathbb{R})}_{\kappa},

where
\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,p}},\mathbb{R})
is endowed with the compact open topology and
b_{p},i_{k,p}
are the coefficients of the Breen-Deligne resolution.
The sup-norm makes this a Banach space.

Proposition

2.2.7
implies that the differentials
S_{n}(A)\to S_{n-1}(A)
induce
\kappa
-continuous group homomorphisms

\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p+1}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,p+1}},\mathbb{R})\to\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,p}},\mathbb{R}).

As both terms are Banach spaces, these are continuous, i.e. have bounded norm.
This implies that
\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S_{*}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S_{n}(A),\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}])
is represented by the cochain complex of Banach spaces

\ldots\to\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,p}}\times T,\mathbb{R})\xrightarrow{d_{p+1}}\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p+1}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,p+1}}\times T,\mathbb{R})\ldots\to

and the boundary maps have bounded norm.
Choose a chain homotopy
h_{*}\colon S(A)_{*}\to S(A)_{*+1}
in
\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
from the multiplication by
2\colon S(A)_{*}\to S(A)_{*}
to the map
S(2)\colon S(A)_{*}\to S(A)_{*}
induced by multiplication by
2
on
A
. This exists by
[
CS19a
, Proposition 4.17]
.
The induced map

h_{n}^{*}\colon\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n+1}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,n+1}},\mathbb{R})_{\kappa}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S(A)_{n+1},\mathbb{R})\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S(A)_{n},\mathbb{R})=\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n}}\underline{\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,n}},\mathbb{R})}_{\kappa}

corresponds to a
\kappa
-continuous and hence continuous map

\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n+1}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,n+1}},\mathbb{R})\to\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,p}},\mathbb{R}),

which induces a continuous map

h_{n}^{*}(T)\colon\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n+1}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,n+1}}\times T,\mathbb{R})\to\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,n}}\times T,\mathbb{R}).

This is a map of Banach spaces and hence has bounded norm.

Assume that

f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(S_{n}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Z}[T],\mathbb{R})=\prod_{k=1}^{b_{n}}\mathcal{C}(A^{i_{k,n}}\times T,\mathbb{R})

with
d_{n}(f)=0
.
Then
2f=S(2)^{*}f+d_{n-1}(h_{n-1}^{*}f)
, whence

f=\frac{1}{2}(S(2)^{*}f+d_{n-1}(h_{n-1}^{*}f)).

In particular,
S(2)^{*}f\in\ker(d_{n})
.
By iterating this process, we find that

f=\frac{1}{2^{m}}S(2^{m})^{*}f+d_{n-1}(\sum_{k=1}^{m}\frac{1}{2^{k}}(h_{n-1}^{*}S(2^{k-1})^{*}f).

As
||\frac{1}{2^{n}}S(2^{n})^{*}f||\leq\frac{1}{2^{n}}||f||
and
d_{n-1}
is
\mathbb{R}
-linear, it follows that

f=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}}d_{n-1}(\frac{1}{2^{k}}(h_{n-1}^{*}S(2^{k-1})^{*}f)).

As
h_{n-1}^{*}(T)
has bounded norm (see above), for
k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

||h_{n-1}^{*}(T)S(2^{k-1})^{*}f||\leq||h_{n-1}^{*}(T)||||S(2^{k-1})^{*}f||\leq||h_{n-1}^{*}(T)||||f||<\infty,

and hence the limit

\sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\frac{1}{2^{k}}(h_{n-1}^{*}(T)S(2^{k-1})^{*}f)\in\mathcal{C}(\sqcup_{k=1}^{b_{n}}A^{i_{k,n}}\times T,\mathbb{R})

exists.
As
d_{n-1}
is continuous and
\mathbb{R}
-linear, this implies that

d_{n-1}(\sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\frac{1}{2^{k}}(h_{n-1}^{*}S(2^{k-1})^{*}f))=f.\qed

Lemma 2.7.7

(
[
CS19a
, Theorem 4.3]
)
.

Suppose
M
is a discrete abelian group.

(i)

The connecting homomorphism of the exponential sequence

0\to\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{T}^{1}\to 0

is an equivalence

M[-1]\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)}).

(ii)

For a (
\kappa
-small) set
I
, the projections
\prod_{I}\mathbb{T}^{1}\to\mathbb{T}^{1}
induce an isomorphism

\bigoplus_{I}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)}).

Proof.

The first statement holds by
Lemma

2.7.5
.
The first statement implies the second statement fo
I
finite. It remains to show that

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})

is an equivalence.
By
1.1.30
, it suffices to prove this for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
By
A.3.5
, under the identification
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})

is the
\kappa
-condensed sheafification of

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni T\mapsto{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa}),

and

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})

is

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni T\mapsto\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

It therefore suffices to show that for
T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

As filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact, it is enough to show that for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
and
T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\pi_{i}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\to\pi_{i}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})

is an equivalence.

By
Lemma

1.5.18
, we have spectral sequences

\displaystyle E_{1}^{p,q}={\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\pi_{-q}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{i_{n_{k},p}}\times T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})

and

E_{1}^{p,q}=\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\pi_{-q}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{i_{n_{k},b}}\times T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\Rightarrow\pi_{-(p+q)}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})

which converge completely to

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\pi_{-(p+q)}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})

and

\pi_{-(p+q)}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\otimes\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa}),

respectively.

Naturality of these spectral sequences (
Lemma

1.5.18
) implies that the map on limit terms is induced by the canonical map of
E_{1}
-pages

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\pi_{-q}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{i_{n_{k},b}}\times T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\to\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\pi_{-q}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{i_{n_{k},p}}\times T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

By
2.5.8
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\pi_{-q}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{F}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{i_{n_{k},b}}\times T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\cong\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{q}(\prod_{F}\mathbb{T}^{1}\times T,M)

and

\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\pi_{-q}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{i_{n_{k},p}}\times T}_{\kappa}],\underline{M}_{\kappa})\cong\prod_{k=1}^{b_{p}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{q}(\prod_{I}{\mathbb{T}^{1}}\times T,M).

As
\prod_{I,F}\mathbb{S}^{1}\times T
are paracompact and Hausdorff, their sheaf cohomology agrees with their Čech cohomology (see e.g.
[
God73
, Theorem 5.1.10]
), and since
\prod_{I}\mathbb{S}^{1}\times T\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\prod_{F}\mathbb{T}^{1}\times T
is an inverse limit of compact Hausdorff spaces, the canonical map

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq I\\
F\text{ finite}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\check{H}^{*}(\prod_{F}\mathbb{T}^{1}\times T,M)\to\check{H}^{*}(\prod_{I}\mathbb{T}^{1}\times T,M)

on Čech cohomology is an isomorphism, cf.
[
God73
, page 231]
.
∎

Corollary 2.7.8
.

For a (
\kappa
-small) set
I
and a discrete abelian group
M
, the canonical map

\oplus_{I}\underline{M}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})

is an equivalence.

Proof.

As (
\kappa
-small) products in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
), the exponential exact sequence

0\to\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{(\kappa)}\to 0

yields a map of fiber sequences
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\oplus_{I}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\oplus_{I}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\oplus_{I}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})}

By
Lemma

2.7.5
, the two middle terms vanish, and by
Lemma

2.7.7
, the upper horizontal map is an equivalence, whence so is the bottom horizontal map.
∎

2.8
Solid modules

A central feature of the condensed formalism is the existence of an extremely well-behaved notion of (non-archimedean) completeness for condensed abelian groups, called solidity, which we review in this section.
Denote by
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(-,-)
the internal Hom of (
\kappa
-)condensed abelian groups.

Definition 2.8.1

(
[
CS19a
, Def. 5.1]
)
.

For a profinite set
S
let

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare}\coloneqq\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z}),\mathbb{Z}).

The counit for
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]\otimes\dashv\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],-)
evaluates to a map

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]\otimes_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\to\mathbb{Z}

which is adjoint to a map
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare}
.

A (
\kappa
-)condensed abelian group
A
is
solid
if for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
, pullback along the map

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare}

is an isomorphism

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare},A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],A).

Denote by
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
the full subcategories of solid abelian groups. More generally, if
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a discrete condensed ring, denote by
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
the full subcategory on
{R}
-modules whose underlying condensed abelian group is solid.

We will show below (
Lemma

2.8.48
) that if
M
is a
(\operatorname{T1})
topological abelian group such that
\underline{M}_{\kappa}/\underline{M}
is solid, then every null-sequence in
M
is summable, and that locally profinite abelian groups represent solid abelian groups (
2.8.52
).
This justifies to consider solidity as a condensed analogue of (non-archimedean) completeness.

The category of solid modules enjoys excellent formal properties, including the existence of a completion functor and a completed tensor product. We now give an overview of the results we prove in this section.

(i)

\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is an abelian category closed under small limits, small colimits and extensions. (
Lemma

2.8.15
,
2.8.30
)

(ii)

The inclusion
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
has a left adjoint
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
, called solidification (
2.8.16
,
2.8.30
).

(iii)

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare}\cong\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
for a set
I
of cardinality
|I|\leq\operatorname{wt}(S)
(
2.8.16
,
2.8.31
,
Lemma

2.8.2
).

(iv)

For a commutative ring
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the localisation
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is symmetric monoidal, i.e. there exists cocontinuous symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
such that
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor. (
Lemma

2.8.44
)

(v)

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,
{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}{R}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
. In particular,
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
has enough projectives (
2.8.18
and
2.8.45
).
If
{R}
is commutative and
P,Q\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
are projective, so is their solid tensor product
P\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}Q
. (
2.8.46
)

We also discuss derived categories of solid modules. The inclusion
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
extends uniquely to a
t
-exact, small colimits preserving functor

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})).

In many cases, this functor admits a left adjoint, for instance for
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
, (
2.8.33
) as well as for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
(
Lemma

2.8.23
) or
\kappa=\aleph_{1}
(
2.8.61
and
2.8.58
), and for
{R}=\mathbb{Z}
(
2.8.27
).

(vi)

The forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is fully faithful with essential image

\{M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\,|\,H_{i}(M)\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}\text{ for all }i\in\mathbb{Z}\}.

(
2.8.26
and
2.8.37
).

(vii)

The localisation
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is symmetric monoidal, and the induced symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
is closed. (
2.8.40
).

We will prove the above statements in a peculiar order, with later proofs building on earlier results.
As a first step, we apply a theorem of Nöbeling and Specker to compute
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
for (
\kappa
-light) profinite sets
S
(
Lemma

2.8.2
).
Next, we show that
\kappa
-condensed solid abelian groups satisfy a stronger locality condition than the one assumed in their definition (
Proposition

2.8.3
).
This serves as the essential ingredient for the proofs of the above claims.
We will first prove the
\kappa
-condensed statements and then use that
\operatorname{Solid}({R})={\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\\
\kappa\text{ regular }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
(
Lemma

2.8.29
) to deduce the corresponding condensed results.
We then show that if
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
has enough projectives, then the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R}))
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
(
Lemma

2.8.23
,
2.8.33
). This in particular holds for
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
as well as for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
.
Our arguments are minor modifications of the discussion in
[
CS19a
, Lectures 5,6]
who proved the statements for
\operatorname{Solid}
and
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
for strong limit cardinals, and worked with the homotopy category of the derived category. Small modifications are necessary since the proofs of
[
CS19a
, Lectures 5,6]
used that for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
has enough projectives. For light solid abelian groups, the proofs can be simplified significantly, see
[
CS23
, Lectures 5,6]
or
[
Rod24
, section 3]
. The above results rely crucially on the fact that (
\kappa
-light) profinite sets generate
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
under colimits. The availability of a well-behaved theory of (non-archimedean) complete abelian group objects is a key advantage of the condensed
topos
over the gros topos.

In
Section

2.8.1
, we give examples of solid abelian groups and compute the solidification of free condensed abelian groups on compact Hausdorff spaces and CW-complexes (
2.8.51
,
2.8.53
). We will use these computations in
Section

2.9
to obtain further identifications of condensed with sheaf cohomology. Combined with
(v)
, they serve as the essential ingredient for our comparison of solid group cohomology with continuous group cohomology.

In
Section

2.8.2
, we characterize (
\kappa
-)condensed rings for which the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})

factors over an equivalence

(2.8.1.1)

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}).

We call such rings (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat and give many examples (
2.8.58
,
2.8.59
and
2.8.60
).
The identification
2.8.1.1
implies that the following holds:
Suppose that
{R}
is a (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat condensed ring.

(i)

The forget functor

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

has a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
. (
2.8.61
)

(ii)

If
{R}
is commutative, there exists a cocontinuous symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
such that
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor. This symmetric monoidal structure is closed and compatible with the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
(
2.8.65
and
2.8.66
).
The induced monoidal structure on the heart
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is the symmetric monoidal structure from
Lemma

2.8.44
.

(iii)

If
{R}^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\cong{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
, then the functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is fully faithful with essential image

\{M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\,|\,H_{i}(M)\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\,\text{ for all }i\in\mathbb{Z}\}.

(
Lemma

2.8.68
). This in particular holds if
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

We now work towards the proof of the statements listed above.
Recall from
Lemma

2.5.26
, that for a (
\kappa
-light) profinite space
S
,

\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\cong\underline{\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})}_{(\kappa)},

where
\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})
is endowed with the discrete topology.
In particular,

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare}\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})}_{(\kappa)},\mathbb{Z}).

Lemma 2.8.2

(Nöbeling, Specker)
.

For a profinite set
S
, there exists a set
I
of cardinality
|I|\leq\operatorname{wt}(S)
such that
\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})\cong\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}
.
In particular, for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
, there exists a (
\kappa
-small) set
I
such that

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare}\cong\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
.

Proof.

This is an immediate consequence of a theorem of Nöbeling
[
Nöb68
]
generalizing work of Specker, see also
[
CS19a
, Theorem 5.4]
for a proof.
They show that for a profinite set
S
, there exists a set
I
with
\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})=\oplus_{I}\mathbb{Z}
.
If
J
is a set such that
X\hookrightarrow\prod_{J}\{0,1\}
, they choose
I
to consists of a collection of finite products of elements of
J
. In particular,
|I|\leq|\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}J^{n}|\leq\max\{\aleph_{0},|J|\}
.
By
2.1.10
, we can choose
|J|\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
.
In particular, if
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal, for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
there exists a set
I
of cardinality
|I|<\kappa
with
\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})\cong\oplus_{I}\mathbb{Z}
.
∎

Our next goal is to prove the following characterisation of solid abelian groups which will be central for proving the results on solid modules listed above.

Proposition 2.8.3
.

(i)

A condensed abelian group
M\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is solid if and only if for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M)

via the pullback along
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
.

(ii)

For a solid abelian group
M
and
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{\blacksquare},M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit},

and in particular,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},M)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})^{\heartsuit}.

(iii)

The category
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under filtered colimits.

This was shown for strong limit cardinals in
[
CS19a
, Lectures 5,6]
and for
\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{light}}(\operatorname{Ab})
in
[
CS23
, Lectures 5,6]
, see also
[
Rod24
]
.
Our proof of
Proposition

2.8.3
is a minor modification of the argument from
[
CS19a
, p. 38ff]
and will be given on page
2.8
after the necessary preparation.
The analogous results for
\operatorname{Solid}
hold as well (
2.8.30
,
2.8.37
and
2.8.45
), we will deduce this from the above statement.

Notation 2.8.4
.

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
let

\mathcal{M}(S,A)\coloneqq\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})}_{\kappa},A).

Example 2.8.5
.

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
by
Lemma

2.8.2
.

By
Lemma

2.8.2
, for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
there exists a
\kappa
-small set
I
such that
\mathcal{M}(S,A)=\prod_{I}A
for all
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
As
\kappa
-small products are exact in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
(
Lemma

2.6.3
), this implies that

\mathcal{M}(S,-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})

is an exact functor.
In particular, the exponential sequence
0\to\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{T}^{1}\to 0
yields exact sequences

0\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{\blacksquare}\to\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{R})\to\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1})\to 0,\,S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}.

Lemma 2.8.6

(
[
CS19a
, Lecture 6]
)
.

Suppose
(J_{i})_{i\in I},(U_{k})_{k\in K}
are small collections of
\kappa
-small sets.
Every group homomorphism

\oplus_{I}\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{\kappa}\to\oplus_{K}\prod_{U_{k}}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{\kappa}\text{ in }\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})

extends uniquely to a map

\oplus_{I}\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\to\oplus_{K}\prod_{U_{k}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\text{ in }\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}).

Proof.

It of course suffices to show this for
I=*
. We show that pullback along
\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}
is an isomorphism

(2.8.6.1)

\displaystyle\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa},\oplus_{K}\prod_{U_{k}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{\kappa},\oplus_{K}\prod_{U_{k}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}).

Since
|J_{i}|<\kappa
, the sequence of
\kappa
-condensed abelian groups

0\to\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\to 0\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})

is exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
), whence it is enough to show that for
k=0,1
,

(2.8.6.2)

\displaystyle\pi_{-k}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\oplus_{K}\prod_{U_{k}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})=\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\oplus_{K}\prod_{U_{k}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})=0,

then
2.8.6.1
follows.
By
2.7.4
and exactness of filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
(
Lemma

2.6.3
),

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})

commutes with filtered colimits.
Since
\kappa
-small products in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
), it follows that

\displaystyle\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\oplus_{K}\prod_{U_{k}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq K\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\prod_{f\in F}\prod_{U_{f}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{J_{i}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}F\subseteq K\\
F\text{ finite }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\prod_{f\in F}\prod_{U_{f}}*

is contractible by
Lemma

2.7.6
.
This proves (
2.8.6.2
).
∎

Proposition 2.8.7

(
[
CS19a
, Lecture 6]
)
.

Suppose
C_{*}\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq 0}
is a chain complex such that

(*)

For all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, there exists a set
J_{i}
and a collection of
\kappa
-light profinite sets
(S^{j})_{j\in J_{i}}
such that
C_{i}=\oplus_{j\in J_{i}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
.

For all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

(2.8.7.1)

\displaystyle\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})_{\geq-1}

and

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq-1}.

Proof.

Suppose that
(C_{*},\partial)
is a chain complex as in the lemma and for
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
j\in J_{n}
choose
I_{j}
,
|I_{j}|<\kappa
such that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\cong\prod_{I_{j}}\mathbb{Z}
.
By
Lemma

2.8.6
, we obtain a chain complex
(C_{*}^{\mathbb{R}},\partial^{\mathbb{R}}_{*})
with
C_{n}=\oplus_{j\in J_{n}}\prod_{I_{j}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}
and
\partial_{n}^{\mathbb{R}}
the unique extension of
\partial_{n}
.
In particular, for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
,
\partial_{n}^{\mathbb{R}}
descends to a group homomorphism

\partial_{n}^{\mathbb{T}^{1}}\colon\oplus_{j\in J_{n}}\prod_{I_{j}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\to\oplus_{j\in J_{n-1}}\prod_{I_{j}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}.

This defines a chain complex
(C_{*}^{\mathbb{T}^{1}},\partial^{\mathbb{T}^{1}})
.
The short exact sequence of chain complexes

0\to C_{*}\to C_{*}^{\mathbb{R}}\to C_{*}^{\mathbb{T}^{1}}\to 0

yields fiber sequences

\displaystyle\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*})\to

\displaystyle\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*}^{\mathbb{R}})

\displaystyle\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*}^{\mathbb{T}^{1}})

and

\displaystyle\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*})\to

\displaystyle\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*}^{\mathbb{R}})

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*}^{\mathbb{T}^{1}}).

It is therefore enough to show that for
A=\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa},\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}
and
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*}^{A})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq 0}

and

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*}^{A})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})_{\geq 0},

then it follows that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{Z}),C_{*})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq-1}

and

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})_{\geq-1}.

Denote by
\mathcal{H}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
the full subcategory on objects
H\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
such that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),H)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq 0}

and

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],H)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})_{\geq 0}

for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.

We first show that
\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa},\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\in\mathcal{H}
.

1.5.4
and
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2, 3.3]
/
A.6.4
imply that

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}),\,\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],\mathbb{Z})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})^{\heartsuit}

are concentrated in degree
0
.
It now follows from the exponential exact sequence that for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})_{\geq 0}.

By
Lemmas

2.7.7
,
2.7.6
and
2.8.2
, for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})=0,

and

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),\mathbb{Z})\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})[-1].

Hence the exponential exact sequence implies that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa})\cong\Sigma\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),\mathbb{Z})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit},

which shows that
\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa},\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\in\mathcal{H}
.

As filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
),
2.7.3
and
2.7.4
imply that
\mathcal{H}\cap\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under filtered colimits.
Since
\kappa
-small products in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
),
\mathcal{H}\cap\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is also closed under
\kappa
-small products.
It now follows from the above that if
(I_{j})_{j\in J}
is a small family of
\kappa
-small sets, then

(2.8.7.2)

\displaystyle\oplus_{j\in J}\prod_{i\in I_{j}}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa},\oplus_{j\in J}\prod_{i\in I_{j}}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\in\mathcal{H}.

We now want to show that for
A=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{T}^{1}
and all complexes
C_{*}^{A}
of the above form,
C_{*}^{A}\in\mathcal{H}
.
We first explain that it suffices to show that
\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A}\in\mathcal{H}
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
For
n\in\mathbb{Z}
, the cofiber sequence
\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A}\to\tau_{\leq n+1}C_{*}^{A}\to H_{n+1}(C_{*}^{A})[n+1]
implies that
for
X\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\tau_{\geq-n}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A})\cong\tau_{\geq-n}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,\tau_{\leq n+1}C_{*}^{A})

and

\tau_{\geq-n}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A})\cong\tau_{\geq-n}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,\tau_{\leq n+1}C_{*}^{A}).

As the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is left-complete (
2.6.14
),
C_{*}^{A}={\underset{n}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A}
, and by the above, for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and
X\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
,

\tau_{\geq-n}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,C_{*}^{A})\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A})

and

\tau_{\geq-n}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,C_{*}^{A})\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(X,\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A}).

It therefore suffices to show that
\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A}\in\mathcal{H}
for all
n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq-1}
.
We prove this by induction on
n
, the case
n=-1
is trivial.
Suppose now that
n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
such that for all complexes
C_{*}^{A}
of the above form,
\tau_{\leq n-1}C_{*}^{A}\in\mathcal{H}
.
Fix such a complex
C_{*}^{A}
and denote by
C_{*}^{A,\leq n}
its stupid truncations.
We have fiber sequences

C_{*}^{A,\leq n}\to\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A}\to\operatorname{Im}(\partial_{n+1}^{A})[n+1],

\ker(\partial_{n+1}^{A})[n+1]\to C_{n+1}^{A}[n+1]\to\operatorname{Im}(\partial_{n+1}^{A})[n+1],

and

C_{*}^{A,\leq n-1}\to C_{*}^{A,\leq n}\to C_{n}^{A}[n].

By induction hypothesis,
\tau_{\leq n-1}C_{*}^{A,\leq n-1}=C_{*}^{A,\leq n-1}\in\mathcal{H}
, and by
2.8.7.2
,
C_{n}^{A}[n],C_{n+1}^{A}[n+1]\in\mathcal{H}
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
Since
\mathcal{H}
is closed under extensions and cofibers and for
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
\mathcal{H}[m]\subseteq\mathcal{H}
, it suffices to show that
\ker(\partial^{A}_{n+1})[1]\in\mathcal{H}
, then it follows that
\tau_{\leq n}C_{*}^{A}\in\mathcal{H}
.

We now show that
\ker(\partial^{A}_{n+1})[1]\in\mathcal{H}
.
Suppose that
C_{*}^{A}
is constructed from a chain complex
C_{*}
with

C_{n}=\oplus_{j\in J_{n}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},S_{j}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\text{ for all }j\in J_{n},n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}.

For
j\in J_{n}
: Since
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]
is compact in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
, there exists a finite subset
F(j)\subseteq J_{n-1}
such that

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\xrightarrow{\partial_{j}|_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}}}\oplus_{k\in J_{i-1}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{k}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}

factors over
\oplus_{k\in F(j)}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{k}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
.
This implies that the induced map

\partial_{n}|_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}}\colon\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}=\prod_{I_{j}}\mathbb{Z}\to\oplus_{k\in J_{n-1}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{k}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}=\oplus_{k\in J_{n-1}}\prod_{U_{k}}\mathbb{Z}

factors over
\oplus_{k\in F(j)}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{k}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
as well. By construction of
\partial_{i}^{A}
, it follows that

\partial_{i}^{A}(\prod_{I_{j}}A)\subseteq\oplus_{k\in F(j)}\prod_{U_{k}}A,

where
I_{j},U_{k}
are such that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}=\prod_{I_{j}}\mathbb{Z},\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{k}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}=\prod_{U_{k}}\mathbb{Z}
.
In particular,
\ker(\partial_{n}^{A})
is a filtered colimit of condensed abelian groups of the form

\ker(\prod_{I}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{U}\underline{A}_{\kappa})

for homomorphisms
f_{A}\colon\prod_{I}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{U}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
with
|I|,|U|<\kappa
.

Since filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact,
2.7.3
and
2.7.4
imply that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{Z}),-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})[1]\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))

and

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})[1]\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})

commute with filtered colimits, so in particular,

\mathcal{H}\cap\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})[1]\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))

is closed under filtered colimits.
We are therefore reduced to showing that for all
\kappa
-small sets
I,U
and all homomorphisms

f_{A}\colon\prod_{I}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{U}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}),

\ker(f_{A})[1]\in\mathcal{H}
.

We first show this for
A=\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}
.
Since for all
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff spaces
X
,
\underline{X}_{\kappa}(*)_{\kappa}=X
, the map
f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}
induces a homomorphism of topological abelian groups
f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}(*)_{\kappa}\colon\prod_{I}{\mathbb{T}^{1}}\to\prod_{J}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}
. By fully faithfulness of
\underline{-}_{\kappa}
(
Proposition

2.2.7
),
f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}=\underline{f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}(*)}_{\kappa}
.
In particular,

\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}})=\underline{\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}(*))}_{\kappa}

is represented by a compact abelian group of weight
\leq\max\{|I|,\mathbb{N}\}<\kappa
.
Since Pontryagin-duality restricts to a contravariant equivalence between compact Hausdorff and discrete abelian groups, taking Pontryagin duals yields an epimorphism

q\colon\oplus_{k}\mathbb{Z}\to\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}(*))^{v}

to the Pontryagin-dual
\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}(*))^{v}
of
\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}(*))
. As subgroup of a free abelian group,
\ker(q)
is free i.e.
\ker(q)=\oplus_{K}\mathbb{Z}
for
|K|\leq|I|
.
By taking Pontryagin duals again we obtain a resolution

0\to\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}}(*))\to\prod_{I}\mathbb{T}^{1}\to\prod_{K}\mathbb{T}^{1}\to 0.

As
\prod_{I}\mathbb{T}^{1}\to\prod_{K}\mathbb{T}^{1}
is a continuous surjection between
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff spaces,

\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{K}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}

is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets by
2.3.7
.
This implies that the induced sequence of
\kappa
-condensed abelian groups

0\to\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}})\to\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\to\prod_{K}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\to 0

is exact.
As
|K|,|I|<\kappa
,
\prod_{K}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa},\prod_{I}\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{\kappa}\in\mathcal{H}
by
Eq.

2.8.7.2
, which shows that
\ker(f_{\mathbb{T}^{1}})[1]\in\mathcal{H}
.

By
2.7.8
, for
|K|<\kappa
,
