\oplus_{K}\mathbb{Z}\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\prod_{K}\mathbb{Z},\mathbb{Z})
, whence
f_{\mathbb{Z}}\colon\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}\to\prod_{J}\mathbb{Z}
is dual to a map
f^{v}\colon\oplus_{J}\mathbb{Z}\to\oplus_{I}\mathbb{Z}
.
This implies that
f_{\mathbb{R}}
is dual to a map
f^{v}_{\mathbb{R}}\colon\oplus_{J}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\to\oplus_{I}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}
.
The map
\oplus_{J}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Coker}(f^{v}_{\mathbb{R}}(*)_{\kappa})
admits a continuous
\mathbb{R}
-linear section, whence

\operatorname{Coker}(f^{v}_{\mathbb{R}}(*)_{\kappa})=\oplus_{K}\mathbb{R}

for
|K|\leq|I|
.
As
\oplus_{J/I}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}\cong\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\circ(*)_{\kappa}(\oplus_{J/I}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})
and
\oplus_{J}\mathbb{R}(*)_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Coker}(f^{v}_{\mathbb{R}})(*)_{\kappa}
admits a continuous section, it follows that

\operatorname{Coker}(f^{v}_{\mathbb{R}})=\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Coker}(f^{v}_{\mathbb{R}}(*)_{\kappa}))=\oplus_{K}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}.

Consequently,
\ker(f_{\mathbb{R}})=\prod_{K}\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}
. Since
|K|<\kappa
,
\ker(f_{\mathbb{R}})\in\mathcal{H}
by
2.8.7.2
.
∎

Notation 2.8.8
.

For a
\kappa
-light profinite set
S
, the connecting homomorphism of the short exact sequence

0\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\to\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{R})\to\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1})\to 0

yields a natural transformation

\partial^{*}\colon\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),-)\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},-)[-1].

Denote by

c_{S}\colon\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),-)\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],-)[-1]

the composition of
\partial^{*}
with pullback along
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
.

Let
\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
be the full subcategory on objects
G
such that for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

(2.8.8.1)

\displaystyle c_{S}(G)\colon\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),G)\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],G)[-1]

is an equivalence.

We will identify
\mathcal{G}
with the derived category of solid abelian groups
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
in
2.8.26
below, but first prove some results on
\mathcal{G}
which enter the proof of
Proposition

2.8.3
.

Lemma 2.8.9
.

\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{G}
.

Proof.

Fix
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.
By
Lemma

2.8.2
, there exists
|I|<\kappa
with
\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})\cong\oplus_{I}\mathbb{Z}
. This implies that
\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{R})=\prod_{I}\mathbb{R}
.

Lemmas

2.7.7
and
2.7.6
imply that for all discrete abelian groups
M
,

\oplus_{I}M[-1]\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},M)[-1].

It therefore suffices to show that pullback along
\eta\colon\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
yields an equivalence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},\mathbb{Z})\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],\mathbb{Z}).

Since
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]
is flat, under the identification

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})),

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],\mathbb{Z})
becomes

\displaystyle\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}

\displaystyle\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}),

\displaystyle T

\displaystyle\mapsto\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S\times T}_{\kappa}],\mathbb{Z}),

cf.
A.3.5
.
By
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2]
/
A.6.4
, for all
T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{S\times T}_{\kappa},\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathcal{C}(S\times T,\mathbb{Z})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit}.

It therefore suffices to show that
\eta
induces an isomorphism

\oplus_{I}\mathbb{Z}\cong\pi_{0}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},\mathbb{Z})\xrightarrow{\eta^{*}}\pi_{0}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],\mathbb{Z})\cong\underline{\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})}_{\kappa}.

This holds by construction of the identification of
Lemma

2.7.7
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.10
.

(i)

If
G\in\mathcal{G}
and
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp}))
is a
\kappa
-condensed
\mathbb{R}
-module, then

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,G)=0.

(ii)

For
G\in\mathcal{G}
and
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, pullback along
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
induces an isomorphism

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{\blacksquare},G)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],G).

Proof.

Suppose
G\in\mathcal{G}
. Evaluating
2.8.8.1
at
S=*
implies that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{T}^{1},G)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z},G)[-1]

via the connecting homomorphism. Since

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{T}^{1},G)\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{R},G)\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z},G)

is a cofiber sequence, this implies that
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{R},G)=0.

It follows that for every
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{R}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}A,M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{R},M))=0.

Since the free modules
\mathbb{R}[A],A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
generate
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))})
under
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits (
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.7.3.14]
),
Proposition

1.4.1
implies that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(V,G)=0

for all condensed
\mathbb{R}
-modules
V
.
In particular, the connecting homomorphism

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),G)\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},G)[-1]

from the exponential exact sequence is an equivalence for all
G\in\mathcal{G}
, which implies that pullback along
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
induces an isomorphism

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},G)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],G)

for all
G\in\mathcal{G}
and all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.11
.

(i)

The category
\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a stable subcategory closed under extensions.

(ii)

For all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under filtered colimits.
In particular, for
n\leq m\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{[n,m]}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under filtered colimits.

Proof.

Since for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),-)\text{ and }\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],-)

are exact functors,

\mathcal{G}
is a stable subcategory closed under extensions.
For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),-)|_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}}\text{ and }\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],-)|_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}}

preserve filtered colimits by
Lemma

2.8.2
,
2.7.4
and
2.7.2
.
Since filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact, this implies that

\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq n}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))

and
\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{[m,n]}
are closed under filtered colimits for all
m\leq n\in\mathbb{Z}
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.12
.

If
C_{*}
is a chain complex as in
Proposition

2.8.7
, then
C_{*}
represents an element in
\mathcal{G}
.

Proof.

By definition,
\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under limits. Since
\kappa
-small products in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
), it follows that
\mathcal{G}\cap\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under
\kappa
-small products.
Lemma

2.8.2
and
Lemma

2.8.9
now imply that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\in\mathcal{G}
for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.
Since
\mathcal{G}\cap\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under filtered colimits (
2.8.11
) and
\kappa
-small products,
\mathcal{G}\cap\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under direct sums. In particular, if
(S_{i})_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
is a small family of profinite sets, then
\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{i}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\in\mathcal{G}
.

As
\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under extensions (
2.8.11
), it follows by induction on the length that every finite length complex

0\to C_{n}\to C_{n-1}\to\ldots\to C_{0}

with
C_{i}=\oplus_{j\in J_{i}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{j}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
,
S_{j}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
represents an element in
\mathcal{G}
.
Suppose now that
C_{*}
is an unbounded complex as in
Proposition

2.8.7
.
Let

C_{*}^{>n}\coloneqq(\ldots\to C_{k+n}\to C_{k+n-1}\to\ldots\to C_{n+1}\to 0)

the stupid connective cover and denote by
C_{*}^{\leq n}
the stupid truncation.
The canonical map

\operatorname{Cone}(C_{*}^{\leq n}\to C_{*})\to C_{*}^{>n}

is a quasi-isomorphism.
By
Proposition

2.8.7
, for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*}^{>n})[-n-1]\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq-1},

i.e.

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*}^{>n})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq n}

and

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*}^{>n})[-n-1]\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq-1},

i.e.

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*}^{>n})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq n}.

This implies that for
i<n
,
C_{*}^{\leq n}\to C_{*}
induces isomorphisms

\pi_{i}(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*}^{\leq n}))\cong\pi_{i}(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))})(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*})

and

\pi_{i}(\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*}^{\leq n}))\cong\pi_{i}(\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*})).

The first isomorphism implies that for
i<n
,

\pi_{i}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*}^{\leq n})\cong\pi_{i}(\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C_{*})).

Indeed, by t-exactness of sheafification and
A.3.5
, both sides are the
\kappa
-condensed sheafification of

\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{op}}\ni T\mapsto\pi_{i}(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S\times T}_{\kappa}],C^{\leq n}_{*}))\cong\pi_{i}(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S\times T}_{\kappa}],C_{*})).

Since for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
C^{\leq n}_{*}\in\mathcal{G}
, and the functors
\pi_{i},i\in\mathbb{Z}
are jointly conservative, this shows that
C_{*}
represents an element in
\mathcal{G}
.
∎

Lemma 2.8.13
.

Denote by
\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
the subcategory from
2.8.8
.
Then

\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit}=\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}.

Proof.

By
2.8.10
, for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, and
G\in\mathcal{G}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},G)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],G),

whence
\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit}\subseteq\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.

We claim that every solid abelian group
M
admits a resolution
C_{*}\to M
with
C_{*}
a complex as in
Proposition

2.8.7
, then
2.8.12
implies that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathcal{G}
.
Since
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
generate
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
under colimits, for
M\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
there exists a set of
\kappa
-light profinite sets
(S_{i})_{i\in I}\subseteq\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
with an epimorphism
\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{i}}_{\kappa}]\to M
.
If
M
is solid, this factors over an epimorphism

\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{i}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\to M
.
Suppose that a partial resolution

C_{n}\xrightarrow{\partial_{n}}\ldots\to C_{n-1}\to M

as in
Proposition

2.8.7
has been constructed.
Choose a small collection of
\kappa
-light profinite sets
(S_{i})_{i\in I}
with a surjection
\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{i}}_{\kappa}]\to\ker(\partial_{n})
.
Since
C_{n}\in\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit}
is solid by the above,
\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{i}}_{\kappa}]\to C_{n}
extends uniquely to a group homomorphism

\partial_{n+1}\colon\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{i}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\to C_{n}.

By construction,
\ker(\partial_{n})\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(\partial_{n+1})
.
Since for
i\in I
,
\partial_{n}\circ\partial_{n+1}|_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{i}}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}}
is an extension of the zero morphism
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S_{i}}_{\kappa}]\xrightarrow{0}C_{n-1}
and
C_{n-1}
is solid,
\partial_{n}\circ\partial_{n+1}=0
, i.e.
\operatorname{Im}(\partial_{n+1})\subseteq\ker(\partial_{n})
.
By repeating this construction we obtain the desired resolution
C_{*}
of
M
.
∎

We can now finally deduce
Proposition

2.8.3
from this.

Proof of
Proposition

2.8.3
.

By
2.8.10
and
Lemma

2.8.13
, for
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
and
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
pullback along
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
is an isomorphism

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M).

Suppose that
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
and
C_{*}\to M
is a resolution of
M
as in
Proposition

2.8.7
. It was shown in the proof of
2.8.12
that such a resolution exists.
By
Proposition

2.8.7
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C_{*})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq-1}.

Since
M\in\mathcal{G}
, it follows that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),M)[1]\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq 0},

which shows that
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit}
is concentrated in degree
0
.

Lemma

2.8.13
and
2.8.11
imply that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit}\cap\mathcal{G}=\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under filtered colimits.
∎

Corollary 2.8.14
.

(i)

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.

(ii)

The family
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
generates
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
under small colimits.

Proof.

By
2.8.12
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\in\mathcal{G}
.
We showed in the proof of
Proposition

2.8.3
that
\mathcal{G}\cap\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))^{\heartsuit}=\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.
Since every solid abelian group admits a resolution as in
Proposition

2.8.7
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
generates
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
under colimits.
∎

Lemma 2.8.15
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
The category

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})

is stable under small limits, colimits and extensions.

Proof.

Since the tensor product on
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is cocontinuous in both variables, the forget functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
reflects limits and colimits, hence it suffices to show that

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})

is stable under small limits, colimits and extensions. It is immediate from the definition that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under limits.
By
Proposition

2.8.3
,
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under filtered colimits.
This implies that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
is closed under direct sums (which are filtered colimits of finite direct sums).

If
0\to A\to B\to C\to 0
is a short exact sequence in
\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}
with
A\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
we obtain a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},A)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},C)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},A)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ldots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],A)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underbrace{\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],A)}_{=0}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ldots}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

By
Proposition

2.8.3
, the right vertical map is an isomorphism and the bottom-right corner is
0
.
Hence by the Snake lemma,
B\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
if and only if
C\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
, which shows that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under extensions and cofibers. We explained above that is also closed under filtered colimits and finite coproducts, and hence under arbitrary small colimits, cf.
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.6, 4.4.2.7]
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.16
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

(i)

The category
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
is presentable and Grothendieck abelian.

(ii)

The forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
.

(iii)

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}.

(iv)

For a condensed
{R}
-module
M
, the condensed abelian group underlying
M^{{\square}{R}}
is
M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
and the
{R}
-module structure is given by

{R}\times M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\to{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\times M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}=({R}\times M)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\to M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}},

where the left two maps are induced by the unit of the solidification adjunction on condensed abelian groups and the right map is the solidification of the multiplication map.

Proof.

By
Lemma

2.8.15
,
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
is closed under limits and colimits.
Hence by
[
AR89
]
,
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
is presentable and the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
.
By
Lemma

2.6.3
, filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact and
\oplus_{X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}{R}[\underline{X}_{\kappa}]
is a generator. By
Lemma

2.8.15
and the above, this implies that filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact and that
(\oplus_{X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}{R}[\underline{X}_{\kappa}])^{{\square}{R}}
is a generator, which proves that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
is Grothendieck abelian. For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
by
2.8.14
. Hence by definition of
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
and
(-)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
.
It is straightforward to check that the left adjoint
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
satisfies the description from
(iv)
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.17
.

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.

Proof.

Denote by
f\colon\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
the forget functor. By
Propositions

2.8.3
and
2.8.16
, for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(f\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}},-)\circ f\colon\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Ab}

is exact.
As
f
is fully faithful, this shows that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.18
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a
\kappa
-condensed ring.

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
{R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
.
For every solid
R
-module
M
, there exists a small family of
\kappa
-light profinite sets
S^{i},i\in I
with an epimorphism
\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S^{i}}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}}\to M
.
In particular,
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
has enough projectives.

Proof.

As the forget functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
reflects small limits and colimits, it follows from
Lemma

2.8.15
that the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
preserves small limits and colimits.
Whence it admits a left adjoint
{R}^{{\square}}[-]
by
[
AR89
]
. As
f
is exact,
{R}^{{\square}}[-]
preserves projectives, and since both are left adjoint to the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
,

(-)^{{\square}{R}}\circ{R}[-]\cong{R}^{{\square}}[-]\circ(-)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}.

It now follows from
2.8.28
that for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

{R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}}={R}^{{\square}}[(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}})]

is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
.

Suppose now that
P\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
. Since
{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/P}}
is a small category, there exists a small family of
\kappa
-light profinite sets
(S^{i})_{i\in I}
and an epimorphism
\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{S^{i}}_{\kappa}\to P
of
\kappa
-condensed sets. This induces an epimorphism
\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S^{i}}_{\kappa}]\to P
of
\kappa
-condensed
{R}
-modules which factors over an epimorphism

\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S^{i}}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}}\to P

since
P
is solid.
∎

Corollary 2.8.19
.

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal. For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
is presentable and in particular admits small limits and colimits.

Proof.

As
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
is Grothendieck abelian (
2.8.16
), its derived category
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
is presentable by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.5.21]
.
In particular, it admits small limits and colimits by
[
Lur09
, Definition 5.5.0.1, Corollary 5.5.2.4]
.
∎

Lemma 2.8.20
.

The
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
is left and right-complete.

Proof.

Since
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
is Grothendieck abelian (
2.8.16
), the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
is right-complete by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.5.21]
.

By
Lemma

2.8.15
and
Lemma

2.6.3
, countable products in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact. This implies that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
has countable products, and that they can be computed on representing chain complexes. In particular,
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
is stable under countable coproducts.
Since the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
is left-separated, it now follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.1.19]
that it is left-complete.
∎

Since
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
is exact, the induced functor
\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
descends to a functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
. We now record basic properties of this functor.

Corollary 2.8.21
.

The functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
preserves small colimits.

Proof.

Since coproducts in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
),
Lemma

2.8.15
implies that they are exact in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
as well.
It follows that coproducts in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
and
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
can be computed on representing chain complexes (as degreewise coproducts), and in particular,
f
preserves coproducts by
Lemma

2.8.15
.

1.4.28
and
Lemma

2.8.15
imply that
f
preserves finite colimits, and hence
f
preserves small colimits by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.6]
.
∎

Remark 2.8.22
.

As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
and
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
are Grothendieck abelian, by
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
, the functor
f
is determined up to contractible choice by being
t
-exact, cocontinuous and restricting to the forget functor

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})

on hearts, see also
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
.

Lemma 2.8.23
.

If
{R}
is a
\kappa
-condensed ring such that
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
has enough projectives, then the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))

has a left adjoint.

This in particular applies if
\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal, cf.
2.6.5
.

Proof.

By
Lemma

2.8.20
, the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is left and right complete and by
Lemma

2.8.15
, filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact.

Lemma

A.1.6
now implies that there exists a unique colimits preserving, right t-exact functor
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
such that

H_{0}\circ(-)^{L{\square}{R}}|_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})}=(-)^{{\square}{R}}

and for all projective
R
-modules
P
,

P^{L{\square}{R}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))^{\heartsuit}.

The composite
f\circ(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
is cocontinuous, right t-exact and carries projectives of
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
to the heart.
As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
has enough projectives (
2.6.5
), filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
) and the
t
-structure
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
is left and right complete (
2.6.14
and
2.6.13
),
Lemma

A.1.6
implies that the unit
\operatorname{id}\to f_{0}\circ(-)^{{\square}{R}}
enhances essentially uniquely to a natural transformation
\operatorname{id}\to f\circ(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
.
We claim that this exhibits
f
as right adjoint to
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
.
Denote by
\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
the full subcategory on objects
X
such that

c(\eta,X)\colon\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X^{L{\square}{R}},-)\xrightarrow{f_{*}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(fX^{L{\square}{R}},f-)\xrightarrow{\eta^{*}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))}(X,f-)

is an equivalence.
We want to show that
\mathcal{D}=\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
.
As
f
and
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
preserve colimits,
\mathcal{D}
is closed under colimits.
Since
f
and
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
are exact,
X\in\mathcal{D}
if and only if
\Sigma^{i}X\in\mathcal{D}
for some
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
By right-completeness of the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, it therefore suffices to show that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}
.
Fix
X\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}
. For
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\displaystyle\pi_{i}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X^{L{\square}{R}},-)

\displaystyle\cong\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X^{L{\square}{R}},\Omega^{i}-)

\displaystyle\cong\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X^{L{\square}{R}},\tau_{\geq 0}\Omega^{i}-)

by right
t
-exactness of
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
, and

\displaystyle\pi_{i}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X,f-)

\displaystyle\cong\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X,\Omega^{i}f-)

\displaystyle\cong\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X,\tau_{\geq 0}\Omega^{i}f-)

\displaystyle\cong\pi_{0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(X,f\tau_{\geq 0}\Omega^{i}-),

by
t
-exactness of
f
.
As
\tau_{\geq 0}\Omega^{i}=\Omega^{i}\tau_{\geq-i}
and
\Omega^{i}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))_{>-\infty}\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))_{>-\infty}
is an equivalence, this shows that
X\in\mathcal{D}
if and only if
\pi_{0}c(\eta,X)(Y)
is an equivalence for all
Y\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{>-\infty}
.
Choose a chain complex
C_{*}
of projective
\kappa
-condensed
{R}
-modules representing
X
which is concentrated in degrees
\geq 0
. This exists since
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
has enough projectives.
Then
X^{L{\square}{R}}
is computed by applying
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
degreewise to
C_{*}
.
Indeed: Denote by
C_{*}^{\leq n}
the stupid truncations of
C_{*}
. Exactness of filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
and
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
implies that
X^{L{\square}{R}}\cong{\underset{k}{\operatorname{colim}}}(C_{*}^{\leq k})^{L{\square}{R}}
.
Using the cofiber sequences

C_{*}^{\leq k}\to C_{*}^{\leq k+1}\to C_{k+1}[k+1],

it follows by induction on
k
that
(C_{*}^{\leq k})^{L{\square}{R}}
is computed by applying
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
degreewise to
C_{*}^{\leq k}
.
The unit for the localisation
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
defines a chain map
C_{*}\to C_{*}^{{\square}{R}}
, and the same inductive argument shows that this represents the homotopy class of the unit
\eta_{X}
.
The argument from the proof of
[
Sta22
,
Tag 0FNC
]
now shows that
\pi_{0}c(\eta,X)(Y)
is an equivalence for all
Y\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))_{>-\infty}
.
∎

We will show below (
2.8.33
,
2.8.61
and
2.8.58
), that the left adjoint also exists over
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
and for
\kappa=\aleph_{1}
.

Lemma 2.8.24
.

The functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
preserves
\kappa
-small limits.

Proof.

Since
\kappa
-small products in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
), they are exact in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
by
Lemma

2.8.15
. This implies that
\kappa
-small products in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
can be computed on the level of chain complexes (as degreewise product).
Since the same holds for
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,
Lemma

2.8.15
implies that
f
preserves all
\kappa
-small products. Since
f
is exact, this shows that
f
preserves all
\kappa
-small limits (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.7]
).
∎

Lemma 2.8.25
.

The forget functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is fully faithful.

Proof.

We want to deduce this from
Lemma

A.1.8
.
By
Lemmas

2.8.15
and
2.8.16
and
Lemma

2.6.3
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
and
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
are Grothendieck abelian, countable products in both categories are exact, and the functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is fully faithful and preserves small limits and colimits.

By
2.8.18
,
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
has enough projectives, and every projective object
p\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
is a direct summand of
\oplus_{S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
.
Proposition

2.8.3
therefore implies that for all solid abelian groups
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
and for all projectives
p\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(p,M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{0}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(p,M)

is concentrated in degree
0
.
The statement now follows from
Lemma

A.1.8
.
∎

The essential image of the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
can be characterized as follows:

Corollary 2.8.26
.

For
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the following are equivalent:

(i)

M
lies in the essential image of the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

(ii)

For all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, the map
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
induces an equivalence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},M)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M).

(iii)

For all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, the map
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
induces an equivalence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M).

(iv)

M
lies in the category
\mathcal{G}
from
2.8.8
.

(v)

For all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
,
H_{i}(M)\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.

Proof.

Since
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
preserves limits and colimits (
Lemma

2.8.15
),
\ref{essentialimageforgetfunctorsolid}\Rightarrow\ref{essentialimageforgethomology}
.
Clearly,
\ref{internallyderivedsolid}\Rightarrow\ref{derivedsolid}
, and by
2.8.10
,
\ref{Gcategoryidentifywithsolid}\Rightarrow\ref{internallyderivedsolid}
.

We now show that
\ref{derivedsolid}\Rightarrow\ref{essentialimageforgetfunctorsolid}
.
Denote by
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{{\square}}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
the full subcategory on objects satisfying
(ii)
.
Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Sp}
is conservative,
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{{\square}}
if and only if for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa},i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
induces an equivalence

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\Sigma^{i}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},M)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\Sigma^{i}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],M).

As
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is presentable, by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.4.15]
, the inclusion

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{{\square}}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))

has a left adjoint
L
, and for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

L(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}])\cong L(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare})
.
By
2.8.10
and
Proposition

2.8.7
, for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{{\square}}
, whence
L(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}])\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}
. In particular,

L(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}])\in\operatorname{ess.im}(f)\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))

by
2.8.16
. As the essential image of
f
is a stable subcategory closed under small colimits (
2.8.21
,
Lemma

2.8.24
), and
\Sigma^{i}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],i\in\mathbb{Z},S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
generates
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
under colimits, it follows that

\operatorname{Im}(L)=\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{{\square}}\subseteq\operatorname{ess.im}(f).

We now show that
\ref{essentialimageforgetfunctorsolid}\Rightarrow\ref{Gcategoryidentifywithsolid}
.
By
Lemma

2.8.13
,
f(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{G}.
Since
\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a stable subcategory closed under extensions and
f
is
t
-exact, this implies that for
n\leq m\in\mathbb{Z}
,

f(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})_{[n,m]})\subseteq\mathcal{G}.

In particular, for
n\leq m\in\mathbb{Z}
and
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
,
\tau_{\leq m}\tau_{\geq n}fA\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{{\square}}
since
f
is
t
-exact.
Right completeness of the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
2.8.11
imply that
\tau_{\leq m}A=\tau_{\leq m}{\underset{n}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\geq n}A\in\mathcal{G}
for all
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
As the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is left-complete (
2.6.14
), and
\mathcal{G}
is closed under limits, this implies that
\operatorname{ess.im}(f)\subseteq\mathcal{G}
.

It remains to show that
\ref{essentialimageforgethomology}\Rightarrow\ref{essentialimageforgetfunctorsolid}
. Suppose
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
with
H_{i}(A)\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
. By
2.6.14
,

A={\underset{k}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\geq k}A={\underset{k}{\operatorname{colim}}}{\underset{i}{\operatorname{lim}}}\tau_{\leq i}\tau_{\geq k}A.

As
\operatorname{ess.im}(f)\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under colimits and countable limits (
2.8.21
,
Lemma

2.8.24
), it is enough to show that for all
n\leq m\in\mathbb{Z}
,
\tau_{\geq n}\tau_{\leq m}A\in\operatorname{ess.im}(f).

Since
\operatorname{ess.im}(f)
is a stable subcategory, we can assume that
n=0
.
The claim now follows by induction on
m
: The case
n=m=0
is trivial, and the induction step follows since
\operatorname{ess.im}(f)\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a stable subcategory.
∎

We will from now on freely identify
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
with the essential image of the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

Corollary 2.8.27
.

For every uncountable cardinal
\kappa
,
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under small limits and colimits.
The inclusion
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}}
.

Proof.

The third characterization of the essential image of the forget functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
from
2.8.26
implies that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under small limits. By
2.8.21
, it is closed under small colimits. As
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}),\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
are Grothendieck abelian (
2.8.16
,
2.6.6
), their derived categories are presentable by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.5.21]
.
It now follows from the adjoint functor theorem (
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
) that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
has a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}}
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.28
.

(i)

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
and
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.

(ii)

\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa}^{L{\square}}=0
.

Proof.

By
2.8.10
and
2.8.12
, for
G\in\mathcal{G}
, and
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],G)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare},G).

As the forget functor factors over an equivalence
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{G}
(
2.8.26
) and
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\in\mathcal{G}
(
2.8.12
), this implies that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{\blacksquare}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
.
By
2.8.17
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.
By
2.8.10
, for
G\in\mathcal{G}
,
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa},G)=*,
whence
\underline{\mathbb{R}^{L{\square}}}_{\kappa}=0
by
2.8.26
.
∎

We now deduce from the above results their condensed analogues. This relies on the following observation.

Lemma 2.8.29
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and choose a regular cardinal
\mu
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

(i)

For regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa\geq\mu
,

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}({R})

restricts to a functor

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R}).

(ii)

This exhibits

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\lambda\geq\mu\\
\lambda\text{ regular }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})\cong\operatorname{Solid}({R})

as colimit in
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
.

(iii)

For
M\in\operatorname{Cond}({R})
,
M\in\operatorname{Solid}({R})
if and only if for all regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
,
r^{\kappa}M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
.

(iv)

For
\kappa\geq\mu
,

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}({R})}\operatorname{Solid}({R})\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})}\operatorname{Solid}({R}).

(v)

\operatorname{Solid}({R})
has small limits and colimits and for
\kappa\geq\mu
,

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Solid}({R})
is closed under small colimits and
\kappa
-small limits.

Proof.

We first show that for regular cardinals
\kappa\leq\lambda
, the left Kan extension

i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab})

restricts to
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}
.
By
Lemma

2.8.15
,
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under small limits and colimits. In particular,
\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
for all small sets
I
.
2.8.14
and
Lemma

2.8.2
imply that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
is generated by
\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z},|I|<\kappa
under small colimits.
For all regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa
, the functor
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab})
preserves
\kappa
-small limits by
2.4.12
.
As
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
also preserves colimits and
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa/\lambda}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa/\lambda}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under small colimits and limits (
Lemma

2.8.15
), this shows that
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}
.
It now follows from
Lemma

A.1.3
that

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\\
\kappa\text{ regular }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})

is a full subcategory.
We claim that it consists precisely of the solid abelian groups.
Fix a regular cardinal
\kappa
and denote by
i_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
the left adjoint.
2.4.19
implies that for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
i_{\kappa}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]
.
Since
i_{\kappa}
preserves
\kappa
-small limits (
2.4.12
),

(i_{\kappa}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}])^{\blacksquare}\cong i_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}])^{\blacksquare}
by
Lemma

2.8.2
.
This implies that
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
if and only if for all regular cardinals
\kappa
,
r^{\kappa}M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
, and hence
{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\\
\kappa\text{ regular }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}=\operatorname{Solid}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
.

Suppose now that
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and choose an uncountable regular cardinal
\mu
such that
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
As for all cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
,

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})}\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa},

it follows from the above that for all
\lambda\geq\kappa\geq\mu
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}({R})
restricts to a functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})
and that

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})=\operatorname{Solid}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})}).

In particular, the induced functors
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}({R})
are fully faithful with essential image

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})}\operatorname{Solid}({R})\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}({R})}\operatorname{Solid}({R}).

We have shown above that for
M\in\operatorname{Cond}({R})
,
M\in\operatorname{Solid}({R})
if and only if for all regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
,
r^{\kappa}M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
.

Finally,

Lemma

2.8.15
and
2.4.12
and
1.4.1
imply that for all regular cardinals
\mu\leq\kappa\leq\lambda
,

\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})

preserves small colimits and
\kappa
-small limits. It follows from
Lemma

A.1.3
that
\operatorname{Solid}({R})
has small limits and colimits and that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Solid}({R})
is closed under
\kappa
-small limits and small colimits.
∎

Corollary 2.8.30
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a discrete condensed ring.

(i)

The category

\operatorname{Solid}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}({R})

is an abelian subcategory stable under small limits, colimits and extensions. In particular,
\operatorname{Solid}({R})
has all small colimits and limits.

(ii)

The forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}({R})
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
.

(iii)

For a condensed
{R}
-module
M
, the condensed abelian group underlying
M^{{\square}{R}}
is
M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
and the
{R}
-module structure is given by

{R}\times M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\to{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\times M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}=({R}\times M)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\to M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}},

where the left two maps are induced by the unit of the solidification adjunction on for condensed abelian groups and the right map is the solidification of the scalar multiplication.

Proof.

Lemmas

2.8.15
,
2.8.29
and
A.1.3
imply that
\operatorname{Solid}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}({R})
is closed under small limits, colimits and extensions and has small limits and colimits.

We now show that the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}({R})
has a left adjoint. Fix a regular cardinal
\mu
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
As

\operatorname{Solid}({R})\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}),

it suffices to show that for all regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa\geq\mu
, the mate of the commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}({R})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda,{\square}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}}

commutes, i.e.

(2.8.30.1)

\displaystyle(-)^{{\square}{R},\lambda}\circ i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}\cong i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda,{\square}}\circ(-)^{{\square}{R},\kappa},

is an equivalence, then it follows from
Lemma

A.1.2
that
{\underset{\lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}(-)^{{\square}{R},\lambda}
is left adjoint to the forget functor.
As
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
is fully faithful, (
2.8.30.1
) holds if and only if the unit

\operatorname{id}\to f_{\kappa}\circ(-)^{{\square}{R},\kappa}

induces an equivalence

(2.8.30.2)

\displaystyle(-)^{{\square}{R},\lambda}\circ i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}\cong(-)^{{\square}{R},\lambda}\circ i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}\circ f_{\kappa}\circ(-)^{{\square}{R},\kappa}.

As the forget functors
g_{\kappa/\lambda}^{{\square}}\circ\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa/\lambda}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa/\lambda}
are conservative,

g_{\kappa/\lambda}\circ(-)^{{\square}{R},\kappa/\lambda}=(-)^{{\square}{\mathbb{Z}},\kappa/\lambda}\ \text{ (by \lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{underivedsolidification})},

g_{\lambda}\circ i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}=i_{\kappa,\mathbb{Z}}^{\lambda}\circ g_{\kappa}\,(\text{by monoidality of }i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}),

and

g_{\kappa}^{{\square}}\circ f_{\kappa}=f_{\kappa}\circ g_{\kappa},

it suffices to show
2.8.30.2
for
{R}=\mathbb{Z}
.
At
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
2.8.30.2
holds by
2.8.28
and
2.8.16
.
As all functors in (
2.8.30.2
) are cocontinuous, this implies the statement for
{R}=\mathbb{Z}
, and hence for general
R
.

By construction, the left adjoint
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
restricts to
(-)^{{\square}{R},\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
for all regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
, whence it follows from
2.8.16
, that for a condensed
{R}
-module
M
,
the abelian group underlying
M^{{\square}{R}}
is
M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
with scalar multiplication given by

{R}\times M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\to{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\times M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}=({R}\times M)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\to M^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}.\qed

Together with
2.4.19
, this implies:

Corollary 2.8.31
.

Suppose
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
\kappa
is a regular cardinal with

R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})).

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, the left adjoint
i_{\kappa}^{{\square}}\colon\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}({R})
sends
{R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}}
to
{R}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}{R}}
.

Proof.

We have shown in the proof of
2.8.30
that
i_{\kappa}^{{\square}}({R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}})=(i_{\kappa}{R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}])^{{\square}{R}}
, where
i_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}({R})
is the functor induced by the symmetric monoidal functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
As their right adjoints are equivalent,

i_{\kappa}\circ R[-]\cong R[-]\circ(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})),

whence by
2.4.19
,
i_{\kappa}{R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]={R}[\underline{S}]
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.32
.

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
choose a regular cardinal
\mu
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

(i)

Then

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R})).

(ii)

For regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))

is fully faithful and preserves colimits and
\kappa
-small limits.

(iii)

The category
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))
is big presentable and has small colimits and small limits.

Proof.

The first statement follows from
Lemma

2.8.29
and

Lemma

1.4.31
.
Recall from
2.8.19
that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
is presentable for all regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
.
Since

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular }\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})),

it suffices to show that for all regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\kappa\geq\mu
, the derived functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R}))

of
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})
is fully faithful and preserves colimits and
\kappa
-small limits, then the second and third statement follow from
Lemma

A.1.3
.

We first deduce fully faithfulness from
Lemma

A.1.8
.
The functor
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})
is fully faithful and preserves
\kappa
-small limits and colimits by
Lemmas

2.8.15
,
1.4.1
and
2.4.12
.
We claim that it also preserves projective objects.
By
2.8.18
, every projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
is a direct summand of
\oplus_{S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}{R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}}
. As
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}
preserves colimits, it therefore suffices to show that
i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}({R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}})
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
.

2.8.31
implies that for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
i^{\lambda,{\square}}_{\kappa}({R}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}{R}})={R}[\underline{S}_{\lambda}]^{{\square}{R}}
, which is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})
by
2.8.17
.
As
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
has enough projectives (
2.8.18
), it now follows from
Lemma

A.1.8
that
\mathcal{D}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa})
is fully faithful.

By
Lemmas

2.8.15
and
2.6.3
,
\kappa
-small products and small coproducts exist and are exact in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
and
\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})
.
In particular,
\kappa
-small products and small coproducts in their derived categories exist and can be computed as degreewise products/coproducts of representing chain complexes, respectively.

Lemma

2.8.29
implies that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})
preserves
\kappa
-small products and coproducts, whence
\mathcal{D}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa})
preserves
\kappa
-small products and small coproducts. As
\mathcal{D}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa})
is exact, it follows from
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.7]
that
\mathcal{D}(i^{\lambda}_{\kappa})
preserves
\kappa
-small limits and small colimits.
∎

Corollary 2.8.33
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a condensed ring.

(i)

The forget functor extends uniquely to a
t
-exact, small colimits preserving functor

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R})).

(ii)

The functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R}))
admits a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
.

Proof.

We first prove the first statement. Choose a regular cardinal
\mu
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
2.8.32
implies that

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R})))\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R})))

where
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}
refers to small colimits preserving,
t
-exact functors. By
Lemma

2.8.29
and
2.8.15
,

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}),\operatorname{Cond}({R}))\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}),\operatorname{Cond}({R})),

where
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}
refers to small colimits preserving, exact functors.
This implies that

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R})))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}),\operatorname{Cond}({R}))}\{f\}

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\geq\mu}{\operatorname{lim}}}\Bigl(\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R})))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R}),\operatorname{Cond}({R}))}\{f|_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})}\}\Bigr)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\geq\mu}{\operatorname{lim}}}\Bigl(\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R})))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R}),\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}({R}))}\{f_{\lambda}\}\Bigr),

where the limits run over all regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\mu
and
f_{(\lambda)}\colon\operatorname{Solid}_{(\lambda)}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\lambda)}({R})
denotes the forget functor.
Since
\operatorname{Cond}_{\lambda}({R})
and
\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})
are Grothendieck abelian (
2.8.16
,
2.6.6
), the right-hand side is contractible by
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
/
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
. This proves
(i)
.

As
\operatorname{Cond}({R})
has enough projectives,
A.1.7
implies that

F\mapsto H_{0}\circ F|_{\operatorname{Solid}({R})}
defines an equivalence

(2.8.33.1)

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{p},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R})))\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Cond}({R}),\operatorname{Solid}({R})),

between small colimits preserving, right
t
-exact functors
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))
which map projectives to the heart, and small colimits preserving functors
\operatorname{Cond}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}({R})
.
(
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))
satisfies the conditions of
A.1.7
by
Lemmas

2.8.20
,
2.8.32
and
2.8.16
and
[
Lur17
, Theorem 1.3.5.21]
.)

Denote by
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
a functor in the fiber of
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
. We claim that this is left adjoint to
f
.

We showed above that
f
is
t
-exact and preserves small colimits.
As
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is stable, big presentable, has small colimits and its
t
-structure is left and right complete (
2.6.14
) and compatible with filtered colimits (
Lemma

2.6.3
),
A.1.7
implies that the unit of the localisation
\operatorname{Solid}({R})\to\operatorname{Cond}({R})
enhances essentially uniquely to a natural transformation
\operatorname{id}\to f\circ(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
.
The same argument as in the proof of
Lemma

2.8.23
shows that this exhibits
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
as left adjoint to
f
.
∎

Definition 2.8.34
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
If it exists, we call the left adjoint

(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))

of the forget functor
derived solidification
.
We write
(-)^{L{\square}}\coloneqq(-)^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
for the derived solidification over abelian groups, which exists by
2.8.27
and
2.8.33
.

Remark 2.8.35
.

1.

As the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is the derived functor of
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
, the derived solidification defined above agrees with the derived functor of solidification at points where the latter is defined by
[
Sta22
,
Tag 0FND
]
.

2.

Suppose that
C_{*}
is a bounded-below chain complex of
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
-acyclic (
\kappa
-)condensed
{R}
-modules, i.e.
C_{n}^{L{\square}{R}}\cong C_{n}^{{\square}{R}}
for all
n\in\mathbb{Z}
.
Then
C_{*}^{L{\square}{R}}\cong C_{*}^{{\square}{R}}
is computed by applying
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
degreewise to
C_{*}
.
Indeed: Using the cofiber sequences
C_{*}^{\leq m}\to C_{*}^{\leq m+1}\to C_{m+1}[m+1]
, it follows by induction on
m
that
(C_{*}^{\leq m})^{L{\square}{R}}=(C_{*}^{{\square}{R}})^{\leq m}
is computed by applying
(-)^{{\square}{{R}}}
degreewise to
C_{*}^{\leq m}
. Hence by exactness of filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
and
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
,

(C_{*})^{L{\square}{R}}\cong{\underset{m}{\operatorname{colim}}}(C_{*}^{\leq m})^{L{\square}{R}}\cong{\underset{m}{\operatorname{colim}}}(C_{*}^{{\square}{R}})^{\leq m}\cong C_{*}^{{\square}{R}}

is computed by applying
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
degreewise to
C_{*}
.

3.

This implies the following:
Suppose that
R
is such that for all
M\in\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
, there exists a
(-)^{L{\square}}
-acyclic
R
-module
A
with an epimorphism
A\to M
. Then the derived functor of solidification
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is everywhere defined by
[
Sta22
,
Tag 0794
]
(in the large universe), applied to the class of
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
-acyclic objects

\mathcal{P}=\{A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\,|\,A^{L{\square}{R}}=A^{{\square}{R}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})^{\heartsuit}\}.

Lemma 2.8.36
.

(i)

The forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is fully faithful.

(ii)

For
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}\cong\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
for some small set
I
of cardinality
|I|\leq\operatorname{wt}(S)
.

(iii)

For all uncountable regular cardinals
\kappa
, the derived solidification

(-)^{L{\square}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})

restricts to

(-)^{L{\square},\kappa}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}),

where
(-)^{L{\square},\kappa}
denotes the derived solidification on the
\kappa
-condensed level.

(iv)

In particular, for all uncountable regular cardinals
\kappa
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\times_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})).

Proof.

By construction (see the proof of
2.8.33
), the forget functor is the colimit of the forget functors
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
over all small regular cardinals, and hence fully faithful by
Lemmas

2.8.25
,
2.8.32
and
A.1.3
.

To prove
(ii)
, we show that for
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
, pullback along the map
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{L{\square}}\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
adjoint to
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
gives an isomorphism

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}},M)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{L{\square}},M).

Fix
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
,
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
and choose a regular cardinal
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(S)
with
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
.
Then
fM\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
and

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}],fM)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],fM).

By
2.8.26
,
2.8.31
and fully faithfulness of
f
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],fM)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}},fM)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}},fM)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}},M).

This shows that the map
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{L{\square}}\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
adjoint to
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
is an equivalence for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
.
By
2.8.31
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}\cong\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
for a small set
I
of cardinality
|I|\leq\operatorname{wt}(S)
. In particular,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
for all
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(S)
.

As for an uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa
,
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under small colimits and generated under small colimits by
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}],S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
is closed under small colimits, this shows that

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))\xrightarrow{(-)^{L{\square}}}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})

factors over

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}).

The induced functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})

is obviously left adjoint to the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, and hence equivalent to
(-)^{{\square},\kappa}
.

For all uncountable regular cardinals
\kappa
, the composite

f_{\kappa}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))

is fully faithful by
2.8.32
and the above. By construction of the forget functor
f
,
f_{\kappa}
factors over
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
f_{\kappa}
therefore factors over a functor

\tilde{f}_{\kappa}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\times_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})).

As

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})),\,\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))

are fully faithful,
\tilde{f}_{\kappa}
is fully faithful.
By
(iii)
, for
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
with
fM\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,
(fM)^{L{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
. As
(fM)^{L{\square}}\cong M
, this shows that
\tilde{f}_{\kappa}
is essentially surjective.
∎

Corollary 2.8.37
.

For
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the following are equivalent:

(i)

M
lies in the essential image of the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

(ii)

For all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
, the unit
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
induces an equivalence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}},M)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}],M).

(iii)

For all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
, the unit
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
induces an equivalence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}},M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}],M).

(iv)

For all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
,
H_{i}(M)\in\operatorname{Solid}
.

Proof.

By construction (see the proof of
2.8.33
), the forget functor is the colimit of the forget functors
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
over all small regular cardinals.
As for all regular cardinals
\kappa
,
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Solid}
is exact (
Lemma

2.8.29
), it follows from
2.8.26
that the essential image of
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
