consists precisely of those
M
such that
H_{i}(M)\in\operatorname{Solid}
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.

Suppose now that
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
satisfies
(ii)
and choose an uncountable regular cardinal
\kappa
with
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

2.8.31
,
2.4.19
and
1.3.40
and our assumption on
M
imply that for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, the unit
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
induces an equivalence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}},M)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}],M).

Whence by
2.8.16
and
2.8.26
,
M
lies in the essential image of

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})).

It now follows from
Lemma

2.8.36
that
M
lies in the essential image of the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})).

Conversely, suppose
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
and
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
.
For regular cardinals
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(S)
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
sends
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]
to
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]
and
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
to
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
by
2.4.19
and
2.8.31
.
Hence by
1.1.30
, there exists a regular cardinal
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(S)
such that
fM\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],fM)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}],fM),

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}},fM)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}},fM),

It now follows from
2.8.26
that
fM
satisfies
(iii)
, and in particular also
(ii)
.
∎

We now explain that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
inherits a closed symmetric monoidal structure from
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

Definition 2.8.38
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal category. A localization

L\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{C}

is symmetric monoidal if there exists a symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{B}
such that
L
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor
L^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{B}^{\otimes}
with the following universal property:
If
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a symmetric monoidal category, pullback along
L^{\otimes}
defines a fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{B}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})

with essential image the symmetric monoidal functors
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
whose underlying functor
\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
inverts
L
-equivalences.

The universal property determines the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{B}
up to contractible choice.
We now show that
(-)^{L{\square}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal localisation.

Lemma 2.8.39
.

For
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,B)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})).

Proof.

For
A,B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
defines an equivalence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A\otimes B,-)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,-)).

Recall from
2.8.26
and
2.8.8
that for
C\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
and
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C)[-1].

This implies that for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and
C\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
,

\displaystyle\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,C))

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathcal{M}(S,\mathbb{T}^{1}),C))

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C)[-1])

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],C))[-1]

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}],\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,C))[-1],

which shows that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,C)\in\mathcal{G}\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}).\qed

By
1.1.30
, for
A,B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
there exists a regular cardinal
\kappa
with

A,B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))

and

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,B)=\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,B).

Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})\times_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))}\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
(
Lemma

2.8.36
), the condensed statement follows from the above.

Corollary 2.8.40
.

The localization
(-)^{L{\square}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
is symmetric monoidal.
The induced symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
is closed.

Proof.

We first show that the fiber of
(-)^{L{\square}}
is a tensor ideal, i.e. that for
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
with
A^{L{\square}}=0
and
B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,
(A\otimes B)^{L{\square}}=0
.
Suppose that
A^{L{\square}}=0
, and fix
B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
C\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
.
By
Lemma

2.8.39
,
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,C)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
, and hence

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}((A\otimes B)^{L{\square}},C)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A\otimes B,C)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,C))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A^{L{\square}},\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(B,C))

\displaystyle=0,

which shows that
(A\otimes B)^{L{\square}}=0
.
Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is stable and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is cocontinuous, it now follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.1.7.4]
that
(-)^{L{\square}}
is a symmetric monoidal localization.

Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a full subcategory and for
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
, the internal Hom
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,-)
restricts to a functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
(
Lemma

2.8.39
), this is a right adjoint to
A\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}-
.
∎

Lemma 2.8.41
.

The symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
is compatible with the
t
-structure.

Proof.

The unit
\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
is connective.
By construction of the symmetric monoidal structure, for
M,N\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
,

M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}N\cong(fM\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}fN)^{L{\square}}.

Since
(-)^{L{\square}}
is left adjoint to the
t
-exact functor
f
, it is right
t
-exact.
Since
f
is
t
-exact and the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is compatible with the symmetric monoidal structure, this implies that for
M,N\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})_{\geq 0}
,
M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}N\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\geq 0}
.
∎

Remark 2.8.42
.

In particular,
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure such that

H_{0}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})_{\geq 0}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}

enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor, see
[
Lur17
, Example 2.2.1.10]
.
This symmetric monoidal structure is closed with internal Hom

\pi_{0}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}(-,-).

Remark 2.8.43
.

As for
T,S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,

(2.8.43.1)

\displaystyle\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T\times S}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})^{\heartsuit},

the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}-
is the derived functor of
-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}}-
.
In more detail: Since the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
is right-complete and
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}-
is cocontinuous in both variables,
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}-
is determined by its valued on bounded-below complexes.

Eq.

2.8.43.1
and exactness of filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
imply that
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}-
can be computed on bounded complexes by resolving both variables with bounded below complexes
C_{*}
with

C_{n}=\oplus_{i\in I_{n}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{i}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}},S^{i}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}

for all
n\in\mathbb{Z}
.

By
Lemma

2.8.2
and
[
Rod24
, Corollary 3.4.3]
, for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\operatorname{light}}
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\operatorname{light}}]^{{\square}}
is flat. In particular, the category of light solid abelian groups has enough flat objects, which implies that for
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\operatorname{light}}
,
M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\operatorname{light}})}-
is the derived functor of
M\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\operatorname{light}}}-
.

An example of Efimov shows that that
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
in general does not have enough flat objects, so in particular,
M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}-
is not the derived functor of
M\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}}-
for general
\kappa
and
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.
More concretely,
M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}-
is the derived functor of
M\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}}-
if and only if for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})^{\heartsuit}
.
This holds for example if the condensed abelian group underlying
M
is pseudo-coherent, see
Lemma

2.8.59
below.

Lemma 2.8.44
.

Suppose
R
is a (
\kappa
-)condensed ring.

(i)

The forget functor

\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}

factors over an equivalence
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}})
.

(ii)

If
{R}
is commutative, then
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is a symmetric monoidal localisation. In particular,
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
inherits a cocontinuous symmetric monoidal structure such that
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor.
The enhancement
(-)^{{\square}{R}}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
of
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is essentially unique.

Proof.

The symmetric monoidal localisation
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
induces a localisation

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})})

with essential image

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
, cf.
Lemma

A.2.7
. The essential image are precisely the solid
{R}
-modules, which shows that
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}})
.

As
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
has small colimits (
Lemmas

2.8.15
and
2.8.30
) and the tensor product is cocontinuous in both variables (the symmetric monoidal structure is closed), for a commutative condensed ring
{R}
,
1.4.2
and
1.4.3
provide a symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}})
and a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
.
Suppose that
w\colon M\to N\in\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is such that
w^{{\square}{R}}
is an equivalence.
As
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor,
N\in\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
,
(w\otimes_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})}N)^{{\square}{R}}
is an equivalence. It now follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.1.7.4]
(in the large universe) that the localisation
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is symmetric monoidal and that the symmetric monoidal enhancement of
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is essentially unique.
∎

Lemma 2.8.45
.

For a profinite set
S
,
{R}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}{R}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}({R})
.
Every solid
{R}
-module is a quotient of
\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S^{i}}]^{{\square}{R}}
for some small family of profinite sets
(S^{i})_{i\in I}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
.
In particular,
\operatorname{Solid}({R})
has enough projectives.

Proof.

By
2.6.5
, for every condensed
{R}
-module
M
, there exists a small collection
S_{i},i\in I
of extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces with a quotient map
\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S_{i}}]\to M
.
If
M
is solid, this factors over a quotient map
\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S_{i}}]^{{\square}{R}}\to M
.
It remains to show that for a profinite set
X
,
R[\underline{X}]^{{\square}{R}}
is projective.

As its right adjoint is exact, the free
R^{{\square}}
-module functor
\operatorname{Solid}\to\operatorname{Solid}({R})
preserves projectives.
It therefore suffices to show that for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}
.
Fix
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})
and choose a regular cardinal
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(S)
. Then
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\cong i_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\lambda}])^{{\square}\mathbb{Z},\kappa}\cong\prod_{J}\mathbb{Z}
for a small set of cardinality
|J|\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
by
Lemmas

2.8.2
and
2.8.31
. We now show that for a small set
I
,
\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}
.

Lemma

2.8.2
and the universal property of Stone-Čech-compactification imply that if
S\coloneqq\beta(I)
is the Stone-Čech compactification of a set
I
, then

\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{Z})\cong{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(S,[-n,n]\cap\mathbb{Z})\cong{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\{-n,n\}^{I}.

There is a monomorphism
\oplus_{I}\mathbb{Z}\hookrightarrow{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\{-n,n\}^{I}
, whence by
Lemma

2.8.2
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}\cong\prod_{K}\mathbb{Z}
for a small set
K
with
|K|\geq|I|
.
This implies that
\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
is a direct summand of
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}\cong\prod_{J}\mathbb{Z}
.
As
(-)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
preserves projectives (its right adjoint is exact),
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
is projective, which shows that
\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
is projective.
∎

Lemmas

2.8.45
and
2.8.18
imply the following, which will be essential for our identification of continuous and solid group cohomology (
3.5.9
).

Corollary 2.8.46
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
. If
P,Q
are projective solid
{R}
-modules, then
P\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}Q
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
.

Remark 2.8.47
.

The analogue of
2.8.46
is very much not satisfied in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
:
For a strong limit cardinal
\kappa
, and a (
\kappa
-light) profinite space
X
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]\otimes_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X^{2}}_{(\kappa)}]
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
if and only if
X
is discrete by
[
CS19
, Proposition 4.8]
.

Proof.

Suppose
P,Q
are projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
.
Lemmas

2.8.45
and
2.8.18
imply that there exist small families of (
\kappa
-light) profinite sets
(S^{i})_{i\in I},(T^{j})_{j\in J}
so that
P
is a direct summand of
\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S^{i}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}{R}}
, and
Q
is a direct summand of
\oplus_{j\in J}{R}[\underline{T^{j}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}{R}}
.
Since
-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}-
is cocontinuous in both variables, this implies that
P\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}Q
is a direct summand of

\oplus_{j\in J}\oplus_{i\in I}{R}[\underline{S^{i}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}{R}}\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}{R}[\underline{T^{j}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}{R}}\cong\oplus_{i\in I}\oplus_{j\in J}{R}[\underline{S^{i}\times T^{j}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}{R}}.

As for all
i,j
,
S^{i}\times T^{j}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,

\oplus_{i\in I}\oplus_{j\in J}{R}[\underline{S^{i}\times T^{j}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}{R}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
by
2.8.18
and
2.8.45
, respectively.
∎

2.8.1
Examples and computations

In this section, we give some examples of solid modules and compute the derived and underived solidification of free abelian groups on compact Hausdorff spaces and CW-complexes. We will use these results to obtain further identifications of condensed with sheaf cohomology in to compute the condensed cohomology (
Section

2.9
), and to compare continuous with solid group cohomology (
Section

3.5.2
).

Lemma 2.8.48
.

Let
\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}
denote one-point compactification of the set of natural numbers, let

P\coloneqq\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}}_{(\kappa)}]/\{\infty\}\coloneqq\operatorname{Coker}(\mathbb{Z}[\{\infty\}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}]),

and denote
by

s\colon P\to P\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})

the homomorphism induced by

\mathbb{N}_{0}\cup\{\infty\}\ni n\mapsto\begin{cases}[n]-[n+1]&n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}\\
[\infty]&n=\infty\end{cases}.

The induced map
s^{{\square}}\colon P^{{\square}}\to P^{{\square}}
is an isomorphism.

Proof.

As
\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\},\mathbb{Z})\to\mathbb{Z}\oplus\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\mathbb{Z},\,f\mapsto(f(\infty),(f(n)-f(\infty))_{n})
is an isomorphism,

P^{{\square}}=\operatorname{Coker}(\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}[\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}]^{{\square}})\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\oplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\mathbb{Z},\mathbb{Z}).

Under this identification,
s^{{\square}}
is pullback along the isomorphism

\oplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\mathbb{Z}\to\oplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\mathbb{Z},(a_{n})_{n}\mapsto(a_{n}-a_{n+1})_{n},

and hence an isomorphism.
∎

Remarks 2.8.49
.

(i)

If
M
is a
(\operatorname{T1})
topological abelian group, then

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(P,\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})=\text{Null}(M)

is the abelian group of nullsequences in
M
, and the lemma implies that if
\underline{M}_{(\kappa)}
is solid, then

\text{Null}(M)\to\text{Null}(M),\,(a_{n})_{n}\mapsto(a_{n}-a_{n+1})_{n}
is an isomorphism, i.e. every nullsequence in
M
is summable.

(ii)

In light condensed abelian groups, summability of all nullsequences characterizes solid abelian groups, i.e. a light condensed abelian group
M
is solid if and only if

s^{*}\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{light}}(\operatorname{Ab})}(P,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\operatorname{light}}(\operatorname{Ab})}(P,M)

is an isomorphism, see e.g.
[
CS23
, Lecture 5]
or
[
Rod24
, Proposition 3.2.3]
.

Lemma 2.8.50

(
[
Sch21
]
)
.

Denote by

c\left(-\right)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{cH\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))

the functor induced by the constant sheaf functor.

(i)

For
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, there is a natural map

M^{L{\square}}\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z}).

(ii)

This is an equivalence for
M=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}],X\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}
.

Proof.

We first construct the map

M^{L{\square}}\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z}).

As
\mathbb{Z}
is solid, for all
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))

by
Lemma

2.8.39
, so it suffices to construct a map

M\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z}),

then this factors uniquely over a map

\eta_{M}\colon M^{L{\square}}\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z}).

The counit of the constant sheaf/global sections adjunction induces a natural transformation

\epsilon\colon c\left(-\right)\circ\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(-,\mathbb{Z})\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(-,\mathbb{Z}),

and the counit for
M\otimes-\dashv\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,-)
yields a map

E\colon M\otimes\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\to\mathbb{Z}.

By definition of
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(-,-)
, the composite

E\circ(\operatorname{id}\otimes\epsilon_{*})\colon M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[X],\mathbb{Z})\right)\to\mathbb{Z}

determines a map

M\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z}).

Denote by

\eta_{M}\colon M^{L{\square}}\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(M,\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})

the induced map. This is by construction natural in the derived
(\kappa)
-condensed abelian group
M
.

We now want to show that for
Y\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,

\eta_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]}
is an isomorphism.
By
2.8.28
/
Lemma

2.8.36
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}
is concentrated in degree
0
.
We first show that the right-hand side is also concentrated in degree
0
.
By
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2]
/
A.6.4
, for
Y\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)(\operatorname{Ab})})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathcal{C}(Y,\mathbb{Z})

is concentrated in degree
0
.
As the constant sheaf functor is
t
-exact, this implies that

c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\right)\cong\underline{\mathcal{C}(Y,\mathbb{Z})}^{\delta}_{(\kappa)}

is concentrated in degree
0
and represented by the discrete abelian group
\mathcal{C}(Y,\mathbb{Z})^{\delta}
.
By
Lemma

2.8.2
,
\mathcal{C}(Y,\mathbb{Z})\cong\oplus_{I}\mathbb{Z}
for some (
\kappa
-small) set
I
.
Since coproducts and (
\kappa
-small) products in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact and the constant sheaf functor preserves coproducts, it follows that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})\cong\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}

is concentrated in degree
0
.
We are therefore reduced to showing that
H_{0}(\eta_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]})
is an isomorphism.
By construction,

c\colon\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\xrightarrow{H_{0}(\eta_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]})}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{\mathcal{C}(Y,\mathbb{Z})}^{\delta}_{(\kappa)},\mathbb{Z})

is the map adjoint to

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]\otimes\underline{\mathcal{C}(Y,\mathbb{Z})}^{\delta}_{(\kappa)}\to\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\to\mathbb{Z},

where the first map is induced by the counit of
c(-)\dashv\Gamma
, and the second map by the adjunction counit for
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]\otimes-\vdash\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}],-)
at
\mathbb{Z}
.
By
2.5.27
, the first map is an isomorphism. The composite
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]\xrightarrow{c}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{\mathcal{C}(Y,\mathbb{Z})}^{\delta}_{(\kappa)},\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]^{\blacksquare}
is the map from the definition of solidity, whence
H_{0}(\eta_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}]})
is an isomorphism.

Denote by
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
the full subcategory on objects
M
for which
\eta_{M}
is an equivalence.
As
(-)^{L{\square}}
and

R\coloneqq\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(-,\mathbb{Z})\circ c\left(-\right)\circ\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(-,\mathbb{Z})

are exact,
\mathcal{C}
is a stable subcategory of
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
Suppose now that
M\in\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
and there exists a resolution
C_{*}\to M
with
C_{n}=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y^{n}}_{(\kappa)}],\,Y^{n}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
We claim that this implies that
M\in\mathcal{C}
.
For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
denote by
c_{n}\colon C_{*}^{\leq n}\to C
the map to from its stupid truncation.
As
(-)^{L{\square}}
and
R
are exact and right t-exact functors and

\operatorname{Cofib}(C_{*}^{\leq n}\to C_{*})\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{>n},

H_{k}(c_{n}^{L{\square}})\colon H_{k}\left((C_{*}^{\leq n})^{L{\square}}\right)\to H_{k}(C_{*}^{L{\square}})\text{ and }H_{k}(R(c_{n}))\colon H_{k}(R(C_{*}^{\leq n}))\to H_{k}(R(C_{*}))

is an isomorphism for
k<n
.
It is therefore enough to show that
C_{*}^{\leq n}\in\mathcal{C}
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, then it follows that
M\cong C_{*}\in\mathcal{C}
.
We prove this by induction on
n
.
The case
n=0
was shown above. The inductive statement follows since
C_{*}^{\leq n}\to C_{*}^{\leq n+1}\to C_{n+1}[n+1]
is a cofiber sequence,
C_{*}^{\leq n},C_{n+1}\in\mathcal{C}
, and
\mathcal{C}
is a stable subcategory.

Suppose now that
X
is a compact Hausdorff space.
By
Lemma

2.1.12
, there exists a quotient map
\pi\colon T\to X
from a
\kappa
-light profinite space
T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
. The simplicial resolution
S_{*}^{\pi}
of
\pi
(
Definition

1.5.16
) is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]
as above, which shows that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]\in\mathcal{C}
.
∎

Corollary 2.8.51
.

Suppose
X
is a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space and endow
\mathcal{C}(X,\mathbb{Z})
with the compact open topology which is discrete.

(i)

Then

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{\mathcal{C}(X,\mathbb{Z})}_{(\kappa)},\mathbb{Z})

naturally in
X
, where
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(-,-)
denotes the internal Hom of
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
.

(ii)

Denote by
\pi_{0}X
the set of connected components of
X
and endow it with the quotient topology of the projection
X\to\pi_{0}X
.
The projection induces an isomorphism
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}
.

(iii)

Endow the set
\pi_{0}^{\gamma}X
of path-connected components of
X
with the quotient topology from the projection
X\to\pi_{0}^{\gamma}X
. If
\pi_{0}^{\gamma}X
is Hausdorff, the projection induces an isomorphism
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}^{\gamma}X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}
.

Proof.

We first recall that for
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq 0}
and
B\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
, the counit
\pi_{0}A\to A
induces an equivalence

\pi_{0}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(A,B)\cong\pi_{0}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\pi_{0}A,B).

Fix
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))_{\leq 0},B\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
The cofiber sequences

\tau_{\geq n}A\to\tau_{\geq n-1}A\to H_{n-1}(A)[n-1]

imply that for
n\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\tau_{\geq n}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\tau_{\geq n-1}A,B)\cong\tau_{\geq n}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\tau_{\geq n}A,B).

As the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is right-complete (
2.6.14
),
{A}={\underset{n\to-\infty}{\operatorname{colim}}}\tau_{\geq n}{A}
, whence

\tau_{\geq n}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}({A},B)\cong\tau_{\geq n}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\tau_{\geq n}A,B)

by the above.

Since
c\left(-\right)
is
t
-exact,
Lemma

2.8.50
now implies that

\displaystyle\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}

\displaystyle\cong\pi_{0}\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\pi_{0}c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(c\left(\pi_{0}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})

\displaystyle\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\underline{\mathcal{C}(X,\mathbb{Z})^{\delta}}_{(\kappa)},\mathbb{Z})

naturally in the (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space
X
.

As
\pi_{0}X
is profinite (
Lemma

2.1.18
) and
\operatorname{wt}(\pi_{0}X)\leq\operatorname{wt}(X)
(
Lemma

2.1.7
), this implies that
X\to\pi_{0}X
induces an isomorphism

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}X}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}

and analogously for
\pi_{0}^{\gamma}X
, provided that this space is Hausdorff.
∎

Corollary 2.8.52
.

Suppose
M
is a topological abelian group.

(i)

If
M
is locally profinite (i.e. locally compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), then
\underline{M}_{(\kappa)}
is solid. This in particular applies to discrete abelian groups.

(ii)

If there exists an uncountable cardinal
\kappa
such that
\underline{M}_{\kappa}
is solid, then
M
is totally path-disconnected.

(iii)

If
M
is Hausdorff and
\underline{M}
is solid, then
M
is totally path-disconnected.

Proof.

We only prove the statement for condensed abelian groups, the statement for
\kappa
-condensed abelian groups can be shown completely analogously.
If
A
is a discrete abelian group, choose a presentation

A=\operatorname{Coker}(\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}\to\oplus_{j\in J}\mathbb{Z})
. As
\text{const}\colon\operatorname{Ab}\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
preserves colimits,

\underline{A}=\operatorname{Coker}(\oplus_{i\in I}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}\to\oplus_{j\in J}\underline{\mathbb{Z}}).

Since
\underline{\mathbb{Z}}
is a solid abelian group (
2.8.14
) and
\operatorname{Solid}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under small colimits, this implies that
\underline{A}
is solid. As
\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{Ab}(\operatorname{T1}\operatorname{Top})\to\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})
preserves limits and
\operatorname{Solid}
is closed under limits, it follows that limits of discrete abelian groups and in particular profinite abelian groups are solid. By van Dantzig’s theorem, every locally profinite abelian group
G
has a profinite open normal subgroup
N\subseteq G
.
Since
G/N
is discrete, the projection
G\to G/N
admits a continuous section (which need not be a group homomorphism) and in particular,
\underline{G}\to\underline{G/N}
is an epimorphism of condensed sets.
This implies that the sequence of condensed abelian groups

0\to\underline{N}\to\underline{G}\to\underline{G/N}\to 0

is exact.
Since
N
is profinite and
G/N
is discrete,
\underline{N}
and
\underline{G/N}
are solid abelian groups by the above.
As
\operatorname{Solid}\subseteq\operatorname{Ab}
is closed under extensions, it follows that
\underline{G}
is a solid abelian group.

Since
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{[0,1]}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}
(
2.8.53
), if
M
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological abelian group such that
\underline{M}
is solid, then

\mathcal{C}([0,1],M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{[0,1]}]^{{\square}},\underline{M})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}}(\mathbb{Z},\underline{M})\cong M,

i.e. every continuous path
[0,1]\to M
is constant.
∎

For a topological space
X
, denote by
\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X]\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}})
the free
\mathbb{Z}
-module on
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X\in\operatorname{Sp}
.
Denote by

c\left(-\right)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))

the functor induced by the constant sheaf functor (
1.3.44
,
A.2.7
and
2.6.9
).

Corollary 2.8.53

(
[
CS19a
, Example 6.5]
)
.

If
X
is a CW-complex, then

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X]\right)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}{}).

Remark 2.8.54
.

The singular chains functor
C_{*}^{\operatorname{sing}}\colon\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
descends to a functor
C_{*}^{\operatorname{sing}}(-)\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
. This functor preserves colimits and is therefore equivalent to
\mathbb{Z}[-]\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
.

Proof.

As every compact subspace of a CW-complex is contained in a finite subcomplex,

\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}={\underset{F\subseteq X}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{F}_{(\kappa)}

is the colimit of its finite subcomplexes.
It therefore suffices to show that for finite CW-complexes
F
, there is an equivalence
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{F}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right)
which is natural with respect to continuous maps.

Lemma

2.1.7
implies that finite CW-complexes are light compact Hausdorff spaces. Fix a finite CW-complex
F
.
By
2.5.8
,

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{F}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(F,\mathbb{Z})

naturally in
F
.
Since
F
is locally contractible, the functor

C^{*}_{\operatorname{\operatorname{sing}}}(-)\colon\operatorname{Op}(F)^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Ab})

which sends an open subset to its complex of singular cochains is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
. For all
k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
C^{k}_{\operatorname{sing}}(-)
is flasque, whence

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(F,\mathbb{Z})\cong C^{*}_{\operatorname{\operatorname{sing}}}(F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ab}}(C_{*}^{\operatorname{sing}(F)},\mathbb{Z})

is represented by the singular cochain complex of
F
. This identification is natural in
F
.
Since
C_{*}^{\operatorname{sing}}(F)\cong\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]
, it follows that

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ab}}(C_{*}^{\operatorname{sing}(F)},\mathbb{Z})\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F],\mathbb{Z})

naturally in
F
.

By
1.3.44
,
1.4.3
and
2.6.9
,
c(-)
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor.
In particular,

c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-)]\right)\otimes c\left(-\right)\cong c\left(-\right)\circ(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}-]\otimes-).

This determines an equivalence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F],-)\circ\Gamma\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right),-)

between their respective right adjoints, which is natural in
F
. As
\Gamma
is
t
-exact (
2.4.27
),
\Gamma(\mathbb{Z})=\mathbb{Z}
, whence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{F}_{(\kappa)}],\mathbb{Z})\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right),\mathbb{Z})

naturally in
F
.

Lemma

2.8.50
now implies that

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{F}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(H\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right),\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})

naturally in
F
.
Since
c\left(-\right)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is
t
-exact,

H_{i}(c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right))\cong c\left(H_{i}(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F])\right)

is solid for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
, whence
c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
by
Lemma

2.8.68
.
We show by induction on
\operatorname{dim}(F)
that the map

\eta_{c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right)}\colon\underbrace{\left(c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right)\right)^{L{\square}}}_{=c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right)}\to\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c\left(\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\right),\mathbb{Z})\right),\mathbb{Z})

from
Lemma

2.8.50
is an equivalence.
This then implies the statement since the target is naturally equivalent to
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{F}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}
by the above.
If
\operatorname{dim}(F)=0
, this holds by
Lemma

2.8.50
.
The inductive step follows as for an
(n+1)
-dimensional finite CW-complex
F
with
n
-sceleton
F^{n}
,

\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F^{n}]\to\mathbb{Z}[\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}F]\to\oplus_{n+1\text{-cells}}\mathbb{Z}[n+1]

is a cofiber sequence in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
and the full subcategory
\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab}))
on objects
M
for which
\eta_{M}
is an equivalence is a stable subcategory.
∎

2.8.2
Derived solid modules over
s
-flat rings

Since the category
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
generally does not have enough flat objects, it is not true for general condensed rings
{R}
that

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}).

We now characterize the rings for which this holds and give many examples below.

Definition 2.8.55
.

A (
\kappa
-)condensed ring
{R}
is (
\kappa
)-
s
-
flat
if for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,

{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})^{\heartsuit},

where
(-)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
denotes the left adjoint of
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
.

This definition is motivated by the following observation:

Proposition 2.8.56
.

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
extends uniquely to a small colimits preserving,
t
-exact functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}).

This functor factors over an equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})

if and only if
R
is (
\kappa
)-
s
-flat.

Proof.

We first prove the
\kappa
-condensed statement. The existence and uniqueness of the functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))
follows from
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
since
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}),\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
are Grothendieck abelian (
2.8.16
and
2.6.6
), see also
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
.

Suppose now that
{R}
is
\kappa\text{-}s
-flat.
We want to apply
[
Lur18a
, Remark C.5.4.11]
to identify

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}),

and we thank Ko Aoki for pointing out this reference to us.

Since
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
is Grothendieck abelian, the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})_{\geq 0}
is accessible by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.5.21]
. Hence by
Lemma

1.4.20
, the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
pulls back to a
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})
with

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})_{\geq 0}}).

As
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
is presentable (
2.8.19
) and its symmetric monoidal structure is closed (
2.8.40
),
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})
is presentable by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
.
By
Proposition

1.4.1
, the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
reflects small limits and colimits. In particular,
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})
is stable by
Lemma

1.4.26
.
As countable products and coproducts and filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
are exact,
{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}_{\geq 0/\leq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
are stable under countable products and coproducts and the
t
-structure is compatible with filtered colimits.
As the forget functor
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
reflects limits and colimits and is
t
-exact, this implies that

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0/\leq 0}\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})

are stable under countable products and coproducts and the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})
is compatible with filtered colimits. It now follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.1.19]
that the
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
is right and left-complete. The category

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0}
is prestable by
[
Lur18a
, Corollary C.1.2.3]
.
As the forget functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0}\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})_{\geq 0}

reflects small limits and colimits,
[
Lur18a
, Example C.1.4.5]
implies that
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0}
is Grothendieck prestable (
[
Lur18a
, Definition C.1.4.2]
).

Next, we show that
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0}
is
0
-complicial (
[
Lur18a
, Definition C.5.3.1]
).
Fix
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0}
. By
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.5.3.2]
, there exists
Q\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
with a map
q\colon Q\to fM\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
such that
H_{0}(q)
is an epimorphism. By
2.8.18
, we can assume that
Q=\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{i}]^{{\square}}
for a small family of
\kappa
-light profinite sets
S^{i},i\in I
. Denote by
p\colon{R}^{{\square}}[Q]\to M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})
the adjoint map.
As
R
is (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat, by definition of the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})
,

R^{{\square}}[Q]\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})^{\heartsuit}.

The map
H_{0}(p)
is an epimorphism. Indeed:
H_{0}({R}^{{\square}}[Q])
is the free
{R}^{{\square}}
-module on
Q
in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
, and
H_{0}(p)\colon H_{0}({R}^{{\square}}[Q])\to H_{0}(M)\in\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}})
is the map adjoint to
H_{0}(q)
.
As the forget functor
f^{\heartsuit}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
preserves colimits and
H_{0}(q)
factors as

Q\xrightarrow{\eta}H_{0}({R}^{{\square}}[Q])\xrightarrow{f^{\heartsuit}H_{0}(p)}H_{0}(M),

it follows that

0=\operatorname{Coker}(f^{\heartsuit}H_{0}(p))=f^{\heartsuit}\operatorname{Coker}(H_{0}(p)),

which shows that
H_{0}(p)
is an epimorphism.
This shows that
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})_{\geq 0}
is
0
-complicial.

By
Lemma

2.8.44
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})^{\heartsuit}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}}).

It now follows from
[
Lur18a
, Remark C.5.4.11]
that the equivalences of their hearts extends to a
t
-exact, small colimits preserving equivalence

\mathcal{D}({\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}).

By
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
/
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
, this is essentially unique and the forget functor

\mathcal{D}({\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})

factors over the above equivalence.

Conversely, suppose that
{R}
is a
\kappa
-condensed ring such that the forget functor factors over an equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}).

By
Lemma

A.1.6
, there exists a unique small colimits preserving, right
t
-exact functor

L\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))

such that for all projectives
P\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
,
L(P)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))^{\heartsuit}
and
H_{0}\circ L|_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}}
is the free
R^{{\square}}
-module functor.
The same argument as in the proof of
Lemma

2.8.23
implies that this is a left adjoint to the forget functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
.
In particular, for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}

fL(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}})\cong fR^{{\square}}[\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}]\cong{R}^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})^{\heartsuit},

which shows that
R
is
\kappa
-
s
-flat.

We now deduce from this the condensed statements.
Fix a condensed ring
{R}
and choose a regular cardinal
\mu
with
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\mu}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
By
Lemma

2.8.29
and
2.8.15
,

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}),\operatorname{Solid})\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}),\operatorname{Solid}),

where
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}
refers to small colimits preserving, exact functors.
By
2.8.32
,

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}),\operatorname{Solid})\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}\kappa\geq\mu\\
\kappa\text{ regular}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}),\operatorname{Solid}),

where
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}
refers to small colimits preserving,
t
-exact functors. This implies that

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}),\operatorname{Cond}({R}))}\{f\}

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\geq\mu}{\operatorname{lim}}}\Bigl(\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R}),\operatorname{Solid})}\{f|_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})}\}\Bigr)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\geq\mu}{\operatorname{lim}}}\Bigl(\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R})),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{ex}}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R}),\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda})}\{f_{\lambda}\}\Bigr),

where the limits run over all regular cardinals
\lambda\geq\mu
. By
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
/
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
, the right-hand side is contractible, i.e. there exists an essentially unique
t
-exact, cocontinuous extension
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
of the forget functor.

Suppose now that
{R}
is
s
-flat.
Lemma

2.8.36
implies that
{R}
is
\kappa
-
s
-flat for all
\kappa\geq\mu
. We claim that the forget functor

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})

admits a left-adjoint
L
, such that for all regular cardinals
\kappa\geq\mu
,
L(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
. Then it follows from the above and the Barr-Beck theorem
[
Lur17
, Theorem 4.7.0.3/Theorem 4.8.5.8]
that
f
factors over an equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})}).

Denote by
\Lambda^{r}
the poset of uncountable regular cardinals.
By the above, the forget functors assemble into a natural transformation

f_{*}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{*}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{*})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda^{r}_{\geq\mu},\operatorname{Pr}^{L})

and for all
\kappa\geq\mu
,
f_{\kappa}
admits a left ajoint
L_{\kappa}
.
Hence by
Lemma

A.1.2
applied to the opposite categories, it suffices to show that for all
\mu\leq\kappa\leq\lambda
, the mate

L_{\lambda}\circ i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}\to i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}\circ L_{\kappa}

of the diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}({R}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{\kappa}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{\lambda}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{\kappa}^{\lambda}}

commutes, then it follows that
L\coloneqq{\underset{\kappa}{\operatorname{colim}}}L_{\kappa}
is a left adjoint of
f
with

L(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}))=L_{\kappa}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))

for all
\kappa\geq\mu
. As
L_{\lambda},i_{\kappa}^{\lambda},L_{\kappa},i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}
are right
t
-exact, cocontinuous and carry projectives to the heart (since
{R}
is
\kappa/\lambda
-
s
-flat), by
Lemma

A.1.6
, it suffices to check that that for
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
,

H_{0}(\beta)\colon H_{0}(L_{\lambda}\circ i_{\kappa}^{\lambda})(M)\to H_{0}(i_{\kappa,R}^{\lambda}\circ L_{\kappa})(M)

is an equivalence. This holds since
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{\lambda}
is symmetric monoidal.
This shows the if-statement for
\operatorname{Solid}
.

Suppose now that
{R}
is a condensed ring such that the forget functor factors over an equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}).

By
Lemmas

1.4.9
,
1.4.31
and
2.8.29
, this implies that for all regular cardinals
\kappa
with

, the forget functor factors over an equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}),

whence
{R}
is
\kappa
-
s
-flat by the above statement on
\kappa
-solid modules.
As the functors

i_{\kappa}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})

are symmetric monoidal and for
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
,
i_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}})\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}]^{{\square}}
(

2.8.36
), this implies that
{R}
is
s
-flat.
∎

Remark 2.8.57
.

By
2.8.43
,
\kappa
-

-flatness is equivalent to
{R}^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}-

{R}^{{\square}}\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}}-
.

Example 2.8.58
.

If
\kappa=\aleph_{1}
, then
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is flat for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
by

and
[

, Corollary 3.4.3]
, and hence all
\aleph_{1}
-condensed rings are
\aleph_{1}\text{-}s
-flat.

Lemma 2.8.59
.

(i)

If
{R}
is a (
\kappa
-)condensed ring such that the underlying condensed abelian group
\underline{R}_{(\kappa)}^{{\square}}
admits a resolution
C_{*}\to\underline{R}_{(\kappa)}^{{\square}}
with
C_{n}=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{n}}_{(\kappa)}],S^{n}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, then
{R}
is (
\kappa
)-
s
-flat.

(ii)

If
G
is a Hausdorff topological group, the group ring
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is
\kappa\text{-}s
-flat.

Proof.

Suppose first that
{R}
is a (
\kappa
-)condensed ring such that the underlying (
\kappa
-)condensed abelian group
\underline{R}_{(\kappa)}^{{\square}}
admits a resolution
C_{*}\to\underline{R}_{(\kappa)}^{{\square}}
with
C_{n}=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{S^{n}}_{(\kappa)}],S^{n}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
.
By exactness of filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
and
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
, for
T\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,

{R}^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]\cong{\underset{m}{\operatorname{colim}}}(C_{*}^{\leq m}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]),

where
C_{*}^{\leq m}
denotes the stupid truncation.
Using the cofiber sequence

C_{*}^{\leq m}\to C_{*}^{\leq m+1}\to C_{m+1}[m+1],

it follows by induction on
m
that
(C_{*}^{\leq m}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}])
is computed by degreewise applying
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}
to
C_{*}^{\leq m}
, and that this is isomorphic to the degreewise
I
-fold product
(C_{*}^{\leq m})^{I}
where
I
is a set with
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\prod_{I}\mathbb{Z}
.
Hence by exactness of filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
,

C_{*}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong C_{*}^{I}.

As (
\kappa
-small) products in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
are exact,
C_{*}^{I}
is a resolution of
({R^{{\square}}})^{I}
, and in particular

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}{R}^{{\square}}\cong({R}^{{\square}})^{I}

is concentrated in degree
0
.

Suppose now that
G
is a Hausdorff topological group.
By
2.4.24
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq G\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}\cong\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},

and hence

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq G\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}.

As the colimit is filtered and filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
are exact (
Lemmas

2.8.15
,
2.8.30
and
2.6.3
),

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq G\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}).

By
Lemma

2.1.18
, for a compact Hausdorff space
K
, the set of connected components
\pi_{0}K
(with quotient topology from
K\to\pi_{0}K
) is profinite and by
Lemma

2.1.7
,
\operatorname{wt}(\pi_{0}K)\leq\operatorname{wt}(K)
. Hence by
2.8.51
, for
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}
,

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}K\times T}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})^{\heartsuit},

which shows that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]
is (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat.
∎

Example 2.8.60
.

If
{R}
is a (
\kappa
-light) profinite ring, then the Breen-Deligne resolution (
[
CS19a
, Theorem 4.5]
) for
\underline{{R}}_{(\kappa)}^{{\square}}=\underline{{R}}_{(\kappa)}
is a resolution as in
i)
of the above lemma. In particular,
\underline{R}_{(\kappa)}
is (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat.

Proposition

2.8.56
implies the following:

Corollary 2.8.61
.

Suppose that
{R}
is a (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat (
\kappa
-)condensed ring.
The functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

preserves small limits and colimits and admits a left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
.

Proof.

We first show that the forget functor preserves small limits and colimits.
As the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}-
commutes with colimits in both variables (
2.8.40
) and
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
has small limits and colimits (
2.8.19
and
2.8.32
), the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})

reflects small limits and colimits (
Proposition

1.4.1
).
By
2.8.27
and
2.8.33
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))

is closed under small limits and colimits.
By
2.6.13
,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})

and by
2.6.8
,
2.4.6
and
1.4.1
, the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))

reflects small limits and colimits.
As
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))}

commutes, this implies that

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

preserves small limits and colimits.
The functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}({R}))
has a left-adjoint by
2.8.33
.
Since
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})
and
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R})
are Grothendieck abelian, their derived categories
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))
are presentable by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.5.21]
.
As
f
preserves small limits and colimits, it follows from the adjoint functor theorem
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
that
f
admits a left adjoint

(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R})).\qed

Corollary 2.8.62
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a (
\kappa
)-
s
-flat condensed ring.
The left-tensoring of

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})

over
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
described in
1.4.7
exhibits

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))})
as
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
-enriched.

Proof.

By
2.6.8
/
2.8.32
,
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
has all small limits and colimits, and by
2.8.40
, the symmetric monoidal structure is closed. The statement now follows from
Lemma

1.4.8
.
∎

Remark 2.8.63
.

The solidification and the constant sheaf functor yield symmetric monoidal left adjoints

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}).

By the above, these functors exhibit
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
as enriched in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
Analogously,
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is enriched in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
,
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
and
\operatorname{Ab}
.

Lemma 2.8.64
.

For a (
\kappa
-
s
)-flat
\kappa
-condensed ring
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

factors as

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})\xrightarrow{q^{*}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{L{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})\xhookrightarrow{f_{LM}^{R}}

\displaystyle\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})),

where

(i)

the left equivalence is supplied by
Proposition

2.8.56
and the right equivalence by
2.6.13
,

(ii)

is restriction of scalars along the algebra map

q\colon{R}^{L{\square}}\to{R}^{{\square}}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})_{\geq 0})\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}))

provided by the unit of the localisation

induced by the symmetric monoidal left adjoint

H_{0}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})_{\geq 0}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}

(
A.2.6
).

(iii)

f_{LM}^{R}
is the right adjoint induced by the symmetric monoidal localization

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\rightleftarrows\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\colon(-)^{L{\square}}

cf.
Lemma

A.2.7
.

Proof.

All functors above are
t
-exact and on hearts, the composite

\displaystyle\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}})\xrightarrow{q^{*}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{L{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})^{\heartsuit}\xhookrightarrow{f_{LM}^{R}}

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)})})^{\heartsuit}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})

is the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})
.
Hence by
2.8.33
or
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
/
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
respectively, it suffices to show that
q^{*}
and
f_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
preserve small colimits.
This follows from
Proposition

1.4.1
since the symmetric monoidal structures on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
and
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
are cocontinuous (they are closed),
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is cocomplete and
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is closed under small colimits by
2.8.21
,
2.8.33
. ∎

For a (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat commutative condensed ring
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, endow

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})

with the symmetric monoidal structure described in
1.4.2
.

Corollary 2.8.65
.

Suppose that
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat commutative condensed ring.
The symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is closed and

(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor.

Proof.

By
2.8.19
and
2.8.32
, respectively, the category
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
has all small limits and colimits.
As the symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
is closed (
2.8.40
),
Lemma

1.4.5
now implies that the symmetric monoidal structure on

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})

is closed.
Since
(-)^{{\square}}=H_{0}\circ(-)^{L{\square}}
is symmetric monoidal, the adjunction unit enhances to a morphism of commutative algebras

\eta\colon{R}\to{R}^{{\square}}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))).

This exhibits
{R}^{{\square}}
as commutative algebra in
\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})
and by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 3.4.1.9]
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})})^{\otimes}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})^{\otimes}

as symmetric monoidal categories.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.8.5.22]
, the free
{R}
-module functor enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor

\displaystyle{R}^{{\square}}[-]^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})\to

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})})

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))})

\displaystyle\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}^{{\square}})),

where we used the identifications from
2.6.7
(which we also used to define symmetric monoidal structures on the derived category).

Let
S\coloneqq{R}^{{\square}}
.
Then

(-)^{L{\square}S}\circ S[-]\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}^{{\square}}))

is left adjoint to

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})\hookrightarrow

\displaystyle\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\eta^{*}}\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)})})(\operatorname{Ab}).

This functor is
t
-exact, preserves small colimits and restricts to the forget functor on hearts, and is therefore equivalent to the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
by
2.8.33
and
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1, Theorem C.5.4.9]
/
[
MW24a
, Proposition A.2]
, respectively. Hence,
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\cong(-)^{L{\square}S}\circ S[-]
, and we are reduced to showing that
(-)^{L{\square}S}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor.
Since
S^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\cong S
, by
Lemma

2.8.64
,

(-)^{L{\square}S}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(S))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{S^{L{\square}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(S))

is the functor induced by the symmetric monoidal functor

(-)^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})).

As
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
have small colimits, and the tensor products on both categories preserves small colimits in both variables (
2.8.40
and
2.6.11
),
(-)^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{LMod}_{S}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})^{\otimes}

by
Lemma

1.4.3
.
∎

Lemma 2.8.66
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat. The symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
provided by the above lemma is compatible with the t-structure, i.e.

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.

The induced symmetric monoidal structure on the heart
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is the one described in
Lemma

2.8.44
.

Proof.

By construction of the symmetric monoidal structure, restriction along the commutative algebra map
{R}\to{R}^{{\square}}
defines a symmetric monoidal equivalence
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}^{{\square}}))\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
. This functor is
t
-exact, we can therefore assume that
{R}={R}^{{\square}}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
. Denote by

f_{R}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(R))\rightleftarrows\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(R))\colon(-)^{L{\square}R}

the solidification adjunction.
Since
R^{L{\square}}\cong R
,
f_{{R}}
is fully faithful by
Lemma

2.8.68
below, i.e.
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}f_{{R}}=1
. As
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
is symmetric monoidal, for
M,N\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
,

(M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}N)\cong(f_{{R}}M)^{L{\square}{R}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(f_{{R}}N)^{L{\square}{R}}\cong(f_{{R}}M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}f_{{R}}N)^{L{\square}{R}}.

Since
f_{{R}}
is
t
-exact, for
M,N\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}
,

(f_{{R}}M\otimes_{{R}}f_{{R}}N)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}

by
Lemma

1.3.32
. As left adjoint of a
t
-exact functor,
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
is right
t
-exact, so in particular

(M\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}N)=(fM\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}fN)^{L{\square}{R}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}.

Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
contains the unit
{R}^{{\square}}
, it now follows from
[
Lur17
, Remark 2.2.1.2]
that
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.
In particular, by
[
Lur17
, Example 2.2.1.10]
,
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure such that
