\pi_{0}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))_{\geq 0}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is symmetric monoidal. This implies that
(-)^{{\square}{R}}
is symmetric monoidal as well, which shows that the induced symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
is the one described in
Lemma

2.8.44
.
∎

Remark 2.8.67
.

In the above situation, the tensor product
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}-
is the derived functor of the tensor product
-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}-
:
Lemma

A.1.6
and
2.8.32
imply that for a general commutative (
\kappa
-)condensed ring
{R}
, there is an essentially unique small colimits preserving, right
t
-exact functor

(-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}^{L}-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

such that

H_{0}\circ(-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}^{L}-)|_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\times\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}=-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}-

and for projectives
P,Q\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})
,
P\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}^{L}Q\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))^{\heartsuit}
.
We call this the derived functor of
-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}-
.

If
R
is (
\kappa
)-
s
-flat, then
-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}-
is such a functor.
For a general commutative, (
\kappa
-)condensed ring
{R}
, we are not aware of a way to construct a symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
which has
-\otimes_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})}^{L}-
as underlying tensor product.

Lemma

2.8.64
implies:

Lemma 2.8.68
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is a (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat ring which is
(-)^{{\square}}
-acyclic, i.e.
{R}^{L{\square}}\cong{R}^{{\square}}
.

(i)

The functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is fully faithful with essential image

\{M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\,|\,H_{i}(M)\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R})\text{ for all }i\in\mathbb{Z}\}.

(ii)

Denote by
g\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
and
g^{{\square}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
the forget functors. Then
g^{{\square}}\circ(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\cong(-)^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\circ g
.

(iii)

For
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})),B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(A,B)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})).

In particular,
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
preserves the internal Hom.

Proof.

We first show
(i)
. By
Lemma

2.8.64
,
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is fully faithful and its essential image consists of those
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
such that

gM\in\operatorname{Im}(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))).

By
2.8.26
and
2.8.37
, these are precisely those
M
with
H_{i}(gM)\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
. As
g
is
t
-exact, this shows
(i)
.
Since
{R}^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\cong{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
,
Lemma

2.8.64
implies that

(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})})

is the functor induced by the symmetric monoidal functor
(-)^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
(
Lemma

A.2.7
), whence

g^{{\square}}\circ(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\cong(-)^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\circ g,

cf.
A.2.8
.
It remains to show that for
B\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
,
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(A,B)\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R})).

Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
is closed under limits,
it suffices to show this for free modules
A={R}[c],c\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
which generate

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))})

under
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits (
2.6.13
and
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.7.3.14]
).
By the above description of the essential image of
f
, it is enough to show that

(2.8.68.1)

\displaystyle g(\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[c],B))\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})

for all
c\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.
The symmetric monoidal structure of the free
{R}
-module functor yields an equivalence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(c,-)\circ g\cong g\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[c],-).

Since
gB\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
, (
2.8.68.1
) now follows from
Lemma

2.8.39
.
∎

For a
(\kappa)
-
s
-flat,
(-)^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
-acyclic ring
{R}
, the essential image of the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

can be characterized as follows:

Corollary 2.8.69
.

Suppose
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
is (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat and
{R}^{L{\square}\mathbb{Z}}\cong{R}^{{\square}\mathbb{Z}}
.

For
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))
, the following are equivalent:

(i)

M
lies in the essential image of the forget functor
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
.

(ii)

For all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
, the adjunction unit
{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]\to{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}{R}}
induces an equivalence

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}{R}},M)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],M).

(iii)

For all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
, the adjunction unit
{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]\to{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}{R}}
induces an equivalence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}{R}},M)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}({R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],M).

Proof.

Clearly,
\ref{solidderivedrmodulesinternally}\Rightarrow\ref{solidderivedrmodules}
.

We now show that
\ref{essentialimagesolidrmodules}\Rightarrow\ref{solidderivedrmodulesinternally}
.
As
(-)^{L{\square}{R}}
is symmetric monoidal,
Lemma

2.8.68
implies that for
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
,

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(A^{L{\square}{R}},-)\circ f

factors over
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}{R})\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
and is right adjoint to

A^{L{\square}{R}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}-\cong(-)^{L{\square}{R}}\circ(A\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}-).

This implies that

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(A,-)\circ f\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))}(A^{L{\square}{R}},-)\circ f,

and in particular
\ref{essentialimagesolidrmodules}\Rightarrow\ref{solidderivedrmodulesinternally}
.

We now show that
\ref{essentialimagesolidrmodules}\Leftrightarrow\ref{solidderivedrmodules}
.
Since
{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
generates
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
under small colimits and shifts,

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}({R}))

is the localization at

\Sigma^{i}{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]\to\Sigma^{i}{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}{R}},S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)},i\in\mathbb{Z},

i.e. the essential image of
f
consists of those
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}({R}))
such that

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\Sigma^{i}{R}[\underline{S}]^{L{\square}{R}},M)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\Sigma^{i}{R}[\underline{S}_{(\kappa)}],M)

is an equivalence for all
S\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)},i\in\mathbb{Z}
. This shows that
\ref{essentialimagesolidrmodules}\Leftrightarrow\ref{solidderivedrmodules}
.
∎

2.9
Cohomology with solid coefficients

We now apply the above computations to compare
(\kappa)
-condensed cohomology with coefficients in solid abelian groups with sheaf and singular cohomology.

Notation 2.9.1
.

Since
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})})
(
2.6.9
), condensed cohomology enhances to a functor

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}),

cf.
1.5.4
.
In this section, we denote by

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,-)\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})

the restriction of this functor to
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
.

2.8.53
implies that cohomology with solid coefficients is homotopy invariant:

Corollary 2.9.2
.

Suppose that
h\colon X\to Y
is a homotopy equivalence.

(i)

For all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,
h
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}_{\kappa}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}_{\kappa}]^{L{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}).

In particular, for all
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})

h^{*}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{Y},A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X},A)

is an equivalence.

(ii)

If
X
and
Y
are
\operatorname{T1}
, then
h
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{X}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{Y}]^{L{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}).

In particular, for all
A\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
,

h^{*}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{Y},A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},A)

is an equivalence.

Proof.

As
(-)^{L{\square}}
is symmetric monoidal and
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{[0,1]}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}
(
2.8.53
), for a (
\kappa
-)condensed set
X
,

\mathbb{Z}[X\times\underline{[0,1]}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}=\mathbb{Z}[X]^{L{\square}}\otimes_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})}\mathbb{Z}\cong\mathbb{Z}[X]^{L{\square}}.

This implies that
\mathbb{Z}[-]^{L{\square}}\circ\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)}
inverts homotopy equivalences.
By
1.5.4
and
2.8.26
,
Lemma

2.8.36
, for
A\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,A)|_{\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})^{\operatorname{op}}}\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[-],A)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[-]^{L{\square}},A).

This implies the statement on cohomology.
∎

In the appendix, we show that gros topos cohomology with coefficients in constant sheaves inverts homotopy equivalences. Together with
2.9.2
, this implies the following:

Corollary 2.9.3
.

Suppose that
A
is a discrete abelian group.

(i)

For a topological space
X
, the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaftopological})

is an equivalence if and only if
X
is homotopy equivalent to a topological space
Y
such that the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(Y,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{Y}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaftopological})

is an equivalence.

(ii)

For a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space
X
, the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},\underline{A})\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaftopologicalwithoutkappa})

is an equivalence if and only if
X
is homotopy equivalent to a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space
Y
such that the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(Y,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{Y},\underline{A})\,\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaftopologicalwithoutkappa})

is an equivalence.

Proof.

It suffices to prove the
\kappa
-condensed statement, then the condensed statement follows from
2.5.4
.
Fix
\lambda\geq\kappa>|X|+|Y|
.
By construction of the comparison map, for a
\lambda
-small topological space
T
, the map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(T,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(T,\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,A))\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{T}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

is an equivalence if and only if

\mathcal{C}(-,A)\to\mathcal{C}_{k}(-,A)\to\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,A)=\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\to{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{T},A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{T},{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa}).

As
\underline{A}_{\kappa}
is solid (
2.8.52
),

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{-},{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{(-)}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\colon(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab}

inverts homotopy equivalences by
2.9.2
.

By
A.5.6
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{-},h_{A})\colon(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Sp}

inverts homotopy equivalences as well.
∎

Lemmas

A.5.4
and
2.9.2
and
Lemma

2.5.24
imply the following:

Lemma 2.9.4
.

Suppose
X
is a topological space which is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible topological space.

(i)

For all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
and all discrete abelian groups
A
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

via the comparison map (
2.5.6.2
).

(ii)

For a solid abelian groups
A\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
, denote by
A(*)^{\delta}
the discrete abelian group
A(*)
.
The counit of the global sections geometric morphism defines a map
\underline{A(*)^{\delta}}_{\kappa}\to A
which induces an isomorphism

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A(*)^{\delta}})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{*}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},A).

(iii)

If
X
is
\operatorname{T1}
, for all solid abelian groups
A\in\operatorname{Solid}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{*}(X,A(*)^{\delta})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},\underline{A(*)^{\delta}})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},A),

where the first equivalence is the comparison map (
2.5.7.1
) and the second map is the counit
\underline{A(*)^{\delta}}\to A
.

Proof.

Recall from
Lemma

2.8.29
that a condensed abelian group
M
is solid if and only if
r^{k}M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
for all regular cardinals
\kappa
. By
2.5.4
, it therefore suffices to prove the
\kappa
-condensed statements.

As for a discrete abelian group
M
,
\underline{M}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
(
2.8.52
), by
2.9.3
and
2.9.2
, we can assume that
X
is locally contractible.
By
Lemma

2.5.24
, it is enough to prove the statement for
X
contractible, and using
2.9.3
and
2.9.2
, we can reduce to the case
X=*
.

For
X=*
,
\operatorname{Shv}(X)\cong\operatorname{An}
, and under this identification, the geometric morphism

{i}^{*}\colon\operatorname{An}\cong\operatorname{Shv}(X)\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\colon{i}_{*}

is the global sections geometric morphism.
The global sections functor stabilizes to a
t
-exact functor (
2.4.27
), whence
{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}B=\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}B=\mathcal{C}(-,B(*)^{\delta})
for all
B\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
.
In particular, for all discrete abelian groups
B
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(*,B)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(*,\underline{B}_{\kappa})

via the comparison map.
By
1.5.3
,
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(*,-)
is the stabilization of the global sections functor.
As the global sections functor
\Gamma
is cocontinuous (
2.4.27
), the unit
\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{An}}\to\Gamma\circ c
is an equivalence. It follows from
1.3.4
that the unit
\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\to\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ c_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is an equivalence as well, whence the counit
\underline{A(*)^{\delta}}_{\kappa}\to A
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(*,\underline{A(*)^{\delta}}_{\kappa})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(*,A).\qed

Remark 2.9.5
.

For a locally contractible space
X
and a discrete abelian group
A
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\operatorname{sing}}}(X,A)

by e.g.
[
Sel16
]
.

2.9.3
and
2.5.19
imply the following:

Corollary 2.9.6
.

Suppose
X
is a topological space which is homotopy equivalent to a locally compact Hausdorff space.

(i)

For all discrete abelian groups
A
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

via the comparison map (
2.5.6.2
).

(ii)

If
X
is a
\operatorname{T1}
topological space, for all discrete abelian groups
A
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{X},\underline{A})

via the comparison map (
2.5.7.1
).

Denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor.

2.5.27
implies that the condensed structure on internal cohomology is constant in the following situation:

Corollary 2.9.7
.

Suppose that
X
is a (
\kappa
-)condensed set and there exists a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space
K
such that
\mathbb{Z}[X]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}
.

For all discrete abelian groups
A
, the counit

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(X,\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)\to\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(X,\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})

is an equivalence.

Example 2.9.8
.

By
2.9.2
,
2.9.7
in particular applies if
X=\underline{Y}_{(\kappa)}
for a (
\operatorname{T1}
) topological space
Y
which is homotopy equivalent to a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space.

Proof.

Denote by
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(-,-)
the internal Hom, by

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Sp})\colon H\mathbb{Z}[-]

the free-forget adjunction and let

\mathbb{Z}[-]\coloneqq H\mathbb{Z}[-]\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})).

By
Lemma

1.4.36
, this restricts to a functor
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set})\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
, and this is left adjoint to the forget functor.
The symmetric monoidal structure of the free module functor
H\mathbb{Z}[-]
yields an equivalence

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(-,f-)\cong f\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[-],-).

Since discrete abelian groups are solid (
2.8.52
),
Lemma

2.8.68
implies that

\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(X,\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\cong f\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[X],\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\cong f\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[X]^{L{\square}},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)}).

We can therefore assume that
X=\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}
is represented by a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space
K
.
The statement now follows from
2.5.27
.
∎

Remark 2.9.9
.

As the forget functor
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
is conservative,
Lemma

1.4.5
implies that for
X
as in the above corollary,

c\left(\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[X],\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[X],\underline{A}_{\kappa})

via the counit for the adjoint pair

c\left(-\right)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\rightleftarrows\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\colon\Gamma.

3
Group Cohomology

The condensed formalism yields a notion of group cohomology for topological groups which we study in this chapter. Our main focus is on its relation to continuous group cohomology and the condensed/singular/sheaf cohomology of classifying spaces.

First, we review the category of
G
-objects for a group object
G
in a big topos. This category is itself a big topos, and we define group cohomology as the cohomology of its terminal object and record some of its basic properties. Under mild conditions on a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, there is a
derived fixed-point functor

(-)^{G}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})

refining group cohomology (
Lemma

3.2.12
), which we also discuss very briefly.
Then we specialize to the condensed setting.
For a (Hausdorff) topological group
G
, the Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence (
1.5.13
) for the cover
\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}\to*
yields a natural comparison map

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,-)\to H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)})

from continuous to
(\kappa\text{-})
condensed group cohomology of the associated (
\kappa
-)condensed group.
Our comparison of sheaf and condensed cohomology implies that this map is an isomorphism in two important cases: For locally profinite groups
G
and solid continuous
G
-modules as coefficients (
3.3.7
), as well as for locally compact groups
G
and finite-dimensional, continuous real
G
-representations as coefficients (
3.3.9
).
However, we will see that condensed group cohomology is in general a much more refined invariant than continuous group cohomology.
In
Section

3.4
, we deduce from homotopy invariance of condensed cohomology with solid coefficients, that for a (Hausdorff) topological group
G
, condensed group cohomology with coefficients in a solid abelian group with trivial
\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}
-action is isomorphic to the condensed cohomology of a classifying space
BG
of numerable principal
G
-bundles.
For many topological groups
G
, the condensed cohomology of a classifying space
BG
is isomorphic to its singular and sheaf cohomology (
Section

3.4.1
).
This leads to plenty examples where condensed group cohomology differs from continuous group cohomology (
3.4.8
).
Finally, we show that for a large class of topological groups, continuous group cohomology with solid coefficients can be identified with
\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{Solid}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])}(\mathbb{Z},\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)})
.
This relies on the existence of enough projectives in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])
(
2.8.18
,
Lemma

2.8.45
) and the computations from
Section

2.8.1
.

3.1
G
-objects in a big topos

Definition 3.1.1
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and equip it with the cartesian monoidal structure.
A group object in
\mathcal{X}
is an algebra
G\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})
such that
\tau_{\leq 0}G\in\operatorname{Alg}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}^{\times})
is a group object, i.e. the shear maps

\displaystyle\tau_{\leq 0}G\times\tau_{\leq 0}G

\displaystyle\to\tau_{\leq 0}G\times\tau_{\leq 0}G

\displaystyle(g,h)

\displaystyle\mapsto(gh,h)

\displaystyle(g,h)

\displaystyle\mapsto(hg,h)

are isomorphisms.
Denote by
\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})
the full subcategory on group objects.
For a group object
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
denote by
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{G}({\mathcal{X}})
the category of left
G
-modules in
\mathcal{X}
.

In this section, we record basic properties of the category of
G
-objects in a big topos. We first show that this category is itself a big topos. Then we recall from
[
NSS15
]
that the
homotopy orbit functor

-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}

(
Definition

3.1.8
) classifies principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles (
Definition

3.1.17
) in
\mathcal{X}
. This will be central for our comparison of condensed group cohomology with cohomology of classifying spaces. To identify
G
-objects with principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles, we review simplicial models for
G
-objects. This also yields handy description of restriction and extension of scalars functors, which we apply to identify stable module categories in
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
with modules over the corresponding group rings (
3.1.27
).

Lemma 3.1.2
.

If
G
is a group object in a topos
\mathcal{X}
, then
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is a topos.

Proof.

By (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.1.0.6]
,
\mathcal{X}^{\times}
is presentably symmetric monoidal. (Cocontinuity of the cartesian monoidal structure follows from universality of colimits). By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.7]
, this implies that
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is presentable and that the forget functor
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}
preserves small limits and colimits.
Using that the forget functor is conservative, it is now straightforward to check that
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
satisfies Giraud’s axioms (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.1.0.6]
).
∎

Lemma 3.1.3
.

Suppose that
R\colon\mathcal{X}\leftrightarrows\mathcal{Y}\colon L
is a geometric morphism (
Definition

1.5.6
) between big topoi.

(i)

L
and
R
lift to an adjoint pair

L^{\operatorname{Alg}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{Y}^{\times})\colon R^{\operatorname{Alg}},

and
L^{\operatorname{Alg}}
preserves group objects.

(ii)

If
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object, then
L\dashv R
lift to an adjoint pair

L^{G}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\rightleftarrows{\mathcal{Y}}^{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}G}\colon R^{G}

and
L^{G}
preserves finite limits.
If
L
is fully faithful, so is
L^{G}
.

Proof.

Since
L
and
R
preserve finite products, they promote uniquely to symmetric monoidal functors (
[
Lur17
, Corollary 2.4.1.9]
) and in particular lift to an adjoint pair

L^{\operatorname{Alg}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{Y}^{\times})\colon R^{\operatorname{Alg}},

cf.
A.2.6
. Next, we show that
L^{\operatorname{Alg}}
preserves group objects.
By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.16]
,
L
and
R
restrict to functors
l\colon\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}\leftrightarrows\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{Y}\colon r
, and
\tau_{\leq 0}L\cong l\tau_{\leq 0}
since both are left adjoint to

(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{X})\circ r.

The functor
l
preserves products and therefore induces a functor
\operatorname{Alg}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}^{\times})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{Y}^{\times})
which preserves group objects. This shows that
L^{\operatorname{Alg}}
preserves group objects.

As explained in
Lemma

A.2.7
,
L
and
R
lift to an adjoint pair

L^{G}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\rightleftarrows{\mathcal{Y}}^{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}G}\colon R^{G},

and if
L
is fully faithful, so is
L^{G}
.
Since the forget functors
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}
and
{\mathcal{Y}}^{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}G}\to\mathcal{Y}
create limits (
Proposition

1.4.1
) and
L
preserves finite limits, it follows that
L^{G}
preserves finite limits.
∎

Together with
Lemma

1.4.9
, this implies:

Corollary 3.1.4
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi.

(i)

The equivalence
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})
restricts to an equivalence

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}).

(ii)

For
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
,
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is a big topos. If
\mu\in\Lambda
is such that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\mu})\subseteq\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
, then

\phantom{}{}_{\mu\backslash}{\Lambda}

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}

\displaystyle\mu\to\lambda

\displaystyle\mapsto{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}

is an exhaustion for
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
by topoi.

(iii)

In particular, for all
\kappa\to\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda
,

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\kappa}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}

are fully faithful, left-exact left adjoints.

Proof.

By
Lemma

3.1.3
, the equivalence
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})
restricts to a fully faithful functor

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}).

Since
\tau_{\leq 0}^{\mathcal{X}}
restricts to
\tau_{\leq 0}^{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
(
Lemma

1.2.5
), this is essentially surjective.
The remaining statements hold by
Lemma

1.4.9
and
Lemma

1.2.4
.
∎

1.4.12
implies:

Corollary 3.1.5
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and

\phi\colon H\to G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group homomorphism.
Restriction of scalars

\phi^{*}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{H}
along
\phi
admits a left adjoint
\phi_{!}\dashv\phi^{*}
.

Remark 3.1.6
.

If
\mathcal{X}
is presentable, i.e. a topos, then
\phi^{*}
also has a right adjoint
\phi_{*}
by
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
.
Being a right adjoint,
\phi^{*}
preserves finite products and hence enhances essentially uniquely to a symmetric monoidal functor

(\phi^{*})^{\times}\colon({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\times}\to({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\times}

by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 2.4.1.9]
.

1.3.30
implies the following:

Corollary 3.1.7
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and
\phi\colon H\to G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group homomorphism.
Denote by
\phi^{*}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{H}
restriction of scalars along
\phi
and by
\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})
its stabilization.
There is an essentially unique symmetric monoidal enhancement
\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})^{\otimes}
of
\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})
with

\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})^{\otimes}\circ\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\cong\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\circ(\phi^{*})^{\times}.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi such that
G,H\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
. For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\phi^{*}|_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}
factors as

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\xrightarrow{\phi^{*}_{\lambda}}{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}^{H}\subseteq{{\mathcal{X}}^{H}},

where
\phi^{*}_{\lambda}
denotes restriction of scalars along
H\to G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
, and by universality of colimits in
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
and
Proposition

1.4.1
,
\phi^{*}_{\lambda}
preserves small colimits.

Denote by

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda,\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\otimes})

the full subcategory on symmetric monoidal functors
F^{\otimes}\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\otimes}
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

F|_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})}\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})

preserves small colimits.
By
3.1.4
,
({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{*})^{\times}
is an exhaustion of
({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\times}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories.
By construction of the symmetric monoidal enhancement

\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\otimes}

(see the proof of
Proposition

1.3.26
), this implies that

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda,\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\otimes})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\times},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\otimes})}\{\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+,H}\circ\phi^{*}\}

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}(\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\otimes}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})^{\otimes},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\otimes})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})^{\times},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\otimes})}\{\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+,H}\circ\phi^{*}\}.

As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\phi^{*}|_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}}
factors as

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\xrightarrow{\phi^{*}_{\lambda}}{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}^{H}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}^{H}

and in particular preserves small colimits (
Proposition

1.4.1
), the right-hand side is contractible by
1.3.30
, i.e. there exists an essentially unique filler
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\times}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\otimes}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{\mathcal{X}}^{H}}^{\times}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})^{\otimes}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(\phi^{*})^{\times}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+,G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(\phi_{\operatorname{Sp}})^{\otimes}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\exists!}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\infty,\otimes}_{+,H}}

such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
(\phi_{\operatorname{Sp}})|_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})}
preserves small colimits.
It remains to show that this is a symmetric monoidal enhancement of
\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})
, i.e. that there is an equivalence
\phi_{\operatorname{Sp}}\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})
.
By
3.1.4
and
1.3.5
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H}))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda}({\mathcal{X}}^{G},{\mathcal{X}}^{H})}\{\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,H}\circ\phi^{*}\}

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}(\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H}))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H}))}\{\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,H}\circ\phi^{*}\}),

and the right-hand side is contractible by
1.3.20
.
It therefore suffices to show that
\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})
enhances to an element of the left-hand side.
By construction, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})|_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})}
factors as
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*}_{\lambda})}\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}}^{H})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})
and in particular preserves small colimits. It remains to describe an equivalence
\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,G}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,H}\circ\phi^{*}
.

As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\phi^{*}_{\lambda}
and
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
are left-exact left adjoints, the mate

\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,H}\circ\phi^{*}\circ({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,G}\circ({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}^{G})

of the outer square in the commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{X}}^{H}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{H})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{\infty}}

is an equivalence. As the mate of the left square is also an equivalence (
1.3.15
), it follows from the pasting law for mates (
[
CSY22
, Lemma 2.2.4]
) that the mate

\beta\colon\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,H}\circ\phi^{*}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\phi^{*})\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,G}

of the right square is an equivalence on
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
. As
\lambda
was arbitrary, this implies that
\beta
is an equivalence.
∎

Definition 3.1.8
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos.
If
i\colon H\subseteq G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a monomorphism, we denote by
\operatorname{res}^{H}_{G}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{H}
restriction of scalars along
i
and by
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{H}
its left adjoint.

For a group object
G\in\mathcal{X}
, we denote by
\operatorname{triv}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}
restriction of scalars along the group homomorphism
G\to*
. The left adjoint of
\operatorname{triv}
is called
homotopy orbit functor
and is denoted
-//G
.
If it exists, the right adjoint of
\operatorname{triv}
is called
G
-
fixed-point functor
and is denoted
(-)^{G}
.

We will show below (
3.1.16
) that if
\mathcal{X}
is a cartesian closed big topos,
G
-fixed-point functors exist for all groups
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
.

Simplicial models for G-objects

We now recall from
[
Lur17
, section 4.2.2]
that
G
-modules in a big topos can be described as simplicial objects encoding a coherent
G
-action on an object
X\in\mathcal{X}
.

Recollection 3.1.9
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos.
By
[
Lur17
, Propositions 2.4.1.7, 4.1.2.10]
and
Proposition

A.3.10
, there is a fully faithul functor

\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})

which sends a group object
G
to the simplicial object
[n]\mapsto G^{n}
with

\displaystyle d_{i}\colon G^{n}

\displaystyle\to G^{n-1},

\displaystyle(g_{1},\ldots,g_{n})

\displaystyle\mapsto(g_{1},\ldots,g_{i}g_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_{n})

and

\displaystyle s_{i}\colon G^{n}

\displaystyle\to G^{n+1},

\displaystyle(g_{1},\ldots,g_{n})

\displaystyle\mapsto(g_{1},\ldots,g_{i-1},1,g_{i},\ldots,g_{n}).

This is natural in the cartesian monoidal category
\mathcal{X}
.
The essential image of this functor consists of those simplicial objects
G\colon\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{X}
satisfying the following two conditions:

(i)

For all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the face maps

\{G([n])\to G(\{i-1,i\})\}_{1\leq i\leq n}

exhibit
G([n])\cong\prod_{i=1}^{n}G(\{i-1,i\})
.

(ii)

The map

\tau_{\leq 0}G([1])\times\tau_{\leq 0}G([1])\cong\tau_{\leq 0}G(\{0,1\})\times\tau_{\leq 0}G(\{1,2\})\cong\tau_{\leq 0}G([2])\xrightarrow{d_{1}}\tau_{\leq 0}G([1])

defines a group structure on
\tau_{\leq 0}G([1])
in
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}.

Lemma 3.1.10
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos,
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object and denote by

(*//G)_{*}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})

the corresponding simplicial object.
There is a fully faithful functor

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\hookrightarrow{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}.

Its essential image consists of the simplicial objects
X\to(*//G)_{*}
such that for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the maps

X([n])\to X(\{n\})\cong X([0]),\,\text{ and }\,X([n])\to(*//G)([n])\cong G^{n}

exhibit
X([n])
as
X([n])\cong G^{n}\times X([0])
.
This is natural in the group object
G
and with respect to finite products-preserving functors of big topoi.

Proof.

This follows from the discussion in
[
Lur17
, Chapter 4]
, see
A.3.13
.
∎

Note for future reference that the simplicial objects in the essential image of

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\hookrightarrow{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})

satisfy
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.1.2.6, 4”]
, i.e. are groupoid objects (
[
Lur09
, Definition 6.1.2.7]
).

Definition 3.1.11
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object.
Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi and
\mu\in\Lambda
with
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\mu})
.
Let

-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\subseteq{\underset{\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X_{\lambda}})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}\to{\underset{\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash\Lambda}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\xrightarrow{{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}}{\underset{\lambda\in\phantom{}_{\mu\backslash\Lambda}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\cong\mathcal{X}

and
\mathbb{B}G\coloneqq(-//G)(*)\coloneqq{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(*//G)_{*}
.

Since for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under finite limits and small colimits and
\Lambda
is filtered, this does not depend on the chosen exhaustion of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi nor the choice of
\mu
.

Denote by
-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
the induced functor

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/*}}\xrightarrow{-//G}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}.

We call
\mathbb{B}G
the
classifying space of principal

\infty
-
G
-
bundles
in
\mathcal{X}
. This terminology is motivated by
3.1.19
below.

Remark 3.1.12
.

By
Lemma

3.1.14
below, the homotopy orbits functor (
Definition

3.1.8
) factors as

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\xrightarrow{-//G}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\xrightarrow{(\mathbb{B}G\to*)_{!}}\mathcal{X},

where
(BG\to*)_{!}
denotes the forget functor. The above notation therefore does not clash with
Definition

3.1.8
.

Proposition 3.1.13

(
[
SS22
, Proposition 3.2.76]
)
.

The functor

-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}

is an equivalence.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi and
\mu\in\Lambda
with
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\mu})
.
Upon replacing
\Lambda
by
{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda
we can assume that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Since
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}_{\infty}
is closed under small colimits, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathbb{B}G\in\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
,
{{{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\subseteq{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
is a full subcategory and

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/*}}\xrightarrow{-//G}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}

restricts to

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\to{{{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}},

which is an equivalence by
[
SS22
, Proposition 3.2.63]
.
This implies that

-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/*}}\xrightarrow{-//G}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}

is an equivalence.
∎

We recall below that
\mathbb{B}G=*//G
classifies principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles.
In preparation for that, we describe extension and restriction of scalars along a group homomorphism in the above model. A group homomorphism
\phi\colon H\to G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})
induces a map
\mathbb{B}\phi\colon\mathbb{B}H\to\mathbb{B}G
.

Lemma 3.1.14
.

Suppose
\phi\colon H\to G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group homomorphism in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
.
Under the equivalences
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}},{\mathcal{X}}^{H}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}H}}
, restriction along
\phi
equals
\mathbb{B}H\times_{\mathbb{B}G}-
and its left adjoint
\phi_{!}\colon{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}H}}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
is postcomposition with
\mathbb{B}\phi
.

Proof.

Since
\phi_{!}\dashv\phi^{*}
, the description of
\phi_{!}
follows from the description of
\phi^{*}
.
Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi and
\mu\in\Lambda
with
H,G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\mu})
. Upon replacing
\Lambda
by
{}_{\mu\backslash}\Lambda
we can assume that
H,G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Denote by

\phi_{\Delta}\colon(*//H)_{*}\to(*//G)_{*}\in{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})

the image of
\phi
under
\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
.
This induces a map

\mathbb{B}\phi\coloneqq{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\phi_{\Delta}\colon\mathbb{B}H\to\mathbb{B}G\in\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}.

The pullback

{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}\xrightarrow{(*//H)_{*}\times_{(*//G)_{*}}-}{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//H)_{*}}}

exists since
\mathcal{X}
has finite limits and restricts to

\phi^{*}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{H}.

For
\lambda\in\Lambda
, the equivalence
-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
restricts to an equivalence
-//^{\lambda}G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\to{{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
, and in
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
,

-//^{\lambda}G\circ\bigl((*//G)_{*}\times_{\mathbb{B}G}(-//^{\lambda}G)\bigr)\cong(-//^{\lambda}G)

by universality of colimits in
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
This implies that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

\operatorname{id}_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}}\cong(*//G)_{*}\times_{\mathbb{B}G}(-//^{\lambda}G),

and hence

\operatorname{id}_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\cong(*//G)_{*}\times_{\mathbb{B}G}(-//G)

since
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
.
In particular,

\phi^{*}=(*//H)_{*}\times_{(*//G)_{*}}-\cong(*//H)_{*}\times_{(*//G)_{*}}((*//G)_{*}\times_{\mathbb{B}G}(-//G))\cong(*//H)_{*}\times_{\mathbb{B}G}(-//G),

so we are reduced to showing that the canonical map

\displaystyle(-//H)\circ((*//H)_{*}\times_{\mathbb{B}G}-)\circ(-//G))

\displaystyle={\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\left(((*//H)_{*}\times_{\mathbb{B}G}-)\circ(-//G)\right)

\displaystyle\to\left(({\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(*//H)_{*})\times_{\mathbb{B}G}-\right)\circ(-//G)=\mathbb{B}H\times_{\mathbb{B}G}(-//G)

is an equivalence.
As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is closed under finite limits and small colimits, it suffices to show the statement for
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
, where it holds by universality of colimits.
∎

The above implies that for a group object
G
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, the homotopy orbits functor
(-//G)
,
\operatorname{triv}
and the free functor
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}
satisfy the following relations:

Corollary 3.1.15
.

Suppose
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
.

(i)

Then

(-//G)\circ\operatorname{triv}\cong-\times\mathbb{B}G\text{ and }(-//G)\circ\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{X}}.

(ii)

For
X,Y\in\mathcal{X}
,
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(X\times Y)\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(X)\times\operatorname{triv}(Y)
naturally in
X
and
Y
.

Proof.

By
Lemma

3.1.14
, under the equivalence
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
,

\operatorname{triv}(-)\cong(-\times\mathbb{B}G\xrightarrow{\pi_{\mathbb{B}G}}\mathbb{B}G),

\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}\colon\mathcal{X}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/*}}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
is postcomposition with
*\to\mathbb{B}G
, and
-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\to\mathcal{X}
is the forget functor (i.e. postcomposition with
\mathbb{B}G\to*
).
This implies that

(-//G)\circ\operatorname{triv}\cong-\times\mathbb{B}G,\,\,(-//G)\circ\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{X}},

and for
X,Y\in\mathcal{X}
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(X\times Y)\cong(X\times Y\to*\to\mathbb{B}G)

\displaystyle\cong\left((X\times\mathbb{B}G)\times_{\mathbb{B}G}Y\to Y\to*\to\mathbb{B}G\right)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{triv}(X)\times_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(Y)

naturally in
X
and
Y
.
∎

This implies that if
\mathcal{X}
is a cartesian closed big topos, there exists a homotopy fixed-point functor

(-)^{G}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}

for all group objects
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
:

Corollary 3.1.16
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos such that the cartesian monoidal structure on
\mathcal{X}
is closed with internal mapping spaces
\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}(-,-)
.
Then

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\xrightarrow{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,-)}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,\mathbb{B}G)}}\xrightarrow{\{\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb{B}G}\}\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,\mathbb{B}G)}-}\mathcal{X}

is right adjoint to
\operatorname{triv}
.

Proof.

Denote by
q_{!}\colon{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\to\mathcal{X}
the forget functor, i.e. postcomposition with
\mathbb{B}G\to*
.
We have the following equivalences of functors

\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}}\times{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\to\operatorname{An}
:

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(-_{1},\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}

\displaystyle(\mathbb{B}G,q_{!}-_{2}))\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,\mathbb{B}G)}\{\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb{B}G}\}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(-_{1},\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,q_{!}-_{2}))\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(-_{1},\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,\mathbb{B}G))}\{\operatorname{const}_{\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb{B}G}}\})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(-_{1}\times\mathbb{B}G,q_{!}-_{2})\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(-_{1}\times\mathbb{B}G,\mathbb{B}G)}\{\pi_{\mathbb{B}G}\}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}}(-_{1}\times\mathbb{B}G,-_{2}).

By
3.1.15
, the right-hand side is equivalent to
\operatorname{Map}_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}}(\operatorname{triv}(-_{1}),-_{2})
.
∎

Principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles

We now recall from
[
NSS15
]
that the forget functor
{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\to\mathcal{X}
classifies
principal

\infty
-
G
-
bundles
.

Definition 3.1.17
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos topos and
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
.
For
B\in\mathcal{X}
, a map
E\to\operatorname{triv}B\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is a
principal

\infty
-
G
-
bundle
if there exists an effective epimorphism
p\colon U\to B\in\mathcal{X}
such that

E\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\operatorname{triv}U\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(U)\in{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}.

Lemma 3.1.18

(
[
NSS15
, section 3.2]
)
.

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
.

For
E\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\subseteq{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}
,

E\cong\check{C}(E([0])\to E//G)\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}},

where
E([0])\to{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}E=E//G
is the canonical map.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi such that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Then
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion of
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
by topoi (
3.1.4
).
For
E\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
E\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
.
The associated element
E\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}\subseteq{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}
is a groupoid over
(*//G)_{*}
, whence

E\cong\check{C}\bigl(E([0])\to{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}^{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}E\bigr)\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}

by effectivity of groupoids in the topos
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
Since
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under finite limits and small colimits,
this implies that

E\cong\check{C}\bigl(E([0])\to{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}^{\mathcal{X}}E\bigr)\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}.\qed

Corollary 3.1.19

(
[
NSS15
, section 3.2]
)
.

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
.

(i)

A map
p\colon E\to\operatorname{triv}B\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\subseteq{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}
is a principal
\infty
-
G
-bundle if and only if

E//G\xrightarrow{p//G}\operatorname{triv}(B)//G\cong\mathbb{B}G\times B\xrightarrow{\pi_{B}}B

is an equivalence.

(ii)

For
B\in\mathcal{X}
denote by
\operatorname{Bun}^{G}_{B}(\mathcal{X})\subseteq{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}
the full subcategory on principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles and by
(\operatorname{triv}B\to*)_{!}\colon{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}\xrightarrow{(\operatorname{triv}B\to*)_{!}}{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/*}}
postcomposition with
\operatorname{triv}B\to*
.
The functor

{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}\xrightarrow{(\operatorname{triv}B\to*)_{!}}{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/*}}\xrightarrow{-//G}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}

induces an equivalence

\operatorname{Bun}^{G}_{\mathcal{X}}(B)\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\times_{\mathcal{X}}\{B\}\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(B,\mathbb{B}G).

Proof.

We begin with the first statement.
Suppose that
E\to\operatorname{triv}B\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is a principal
\infty
-
G
-bundle and
p\colon U\to B\in\mathcal{X}
such that

E\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\operatorname{triv}U\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(U)\in{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi such that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, and choose
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
E\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
and
U,X\in\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
As
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under finite limits and small colimits (
Lemma

1.2.4
),
p\colon U\to X
is an effective epimorphism in
\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}
.
The functor
\operatorname{triv}\colon\mathcal{X}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
restricts to
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}\colon\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
, the restriction along
G\to*\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
.
Since
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}
preserves small limits and colimits,
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}(p)
is an effective epimorphism in
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
.
As colimits in
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
are universal and
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is closed under finite limits and small colimits (
3.1.4
,
Lemma

1.2.4
), this implies that

E\cong{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}E\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\check{C}(\operatorname{triv}p)

in
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
and
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
.
By
3.1.15
, for
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\displaystyle E\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\check{C}(\operatorname{triv}p)([n])

\displaystyle=E\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\operatorname{triv}U\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\operatorname{triv}\underbrace{(U\times_{B}\ldots\times_{B}U)}_{n\text{ times }}

\displaystyle\cong(\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(U))\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\operatorname{triv}\underbrace{(U\times_{B}\ldots\times_{B}U)}_{n\text{ times }}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(*)\times\operatorname{triv}U\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\operatorname{triv}\underbrace{(U\times_{B}\ldots\times_{B}U)}_{n\text{ times }}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(*)\times\operatorname{triv}\check{C}(p)([n])

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(\check{C}(\operatorname{triv}p)[n]).

This defines an isomorphism of simplicial objects
E\times_{\operatorname{triv}B}\check{C}(\operatorname{triv}p)\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(\check{C}(\operatorname{triv}(p)))
.
As
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\xrightarrow{-//G}\mathcal{X}
preserves colimits, it follows from
3.1.15
that

E//G\cong\left({\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}\check{C}(p)\right)//G\cong{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\check{C}(p)\cong B.

By construction, this equivalence is the composition

E//G\to\operatorname{triv}B//G\cong\mathbb{B}G\times B\xrightarrow{\pi_{B}}B.

For the converse implication of
(i)
, it suffices to show that for all
E\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
, the adjunction unit of
-//G\dashv\operatorname{triv}
defines a bundle map
E\to\operatorname{triv}E//G
.
By
Lemma

3.1.18
,

E\cong\check{C}(E([0])\to E//G)\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}},

whence
E([0])\to E//G
is an effective epimorphism in
\mathcal{X}
.
For
X\in\mathcal{X}
,

\operatorname{triv}X\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\subseteq{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}}

is the simplicial object

(*//G)_{*}\times X\xrightarrow{\pi}(*//G)_{*}\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}},

where
\pi
denotes the projection.

Lemma

3.1.10
implies that

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\subseteq{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)}}

is closed under pullbacks which are computed pointwise. This implies that
E\times_{\operatorname{triv}E//G}\operatorname{triv}E([0])
is represented by the simplicial object

[n]\mapsto E([n])\times_{E//G}E([0]),

where the pullback is computed with respect to the canonical maps
E([n])\to{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}E=E//G
.
By
Lemma

3.1.18
, this is equivalent to

\check{C}(E[0]\to E//G)\times_{E//G}E([0])\cong\check{C}(E([0])\times_{E//G}E([0])\xrightarrow{\pi_{1}}E([0])),

and

(E([0])\times_{E//G}E([0])\xrightarrow{\pi_{1}}E([0]))\cong(d_{1}\colon E([1])\to E([0]))

is the face map of the simplicial object
E
. By
Lemma

3.1.10
,

(d_{1}\colon E([1])\to E([0]))\cong(G\times E([0])\xrightarrow{\pi_{E([0])}}E([0])).

This shows that

E\times_{\operatorname{triv}E//G}\operatorname{triv}E([0])\cong\check{C}(G\to*)\times E([0])\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(E[0])\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/(*//G)_{*}}},

which proves the characterization of bundles.

For
B\in\mathcal{X}
, the equivalence
-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
induces an equivalence

{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/B\times\mathbb{B}G}}.

Denote by

\pi\colon{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/B\times\mathbb{B}G}}\xrightarrow{(B\times\mathbb{B}G\to B)_{!}}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/B}}

the composition of this equivalence with postcomposition with the projection
B\times\mathbb{B}G\to B
.
By the above characterization of bundles,
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Bun}^{G}_{\mathcal{X}}(B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\{\operatorname{id}_{B}\}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{\mathcal{X}}_{/B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi}

is a pullback.
As
{{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}_{/\operatorname{triv}B}}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/B\times\mathbb{B}G}}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/B}}\times_{\mathcal{X}}{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
, it follows that

\operatorname{Bun}^{G}_{\mathcal{X}}(B)\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}\times_{\mathcal{X}}\{B\}=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{X}}(B,\mathbb{B}G).\qed

We have shown in the above proof that for all
E\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
, the adjunction unit for
(-//G)\dashv\operatorname{triv}
evaluates to a principal
\infty
-
G
-bundle
E\to\operatorname{triv}E//G
.
In particular, there is no distinction between objects with an
\infty
-
G
-action and (total spaces) of principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles.
The unit evaluates to a principal
\infty
-
G
-bundle
*\to\operatorname{triv}\mathbb{B}G
, where
*
denotes the terminal object of
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
.
One should think of this as the universal principal
\infty
-
G
-bundle: The above proof shows that for
E\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
,

E\cong E//G\times_{\mathbb{B}G}*\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G},

i.e.
E
is
classified
by the map
(E\to*)//G\colon E//G\to\mathbb{B}G
.

Corollary 3.1.20
.

For a group object
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
,

\Omega\mathbb{B}G\cong G\in\mathcal{X}.

Proof.

By
Lemma

3.1.18
,

G\cong(*//G)_{*}([1])\cong\check{C}(*\to\mathbb{B}G)([1])\cong*\times_{\mathbb{B}G}*\cong\Omega\mathbb{B}G.\qed

Modules over group rings

Definition 3.1.21
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos. The symmetric monoidal functor

\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\colon\mathcal{X}^{\times}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\otimes}\text{ (\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{symmetricmonoidalstructureonspectrumobjects})}

induces a functor
\mathbb{S}[-]\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
.
Recall from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.4.3/Example 3.2.4.4]
that for a symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
,
\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
admits a monoidal structure such that the forget functor
\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{C}
enhances to a monoidal functor.
For a ring spectrum
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
and a group object
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
, the
{R}
-linear
group ring
of
G
is

{R}[G]\coloneqq{R}\otimes_{\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))}\mathbb{S}[G]\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})).

Our next goal is to show that under mild conditions on a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, there is an equivalence

\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}),

see
3.1.27
below.

Lemma 3.1.22
.

Suppose that
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
.
The stabilization (
Definition

1.3.3
) of
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}
factors over an equivalence

\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\xrightarrow{f}\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),

where
f
denotes the forget functor.

Proof.

For a symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{C}
,
\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C}),c\mapsto c\otimes-
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor, where
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})
is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure given by composition, cf.
[
Lur17
, page 656]
/
A.3.14
.

The forget functor
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}=\operatorname{LMod}_{G}({\mathcal{X}})\to\mathcal{X}
exhibits
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
as monadic over
\mathcal{X}
with monad

G\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{X})).

Hence by
[
Lur17
, Example 4.7.3.10/Theorem 4.7.3.5]
, its stabilization exhibits
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
as monadic over
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
with monad

\operatorname{Sp}(G\times-)=\mathbb{S}[G]\otimes-\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))),

i.e.
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
.
∎

Remark 3.1.23
.

If it exists, a commutative enhancement of
G
determines a commutative enhancement of
\mathbb{S}[G]
which defines a symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
. For
G\neq 0
, this is different from the structure induced by the cartesian monoidal structure on
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
: The forget functor
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is symmetric monoidal, which fails for the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
induced by the commutative algebra structure of
\mathbb{S}[G]
(if
G\neq 0
).

Definition 3.1.24
.

If
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, denote by
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
the stabilization of the restriction
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\mathcal{X}
.
By
Lemma

3.1.22
and
Proposition

1.4.1
,
this admits a left adjoint which we denote by
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
.

Remark 3.1.25
.

Since
\Omega^{\infty}\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\cong\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*}\Omega^{\infty}
,
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
.

1.3.20
and
3.1.15
imply the following:

Lemma 3.1.26
.

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
.
There is a preferred equivalence

\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1})\otimes\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1})\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1}\otimes-_{2})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})).

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi such that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Denote by

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda,v}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}))

the full subcategory on functors
F
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
F|_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})}
preserves small colimits separately in both variables.
Recall from
Lemma

1.3.5
that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{*})
is an exhaustion of
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
by presentable categories.
By construction (see the proof of
Lemma

1.3.10
),

\Sigma^{\infty}_{\mathcal{X},+}={\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\left((\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}\right).

Alternatively, this follows from
1.3.15
and
1.2.4
.

1.3.20
and
A.1.4
now imply that

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda,v}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}))

\displaystyle\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\times\mathcal{X}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}))\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{X},\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})),

\displaystyle F

\displaystyle\mapsto F\circ(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\times\Sigma^{\infty}_{+})

is fully faithful. We now explain that

\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1})\otimes\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1}),\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1}\otimes-_{2})\in\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda,v}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})).

By construction (
1.4.12
),
\operatorname{triv}
restricts to
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}\colon\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
, and hence
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
restricts to
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})
.
This functor is cocontinuous.
As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{*})^{\otimes}
is an exhaustion of
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\otimes}
by presentably symmetric monoidal categories, the proof of
1.4.12
shows that
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
restricts to left adjoints

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
.
Since
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
and
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
are presentably symmetric monoidal subcategories (
Definitions

1.3.24
and
1.3.26
), it follows that

\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1})\otimes\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1}),\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-_{1}\otimes-_{2})\in\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\Lambda,v}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})).

We are therefore reduced to describing an equivalence

\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-_{1})\otimes\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-_{2})\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-1)\otimes\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-_{2})).

Since
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}
and
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\operatorname{triv}
(
3.1.25
and
3.1.7
),
symmetric monoidality of
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
yields an equivalence

\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-_{1})\otimes\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-_{2})\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(-_{1})\times\operatorname{triv}(-_{1})).

By
3.1.15
,
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(-_{1})\times\operatorname{triv}(-_{2})\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(-_{1}\times-_{2})
, whence

\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(-_{1})\times\operatorname{triv}(-_{2}))\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(-_{1}\times-_{2}).

As
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}
and
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}
is symmetric monoidal, the right-hand side is equivalent to
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-_{1})\otimes\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}(-_{2}))
.
∎

Corollary 3.1.27
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
admits
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
and
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}).

Proof.

The symmetric monoidal functor
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
(
3.1.7
) exhibits
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
as left-tensored over
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
. We claim that this is the left tensoring induced by the cocartesian fibration of operads

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\otimes}\times_{\operatorname{Comm}^{\otimes}}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{B}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}

as described in
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.3.3.7]
, then the statement follows from
Lemma

A.2.9
. We will deduce this from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.5.8]
.
By
Lemma

3.1.22
,
Proposition

1.4.1
,
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is conservative and preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits.
By
3.1.7
, it enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor, which implies that the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
Since

\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}=\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})},

it follows that
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits. This shows that the action map

-\otimes-\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\times\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})

preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
By
Lemma

3.1.26
,

L\coloneqq\mathbb{S}[G]\otimes-\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})

is equivalent to
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-)
, and hence right adjoint to
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
.
For
m\in\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
and
x\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
, the counit
\epsilon\colon L\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\to\operatorname{id}
and the identification
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-\otimes-)\cong\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-\otimes-)
from the proof of
Lemma

3.1.26
induce a map

c_{x,m}\colon L(x\otimes\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}m)\cong\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(x)\otimes L(\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}m)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}\otimes\epsilon}\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(x)\otimes m.

By construction of the identification
L(x\otimes\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}m)\cong\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(x)\otimes L(\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}m)
, the adjoint map

x\otimes\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}m\to\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}x\otimes m)

is an equivalence.

[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.5.8]
now implies that there exists a
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
-linear equivalence

\operatorname{RMod}_{A}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}),

where
A=\operatorname{Mor}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\mathbb{S}[G],\mathbb{S}[G])
the endomorphism algebra of
\mathbb{S}[G]
and
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
is left-tensored over
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
via
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\otimes}
.
The algebra structure on
A
is induced by the counit for
L\dashv\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
and the equivalence
c_{\mathbb{S}[G],S[G]}
, i.e. under the fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\otimes}_{\operatorname{rev}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})))

induced by the symmetric monoidal functor

\displaystyle\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})_{\operatorname{rev}}

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))

\displaystyle c

\displaystyle\mapsto c\otimes-,

A
becomes the endomorphism monad of the adjunction
L\dashv\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
. By
Lemma

3.1.22
, the equivalence

L\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-)

yields an equivalence
A\cong\mathbb{S}[G]^{\operatorname{rev}}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})).

∎

3.1.27
and
Lemma

1.4.32
imply the following:

Corollary 3.1.28
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos with the following properties:

(i)

\mathcal{X}
admits an exhaustion (
Definition

1.2.1
) by hypercomplete, 1-localic topoi,

(ii)

\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
has countable coproducts,

(iii)

\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
preserves them in both variables.

For a discrete group
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
and
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}))
,
