\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}R}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}).

3.1.28
in particular applies to
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
, or more generally to categories of accessible hypersheaves on a hyperaccessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
with
\mathcal{C}
is a 1-category.

Proof.

By
3.1.27
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}).

The statement now follows from
Lemma

1.4.32
.
∎

We will use the following observation to describe
{R}
-linear enhancements of group cohomology, see
3.2.4
below.

Lemma 3.1.29
.

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
. Denote by
c_{\mathcal{X}}\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{X}
and
c_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\colon\operatorname{An}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
the constant sheaf functors (
Definition

1.3.42
) for
\mathcal{X}
and
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
, respectively.

There is an essentially unique equivalence
\operatorname{triv}\circ c_{\mathcal{X}}=c_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}
.

Proof.

By
Lemma

1.3.41
, it suffices to show that

\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{c_{\mathcal{X}}}\mathcal{X}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{triv}}{\mathcal{X}}^{G}

preserves colimits and the terminal object. Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi and
\lambda\in\Lambda
with
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
.
Then
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{X}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{triv}}{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
factors as
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}}{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
, where
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}
denotes restriction of scalars along
G\to*\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
. By
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.9]
and
3.1.5

\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}
is a left-exact left adjoint, and by
3.1.4
and
1.2.4
,
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
is a left-exact left adjoint.

Lemmas

1.2.4
and
1.3.41
imply that the constant sheaf functor for
\mathcal{X}
factors as
\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{c_{\lambda}}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{X}
, where
c_{\lambda}
denotes the constant sheaf functor for
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
This shows that
\operatorname{triv}\circ c_{\mathcal{X}}
preserves colimits and the terminal object, and hence there is an essentially unique equivalence
\operatorname{triv}\circ c_{\mathcal{X}}\cong c_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}
.
∎

Remark 3.1.30
.

The essentally unique equivalence
\operatorname{triv}\circ c_{\mathcal{X}}\cong c_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}
defines a mate transformation

\beta\colon\Gamma_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\circ\operatorname{triv}\to\Gamma_{\mathcal{X}},

where
\Gamma_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}
,
\Gamma_{\mathcal{X}}
denote the global sections functors of
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
and
\mathcal{X}
, respectively. This stabilizes to a natural transformation

\beta_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\Gamma_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G},\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\to\Gamma_{\mathcal{X},\operatorname{Sp}}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}).

By
1.3.4
,
\beta_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is the Beck-Chevalley transformation associated to the commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{id}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}}

The symmetric monoidal structure of
c_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})},c_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}
(
1.3.44
) and
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
(
3.1.7
) determine an enhancement of
\beta_{\operatorname{Sp}}
to a transformation of lax symmetric monoidal functors. This follows from
Lemma

A.2.3
. In particular, we obtain a natural transformation

\beta_{\operatorname{Alg},\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\Gamma_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G},\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\to\Gamma_{\mathcal{X},\operatorname{Sp}}\in\operatorname{Fun}\left(\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})),\operatorname{(C)Alg}(\operatorname{Sp})\right)

between the induced functors on (commutative) algebra objects.

3.2
Group cohomology in a big topos

We are now prepared to discuss two notions of group cohomology in a big topos.

Definition 3.2.1

(Group cohomology)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos and
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object.

(i)

Define
group cohomology
of
G
in
\mathcal{X}
as

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\coloneqq\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}(*,-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})

the cohomology (
Definition

1.5.1
) of the terminal object in the big topos
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
.

(ii)

If
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
admits a right adjoint, we denote it by

\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}})

and refer to it as
internal group cohomology
of
G
in
\mathcal{X}
.

Remarks 3.2.2
.

1.

Group cohomology is the stabilization (
Definition

1.3.3
) of the global sections functor
\Gamma_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\to\operatorname{An}
(
Definition

1.3.42
), cf.
1.5.3
.

2.

Denote by
\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp},\mathcal{X}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}
the stabilization of the global sections functor in
\mathcal{X}
.
If internal group cohomology exists, then

\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)

since both are right adjoint to the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor
c_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\colon\operatorname{An}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
, which factors as
\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{c_{\mathcal{X}}}\mathcal{X}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{triv}}{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
by
Lemma

3.1.29
.

3.

Internal group cohomology is not internal cohomology of the terminal object in the topos
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
(
Definition

1.5.1
), the latter is the identity
\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}
.

4.

If
\mathcal{X}
is cartesian closed, then
\operatorname{triv}
has a right adjoint by
3.1.16
, and hence internal group cohomology
\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)=(-)^{G}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
exists for all groups
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
by
1.3.4
.

Remark 3.2.3
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos which admits an exhaustion by hypercomplete, 1-localic topoi,
\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
admits countable coproducts,
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
preserves them in both variables. This holds for example if
\mathcal{X}=\operatorname{hypShv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C})
for a hyperaccessible explicit covering site
(\mathcal{C},S)
with
\mathcal{C}
a
1
-category, e.g.
\mathcal{X}=\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.

By
3.1.28
, for
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\heartsuit})
and
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})).

Denote by
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
the forget functor.
Then

H_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(G,f-)\cong\pi_{-*}\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})}({R},-)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}({R},-)

by
1.3.40
.

Remarks 3.2.4
.

It is natural to consider the following enhancements of group cohomology:

1.

As group cohomology is right adjoint to the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor
c_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
(
1.5.3
),
1.3.44
determines an enhancement of group cohomology to a lax symmetric monoidal functor

\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Sp}^{\otimes},

cf.
Lemma

A.2.3
. In particular, for
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
, group cohomology enhances to a functor

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)_{R}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}}).

For
{R}\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
, restriction of scalars along the algebra map
\beta_{R}\colon\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}{R}\to\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}
decribed in
3.1.30
yields a functor

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)_{R}\coloneqq\beta_{R}^{*}\circ H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)_{\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}})

enhancing group cohomology.

2.

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos such that internal group cohomology of
G
in
\mathcal{X}
exists. For every
{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))
, internal group cohomology enhances to a functor

\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}R}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}).

Indeed, the symmetric monoial structure of
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
determines an enhancement of
\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)
to a lax symmetric monoidal functor. This implies that
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)
enhances to an adjoint pair

\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{R}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}})})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})\colon\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)_{R}

such that
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{triv}{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G{,}-)_{R}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G{,}-)}

commutes, cf.
Lemma

A.2.7
.

Lemma

3.1.3
and
Lemma

1.5.7
imply that group cohomology is invariant under geometric morphisms:

Corollary 3.2.5
.

Suppose that
R\colon\mathcal{Y}\leftrightarrows\mathcal{X}\colon L
is a geometric morphism and
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
.
By
Lemma

3.1.3
,
K\coloneqq L^{\operatorname{Alg}}G\in in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{Y})\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{Y})
. Denote by

R^{G}\colon{\mathcal{Y}}^{K}\leftrightarrows{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\colon L^{G}

the induced adjunction (
Lemma

3.1.3
).

Then

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong H_{\mathcal{Y}}(K,R^{G}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-).

In particular, group cohomology in a big topos can always be computed in a subcategory which is a topos:

Corollary 3.2.6
.

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}_{\infty}
is a big topos and
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is an exhaustion of
\mathcal{X}_{\infty}
by topoi.
Suppose
\lambda\in\Lambda
is such that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\infty})
, denote by

r_{\lambda}\colon\mathcal{X_{\infty}}\to\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}

the right adjoint of
\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{X_{\infty}}
(
Lemma

1.2.4
), and by
r^{G}_{\lambda}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\infty}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{{\lambda}}
the induced right adjoint (
Lemma

3.1.3
).
Then

H_{\mathcal{X}_{\infty}}(G,-)\cong H_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(G,-)\circ(r_{\lambda}^{G})_{\operatorname{Sp}},

and in particular,

H_{\mathcal{X}_{\infty}}(G,-)|_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})}=H_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(G,-).

If
G
is a discrete group, group cohomology with coefficients in a trivial
\mathbb{Z}[G]
-module is isomorphic to the singular/sheaf cohomology of the classifying space
BG
of numerable principal
G
-bundles.
This has the following generalization:

Proposition 3.2.7
.

Suppose
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
and denote by
\mathbb{B}G
the classifying space of principal
\infty
-
G
-bundles in
\mathcal{X}
(
Definition

3.1.11
).
The adjunction
-//G\dashv\operatorname{triv}
induces an equivalence

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\circ\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,-)

of functors
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}
.

Remark 3.2.8
.

For a group object
G
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
,
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
is
t
-exact.
Indeed: Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi such that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
. By construction,
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
restricts to
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
(the stabilization of restriction of scalars along
G\to*\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
), and since
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}
admits a right adjoint,
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact by
Lemma

1.3.16
. By construction of the
t
-structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
(
Lemma

1.3.12
), this implies that
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact. In particular, if
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
, then
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
restricts to a functor

\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{\heartsuit}\colon\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})^{\heartsuit}\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\heartsuit}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})

which endows an abelian group object
M\in\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
with the trivial
G
-action.

Proof of
Proposition

3.2.7
.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
by topoi and
\lambda\in\Lambda
with

G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}),

and denote by
r^{\lambda,(G)}\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{(G)}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{(G)}
the right adjoint of
{\mathcal{X}}^{(G)}_{\lambda}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{X}}^{(G)}
. Since
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under colimits and finite limits,
\mathbb{B}G\in\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
is the classifying space of
G
in
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
.
By construction,
\operatorname{triv}
restricts to
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}\colon\mathcal{X}\to{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}
(restriction of scalars along
G\to*\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})
), and

(3.2.8.1)

\displaystyle r^{\lambda,G}\circ\operatorname{triv}=\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}\circ\ r^{\lambda},

cf.
A.2.8
.
By
1.5.8
,
\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})\to\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})
admits a left adjoint
L
with

L\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda})}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}\circ(-//G),

where
-//G\colon{\mathcal{X}}^{G}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
denotes the homotopy orbits functor.
1.3.40
implies that

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(\mathbb{B}G,-)\cong\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}_{\lambda})}(L\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}(*),-)\cong H_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(G,-)\circ\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}.

By
3.2.8.1
,

r^{\lambda,G}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}=\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\ r^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}},

and hence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(\mathbb{B}G,-)\circ r^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\cong H_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(G,-)\circ\operatorname{triv}^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ r^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\cong H_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(G,-)\circ r^{\lambda,G}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}.

By
3.2.6
and
1.5.9
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(\mathbb{B}G,-)\circ r^{\lambda}_{\operatorname{Sp}}

and

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong H_{\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}}(G,-)\circ r^{\lambda,G}_{\operatorname{Sp}}.\qed

If
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
and
E\to\operatorname{triv}B
is a principal
\infty
-
G
-bundle in
\mathcal{X}
, the classifying map
c\colon B\cong E//G\to\mathbb{B}G
(
3.1.19
) induces a natural transformation

c^{*}\colon H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{B}G,-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(B,-)

of functors
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}
.

Corollary 3.2.9
.

Suppose
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
and
E\to\operatorname{triv}B
is a principal
\infty
-
G
-bundle.
Suppose that
M\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is such that for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the projection
G^{p}\times\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*}E\to G^{p}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p},M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p}\times\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*}E,M).

Then pullback along the classifying map
B\to\mathbb{B}G
is an equivalence

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(M))\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(B,M).

Proof.

Denote by
E_{*}
the action groupoid of
E
, i.e. the image of

E
under

{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\hookrightarrow{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})}_{/*//G}}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X}).

By construction of the identification
{\mathcal{X}}^{G}\cong{{\mathcal{X}}_{/\mathbb{B}G}}
and
1.3.38
,

c^{*}
is the totalization of the morphism of cosimplicial objects

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}((*//G)_{*},-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(E_{*},-)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta,\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}))

induced by the map
E_{*}\to(*//G)_{*}
.
This implies the statement as for
[n]\in\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
,

E([n])\cong(*//G)([n])\times E([0])\cong G^{n}\times\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*}E

and
E([n])\to(*//G)([n])
is the projection.
∎

For a group object
G
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
, we obtain the following spectral sequence by applying
1.5.13
to the effective epimorphism
G\to*\in{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
:

Corollary 3.2.10
.

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
. There is a spectral sequence of functors
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Ab}
with
E_{1}
-page

E_{1}^{p,q}=\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{q}(G^{p},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-).

On bounded above objects
\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})_{\leq n}
, this converges completely to
H_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(G,-)
.

Proof.

By
1.5.13
, there is a spectral sequence with
E_{1}
-page

E_{1}^{p,q}=\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}^{q}(G^{p+1},-)

which converges completely to
H_{\mathcal{X}}^{p+q}(G,-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}(*,-)
on bounded above spectrum objects.
For all
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the map
G^{m}\to G^{m+1},g\mapsto(1,g)
is adjoint to an equivalence
\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(G^{m})\cong G^{m+1}
. Hence by
3.1.25
,

\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\check{C}(G\to*)([m])\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}G^{m+1}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*}(G^{m})\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}}G^{m}

for all
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
. It follows from
1.3.40
that for all
p,q\in\mathbb{Z}
,

\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}^{q}(G^{p+1},-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}^{q}(G^{p},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-).\qed

Remark 3.2.11
.

For
M\in\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})^{\heartsuit}\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})
, the spectral sequence (
3.2.10
) is concentrated in the upper right quadrant, whence we obtain an edge homomorphism

E_{2}^{*,0}(M)\twoheadrightarrow E_{2}^{*,\infty}(M)\hookrightarrow H_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(G,M).

Denote by
S_{*}^{G}\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))
the simplicial resolution of
\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G\to*\in\tau_{\leq 0}{\mathcal{X}}^{G}
(
Definition

1.5.16
). Then

E_{1}^{*,0}|_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}(S_{*}^{G},-),

i.e. the edge homomorphism is a natural transformation

E_{2}^{*,0}|_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}(S_{*}^{G},-))\Rightarrow H_{\mathcal{X}}^{*}(G,-)|_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})}

of functors
\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{0}^{\mathcal{X}}G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})})\to\operatorname{grAb}
.

We will apply this below to compare condensed with continuous group cohomology.

3.2.1
Internal Group Cohomology

We now record some basic results on internal group cohomology.

Lemma 3.2.12
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has all
\Delta
-indexed limits and all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is closed.

For all group objects
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
, internal group cohomology
\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)
exists and

\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong{\underset{p\in\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p},-)\circ\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-).

Remark 3.2.13
.

The conditions of the lemma are satisfied if
\mathcal{X}
is a topos or the category of (hyper)accessible sheaves on a (hyper)accessible explicit covering site (
Lemma

1.3.28
).

Proof.

Recall from
Lemma

3.1.22
that
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
.
As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and its monoidal structure is closed, by
Proposition

1.4.1

\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
has all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the forget functor

\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})

reflects them.
Since
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor, it follows that the tensor product on
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
preserves
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits in both variables.
In particular,

\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)\cong\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)\otimes{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\check{C}(G\to*)\cong{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)\otimes\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\check{C}(G\to*)),

where we used that
{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\check{C}(G\to*)\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}(*)
is the monoidal unit of
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
. By
3.1.25
and
Lemma

3.1.26
, for
[n]\in\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}\check{C}(G\to*)([n])

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,{\mathcal{X}}^{G}}G^{n+1}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})}\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}}G^{n})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{ind}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(-\otimes_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}}G^{n})

is left adjoint to

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+,\mathcal{X}}G^{n},-)\circ\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}=\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{n},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-).

Since
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed limits and
\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G})
has all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits,

\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))

is closed under
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and they are computed pointwise (
Lemma

A.1.1
). Analogously,

\operatorname{Fun}^{R}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}^{G}),\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}))

is closed under
\Delta
-indexed limits and they can be computed pointwise.

[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.2.6.2]
now implies that
{\underset{n\in\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{n},-)\circ\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
is right adjoint to
\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)
.
∎

Suppose
G
is a group object in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
such that internal group cohomology
\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)
exists. As
H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)
(
3.2.2
), the adjunction counit of the stabilization of the global sections geometric morphism
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}(-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\colon\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}
provides a natural transformation

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\right)\to\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-).

In rare cases, this is an equivalence:

Corollary 3.2.14
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos such that
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has all countable products and all
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
is closed.
Suppose that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})
and
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{S}[G]}({\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})})
is such that for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}M)\right)\cong\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}M)

via the counit of
c(-)\dashv\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}
.
Then
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,M)\right)\cong\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,M)
via the counit.

Proof.

As
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has countable products (by assumption) and finite limits (
Lemma

1.3.2
),
\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
has all countable limits (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.6]
), and in particular all
\Delta
-indexed limits. By
Lemma

3.2.12
,

\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong{\underset{p\in\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-),

whence

H_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G,-)\cong{\underset{p\in\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong{\underset{p\in\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(G^{p},-).

The statement now follows from
Lemma

1.3.45
.
∎

3.2.2
Condensed Group Cohomology

We now specialize the above discussion to condensed group cohomology.

Definition 3.2.15
.

For a (
\kappa
-)condensed group
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An}))
, denote by

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)\coloneqq H_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}(G,-)

its (
\kappa
-condensed) group cohomology, and by

\underline{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)\coloneqq\underline{H}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}(G,-)

the internal (
\kappa
-)condensed group cohomology.
The latter exists by
3.2.2
.

Remark 3.2.16
.

For a discrete (
\kappa
-)condensed group
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Sp}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}^{G})})\cong\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))(\text{ \lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{derivedgmodules}}).

Denote by
f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))\to\operatorname{Sp}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})}^{G})
the forget functor. Then

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{*}(G,f-)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])}(\mathbb{Z},-)\text{ (\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{groupcohomologyisext})}.

Moreover, (
\kappa
-)condensed group cohomology

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)
refines to a functor

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)_{\mathbb{Z}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})})))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}),

and internal (
\kappa
-)condensed group cohomology enhances to a functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})),\text{ cf. \lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{remarkgroupcohomologyrefines}}.

3.2.6
implies that condensed group cohomology can always be computed on some level

\operatorname{Sp}({\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}^{G})\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}({\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})}^{G}):

Corollary 3.2.17
.

Suppose
G
is a Hausdorff topological group.

(i)

If
\kappa
is an uncountable regular or strong limit cardinal with
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>|G|
, then

H_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G},-)|_{\operatorname{Sp}({\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}})}\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},-).

(ii)

In particular, if
M
is a
\operatorname{T1}
continuous
G
-module, for all uncountable regular/strong limit cardinals
\kappa
with
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>\max\{|M|,|G|\}
,

H_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G},\underline{M})\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

Proof.

By
2.4.19
, for all regular cardinals and all strong limit cardinals
\kappa
with
\operatorname{cof}(\kappa)>|G|
,

\underline{G}=\underline{G}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set}).

The statement now follows from
3.2.6
and
2.4.13
since

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Grp})\cong\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Grp})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})

and

\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})\cong\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Ab})\times_{\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{Set})}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set}).\qed

3.2.14
implies that internal (
\kappa
-)condensed group cohomology is constant in some cases:
Denote by
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor.

Corollary 3.2.18
.

Suppose
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
and there exists a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space
K
with
\mathbb{Z}[G]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}
in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
.
If
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
is such that the condensed abelian group underlying
A
is represented by a discrete abelian group, then

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,A)\right)\cong\underline{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,A).

We prove this below. Together with
2.9.2
, it implies the following more concrete statement:

Corollary 3.2.19
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group.

(i)

If
G
is homotopy equivalent to a
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff space, for all discrete continuous
G
-modules
A
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\right)\cong\underline{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa}).

(ii)

If
G
is Hausdorff and homotopy equivalent to a compact Hausdorff space, for all discrete continuous
G
-modules
A
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(H_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G},\underline{A})\right)\cong\underline{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G},\underline{A}).

Remark 3.2.20
.

For profinite groups,
3.2.19
was established in
[
AB20
, Lemma 2.5]
.

3.2.19
in particular applies to (
\kappa
-light) locally compact Hausdorff abelian groups with finitely many connected components:
By the structure theorem for locally compact abelian groups (see e.g.
[
HM23
, Theorem 4]
), every locally compact Hausdorff abelian group
A
is isomorphic to a product
\mathbb{R}^{n}\times B
, where
B
admits a compact open subgroup
K\subseteq B
.
The space
B
is homeomorphic to
\sqcup_{\pi_{0}B}K
and hence compact of weight
\leq\operatorname{wt}(A)
and
A
is homotopy equivalent to
B
.

Internal condensed group cohomology has a non-constant condensed structure in many cases. For example, for a continuous
G
-module
M
,

\underline{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{0}(G,M)=\underline{M^{G}}_{(\kappa)},

is represented by the
G
-fixed-points of
M
(with subspace topology), whereas

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}^{0}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},M)\right)=\underline{(M^{G})^{\delta}}_{\kappa}

is represented by the discrete abelian group
(M^{G})^{\delta}
.

Proof of
3.2.18
.

By assumption, there exists a (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space
K
with
\mathbb{Z}[G]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}
in
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
.
This implies that for
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\mathbb{Z}[{G}^{p}]^{L{\square}}\cong\bigotimes^{L{\square}}_{i=1,\ldots,p}(\mathbb{Z}[G]^{L{\square}})\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K^{p}}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}.

Hence by
2.9.7
, for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and all discrete abelian groups
A
,

c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\left(\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G^{p},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})\right)\cong\underline{\mathbb{H}}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G^{p},\underline{A}_{(\kappa)})

via the adjunction counit for
c_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv\Gamma_{\operatorname{Sp}}
.
The statement now follows from
3.2.14

since
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
has small limits and colimits (
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.5.2.4]
/
2.4.12
) and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Sp})
is closed (
2.4.6
).
∎

3.3
Condensed and continuous group cohomology

We now compare (
\kappa
-)condensed group cohomology of a (T1) topological group
G
with its continuous group cohomology.

Definition 3.3.1
.

For a discrete group
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
in a big topos
\mathcal{X}
denote by

S_{*}^{G}\to\mathbb{Z}\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}))

the simplicial resolution of
G\to*\in\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
(
Definition

1.5.16
).

For a group
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Set})
and a
G
-module
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}})
, the cochain complex

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}})}(S_{*}^{G},M)\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}}))

obtained by applying
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}(-,M)
to the simplicial resolution
S_{*}^{G}\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}}))
componentwise is called the
complex of

G
-
cochains in

M
.

Explicitly, for
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}})}(S_{i}^{G},M)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Set}}(G^{i},M)

and for
i\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
and
f\in\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Set}}(G^{i-1},M)
,

\displaystyle\partial_{i-1}f\colon G^{i}

\displaystyle\to M,

\displaystyle(g_{1},\ldots,g_{i})

\displaystyle\mapsto g_{1}f(g_{2},\ldots,g_{i})+\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}(-1)^{j}f(g_{1},\ldots,g_{j-1},g_{j}g_{j+1},g_{j+2}\ldots,g_{i})+(-1)^{i}f(g_{1},g_{2},\ldots,g_{i-1}).

Definition 3.3.2
.

If
G
is a topological group, a
continuous

G
-module
M
is a topological abelian group
M
with a continuous
G
-action
G\times M\to M
by linear maps.
Denote by
\operatorname{Cont}^{G}
the category of continuous
G
-modules with
G
-equivariant, continuous linear maps.

Lemma 3.3.3
.

Suppose that
G
is a topological group and
M
is a continuous
G
-module.
The continuous/
k
-continuous/
\kappa
-continuous maps
G^{*}\to M
define subcomplexes

\mathcal{C}(G^{*},M)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{k}(G^{*},Y)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(G^{*},M)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}({\operatorname{Ab}})}(S_{*}^{G},M)

of the complex of
G
-cochains in
M
.

Proof.

This follows from continuity of the
G
-action on
M
and the group multiplication of
G
. ∎

Definition 3.3.4
.

If
G
is a topological group and
M
is a continuous
G
-module, we denote by

\mathcal{C}(G^{*},M)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{k}(G^{*},Y)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(G^{*},M)

the complexes of
continuous
/
k-continuous
/
\kappa
-
continuous cochains
of
G
in
M
.
Their cohomology groups are called the
continuous
/
k-continuous
/
\kappa
-
continuous group cohomology
of
G
with coefficients in
M
, and are denoted by

\displaystyle H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,M)

\displaystyle\coloneqq H^{*}(\mathcal{C}(G^{*},M)),

\displaystyle H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,M)

\displaystyle\coloneqq H^{*}(\mathcal{C}_{k}(G^{*},M)),

\displaystyle H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G^{*},M)

\displaystyle\coloneqq H^{*}(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(G^{*},M)),

respectively.

Lemma

3.3.3
yields natural transformations

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,-)\to H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\to H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Cont}^{G},\operatorname{grAb}).

2.4.18
and
Proposition

2.2.7
imply:

Corollary 3.3.5
.

Suppose that
G
is a topological group and
M
is a continuous
G
-module.

(i)

For all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,

\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(G^{*},M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])}(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}},\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

(ii)

If
G
and
M
are
\operatorname{T1}
, then

\mathcal{C}_{k}(G^{*},M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}(S_{*}^{\underline{G}},\underline{M}).

This implies that the Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence for the cover
\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}\to*
(
3.2.10
) interpolates between
\kappa/k
-continuous and
(\kappa)
-condensed group cohomology, cf.
3.2.11
:

Corollary 3.3.6
.

(i)

Suppose
G
is a Hausdorff topological group.
There is an upper quadrant spectral sequence of functors
\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}\to\operatorname{Ab}
with

E_{1}^{p,q}=\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}^{q}(\underline{G^{p}},-)\text{ and }E_{2}^{*,0}=H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-),

which converges to
H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\underline{-})
. The edge homomorphism is a natural transformation

H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\to H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\underline{-})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G},\operatorname{grAb}).

(ii)

Suppose
G
is a topological group and
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal.
There is an upper quadrant spectral sequence of functors
\operatorname{Cont}^{G}\to\operatorname{Ab}
with

E_{1}^{p,q}=\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{q}(\underline{G^{p}}_{\kappa},-)\text{ and }E_{2}^{*,0}=H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)

which converges to
H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{-}_{\kappa})
.
The edge homomorphism is a natural transformation

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\to H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{-}_{\kappa})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Cont}^{G},\operatorname{grAb}).

Corollary 3.3.7

(
[
AB20
, Lemma 2.1]
)
.

(i)

Suppose
G
is a Hausdorff topological group which is homotopy equivalent to a coproduct of profinite sets.
If
M
is a
\operatorname{T1}
continuous
G
-module such that
\underline{M}
is solid, then the spectral sequence from
3.2.10
collapses at the
E_{2}
-page and yields

H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\underline{M}).

(ii)

Suppose that
G
is a topological group which is homotopy equivalent to a coproduct of
\kappa
-light profinite sets. If
M
is a continuous
G
-module such that
\underline{M}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
, the spectral sequence from
3.2.10
collapses at the
E_{2}
-page and yields

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa}).

Example 3.3.8
.

By van Dantzig’s theorem, the above corollary in particular applies to (
\kappa
-light) locally profinite groups.

Proof.

If
G\to\sqcup_{i\in I}X(i)
is a homotopy equivalence with
X(i)\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
for all
i\in I
, for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
,

G^{p}\to(\sqcup_{i\in I}X(i))^{p}=\sqcup_{(i_{1},\ldots,i_{p})\in I^{p}}X({i_{1}})\times X({i_{2}})\times\ldots\times X({i_{p}})

is a homotopy equivalence and
X({i_{1}})\times X({i_{2}})\times\ldots\times X({i_{p}})\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
.
By
2.9.2
, this induces an isomorphism

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong\oplus_{i\in I^{p}}\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{k=1}^{p}\underline{X({i_{k}})}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}).

2.8.69
now implies that for
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
,

\displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{G^{p}}_{(\kappa)},M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{p}}_{(\kappa)}],M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{p}}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}},M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\oplus_{i\in I^{p}}\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{k=1}^{n}\underline{X({i_{k}})}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}},M)

\displaystyle\cong\prod_{i\in I^{n}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{k=1}^{p}\underline{{X({i_{k}})}}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}},M)

\displaystyle\cong\prod_{i\in I^{n}}\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))}(\mathbb{Z}[\prod_{k=1}^{p}\underline{{X({i_{k}})}}_{(\kappa)}],M),

where we used that coproducts in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
).
The right-hand side is concentrated in degree
0
by
Proposition

2.8.3
.
∎

2.5.19
and
2.5.21
imply:

Corollary 3.3.9
.

Suppose that
G
is a locally compact Hausdorff topological group and
V
is a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space with a linear, continuous
G
-action.
For
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(G)
, the spectral sequence from
3.3.6
collapses at the
E_{2}
-page and yields

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,V)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,V)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{V}_{\kappa}).

Analogously,

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,V)\cong H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,V)\cong H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\underline{V}).

Proof.

This follows from

2.5.19
and
2.5.21
, since every locally compact Hausdorff topological group is paracompact, see e.g.
[
AU13
, page 1]
.
∎

Remark 3.3.10
.

Continuous group cohomology is insensitive with respect to the higher terms

(E_{1}^{p,q}=\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{q}(\underline{G}^{p},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-))_{p,q\geq 1}

of the spectral sequence from
3.2.10
, which are nontrivial in many cases.
For example,
[
Bre97
, Corollary II.16.21]
and
2.5.19
imply that if
G
is locally compact Hausdorff (and
\kappa
-light), then
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},A)
is concentrated in degree
0
for all discrete abelian groups
A
if and only if
G
is locally profinite.
This suggests that continuous group cohomology is a coarser invariant than condensed group cohomology.

Their difference can be made more explicit:
Continuous group cohomology with coefficients in a discrete continuous
G
-module only depends on the group of connected components
\pi_{0}G
of
G
: For a discrete continuous
G
-module
M
,

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(\pi_{0}G,M),

where
\pi_{0}G
is endowed with the quotient topology, and analogously for
k
-continuous/
\kappa
-continuous group cohomology provided that
G^{i}
is compactly generated/
\kappa
-compactly generated for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
or alternatively, that
G
is locally path-connected.

We will see in
Section

3.4
, specifically
3.4.8
that
H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G},\underline{M})
also encodes information on the homotopy type of the connected component of the identity
G^{0}\subseteq G
.

Condensed group cohomology has better exactness properties than continuous group cohomology:

Example 3.3.11
.

The exponential sequence
0\to\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{T}^{1}\to 0
induces a short exact sequence of (
\kappa
-)condensed abelian groups

0\to\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{(\kappa)}\to 0.

Suppose
G
is a (
\operatorname{T1}
) topological group and consider the above as condensed
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]
-modules with trivial
G
-action. This induces a long exact sequence of abelian groups

\displaystyle 0\to\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{T}^{1}\to H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{1}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{(\kappa)})

\displaystyle\to H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{1}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{(\kappa)})\to H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{1}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{\mathbb{T}^{1}}_{(\kappa)})

\displaystyle\to H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{2}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{\mathbb{Z}}_{(\kappa)})\to\ldots.

Continuous group cohomology does not fit into such a long exact sequence:
For a continuous
G
-module with trivial
G
-action
M
,
H^{1}_{\operatorname{cont}}(G,M)
is the group of continuous group homomorphisms
G\to M
. In particular, if
G
is compact, then
H^{1}_{\operatorname{cont}}(G,\mathbb{R})=0
, whereas
H^{1}_{\operatorname{cont}}(G,\mathbb{T}^{1})=\widehat{G}
is the Pontrjagin-dual of
G
.
Since
H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,\mathbb{Z})\cong H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(\pi_{0}G,\mathbb{Z})
, this shows that if
0\neq G
is a compact and connected topological group, there is no exact sequence

\ldots\to H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{1}(G,\mathbb{Z})\to H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{1}(G,\mathbb{R})\to H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{1}(G,\mathbb{T}^{1})\to H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{2}(G,\mathbb{Z})\to\ldots.

Comparison with group cohomology in the gros topos

[
Fla08
]
studied group cohomology in the gros topos of topological spaces (
Definition

2.5.12
). Ibid. used universe enlargement to deal with size issues, which corresponds to taking
\lambda
a regular strong limit cardinal.
The spectral sequence provided by
3.2.10
in the gros topos, and the equivalence of sheaf and gros topos cohomology (
2.5.15
) imply that if
G
is a
\lambda
-small topological group and
M
is a continuous
G
-module such that
H^{q}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},\mathcal{C}(-,M))=0
for all
p,q\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
, then

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}^{*}(h_{G},h_{M})

where
h_{G},h_{M}
denote the sheaves represented by
G
and
M
respectively. This was shown in
[
Fla08
]
.
It applies in the following two cases (both shown by
[
Fla08
]
):

(i)

If
G
is locally profinite, in which case
\mathbb{Z}[h_{G^{p}}]
is projective in
\operatorname{Shv}_{LS}(\operatorname{Top}^{\kappa},\operatorname{Ab})=\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})^{\heartsuit}
: By van Dantzig’s theorem, every locally profinite group is a coproduct of profinite sets and for
X\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\lambda}
,

\mathbb{Z}[h_{X}]
is projective in
\operatorname{Shv}_{LS}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},\operatorname{Ab})
since for
i>0
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_{\operatorname{Shv}_{LS}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[h_{X}],-)|_{\operatorname{Shv}_{LS}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},\operatorname{Ab})}

\displaystyle\cong\mathbb{H}_{\widehat{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}^{i}(h_{X},-)|_{\operatorname{Shv}_{LS}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},\operatorname{Ab})}

\displaystyle\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}^{i}(h_{X},-)|_{\operatorname{Shv}_{LS}(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda},\operatorname{Ab})}

\displaystyle\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{i}(X,\pi_{0}{t}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)=0.

Here
\widehat{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}\subseteq\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}
denotes the subcategory on hypercomplete objects.
The vanishing of sheaf cohomology is
[
Sta22
,
Tag 0A3F
]
, the identifications hold by
1.5.4.2
,
Lemmas

1.5.7
and
2.5.15
.

(ii)

If
G
is locally compact Hausdorff and
M
is a finite-dimensional, continuous real
G
-representation. This follows from
Lemma

2.5.21
since locally compact Hausdorff groups are paracompact (
[
AU13
, page 1]
).

Suppose
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal and
\lambda\geq\kappa
is a strong limit cardinal.
In
Section

2.5
(page
2.5
), we described a geometric morphism

(3.3.11.1)

{j}_{*}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\leftrightarrows\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}\colon{j}^{*},{j}^{*}\dashv{j}_{*}.

For
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})
, this yields a geometric morphism

(3.3.11.2)

{j}^{G}_{*}\colon{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}^{{j}^{*}G}\leftrightarrows{(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})}^{G}\colon{j}^{G,*},

cf.
Lemma

3.1.3
. In particular,

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}({j}^{*}G,-)\cong H_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(G,{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)

by
Lemma

1.5.7
.
If
G=h_{G}
is represented by a
\lambda
-small topological group
G
, then
{j}^{*}h_{G}=\underline{G}_{\kappa}
by
Lemma

2.5.14
, and if
A
is a continuous
G
-module
A
, then
\pi_{0}{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\cong\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(-,A)
with the obvious
h_{G}=\mathcal{C}(-,G)
-action.

Lemma 3.3.12
.

Suppose
\kappa\leq\lambda
are uncountable cardinals and
G
is a
\lambda
-small topological abelian group.

(i)

If
A\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])
is such that the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{G}^{p}_{\kappa},A)\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaf})

is an isomorphism for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, then

H_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{G},\pi_{0}{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},A).

(ii)

If
A
is a topological group such that the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{G}^{p}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaftopologicalwithoutkappa})

is an isomorphism for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, then

H_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{G},h_{A})\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa}).

This applies for example in the following two cases:

(i)

G
is
\kappa
-light, locally compact Hausdorff and
A
is a product of a discrete group and a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space (
2.5.19
),

(ii)

G
is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible or
\kappa
-light locally compact Haudorff space and
A
is discrete (
Lemmas

2.9.4
and
2.9.6
).

Proof.

We only prove the first statement, the second statement can be shown completely analogously.
By
1.3.38
,

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},-)\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathbb{H}_{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}}}(\check{C}(\underline{G}_{\kappa}\to*),-)

and

H_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{G},-)\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathbb{H}_{{(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})}^{h_{G}}}(\check{C}(h_{G}\to*),-).

By
Lemma

1.5.7
, the geometric morphism
3.3.11.2
induces a map of cosimplicial spectra

\mathbb{H}_{{(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})}^{h_{G}}}(\check{C}(h_{G}\to*),\pi_{0}{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{{(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})}^{h_{G}}}(\check{C}(h_{G}\to*),{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}}}(\check{C}(\underline{G}_{\kappa}\to*),A).

For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\mathbb{H}_{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}}}(\check{C}(\underline{G}_{\kappa}\to*),-)[n]\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa}^{n},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-),

and

\mathbb{H}_{{\operatorname{Cond}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}^{h_{G}}}(\check{C}(h_{G}\to*),-)[n]\cong\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{G^{n}},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)

by
1.3.40
and
3.1.25
.
As
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\circ{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}={j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
and
\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
is
t
-exact, it follows that

H_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(\check{C}(h_{G}\to*),\pi_{0}{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)([n])\cong\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}(h_{G^{n}},\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{0}{j}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)=\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}}(h_{G^{n}},\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\operatorname{res}^{G}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-).

Under these identifications, the above morphism of cosimplicial spectra agrees with the map

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(-,\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(-,{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}({j}^{*}-,-)

induced by
\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\to{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
and the equivalence from
Lemma

1.5.7
. By
2.5.18
, this is an equivalence if and only if the comparison map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},\pi_{0}{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{G^{p}}_{\kappa},A)\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaf})

is an isomorphism for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
∎

3.4
Condensed group cohomology and cohomology of classifying spaces

In this section, we compare condensed group cohomology of a topological group
G
with the condensed cohomology of a classifying space
BG
for numerable principal
G
-bundles.
We refer to
[
Die08
, section 14.4]
for basic material on classifying spaces and principal bundles.
The main result is that condensed group cohomology with coefficients in a solid abelian group
M
with trivial
G
-action is isomorphic to the condensed cohomology of
BG
with coefficients in
M
. This will follow from our general discussion around
3.2.9
and homotopy invariance of condensed cohomology with solid coefficients (
2.9.2
).

We start with some preliminaries on principal
G
-bundles. Recall that for a topological group
G
, the Milnor join construction (
[
Mil56
]
) yields a universal numerable principal
G
-bundle
EG\to BG
.

Lemma 3.4.1
.

If
G
is a Hausdorff topological group, the classifying space
BG
of numerable principal
G
-bundles obtained through the Milnor join construction is Hausdorff.

Proof.

We first show that
EG
is Hausdorff.
Recall that elements of
EG
are represented by tuples

(g_{i},t_{i})_{i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\in(G\times[0,1])^{\mathbb{N}}
such that
t_{i}=0
for all but finitely many
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
\sum_{i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}t_{i}=1
, and two such tuples
(g_{i},t_{i}),(h_{i},s_{i})
represent the same element if and only if
t_{i}=s_{i}
for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
t_{i}\neq 0
,
g_{i}=h_{i}
.
The topology on
EG
is the coarsest topology such that the projections

\displaystyle p_{i}\colon EG\to[0,1],(g_{i},t_{i})_{i}\mapsto t_{i}

and

\displaystyle q_{i}\colon p_{i}^{-1}(]0,1])\to G,(g_{i},t_{i})\mapsto g_{i}

are continuous for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.

Suppose now that
(g_{i},t_{i}),(h_{i},s_{i})
represent two distinct elements in
EG
.
If there exists
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
t_{i}\neq s_{i}
, choose disjoint open neighborhoods
t_{i}\in U\subseteq[0,1],s_{i}\in V\subseteq[0,1]
.
Then

(g_{i},t_{i})_{i}\in p_{i}^{-1}(U)

and

(h_{i},s_{i})\in p_{i}^{-1}(V)

are disjoint open neighborhoods in
EG
.
Suppose now that
t_{i}=s_{i}
for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
. As
(g_{i},t_{i}),(h_{i},s_{i})
represent distinct elements, there has to exist
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
such that
t_{n}\neq 0
and
g_{n}\neq h_{n}
.
Since
G
is Hausdorff, there exist disjoint open neighborhoods
g_{n}\in U\subseteq G,h_{n}\in V\subseteq G
. Now

(g_{i},t_{i})_{i}\in q_{n}^{-1}(U),(h_{i},s_{i})_{i}\in q_{n}^{-1}(V)

are disjoint open neighborhoods in
EG
. This shows that
EG
is Hausdorff.

Suppose now that
[(g_{i},t_{i})_{i}],[(h_{i},s_{i})_{i}]\in BG=EG/G
represent two distinct elements.
The projections
(p_{i})_{i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}
descend to continuous maps
\overline{p}_{i}\colon BG\to[0,1]
.
If there exists
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
such that
t_{i}\neq s_{i}
, then choose disjoint open neighborhoods
t_{i}\in U\subseteq[0,1],s_{i}\in V\subseteq[0,1]
.
Then
[(g_{i},t_{i})_{i}]\in\overline{p}_{i}^{-1}(U)
and
[(h_{i},s_{i})]\in\overline{p}_{i}^{-1}(V)
are disjoint open neighborhoods in
BG
.
Suppose now that
t_{i}=s_{i}
for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and choose
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
t_{i}>0
.
The proof of
[
Mil56
, Theorem 3.1]
shows that

V_{i}\coloneqq\overline{p}_{i}^{-1}(]0,1[)\subseteq BG

is an open subset of
BG
over which the bundle
\pi\colon EG\to BG
trivializes.
Since

\pi^{-1}(V_{i})\cong G\times V_{i}\subseteq EG

is a subspace, it is Hausdorff. This implies that
V_{i}
is Hausdorff. As
[(t_{i},g_{i})],[(s_{i},h_{i})]\in V_{i}
, they can be separated by disjoint open neighborhoods in
V_{i}
and hence in
BG
.
∎

Lemma 3.4.2
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group and
E\to B
is a principal
G
-bundle.

(i)

For all uncountable cardinals
\kappa
,
\underline{E}_{\kappa}\to\underline{B}_{\kappa}
is a principal
\infty
-
\underline{G}_{\kappa}
-bundle in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
(
Definition

3.1.17
).

(ii)

If
B
and
G
are
\operatorname{T1}
, then so is
E
and
\underline{E}\to\underline{B}
is a principal
\infty
-
\underline{G}
-bundle in
\operatorname{Cond}(\operatorname{An})
.

Proof.

Choose an open cover
B=\cup_{i\in I}U_{i}
such that for all
i\in I
,
E\times_{B}U_{i}\cong G\times U_{i}
as topological spaces with
G
-action over
U_{i}
.
Then
E=\bigcup_{i\in I}E\times_{B}U_{i}
is an open cover. In particular, if
B
and
G
are
\operatorname{T1}
, then
E\times_{B}U_{i}\cong G\times U_{i}
is
\operatorname{T1}
for all
i\in I
, which implies that
E
is
\operatorname{T1}
.
As the local section topology is coarser than the
\kappa
-condensed topology on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
(
Lemma

A.4.21
),
p\colon\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{U_{i}}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{B}_{(\kappa)}
is an effective epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
.
Since
\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)}
commutes with pullbacks and small colimits are universal in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
(
2.4.5
),

\displaystyle\underline{E}_{(\kappa)}\times_{\underline{B}_{(\kappa)}}\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{U_{i}}_{(\kappa)}

\displaystyle\cong\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{E}_{(\kappa)}\times_{\underline{B}_{(\kappa)}}\underline{U_{i}}_{(\kappa)}

\displaystyle\cong\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{E\times_{B}U_{i}}_{(\kappa)}

\displaystyle\cong\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{G\times_{B}U_{i}}_{(\kappa)}

\displaystyle\cong\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}\times_{\underline{B}_{(\kappa)}}\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{U_{i}}_{(\kappa)}.\qed

By
Lemma

3.4.2
and
3.1.19
, every numerable principal
G
-bundle
E\to B
determines a map
\underline{B}_{(\kappa)}\cong\underline{E}_{(\kappa)}//\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}\to\mathbb{B}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}
to the classifying space
\mathbb{B}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}
of principal
\infty
-
\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}
-bundles in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
.
By
Proposition

3.2.7
, this induces a map

(3.4.2.1)

\displaystyle H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\mathbb{B}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{BG}_{\kappa},-).

(Without
\kappa
, both sides are only defined if
G
and
BG
are
\operatorname{T1}
).

The condensed anima represented by a classifying space of numerable principal
G
-bundles is very different from the classifying space of principal
\infty
-
\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}
-bundles in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{An})
:
If
EG\to BG
is a universal numerable principal
G
-bundle, then
\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)}\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
is
0
-truncated. On the other hand,
\pi_{1}(\mathbb{B}\underline{G}_{\kappa})=\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}
(
3.1.20
), and in particular
\underline{BG}_{\kappa}\not\cong\mathbb{B}\underline{G}_{\kappa}
if
G\neq 0
.
However, since the total space
EG
of a universal numerable principal
G
-bundle is contractible as space without group action (see e.g.
[
Die08
, Theorem 14.4.12]
), homotopy invariance of cohomology with solid coefficients (
3.2.9
) and
2.9.2
imply the following:

Corollary 3.4.3
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group and
BG
is a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles.
Denote by
f
the forget functor

\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}({\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})})\to\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})).

(i)

For
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa})
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{BG}_{\kappa},fM)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}fM)

via the map
3.4.2.1
.

(ii)

If
G
is Hausdorff and
BG
is a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles
BG
which is
\operatorname{T1}
(e.g. the Milnor join construction), for all
M\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid})
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{BG},fM)\cong H_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G},\operatorname{triv}_{\operatorname{Sp}}fM)

via the map
3.4.2.1
.

Proof.

Choose a universal numerable principal
G
-bundle
EG\to BG
. Since
EG
is contractible (
[
Die08
, Theorem 14.4.12]
), by
2.9.2
, for all
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
and
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the projection
G^{p}\times EG\to G^{p}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}^{p},M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}^{p}\times\underline{EG}_{(\kappa)},M)

(without
\kappa
, both sides are only defined if
G
and
EG
are
\operatorname{T1}
).
The statement now follows from
3.2.9
.
∎

3.4.1
Cohomology of classifying spaces

We now show that for many topological groups, the condensed cohomology of their classifying space agrees with its sheaf and singular cohomology.
Together with
3.4.3
, this yields many examples where condensed group cohomology differs from continuous group cohomology, see
3.4.8
.

Homotopy invariance of gros topos/sheaf cohomology with constant coefficients (
A.5.6
) and homotopy invariance of condensed cohomology with solid coefficients (
2.9.2
) imply the following:

Lemma 3.4.4
.

Suppose that
M
is a discrete abelian group,
G
is a topological group and
BG
is a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles.

(i)

If for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the
map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},M)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{G^{p}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaftopological})

is an equivalence, then

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{BG}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})

via the map (
2.5.6.2
).

(ii)

If
G
is
\operatorname{T1}
and
BG
is
\operatorname{T1}
(e.g. the classifying space obtained through the Milnor-join construction), and for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the map

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},M)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},M_{\kappa})\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G^{p}},\underline{M})\,\,(\ref{comparisonmapkappacondensedsheaftopologicalwithoutkappa})

is an equivalence, then

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{BG},\underline{M})

via the map (
2.5.7.1
).

Proof.

Denote by
EG\to BG
a universal principal
G
-bundle. Since
EG
is contractible (
[
Die08
, Proposition 14.4.6]
), our assumption and
2.9.3
imply that
G^{p}\times EG
is
\epsilon
-(
\kappa
-)
M
-exact (
2.5.23
) for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
. As
EG\to BG
is a local section cover, and for
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\check{C}(EG\to BG)([p])\cong G^{p}\times EG,

the statement now follows from
2.5.23
.
∎

Corollary 3.4.5
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group with one of the following properties:

(i)

G
is homotopy equivalent to a locally
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff topological space.

(ii)

G
is homotopy equivalent to a space which is locally contractible.

If
BG
is a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles, for all discrete abelian groups
M
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{BG}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})

via the map (
2.5.6.2
).
If in addition to the above,
G
is Hausdorff and
BG
is a
\operatorname{T1}
classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles (e.g. the Milnor join construction), then for all discrete abelian groups
M
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{BG},\underline{M})

via the map (
2.5.7.1
).

Proof.

It suffices to prove the
\kappa
-condensed statement, then the condensed statement follows from
2.5.4
.
By
2.9.3
,
2.5.19
and
2.9.4
, our conditions on
G
imply that for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and all discrete abelian groups
M
, the map (
2.5.6.2
)

(3.4.5.1)

\displaystyle\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(G^{p},M)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{G^{p}}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa})

is an equivalence.
The statement now follows from
Lemma

3.4.4
.
∎

Lemma 3.4.6
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group which is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible topological space and
BG
is a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles.

(i)

For all solid abelian groups
M\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{BG}_{\kappa},\underline{M(*)^{\delta}}_{\kappa})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{BG}_{\kappa},M),

where
M(*)^{\delta}
denotes the discrete abelian group
M(*)
.

(ii)

If
G
is Hausdorff and
BG
is
\operatorname{T1}
(e.g. the Milnor join construction), then for all solid abelian groups
M\in\operatorname{Solid}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{BG},\underline{M(*)^{\delta}})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{BG},M).

Proof.

Fix a universal numerable principal
G
-bundle
EG\to BG
.
As
\underline{EG}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)}
is a principal
\infty
-
\underline{G}_{\kappa}
-bundle (
Lemma

3.4.2
),

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)},-)={\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\check{C}(\underline{EG}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)}),-)

by
Lemmas

3.1.18
,
3.1.19
and
1.3.38
.
As
EG
is contractible, our assumption on
G
implies that for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\check{C}(EG\to BG)([p])=G^{p}\times EG

is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible space, whence the counit
\underline{M(*)^{\delta}}_{(\kappa)}\to M
of the constant sheaf/global sections geometric morphism induces an equivalence of cosimplicial spectra

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\check{C}(\underline{EG}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)}),\underline{M(*)^{\delta}}_{(\kappa)})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\check{C}(\underline{EG}_{(\kappa)}\to\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)}),M)

by
Lemma

2.9.4
. (Without
\kappa
, the terms are only defined if
G
and
BG
are
\operatorname{T1}
, in which case
EG
is
\operatorname{T1}
as well).
∎

Lemma 3.4.7
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group and
BG
is a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles.
For all discrete abelian groups
M
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{*}(BG,M)\cong H^{*}_{\operatorname{sing}}(BG,M)

and naturally in
M
.

Proof.

We claim that
BG
is semi-locally contractible (in the sense of
[
Sel16
]
), then the statement follows from
[
Sel16
]
. Fix an open subset
U\subseteq BG
. As
U\times_{BG}EG\to U
is a principal
G
-bundle, there exists an open cover
U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_{i}
such that
EG\times_{BG}U_{i}\cong G\times U_{i}
as spaces with
G
-action over
U_{i}
.
As
BG
is a classifying space for principal
G
-bundles, this implies that the inclusion
U_{i}\to BG
is homotopic to a constant map for all
i\in I
.
∎

The identification of condensed cohomology with cohomology of classifying spaces yields many examples where condensed group cohomology differs from continuous group cohomology:

Corollary 3.4.8
.

Suppose
G
is a path-connected topological group which satisfies one of the following conditions:

(i)

G
is homotopy equivalent to a (
\kappa
-light) locally compact Hausdorff space.

(ii)

G
is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible topological space.

(iii)

There exists a classifying space for numerable principal
G
-bundles which is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible space or to a locally (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff space.

•

If for all discrete abelian groups
M
,

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{M}_{\kappa}),

then
G
is weakly contractible.

•

If
G
is Hausdorff and for all discrete abelian groups
M
,

H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G},\underline{M}),

then
G
is weakly contractible.

Proof.

Since
G
is path-connected, so is
G^{i}
for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and in particular every
\kappa
/
k
-continuous map
G^{i}\to M
to a discrete abelian group is constant.
This implies that for all discrete continuous
G
-modules
M
,

M\cong H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,M)

is concentrated in degree
0
.

We now show that under the assumptions on
G
, for all discrete abelian groups
M
,

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})\cong H^{*}_{\operatorname{sing}}(BG,M).

By
3.4.3
and
2.8.52
, for all discrete abelian groups
M
(with trivial
G
-action),

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)}).

If
G
is homotopy equivalent to a (
\kappa
-light) locally compact Hausdorff space or to a locally contractible space, for all discrete abelian groups
M
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})

by
3.4.5
, and if there exists a classifying space
BG
for numerable principal
G
-bundles which is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible or locally (
\kappa
-)light compact Hausdorff space, then

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\underline{BG}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)})

by
Lemmas

2.9.4
and
2.9.6
, respectively.
By
Lemma

3.4.7
,

H^{*}_{\operatorname{sing}}(BG,M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{*}(BG,M).

In particular, if

H_{\operatorname{\kappa/k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,M)\cong H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{M}_{(\kappa)}),

then
H^{*}_{\operatorname{sing}}(BG,M)
is concentrated in degree
0
for all discrete abelian groups
M
.
Since
BG
is connected and
\pi_{1}(BG)=\pi_{0}(G)=0
(we assumed
G
to be path-connected), it follows from the Hurewicz theorem that
BG
is weakly contractible.
As
G
is weakly homotopy equivalent to
\Omega BG
, this implies that
G
is weakly contractible.
∎

3.5
Solid group cohomology

When working with solid coefficients, it is natural to consider the following variant of group cohomology:

Definition 3.5.1

(Solid group cohomology)
.

Suppose
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
is a (
\kappa
)-condensed group and denote by
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
the category of solid
\mathbb{Z}[G]
-modules (
Definition

2.8.1
).
By
2.8.63
,
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))
is
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})
-enriched. Denote by

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))}(-,-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})

the enriched mapping functor and consider
\mathbb{Z}
as
\mathbb{Z}[G]
-module with trivial
G
-action.

Solid group cohomology
of
G
is defined as

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}(G,-)\coloneqq\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))}(\mathbb{Z},-),

and the solid cohomology groups are

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}^{q}\coloneqq\pi_{-q}H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}(G,-)=\operatorname{Ext}^{q}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])}(\mathbb{Z},-),q\in\mathbb{Z}.

The category
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
admits plenty projectives (
2.8.18
and
2.8.45
), which makes solid cohomology more computationally accessible than condensed group cohomology.
In this section, we compare continuous, condensed and solid group cohomology and show that for a broad class of topological groups, solid group cohomology recovers continuous group cohomology. For locally profinite groups, solid, condensed and continuous group cohomology were identified in
[
AB20
]
.

Notation 3.5.2
.

Suppose that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
is a (
\kappa
-)condensed group.
We denote by
(-)^{{\square}G}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
the left adjoint of the forget functor.
If the left adjoint of the forget functor

f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}{\mathbb{Z}[G]})\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))

exists, we denote it by
(-)^{L{\square}G}
and call it derived solidification.

We denote by
(-)^{{\square}}\colon\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
and
(-)^{L{\square}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
the left adjoints of the forget functors.

Recall from
Lemma

2.8.23
,
2.8.33
,
2.8.58
and
2.8.61
that the derived solidification exists over
\operatorname{Cond}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
as well as over
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
for strong limit cardinals
\kappa
and for
\kappa=\aleph_{1}
. It also exists if
G=\underline{H}_{(\kappa)}
for a Hausdorff topological group
H
(and arbitrary
\kappa
) by
2.8.61
and
2.8.59
.

3.5.1
Solid and condensed group cohomology

Suppose
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
.
Recall from
3.2.16
that (
\kappa
-)condensed group cohomology enhances to a functor

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab}).

We want to compare

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)\circ f\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})

with solid group cohomology.
If the derived solidification
(-)^{L{\square}G}
exists, the counit
\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}G}\to\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}{\mathbb{Z}[G]})
induces a map

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}sol}}(G,-)\to\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))}(\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}G},-)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(G,-)\circ f.

Lemma 3.5.3
.

Suppose that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
is a (
\kappa
-)condensed group such that the derived solidification
(-)^{L{\square}G}
exists.
Then

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}(G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)\circ f\in\operatorname{Fun}\bigl(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\bigr)

if and only if
\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}G}\cong\mathbb{Z}
.

Proof.

Denote by
\pi_{0}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[{G}]))_{\geq 0}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
