the left adjoint of the inclusion. Then
\pi_{0}\circ(-)^{L{\square}G}\cong(-)^{{\square}G}
since their right adjoints are equivalent. As
\mathbb{Z}^{{\square}G}\cong\mathbb{Z}
, this implies that
\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}G}\cong\mathbb{Z}
if and only if the counit
\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}G}\to\mathbb{Z}
is an equivalence, which proves the if-statement.

Denote by
g\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Sp}
the forget functor.
Since

\Omega^{\infty}gH_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}(G,-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))}(\mathbb{Z},-)

and

\Omega^{\infty}gH_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)\circ f\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))}(\mathbb{Z},-)\circ f\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))}(\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}G},-),

the only-if statement follows from the Yoneda lemma.
∎

Corollary 3.5.4
.

Suppose that
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
is such that
\mathbb{Z}[G]
is (
\kappa
-)-s-flat (
Definition

2.8.55
) and
\mathbb{Z}[G]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[G]^{{\square}}
.
Then

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}(G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}(G,-)\circ f\in\operatorname{Fun}\bigl(\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])),\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Ab})\bigr).

Proof.

Denote by
g^{{\square}}\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)})
and
g\colon\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G]))\to\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
the forget functors.
By
2.8.61
, the left adjoint
(-)^{L{\square}G}
exists and by
Lemma

2.8.68
,
g^{{\square}}(\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}G})\cong\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}
.
Since
g^{{\square}}
is conservative, the statement now follows from
Lemma

3.5.3
.
∎

Notation 3.5.5
.

For a topological space
X
denote by
\pi_{0}X
the set of connected components of
X
and endow it with the quotient topology induced by the projection
X\to\pi_{0}X
.

Corollary 3.5.6
.

Suppose that
G
is a topological group such that the quotient map
G\to\pi_{0}G
is a homotopy equivalence and
\pi_{0}G
is locally compact.

For cardinals
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(G)
,

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}sol}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},-)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cond}}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},-)\circ f.

If
G
is
\operatorname{T1}
, then also

H_{\operatorname{sol}}(\underline{G},-)\cong H_{\operatorname{cond}}(\underline{G},-)\circ f

via the above natural transformation.

Example 3.5.7
.

3.5.6
in particular applies to locally profinite groups. The statement for locally profinite groups was shown in
[
AB20
]
.

Proof.

By
2.1.19
,
\pi_{0}G
is a totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff topological group of
\operatorname{wt}(\pi_{0}G)\leq\operatorname{wt}(G)
. By van Dantzig’s theorem,
\pi_{0}G
is a coproduct of profinite sets. In particular,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{(\kappa)}]
is
(-)^{{\square}}
-acyclic for all
\kappa>\operatorname{wt}(G)
by
2.8.28
/
Lemma

2.8.36
.

By
2.9.2
,

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{(\kappa)}]^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}},

whence
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]
is (
\kappa
-)
s
-flat (
Definition

2.8.55
) by
Lemma

2.8.59
. In particular,
(-)^{L{\square}G}
exists by
2.8.61
.
The statement now follows from
3.5.4
.
∎

3.5.2
Solid and continuous group cohomology

Notation 3.5.8
.

For an uncountable cardinal
\kappa
and a topological group
G
denote by

\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{Cont}^{G}

the full subcategory on continuous
G
-modules
M
such that
\underline{M}_{\kappa}
is solid.

For a Hausdorff topological group
G
denote by

\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}}\subseteq\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}

the full subcategory on
\operatorname{T1}
continuous
G
-modules
M
such that
\underline{M}
is solid.

The goal of this section is to prove the following result:

Theorem 3.5.9
.

Suppose that
G
is a topological group which is a finite product of topological groups
\{G_{i}\}_{i=1,\ldots,n}
each of which satisfies one of the following properties, respectively:

(i)

G_{i}
is homotopy equivalent to a coproduct of (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff spaces.

(ii)

G_{i}
is homotopy equivalent to a Hausdorff space and to a locally contractible space.

(iii)

G_{i}
is locally connected and locally (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff.

Then there is a natural isomorphism

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{sol}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},-)\circ\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa},\operatorname{grAb}).

If in addition to the above,
G
is Hausdorff, then

H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{sol}}^{*}(\underline{G},-)\circ\underline{(-)}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}},\operatorname{grAb}).

Remark 3.5.10
.

The conditions of
3.5.9
are satisfied by a broad class of topological groups:

(i)

If
G
is locally compact abelian, then
G\cong\mathbb{R}^{n}\times H
where
H
admits a compact open subgroup (see e.g.
[
HM23
, Theorem 4]
), whence
G
satisfies
3.5.9
.

(ii)

Lie groups are locally contractible and hence satisfy
3.5.9
.

(iii)

By van Dantzig’s theorem, locally profinite groups are coproducts of compacta, whence
3.5.9
applies to them as well.
The statement for locally profinite groups was established in
[
AB20
]
.

The author is unaware whether there exist Hausdorff topological groups whose solid group cohomology is not isomorphic to their
k
-continuous group cohomology.

3.5.9
is an immediate consequence of
3.5.15
and
3.5.9
below. It follows from the following two observations:

(i)

For large classes of topological groups, including those satisfying
3.5.9
, the degreewise solidification
(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
of the simplicial resolution is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
(
Lemma

3.5.11
).

(ii)

Under the assumptions of
3.5.9
, this solidified resolution is a projective resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])
(
Lemma

3.5.16
).

Lemma 3.5.11
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group.

(i)

If
G
is homotopy equivalent to a Hausdorff space, the degreewise (underived) solidification of the simplicial complex
(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{\kappa}}
is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])
.

(ii)

If
G
is Hausdorff, the degreewise (underived) solidification of the simplicial complex
(S_{*}^{\underline{G}})^{{\square}\underline{G}}
is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
in
\operatorname{Solid}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])
.

Proof.

Since
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}})
and the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
is cocontinuous in both variables (the symmetric monoidal structure is closed
2.8.42
), the forget functor
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
creates small limits and colimits by
Proposition

1.4.1
.
It therefore suffices to show that the chain complex of solid abelian groups underlying
(S_{*}^{\underline{G}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
.
By
2.8.16
/
2.8.16
, this chain complex is given by applying
(-)^{{\square}}
, the left adjoint of
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
, degreewise to
S_{*}^{\underline{G}}
.
For a
(\kappa
-)condensed set
X
denote by
S_{*}^{X}\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab}))
the simplicial resolution of
X\to*
(
Definition

1.5.16
).
A homotopy equivalence
G\to X
induces a chain map
S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}}\to S_{*}^{\underline{X}_{\kappa}}
, and by
2.9.2
, the induced map
(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}})^{{\square}}\to(S_{*}^{\underline{X}_{\kappa}})^{{\square}}
is an isomorphism of chain complexes. It therefore suffices to show that for a Hausdorff space
X
,
(S_{*}^{\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}}
is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
.
Fix
n\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
and denote by
\pi_{i}\colon X^{n}\to X,1\leq i\leq n
the projections.
For a compact Hausdorff space
K
and a continuous map
f\colon K\to X^{i}
,

f(K)\subseteq(\cup_{i=1}^{n}\pi_{i}f(K))^{n}\subseteq X^{n},

and
\cup_{i=1}^{n}\pi_{i}(f(K))\subseteq X
is Hausdorff (since
X
is) and compact as quotient of
\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}K
. Hence by
Lemma

2.1.7
,
\operatorname{wt}(\cup_{i=1}^{n}\pi_{i}(K))\leq\operatorname{wt}(\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}K)\leq\operatorname{wt}(K)
.
This shows that for
n\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
,

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K^{n}}_{(\kappa)}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\to X^{n}\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K}\cong\underline{X^{n}}_{(\kappa)}

(
2.4.24
), and hence

S_{*}^{\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}S_{*}^{\underline{K}_{(\kappa)}}.

As solidification is a left adjoint, it follows from
2.8.51
that

(3.5.11.1)

(S_{*}^{\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(S_{*}^{\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}K\subseteq X\\
K\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(S_{*}^{\underline{\pi_{0}K}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}},

where
\pi_{0}K
denotes the topological space of connected components of
K
with quotient topology from
K\to\pi_{0}K
. By
Lemma

2.1.18
,
\pi_{0}K
is profinite and by
Lemma

2.1.7
,
\operatorname{wt}(\pi_{0}K)\leq\operatorname{wt}(K)
.
By
2.8.28
/
Lemma

2.8.36
for
P\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
,

S_{*}^{\underline{P}_{(\kappa)}}
is a
(-)^{{\square}}
-acyclic resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
, and hence

(S_{*}^{\underline{P}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}^{L{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}),

cf.
2.8.35
.
This means that for
P\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{(\kappa)}
, the degreewise solidification
(S_{*}^{\underline{P}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}}
of
S_{*}^{\underline{P}_{(\kappa)}}
is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
.
Since filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
are exact (
Lemma

2.6.3
), and
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}\subseteq\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})
is closed under limits and colimits (
Lemma

2.8.15
,
2.8.30
), filtered colimits in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
are exact.
It now follows that for
X
Hausdorff,
(S_{*}^{\underline{X}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}}
is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
.
∎

Together with
3.3.5
, this yields a comparison map from
\kappa
-/
k
-continuous group cohomology with solid coefficients to solid group cohomology for Hausdorff topological groups:

Recollection 3.5.12
.

Suppose
G
is a Hausdorff topological group.
As
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])
has enough projectives (
2.8.18
and
2.8.45
), there exists a projective resolution
P_{*}\to\mathbb{Z}
in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])
. This computes solid group cohomology (see e.g.
[
Sta22
,
Tag 06XR
]
), i.e.

H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])}(P_{*},-))\cong H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},-).

As
(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
is a resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
(
Lemma

3.5.11
), the identity
\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb{Z}}
lifts to a chain map
P_{*}\to(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
(
[
Wei94
, Proposition 2.2.6]
).
By
3.3.5
,

\displaystyle H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)|_{\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa}}

\displaystyle\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])}(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}},\underline{-}_{\kappa}))|_{\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa}}

\displaystyle\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])}((S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{\kappa}},\underline{-}_{\kappa}))|_{\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa}}

and

\displaystyle H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)|_{\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}}}

\displaystyle\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}(S_{*}^{\underline{G}},\underline{-}))|_{\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}}}

\displaystyle\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}((S_{*}^{\underline{G}})^{{\square}\underline{G}},\underline{-}))|_{\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}}}.

Pullback along the chain map
P_{*}\to(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
therefore defines natural transformations

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}(G,-)\longrightarrow H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])}(P_{*},-))\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}sol}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{(-)}_{\kappa})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa},\operatorname{grAb})

and

H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}(G,-)\longrightarrow H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}(P_{*},-))\cong H_{\operatorname{sol}}^{*}(\underline{G},\underline{(-)})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}},\operatorname{grAb}),

respectively.

Remarks 3.5.13
.

The natural transformation

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}(G,-)\longrightarrow H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])}(P_{*},-))\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}sol}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{(-)}_{\kappa})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa},\operatorname{grAb})

exists more generally if
G
is not Hausdorff, but merely homotopy equivalent to a Hausdorff topological space.
Since the chain map
P_{*}\to(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
is unique up to chain homotopy equivalence (
[
Wei94
, Proposition 2.2.6]
), the comparison map is independent of choices.

The composition

H_{\operatorname{\kappa/k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)|_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])}\to H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}sol}}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)})\to H_{\operatorname{cond}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)})

is the map induced by the edge homomorphism from
3.3.6
.

Lemma 3.5.14
.

For a (
\kappa
-)condensed group
G\in\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Set}))
, the degreewise solidification
(S_{*}^{G})^{{\square}G}
of the simplicial resolution is a chain complex of projectives in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
if and only if
\mathbb{Z}[G]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
.

Proof.

Denote by

F\colon\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]^{{\square}}}({\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}})

the free
\mathbb{Z}[G]^{{\square}}
-module functor (
Lemma

2.8.44
).
Since the forget functor (the right adjoint of
F
) reflects exact sequences, a solid abelian group
P\in\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
if and only if
F(P)
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])
.
In particular,

(S_{i}^{G})^{{\square}G}=\mathbb{Z}[{G^{i+1}}]^{{\square}G}\cong F(\mathbb{Z}[{G^{i}}]^{{\square}})

is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[G])
if and only if

\mathbb{Z}[G^{i}]^{{\square}}\cong\otimes^{i}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}}\mathbb{Z}[G]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
. Since tensor products of projectives are projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
(
2.8.46
), this holds for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
if and only if
\mathbb{Z}[G]^{{\square}}
is a projective solid abelian group.
∎

Corollary 3.5.15
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group.

(i)

If
G
is homotopy equivalent to a Hausdorff space and
\kappa
is an uncountable cardinal such that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
, then

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}sol}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{\kappa},-)\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])}(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{\kappa}},-))|_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}])}.

(ii)

If
G
is a Hausdorff topological group and
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}
, then

H_{\operatorname{sol}}^{*}(\underline{G},-)\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}(S_{*}^{\underline{G}},-))|_{\operatorname{Solid}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}])}.

In particular, under the above assumptions on
G
,

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}sol}}^{*}(\underline{G},-)\circ\underline{(-)}_{\kappa}\colon\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa}\to\operatorname{grAb},

and

H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{sol}}^{*}(\underline{G},-)\circ\underline{(-)}\colon\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}}\to\operatorname{grAb},

respectively.

Proof.

By
Lemma

3.5.11
and
Lemma

3.5.14
, our assumptions imply that
(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
is a projective resolution of
\mathbb{Z}
, whence

H_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})sol}}^{*}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},-)\cong H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])}((S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}})^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}},-)

by e.g.
[
Sta22
,
Tag 06XR
]
.
The right-hand side is isomorphic to

H^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])}(S_{*}^{\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}},-)|_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}])}

by definition of
(-)^{{\square}\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}}
.
The comparison with
k/\kappa
-continuous group cohomology is
3.3.5
.
∎

3.5.9
is now a consequence of the following observation:

Lemma 3.5.16
.

Suppose that
G
is a topological group which is a finite product of topological groups
\{G_{i}\}_{i=1,\ldots,n}
each of which satisfies one of the following properties, respectively.

(i)

G_{i}
is homotopy equivalent to a coproduct of (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff spaces.

(ii)

G_{i}
is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible topological space.

(iii)

G_{i}
is locally connected and locally (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff.

Endow
\pi_{0}G
with the quotient topology from the projection
G\to\pi_{0}G
.

Then the following hold:

–

\pi_{0}G
is a coproduct of (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff spaces.

–

The quotient map induces an isomorphism
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
and
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.

–

If in addition to the above,
G
is Hausdorff, then
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}
.

Proof.

We first reduce to the case that
G
satisfies one of the above conditions.
Write

G=\prod_{k=1}^{3}\prod_{i=1}^{n_{i}}G_{k,i}

as a product of topological groups such that
G_{k,i}
satisfies property
k
of
Lemma

3.5.16
.
Then
\prod_{i=1}^{n_{k}}G_{i,k}
satisfies property
(k)
for
1\leq k\leq 3
, so we can assume that
G=\prod_{k=1}^{3}G_{k}
for
G_{k}
a group satisfying property
(k)
.
We first show that

\pi_{0}(G_{1}\times G_{2}\times G_{3})\to\pi_{0}G_{1}\times\pi_{0}G_{2}\times\pi_{0}G_{3}

is a homemorphism, i.e. that
G_{0}\times G_{1}\times G_{3}\to\pi_{0}G_{1}\times\pi_{0}G_{2}\times\pi_{0}G_{3}
is a quotient map. If
h\colon G_{2}\to X
is a homotopy equivalence to a locally contractible topological space, then
h
descends to a continuous bijection
\pi_{0}G\to\pi_{0}X
. As
\pi_{0}X
is discrete, this implies that
\pi_{0}G
is discrete, i.e.
G_{2}
is locally connected.
This implies that
G_{4}\coloneqq G_{2}\times G_{3}
is locally connected. Denote by
C\subseteq G_{4}
the connected component of the identity. Then
G_{4}\cong C\times\pi_{0}G_{4}
as topological spaces (not necessarily as groups).
In particular,
G_{1}\times G_{4}\to G_{1}\times\pi_{0}G_{4}
is a quotient map. As
\pi_{0}G_{4}
is discrete,
G_{1}\times\pi_{0}G_{4}\to\pi_{0}G_{1}\times\pi_{0}G_{4}
is a quotient map as well, which shows that
G_{1}\times G_{2}\times G_{3}\to\pi_{0}G_{1}\times\pi_{0}G_{2}\times\pi_{0}G_{3}
is a quotient map.

As

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{(-)}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\colon(\operatorname{T1})\operatorname{Top}\to\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})

is symmetric monoidal and projective solid abelian groups are stable under solid tensor products, we are now reduced to proving the statement for groups satisfying one of the conditions
i)-iii)
of the lemma, respectively. We do this case-by-case.

(i)

If
h\colon G\to\sqcup_{i\in I}K(i)
is a homotopy equivalence to a coproduct of
(\kappa\text{-})
light compact Hausdorff spaces, then

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K(i)}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}

by
2.9.2
. By
2.8.51
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K(i)}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\oplus_{i\in I}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}K(i)}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}
, where
\pi_{0}K(i)
is endowed with quotient topology.
The space
\pi_{0}K(i)
is profinite (
Lemma

2.1.18
), and by
Lemma

2.1.7
,
\operatorname{wt}(\pi_{0}K(i))\leq\operatorname{wt}(K(i))
.
2.8.18
and
2.8.45
now imply that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}K(i)}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
.
It remains to show that
h
descends to a homeomorphism
\pi_{0}G\cong\sqcup_{i\in I}\pi_{0}K(i)
.
Choose a homotopy inverse
f
of
h
. Then
G=\sqcup_{i\in I}f^{-1}(K(i))
as topological space, which implies that
f
and
h
restrict to mutually inverse homotopy equivalences
K(i)\simeq f^{-1}(G_{i})
for all
i\in I
. The map
h
descends to continuous bijections
h_{i}\colon\pi_{0}K(i)\to\pi_{0}f^{-1}(G_{i}),i\in I
, which shows that
\pi_{0}G=\sqcup_{i\in I}\pi_{0}f^{-1}(K(i))
is a coproduct of compacta. As
\pi_{0}G
is Hausdorff (
2.1.19
),
\pi_{0}f^{-1}(K(i))
is Hausdorff for all
i\in I
. In particular, the maps
h_{i}
are homeomorphisms.

(ii)

Suppose now that
G
is homotopy equivalent to a locally contractible topological space. We explained above that
\pi_{0}G
is discrete in this case.
By
Lemma

2.9.4
, for all solid abelian groups
M
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}},M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}],M)

\displaystyle\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{0}(\underline{G}_{(\kappa)},M)

\displaystyle\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{0}(G,M(*)^{\delta})

\displaystyle\cong\mathcal{C}(G,M(*)^{\delta})

\displaystyle\cong\mathcal{C}(\pi_{0}G,M(*)^{\delta}),

and

\displaystyle\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}},M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{(\kappa)}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{(\kappa)}],M)

\displaystyle\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa\text{-})cond}}^{0}(\pi_{0}G,M)

\displaystyle\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}^{0}(\pi_{0}G,M(*)^{\delta})

\displaystyle\cong\mathcal{C}(\pi_{0}G,M(*)^{\delta}),

whence
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\oplus_{\pi_{0}G}\mathbb{Z}
is projective in
\operatorname{Solid}_{(\kappa)}
.

(iii)

Suppose now that
G
is locally (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff and locally connected and denote by
G^{0}
the connected component of the identity.
Then
\pi_{0}G
is discrete and
G\cong\sqcup_{x\in\pi_{0}G}G^{0}
as topological space. This implies that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong\oplus_{\pi_{0}G}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{0}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}
and the quotient map

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\to\oplus_{\pi_{0}G}\mathbb{Z}=\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}

is the coproduct of the projections
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{0}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\to\mathbb{Z}^{{\square}}
. It is therefore enough to show that
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{0}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}=\mathbb{Z}
.
Below, we will construct an ascending sequence
K_{n}\subseteq K_{n+1}
of (
\kappa
-light) compact connected subspaces such that
G^{0}=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}K_{n}
and for all compact subspaces
C\subseteq G^{0}
, there exists
N\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
C\subseteq K_{N}
.
Then it follows from
2.4.24
that

\underline{G^{0}}_{(\kappa)}\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}C\subseteq G^{0}\\
C\in\operatorname{CH}_{(\kappa)}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{C}_{(\kappa)}\cong{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\underline{K_{n}}_{(\kappa)}

and in particular
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{0}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}={\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{Z}[\underline{K_{n}}_{(\kappa)}]^{{\square}}\cong{\underset{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{Z}=\mathbb{Z}
by
2.8.51
.

We now construct such an exhaustion by compact, connected subspaces. Choose a (
\kappa
-light) compact neighborhood
e_{G}\in V\subseteq G
of the identity and an open, connected neighborhood
e_{G}\in U\subseteq V^{\circ}
, where
V^{\circ}
denotes the interior of
V
. Then
\overline{U}\subseteq V
,
\overline{U}
is compact Hausdorff and connected (as closure of a connected set) and
\operatorname{wt}(\overline{U})\leq\operatorname{wt}(V)
. Since

\tau\colon G\times G\to G,(g,h)\mapsto gh^{-1}

is continuous,
K_{0}\coloneqq\tau(\overline{U}\times\overline{U})\subseteq G
is a compact connected subspace.
As continuous surjections between compact Hausdorff spaces are quotient maps,

\operatorname{wt}(K_{0})\leq\operatorname{wt}(\overline{U})\leq\operatorname{wt}(V)

by
Lemma

2.1.7
. Define recursively

K_{n+1}\coloneqq\tau(K_{n}\times K_{n})\subseteq G.

It follows by induction that
K_{n}
is compact and connected and that
\operatorname{wt}(K_{n})\leq\operatorname{wt}(V)
(
Lemma

2.1.7
). Moreover,
K_{n}=\tau(K_{n}\times\{1\})\subseteq K_{n+1}
.
If
x,y\in K_{\infty}\coloneqq\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}K_{n}
choose
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
x,y\in K_{n}
. Then
xy^{-1}\in K_{n+1}
, which shows that
K_{\infty}\subseteq G^{0}
is a subgroup.
Since
U\subseteq K_{\infty}
and
K_{\infty}
is a subgroup,
K_{\infty}=\bigcup_{k\in K_{\infty}}kU
which shows that
K_{\infty}\subseteq G^{0}
is an open subgroup. This implies that
G^{0}=\sqcup_{g\in G^{0}/K_{\infty}}gK_{\infty}
, whence
G^{0}=K_{\infty}
by connectedness of
G^{0}
. Since
G^{0}=\bigcup_{k\in K_{\infty}}Uk^{-1}
is an open cover, for
C\subseteq G
compact, there exists a finite subset
F\subseteq K_{\infty}
such that
C\subseteq\bigcup_{f\in F}^{n}Uf^{-1}
.
If
N\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
is such that
F\subseteq K_{N}
, then
C\subseteq\tau(U\times K_{N})\subseteq K_{N+1}
. ∎

For topological groups as in
3.5.9
,
solid/continuous group cohomology can be identified with the continuous group cohomology of the group
\pi_{0}G
(endowed with the quotient topology from
G\to\pi_{0}G
):

Lemma 3.5.17
.

Suppose
G
is a topological group as in
3.5.9
.

(i)

Restriction along
p\colon G\to\pi_{0}G
yields an equivalence

p^{*}\colon\operatorname{Cont}^{\pi_{0}G}_{{\square},\kappa}\cong\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa},

and

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(\pi_{0}G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\circ p^{*}\colon\operatorname{Cont}^{\pi_{0}G}_{{\square},\kappa}\to\operatorname{grAb}.

(ii)

If
G
is in addition Hausdorff, then restriction along
p\colon G\to\pi_{0}G
is an equivalence

p^{*}\colon\operatorname{T1Cont}^{\pi_{0}G}_{{\square}}\cong\operatorname{T1Cont}^{G}_{{\square}},

and

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(\pi_{0}G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{k\text{-}cont}}^{*}(G,-)\circ p^{*}\colon\operatorname{T1Cont}^{\pi_{0}G}_{{\square}}\to\operatorname{grAb}.

Remark 3.5.18
.

In contrast to the above condensed group cohomology also depends on the connected component
G^{0}
, see the discussion around
3.4.8
. This yields many examples where condensed group cohomology differs from solid group cohomology.

Proof.

We only prove the
\kappa
-condensed statement, the condensed statement can be shown completely analogously.
Since
p\colon G\to\pi_{0}G
is surjective,

p^{*}\colon\operatorname{Cont}^{\pi_{0}G}\to\operatorname{Cont}^{G}

is fully faithful. Suppose that
M\in\operatorname{Cont}^{G}
is such that
\underline{M}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
.
The action map
G\times M\to M
induces a map of condensed abelian groups
\mu\colon\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\underline{M}_{\kappa}\to\underline{M}_{\kappa}
.
Since
\underline{M}_{\kappa}
is solid, this extends to a map

\mu^{{\square}}\colon(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\underline{M}_{\kappa})^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}^{{\square}}\underline{M}_{\kappa}\to\underline{M}_{\kappa}.

By
Lemma

3.5.16
,
\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}\cong\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}}
via the projection, this implies that
\mu
factors over a map

\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{\kappa}]\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\underline{M}_{\kappa}\to\underline{M}_{\kappa},

and hence the
G
-action
\underline{G}_{\kappa}\times\underline{M}_{\kappa}\to\underline{M}_{\kappa}
factors as
\underline{G}_{\kappa}\times\underline{M}_{\kappa}\to\underline{\pi_{0}G}_{\kappa}\times\underline{M}_{\kappa}\to\underline{M}_{\kappa}
.
The underlying map
\pi_{0}G\times M\to M
is
\kappa
-continuous and hence continuous as
\pi_{0}G
is
\kappa
-compactly generated by
Lemma

3.5.16
.
This shows that
p^{*}\colon\operatorname{Cont}^{\pi_{0}G}_{{\square},\kappa}\to\operatorname{Cont}^{G}_{{\square},\kappa}
is essentially surjective.

By
Proposition

2.2.7
and
Lemma

3.5.16
, for a topological abelian group
M
with
\underline{M}_{\kappa}\in\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}
,

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(G^{i},M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{i}}_{\kappa}],M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{G^{i}}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}},M)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Solid}_{\kappa}}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{(\pi_{0}G^{i})}_{\kappa}]^{{\square}},\underline{M}_{\kappa})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})}(\mathbb{Z}[\underline{\pi_{0}(G^{i})}_{\kappa}],\mathbb{Z})

\displaystyle\cong\mathcal{C}_{\kappa}(\pi_{0}(G^{i}),M)

via the projection
G^{i}\to\pi_{0}G^{i}
.
We have shown in the proof of
3.5.9
that
\pi_{0}(G^{i})\cong(\pi_{0}G)^{i}
for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, and hence

H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}(G,-)\circ p^{*}\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}(\pi_{0}G,-)\circ p^{*}
.
As
\pi_{0}(G^{i})
is
\kappa
-compactly generated for all
i\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
,

H_{\operatorname{cont}}^{*}(\pi_{0}G,-)\cong H_{\operatorname{\kappa\text{-}cont}}^{*}(\pi_{0}G,-).\qed

Appendix A
Appendix

A.1
Adjunctions and filtered colimits of categories

In this section, we record some basic results on adjunctions and filtered colimits of categories which we repeatedly used to generalise results from presentable to big presentable categories.
For categories
\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}
denote by
\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
the full subcategory on left adjoint functors.

Lemma A.1.1
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}
are categories and
I
is a category such that
\mathcal{D}
admits
I
-indexed colimits and
\mathcal{C}
admits
I^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed limits. Then the following hold:

(i)

\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
is closed under
I
-indexed colimits and
I
-indexed colimits can be computed pointwise.

(ii)

\operatorname{Fun}^{R}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{C})
is closed under
I
-indexed limits and they can be computed pointwise.

Proof.

It suffices to prove the statement on left adjoint functors, then the statement on right adjoint functors follows from replacing
\mathcal{C}
and
\mathcal{D}
by their opposites.
Denote by

(-)^{R}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{R}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{op}}

the equivalence provided by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.2.6.2]
and suppose
F\colon I\to\operatorname{Fun}^{L}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
is some diagram.
As
\mathcal{D}
has all
I
-indexed colimits,
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
has all
I
-indexed colimits and they can be computed pointwise by
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.1.2.3]
.
Analogously,
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{C})
has all
I^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed limits and they can be computed pointwise.
This implies that for
d\in\mathcal{D}
,
c\in\mathcal{C}
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(({\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F_{i})(c),d)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}({\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F_{i}(c),d)\cong{\underset{i\in I^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(F_{i}(c),d)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,F_{i}^{R}(d))

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,{\underset{i\in I^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}(F_{i}^{R}(d)))\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,({\underset{i\in I^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}F_{i}^{R})(d)).

This equivalence is clearly natural in
c,d
and exhibits
{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{colim}}}F_{i}
as left adjoint to
{\underset{i\in I^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{lim}}}F_{i}^{R}
.
∎

We repeatedly used the following result to
glue
left adjoints.

Lemma A.1.2
.

Suppose that
\Lambda
is a possibly large category,
l\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
and for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
l({\lambda})
admits a right adjoint such that the mate of the commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}_{\mu}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D_{\lambda}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}_{\mu}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C(\lambda\to\mu)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces l({\lambda})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces l({\mu})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D(\lambda\to\mu)}

commutes.

(i)

There exist
r\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
with
r(\lambda)=r_{\lambda}
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
and
\epsilon\colon l\circ r\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}}
such that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\epsilon(\lambda)
exhibits
r(\lambda)
as right adjoint to
l({\lambda})
.

(ii)

By taking the colimit over
\Lambda
, we obtain functors

l_{\infty}\colon{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}_{*}\to{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}C_{*}\text{ and }r_{\infty}\colon{\underset{\lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}C_{*}\to{\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}_{*}

and a natural transformation
\epsilon_{\infty}\colon l_{\infty}r_{\infty}\to\operatorname{id}
which exhibits
l_{\infty}
as left adjoint to
r_{\infty}
.

Proof.

This follows from a characterization of parametrized adjoint functors
[
MW24
, Corollary 3.2.3, 3.2.8/Corollary 3.2.3]
/ the discussion of relative adjunctions in
[
Lur17
, section 7.3]
.
Work in the large universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
so that
\Lambda
is small and
identify

\operatorname{Fun}(\Lambda,\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathcal{U}_{1}-\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\Lambda)^{\operatorname{op}},\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}),

where presheaves are taken in the universe
\mathcal{U}_{1}
and
\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathcal{U}_{1}-\operatorname{lim}}
refers to the category of
\mathcal{U}_{1}
-small limits-preserving functors.
By
[
MW24
, Corollary 3.2.3, 3.2.8]
, there exist

r\colon\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}\in\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathcal{U}_{1}-\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\Lambda^{\operatorname{op}})^{\operatorname{op}},\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})

with
r(\lambda)=r_{\lambda}
for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
and natural transformations

\epsilon\colon l\circ r\to\operatorname{id},\eta\colon\operatorname{id}\to r\circ l

satisfying the triangle identities.
It follows that

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\epsilon(\lambda)\colon{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}l(\lambda)\circ{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}r(\lambda)\to\operatorname{id}_{{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}(\lambda)}

and

{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\eta(\lambda)\colon\operatorname{id}_{{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(\lambda)}\to{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}r(\lambda){\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}l(\lambda)

satisfy the triangle identities and hence exhibit
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}l(\lambda)
as left adjoint to
{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}r(\lambda)
.
∎

Lemma A.1.3
.

Suppose that
\Lambda
is a possibly large filtered category and
\mathcal{B}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is a diagram of large categories such that for all
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
is fully faithful.
Denote by
\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
its colimit in the very large category of large categories
\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
.

(i)

For all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is fully faithful.

(ii)

If for all
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
is a left adjoint, then
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}
is a left adjoint and in particular preserves all colimits.

(iii)

If
I
is a category such that for all
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
preserves
I
-indexed (co)limits, then
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}
preserves
I
-indexed (co)limits, respectively.

(iv)

Suppose
I
is a category such that for all
F\colon I\to\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
, there exists
\lambda\in\Lambda
such that
F
factors over
I\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
. If
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
has
I
-indexed (co)limits for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
and for all
\lambda\to\kappa\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}
preserves
I
-indexed (co)limits, then
{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}
has all
I
-indexed (co)limits.

Proof.

(i)

For
\kappa\to\lambda\in\Lambda
denote by

\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\xrightarrow{i^{\lambda}_{\kappa}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\xrightarrow{i_{\lambda}}\mathcal{B}_{\infty}

the canonical maps.
For
\lambda\in\Lambda
and
b,c\in\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(i_{\lambda}b,i_{\lambda}c)\cong{\underset{\mu\in\phantom{}_{\lambda\backslash}\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{B_{\mu}}(i_{\lambda}^{\mu}b,i_{\lambda}^{\mu}c),

see e.g
[
Roz
]
in the large universe.
By assumption, this is a filtered colimit over equivalences, which shows fully faithfulness of
i_{\lambda}
.

(ii)

Suppose now that
\lambda
is such that for all
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda
,
i_{\lambda}^{\mu}\colon\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
is a left adjoint. We want to construct a left adjoint to
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
.
Since
\Lambda
is filtered,
{\underset{\kappa\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\cong{\underset{\mu\in\lambda\backslash\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
.
Denote by
c\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\colon\phantom{}_{\lambda\backslash}\Lambda\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
the constant functor with value
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}
, and denote by

c\colon c\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{*}\in\operatorname{Fun}(_{\lambda\backslash}\Lambda,\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})

the canonical natural transformation.
For
\lambda\to\mu\in\lambda\backslash\Lambda
, choose a right adjoint

r_{\mu}\colon\mathcal{B}_{\mu}=\mathcal{B}(\mu)\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}=c\mathcal{B}(\mu)

of
c(\mu)=i_{\lambda}^{\mu}=\mathcal{B}(\lambda\to\mu)
.
We claim that for
(\lambda\to\kappa)\to(\lambda\to\mu)\in\phantom{}_{\lambda\backslash}\Lambda
, the mate of
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}(\kappa)=\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}(\mu)=\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B_{\kappa}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}_{\mu}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c(\kappa)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{id}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c(\mu)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}(\kappa\to\mu)}

commutes, i.e.

\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}r^{\kappa}_{\lambda}\to r^{\mu}_{\lambda}k(\mu)\operatorname{id}_{B_{\lambda}}r^{\kappa}_{\lambda}\cong r^{\mu}_{\lambda}c(\mu)c(\kappa)r^{\kappa}_{\lambda}\to r^{\mu}_{\lambda}\mathcal{B}(\lambda\to\mu)

is an equivalence. The first map is induced by a unit whitnessing
k(\mu)=\mathcal{B}(\lambda\to\mu)\dashv r^{\mu}_{\lambda}
and hence an equivalence since
\mathcal{B}(\lambda\to\mu)
is fully faithful.
Since both are right adjoint to
\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to\mathcal{B}_{\kappa}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
,
r^{\mu}_{\lambda}\cong r^{\kappa}_{\lambda}\circ r^{\mu}_{\kappa}
.
As
\mathcal{B}(\kappa\to\mu)
is fully faithful, under this equivalence, the right map becomes

r^{\kappa}_{\lambda}(c(\kappa)r^{\kappa}_{\lambda}\to\operatorname{id})
which is an equivalence by fully faithfulness of
c(\kappa)=\mathcal{B}(\lambda\to\kappa)
.
It now follows from
Lemma

A.1.2
, that

i_{\lambda}\colon\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}={\underset{\lambda\backslash\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}c\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}\to{\underset{\lambda\backslash\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}

is left adjoint to
{\underset{\mu\in\phantom{}_{\lambda\backslash}\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}r^{\mu}_{\lambda}
.

(iii)

Suppose that
I
is a diagram such that for all
\lambda\to\mu
in
\Lambda
,
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\to\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
preserves
I
-indexed (co)limits. Suppose
F\colon I\to\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
has a limit
{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}^{\lambda}F
in
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}
.
The projections
{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}^{\lambda}F\to F_{i}
induce a natural transformation

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B}_{\infty}}(-,i_{\lambda}{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}^{\lambda}F)\to{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(-,i_{\lambda}F_{i})\in\operatorname{Fun}({\underset{\Lambda}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{B}_{*}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}).

For all
\lambda\to\mu\in\Lambda
and all
b\in\mathcal{B}_{\mu}^{\operatorname{op}}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}}
, this is an equivalence since
\mathcal{B_{\lambda}}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\mu}
preserves
I
-indexed limits and
\mathcal{B}_{\mu}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_{\infty}
is fully faithful. This shows that

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(-,i_{\lambda}{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}^{\lambda}F)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B_{\infty}}}(-,i_{\lambda}F_{i})\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{B}_{\infty}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}),

i.e.
i_{\lambda}({\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}^{\lambda}F)
is the limit of
i_{\lambda}F
in
\mathcal{B_{\infty}}
.
The dual argument shows the statement on colimits.

(iv)

The fourth statement is an immediate consequence of the third.

∎

Lemma A.1.4
.

If
\mathcal{C}_{*}\colon I\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is a possibly large diagram of large categories, for
i\in I
denote by
p_{i}\colon{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}_{i}
the canonical map.
For
x,y\in{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}_{*}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}_{*}}(x,y)\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}_{i}}(p_{i}(x),p_{i}(y)).

Proof.

This holds as
\operatorname{Map}_{{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}_{*}}(x,y)
is the pullback of

*\xrightarrow{(x,y)}{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}_{*}\times{\underset{i\in I\mathcal{C}_{*}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\xleftarrow{(\text{s,t})}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}_{*}),

in
\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}
where
s,t
denote the source and target maps, and

\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},{\underset{I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\mathcal{C}_{*})\cong{\underset{i\in I}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{C}_{i})
.
∎

We used the following elementary observation in our discussion of accessible (hyper)sheaves.

Lemma A.1.5
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is an accessible category.
For every object
x\in\mathcal{X}
, there exists a regular cardinal
\kappa
such that
x
is
\kappa
-compact.

Proof.

Choose a regular cardinal
\lambda
such that
\mathcal{X}
is
\lambda
-accessible.
By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.4.2.2]
, every object in
\mathcal{X}
is a
\lambda
-filtered colimit of
\lambda
-compact objects. For
x\in\mathcal{X}
choose a regular cardinal
\kappa\geq\lambda
such that
x
is a
\kappa
-small colimit of
\lambda
-compact objects.
As
\kappa
-filtered colimits commute with
\kappa
-small limits in
\operatorname{An}
(
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.3.3.3]
), this implies that
x
is
\kappa
-compact.∎

A.1.1
Derived functors

We now record two results about derived functors which we used in our discussion of solid modules.

Lemma A.1.6
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{A}
is a Grothendieck abelian category with enough projectives and
\mathcal{D}
is a stable, presentable category with an accessible, left and right-complete
t
-structure
(\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\leq 0})
which is compatible with filtered colimits.
Denote by

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p},\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}),\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{D}(A),\mathcal{D})

the full subcategory on small colimits preserving, right
t
-exact functors
F\colon\mathcal{D}(A)\to\mathcal{D}
such that for all projective objects
P\in\mathcal{A}
,
F(P)\in\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}
.

Then

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p},\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(A),\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}),F\mapsto H_{0}\circ F|_{\mathcal{A}}

is an equivalence.

Proof.

Let
\mathcal{D}(A)_{>-\infty}\coloneqq{\underset{n\to-\infty}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{D}(A)_{\geq n}
. By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 1.3.3.2, Theorem 1.3.5.24]
,

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p}}(\mathcal{D}(A)_{>-\infty},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-ex}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}),F\mapsto H_{0}\circ F|_{\mathcal{A}}

is an equivalence, where the left-hand side denotes right
t
-exact functors
F\colon\mathcal{D}(A)_{>-\infty}\to\mathcal{D}
such that for all projective objects
P\in\mathcal{A}
,
F(P)\in\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}
.

By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.7]
, a right exact functor
\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}
preserves small colimits if and only if it preserves coproducts, and a right
t
-exact functor
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{>-\infty}\to\mathcal{D}
preserves small colimits if and only if it preserves small coproducts. As small coproducts in
\mathcal{A}
are exact, under the above equivalence, a functor
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{>-\infty}\to\mathcal{D}
preserves small coproducts if and only if
H_{0}\circ F|_{\mathcal{A}}
does.
Whence the above restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p},\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(A)_{>-\infty},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-ex},\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}).

Restriction defines an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p}}(\mathcal{D}(A)_{>-\infty},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p}}(\mathcal{D}(A)_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0}).

As the
t
-structures on
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
and
\mathcal{D}
are right-complete (
[
Lur17
, Theorem 1.3.5.21]
) and
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0}
are Grothendieck prestable (
[
Lur18a
, Definition C.1.4.2]
), by
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1 and Remark C.1.2.10]
, restriction is an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}),\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0}).

This restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}),\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{p}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0})

between those functors which carry projectives in
\mathcal{A}
to
\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}
.
∎

Corollary A.1.7
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{D}
is a stable, big presentable category which has small colimits, and
(\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\leq 0})
is a left-complete
t
-structure such that the following holds:

•

There is an exhaustion
\mathcal{D}_{*}\colon M\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
for
\mathcal{D}
by presentable categories such that for all
\mu\in M
,
(\mathcal{D}_{\mu}\cap\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\mu}\cap\mathcal{D}_{\leq 0})
is an accessible, right-complete
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}_{\mu}
which is compatible with filtered colimits.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is a hyperaccessible explicit covering site,
\mathcal{C}
is a 1-category and
R\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab}))
is such that
\mathcal{A}\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab})})
has enough projectives.

Then

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{p},\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(A),\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}),F\mapsto H_{0}\circ F|_{\mathcal{A}}

is an equivalence.

Proof.

By
[
Lur17
, Theorem 1.3.3.2, Theorem 1.3.3.7]
,

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-t-ex},\operatorname{p}}(\mathcal{D}(A)_{>-\infty},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{r-ex}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}),F\mapsto H_{0}\circ F|_{\mathcal{A}}.

As coproducts in
\mathcal{A}
are exact (this follows from
Propositions

1.4.1
and
1.1.15
), the same argument as in the proof of
Lemma

A.1.6
shows that this restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{p},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{>-\infty},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{\heartsuit}).

It remains to show that restriction defines an equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}),\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0}).

Denote by
\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
the large poset of regular cardinals
\lambda
such that
(\mathcal{C},S)
is
\lambda
-hyperaccessible and choose
r\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C}}
with

{R}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{r},\operatorname{Ab}))\subseteq\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Shv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab}).

Recall from
Lemma

1.4.32
that there is a
t
-exact equivalence

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})})\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq r}}{\operatorname{colim}}}{\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp})})}.

By construction (see the proof of
Lemma

1.4.32
) this is a filtered colimit of
t
-exact equivalences

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp})}),\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq r},

where
\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}\coloneqq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{Shv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Ab})})
.

Propositions

1.4.1
,
1.1.15
and
1.1.28

imply that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq r}
,

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp})})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})})\cong\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})

preserves small colimits and that small colimits in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})})
can always be computed on some stage

\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}_{S}(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp})})\subseteq\operatorname{LMod}_{{R}}({\operatorname{hypShv}^{\operatorname{acc}}_{S}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp})})\cong\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}).

It now follows from
Lemma

1.3.12
that

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}),-)\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}),-)

and that

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0},-)\cong{\underset{\lambda\in\Lambda}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0},-).

We are therefore reduced to showing that for all
\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{C},\geq r}
, restriction

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0})

is an equivalence.
Fix
\lambda\in\Lambda
. By
[
AGV71
, Exposé 2, 6.7]
,
\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}

is Grothendieck abelian. Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{D}_{*}\colon M\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
by presentable categories such that the induced
t
-structure on
\mathcal{D}_{\mu}
is right-complete, accessible and compatible with filtered colimits for all
\mu\in M
.
As for all
\mu\to\kappa\in M
,
\mathcal{D}_{\mu}\to\mathcal{D}_{\kappa}
preserves colimits, is fully faithful and
t
-exact, for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,

c_{1}\colon{\underset{\mu\in M}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{D}_{\mu})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{D})

and

c_{2}\colon{\underset{\mu\in M}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\mu,\geq 0})\to\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0})

are fully faithful by
Lemma

A.1.3
. By
1.3.18
and
1.4.26
and
[
Lur17
, Theorem 1.3.5.21]
,
c_{1}
is essentially surjective.
The
t
-structures on
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})
and
\mathcal{D}_{\mu}
are right-complete (by
[
Lur17
, Theorem 1.3.5.21]
and assumption on
\mathcal{D}_{\mu}
), and
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0}
are Grothendieck prestable (
[
Lur18a
, Definition C.1.4.2]
).
[
Lur18a
, Proposition C.3.1.1 and Remark C.1.2.10]
now implies that

{\underset{\mu\in M}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim},\operatorname{r-t-ex}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}),\mathcal{D}_{\mu})\cong{\underset{\mu\in M}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0},\mathcal{D}_{\mu,\geq 0})

via restriction.

It remains to show that
c_{2}
is essentially surjective.
As
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})
is presentable, there exists an small collection of objects
\mathcal{C}
which generates
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})
under small colimits.
For a functor
F\colon\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}_{\lambda})_{\geq 0}\to\mathcal{D}
choose
\mu\in M
such that
\oplus_{c\in\mathcal{C}}F(c)\in\mathcal{D}_{\mu,\geq 0}
. As
\mathcal{D}_{(\mu),\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}_{(\mu)}
is closed under small colimits, this implies that for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,

F(c)=\operatorname{Cofib}(\oplus_{d\in\mathcal{C}}F(d)\to\oplus_{d\in\mathcal{C},c\neq d}F(d)\to\oplus_{d\in\mathcal{C}}F(d))\in\mathcal{D}_{\mu}\subseteq\mathcal{D}.

As
\mathcal{D}_{\mu}\subseteq\mathcal{D}
is closed under small colimits and
F
is cocontinuous, this implies that
F
factors over
\mathcal{D}_{\mu,\geq 0}
, which shows that
c_{2}
is essentially surjective.
∎

Lemma A.1.8
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}
are Grothendieck abelian categories such that countable products in
\mathcal{A}
and
\mathcal{B}
are exact, and
l\colon\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{B}
is an exact, fully faithful functor which preserves small colimits and countable products.
Suppose that
\mathcal{A}
has enough projectives, and for all projectives
p\in\mathcal{A}
and all
a\in\mathcal{A}
,

\operatorname{Ext}^{*}_{\mathcal{B}}(lp,lb)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{0}_{\mathcal{B}}(lp,lb)

is concentrated in degree
0
.

Then the derived functor of
l
,
L\colon\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\to\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})
is fully faithful.

Proof.

We proceed analogous to the proof of
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.3.7]
.

Since
\mathcal{A}
and
\mathcal{B}
are Grothendieck abelian, the
t
-structures on their derived categories
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}),\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})
are right-complete by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.3.5.21]
.
As countable products in
\mathcal{A}
and
\mathcal{B}
exist and are exact,
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
and
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})
admit countable products and they can be computed on the level of representing chain complexes. In particular,
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
and
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})_{\geq 0}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})
are stable under countable products. It now follows from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.2.1.19]
that the
t
-structures on
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
and
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})
are left-complete.

This implies that

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(-,-)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{m\to-\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{n\to\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\tau_{\geq m}-,\tau_{\leq n}-)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{m\to-\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{n\to\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{A}}(\tau_{\leq n}\tau_{\geq m}-,\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}-)

and

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})}(-,-)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{m\to-\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{n\to\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})}(\tau_{\geq m}-,\tau_{\leq n}-)

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{m\to-\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}{\underset{n\to\infty}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{B}}(\tau_{\leq n}\tau_{\geq m}-,\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}-).

As coproducts and countable products in
\mathcal{A}
and
\mathcal{B}
are exact, and
l
preserves small colimits, finite limits and countable products,
L
preserves coproducts and countable products (which can be computed degreewise on representing chain complexes).
L
also preserves mapping cones and hence arbitrary small colimits by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.7]
.
It follows from
Lemma

1.4.26
that
L
also preserves finite limits and hence countable limits by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.4.2.7]
.
Since
L
is
t
-exact, it follows that under the above identifications,

L_{*}\colon\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(-,-)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})}(L-,L-)

is the limit of the natural transformations

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}-,\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}-)\to

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(L\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}-,L\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}-)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}L-,\tau_{\geq m}\tau_{\leq n}L-)

induced by
L_{*}
.

It therefore suffices to show that
L_{*}
restricts to a fully faithful functor
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})\to\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})
.
Denote by
R\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
the full subcategory on objects
r
such that for all
a\in\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
,

L_{*}\colon\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(a,r)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})}(La,Lr)

is an equivalence.
As
R
is closed under finite limits, shifts and extensions, it suffices to show that
\mathcal{A}\subseteq R
, then it follows that
R=\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
.
Fix
a\in\mathcal{D}^{b}(A)
and represent it by a chain complex of projectives
p_{*}
which is concentrated in degrees
\geq-n
.
Denote by
p_{*}^{\leq 0}
the stupid truncation of
p_{*}
.
As
\operatorname{Cofib}(p_{*}^{\leq 0}\to p_{*})\in\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})_{\geq 1}
, for
r\in\mathcal{A}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(p_{*},r)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(p_{*}^{\leq 0},r)

and

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})}(Lp_{*},Lr)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})}(L(p_{*}^{\leq 0}),Lr),

where we used again that
L
is
t
-exact.

We are therefore reduced to showing that for a bounded complex of projectives
p_{*}
and
r\in\mathcal{A}
,

L_{*}\colon\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(p_{*},r)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})}(Lp_{*},Lr)

is an equivalence.
We show the stronger statement that for a bounded complex of projectives
p_{*}
and
r\in\mathcal{A}
,

L_{*}\colon\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{A}}(p_{*},r)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{B}}(Lp_{*},Lr)

is an equivalence for all
k\in\mathbb{Z}
.

Fix
r\in\mathcal{A}
and denote by
G_{r}\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
the category on objects
a
such that

L_{*}\colon\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{A}}(a,r)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{B}}(La,Lr)

is an equivalence for all
k\in\mathbb{Z}
.
As
L
is cocontinuous,
G_{r}
is closed under colimits, extensions and shifts. It therefore suffices to show that for all projective objects
p\in\mathcal{A}
,
p\in G_{r}
, then it follows that
G_{r}
contains all bounded complexes of projectives.
Fix a projective object
p\in\mathcal{A}
.
As

L(p)=l(p),L(r)=l(r)\in\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B})^{\heartsuit}

and
p,r\in\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})^{\heartsuit}
,
for
k<0
,

\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{A}}(p,r)=0=\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{B}}(Lp,Lr).

For
k>0
,
\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{A}}(p,r)=0
since
p
is projective and
\operatorname{Ext}^{k}_{\mathcal{B}}(Lp,Lr)=0
by our assumption on
l
.
The map
L_{*}\colon\operatorname{Ext}^{0}_{\mathcal{A}}(p,r)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{0}_{\mathcal{A}}(Lp,Lr)
is an equivalence by fully faithfulness of
l
.
∎

A.2
Operadic adjunctions

In this section, we recall how a monoidal adjunction/localization induces an adjunction/localization on module categories. Everything is a well-known and straightforward consequence of the results on relative adjunctions from
[
Lur17
, section 7.3.2]
.
We freely use the notation established in
[
Lur17
, Chapters 2,4]
.
We first recall the results for a general operad before specialising to module categories.

Definition A.2.1
.

Suppose
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\to N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
is an operad (
[
Lur17
, Definition 2.1.1.10]
).

(i)

We refer to
\mathcal{O}\coloneqq\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{*}}\{<0>\}
as the category underlying
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
.

(ii)

For an
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal (
[
Lur17
, Definition 2.1.2.13]
) category
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
, its underlying category is
\mathcal{C}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\{[0]\}
.

(iii)

If
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\in{{{\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}}}_{/\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}}
are
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal categories, a lax
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functor is an operad map (
[
Lur17
, Definition 2.1.2.7]
)
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
over
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
.
We denote by
\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}-\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}_{{{\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}}_{/\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}}}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})
the full subcategory on lax
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functors.

Lemma A.2.2
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\in{{{\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}}}_{/\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}}
are
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal categories and
F,G\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}-\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})
are lax
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functors.
Denote by

i\colon\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\{<1>\}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}

the canonical functor.

A natural transformation
\eta\colon F\to G\in\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})
is an equivalence if and only if for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
, the induced natural transformation
\eta_{io}\colon F_{io}\to G_{io}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{io\},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{io\})
is an equivalence.

Proof.

Denote by
\mathcal{O}^{\circ}\subseteq\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
the wide subcategory on inert morphisms (
[
Lur17
, Definition 2.1.2.3]
), and let

\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\coloneqq\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\mathcal{O}^{\circ},\,\,\mathcal{D}^{\circ}\coloneqq\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\mathcal{O}^{\circ}.

As cocartesian fibrations are stable under pullback (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 2.4.2.3]
),
\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\to\mathcal{O}^{\circ}
and
\mathcal{D}^{\circ}\to\mathcal{O}^{\circ}
are cocartesian fibrations.
A morphism
a\to b\in\mathcal{C}^{\circ}
is
(\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\to\mathcal{O}^{\circ})
-cocartesian if and only if its image in
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is
(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes})
-cocartesian (
[
Lur18
,
Tag 01UF
]
). Hence by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 2.4.1.3]
, the
(\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\to\mathcal{D}^{\circ})
-cocartesian morphisms in
\mathcal{C}^{\circ}
are precisely the inert morphisms, and analogously for
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
.
Pullback along
\mathcal{O}^{\circ}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
therefore defines a functor

(-)^{\circ}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}-\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{CoCart}/\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}(\mathcal{C}^{\circ},\mathcal{D}^{\circ})

from the category of lax
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functors
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
to the category of functors of coartesian fibrations
\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\to\mathcal{D}^{\circ}
over
\mathcal{O}^{\circ}
.
As
\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\to\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is essentially surjective, this functor is conservative.
By 2-categorical straightening unstraightening (
[
BB24
, Proposition A.2.9]
), the right-hand side is equivalent to the category
\operatorname{Nat}(\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\mathcal{C}^{\circ},\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\mathcal{D}^{\circ})
of natural transformations

\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\to\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\mathcal{D}^{\circ}
of functors
\mathcal{O}^{\circ}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{(\infty,2)}
.
By
[
Lur17
, Definition 2.1.2.13]
, for
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
and

o=(o_{1},\ldots,o_{n})\in\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}_{<n>}\cong\mathcal{O}^{n},

the inert morphisms
o\to o_{i}\in\mathcal{O}^{\circ}
induce an equivalence

\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}(\mathcal{C}^{\circ})(o)=\mathcal{C}^{\circ}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\{o\}=\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{o\}\cong\prod_{i=1}^{n}\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{o_{i}\}=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}(\mathcal{C}^{\circ})(o_{i}),

and analogously for
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
.
Since
F^{\circ},G^{\circ}
are maps of cocartesian fibrations, under these identifications,

\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}F^{\circ}(o)\cong\prod_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}F^{\circ}(o_{i}),\,\,\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}G^{\circ}(o)\cong\prod_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}G^{\circ}(o_{i}),

and

\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\eta^{\circ}(o)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\eta^{\circ}(o_{i}).

In particular,
\eta^{\circ}
is an equivalence if and only if for all
o\in\mathcal{O}^{\circ}_{<1>}=\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}_{<1>}
,

\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}\eta^{\circ}(o)\colon\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}F^{\circ}(o)\to\operatorname{\operatorname{st}}_{\mathcal{O}^{\circ}}G^{\circ}(o)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{o\},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{o\})

is an equivalence.
∎

Lemma A.2.3

(
[
Lur17
, Corollary 7.3.2.7]
)
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
is an
\infty
-operad and denote by

i\colon\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\{<1>\}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}

the canonical functor.
Suppose that
p_{\mathcal{C}}\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\,p_{\mathcal{D}}\colon\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
are
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal categories and
L\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a strong
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functor (
[
Lur17
, Definition 2.1.3.7]
) such that for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
, the induced functor

L_{io}\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{io\}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{io\}

admits a right adjoint.

(i)

There exists a lax
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functor
R\colon\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
which is right adjoint to
L
relative to
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
, i.e. there exists a unit transformation
\eta\colon 1\to RL
such that
p_{\mathcal{C}}\circ\eta\colon p_{\mathcal{C}}\to p_{\mathcal{C}}RL
is an equivalence.

(ii)

For all
o\in\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
,
\eta_{o}\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}}\{o\}}\to R_{o}L_{o}
exhibits
R_{o}
as right adjoint to
L_{o}
.

Remark A.2.4
.

In the situation of the above lemma, the counit
\epsilon LR\to\operatorname{id}
is also relative to
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
, i.e.
p_{\mathcal{D}}(\epsilon)
is an equivalence.
Indeed: As
R
is lax
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal,
p_{\mathcal{D}}=p_{\mathcal{C}}\circ R
.
By the triangle identities, for
d\in\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
,
R(\epsilon_{d})\circ\eta_{Rd}=id_{Rd}
, whence

id_{p_{\mathcal{C}}(Rd)}=p_{\mathcal{D}}(\epsilon_{d})\circ p_{\mathcal{C}}(\eta_{Rd}).

As
p_{\mathcal{C}}(\eta_{Rd})
is an equivalence, this shows that
p_{\mathcal{D}}(\epsilon_{d})
is an equivalence.
The triangle identities moreover imply that for all
o\in\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
,
\epsilon_{o}
is a counit for the adjunction
R_{o}\dashv L_{o}
.

Corollary A.2.5
.

In the situation of
Lemma

A.2.3
, denote by
R\colon\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
the right adjoint relative to
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
.

(i)

A relative adjunction unit
\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}}\to RL
is an equivalence if and only if
L_{io}
is fully faithful for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
.

(ii)

A relative adjunction counit
LR\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{D}}
is an equivalence if and only if for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
,
L_{io}
admits a fully faithful right adjoint.

Proof.

By
Lemma

A.2.2
, a relative adjunction unit
\eta
is an equivalence if and only if for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
,

\eta_{io}\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}_{io}}\to(RL)_{io}\cong R_{io}L_{io}

is an equivalence. Since for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
,
\eta_{io}
exhibits
R_{io}
as right adjoint to
L_{io}
(
Lemma

A.2.3
), this holds if and only if
L_{io}
is fully faithful for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
.
The same argument shows that the adjunction counit is an equivalence if and only if
R_{io}
is fully faithful for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
.
∎

By definition of
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-algebras (
[
Lur17
, Definition 2.1.3.1]
), pushforward along a lax
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functor
f\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
defines a map

\displaystyle f_{\operatorname{Alg}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}_{/\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Alg}_{/\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}).

In particular, a lax monoidal functor
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
induces a map

\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})
, and a lax symmetric monoidal functor
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
induces a map
\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})
.

Corollary A.2.6
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
are
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal categories and
L\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a strong
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
-monoidal functor such that for all
o\in\mathcal{O}
,
L_{o}
admits a right adjoint.
Denote by
R\colon\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
its right adjoint relative to
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
provided by
Lemma

A.2.3
and by
\eta\colon 1\to RL
an adjunction unit relative to
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
.

(i)

\eta
exhibits
L_{\operatorname{Alg}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}_{/\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Alg}_{/\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})
as left adjoint to
R_{\operatorname{Alg}}
.

(ii)

If for all
o\in\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}
,
L_{io}
respectively
R_{io}
is fully faithful, then so are
L_{\operatorname{Alg}}
and
R_{\operatorname{Alg}}
, respectively.

A.2.1
Module categories

We now specialize the above results to module categories, see
[
Lur17
, section 4.2]
for the relevant definitions.
Suppose that
L\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is a strong monoidal functor such that the underlying functor of categories
l\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
admits a right adjoint. By
Lemma

A.2.3
,
L
admits a lax monoidal right adjoint
R\colon\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
.
The functors
L,R
pull back to functors

L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\times_{\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}}\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}\leftrightarrows\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}}\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}\colon R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}

over
\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}
. The functor
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
is strong
\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}
-monoidal and
R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
is lax
\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}
-monoidal.
The relative adjunction unit provided by
Lemma

A.2.3
induces a natural transformation

\eta_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon 1\to R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}

which exhibits
R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
as right adjoint to
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
relative to
\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}
.
Hence by
A.2.6
,
pushforward along
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}},R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
defines an adjoint pair

L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{D}})\colon R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}

and pushforward along
\eta_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
is a unit for this adjunction.
In particular, if
l
or
r
is fully faithful then so are
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}},R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
, respectively by
A.2.5
,
A.2.6
.

Lemma A.2.7
.

For
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
, the adjunction
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\dashv R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
lifts to an adjoint pair

L_{LM}^{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})\colon R_{LM}^{A}.

The right adjoint
R_{LM}^{A}
factors as

\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{C}})\xrightarrow{\eta_{A}^{*}}\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}}),

where
\eta_{A}^{*}
is restriction of scalars along the adjunction unit
\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}(A)\colon A\to R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
.

Proof.

By construction, pushforward along
L,R
, respectively
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}},R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
yields commutative diagrams
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L^{\operatorname{Alg}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R^{\operatorname{Alg}}}

where the bottom horizontal maps are the adjoint pair provided by
A.2.6
for the operad
\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}
. Denote by
\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}\colon\operatorname{id}\to R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}
a relative adjunction unit whitnessing
L^{\operatorname{Alg}}\dashv R^{\operatorname{Alg}}
.
The above diagrams imply that for
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
,
