L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}},R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
pull back to functors

L^{A}_{LM}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})

and

\tilde{R}^{A}_{LM}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}}).

Denote by
R^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
the composition of
\tilde{R}^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
with restriction
of scalars

\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}^{*}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{D}})

along the adjunction unit
\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}(A)\colon A\to R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.2]
,
(\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}))
is a cartesian fibration. For a cartesian lift
M\to N\in\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})
of an algebra homomorphism
\phi\colon A\to B
,
\phi^{*}(N)=M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
.
In particular, if
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
and
c\colon(A,N)\to R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(A,M)
is a cartesian lift of
A\to R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A
, then

N=R^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}L^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}}).

Since
c\colon N\to R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}M
is cartesian, there exists a unique filler
\eta^{A}_{M}\colon(A,N)\to R^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}L^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}M
for
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(A,M)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(A,N)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(A,M)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta^{A}_{M}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\exists!}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c}

lifting
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{id}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}}

As
\eta^{A}_{M}
lifts
id_{A}
,
\eta^{A}_{M}
defines a morphism
\eta^{A}(M)\colon M\to R^{A}_{LM}L^{A}_{LM}(M)\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
. We now show that these morphisms exhibit
R_{LM}^{A}
as right adjoint to
L_{LM}^{A}
in the sense of
[
Lan21
, Proposition 5.1.10]
.

For
T\in\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{C}})
, choose a cartesian lift

l\colon(A,S)\to R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A,T)

of
\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}(A)\colon A\to R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A
.
Since
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})
maps
R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}(T)
to
(A,S)
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})}(-,R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}(T))=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}(-,(A,S))\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}(A,A)}\{\operatorname{id}_{A}\}.

Pushforward along the cartesian morphism
l
induces an equivalence

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}(-,(A,S))

\displaystyle\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}(A,A)}\{\operatorname{id}_{A}\}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}(-,R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A,T))\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}(A,R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A)}\{\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}(A)\}.

R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
and the adjunction unit
\eta_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
yield an equivalence

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}(L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}-,-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}(-,R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}-)

lifting the equivalence

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D})}(L^{\operatorname{Alg}}-,-)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}(-,R^{\operatorname{Alg}}-)

provided by
R^{\operatorname{Alg}}
and the adjunction unit
\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}
.
This induces an equivalence

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}

\displaystyle(L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}-,-)\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}(L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A,L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A)}\{\operatorname{id}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}(A)}\}

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})}(-,R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}-)\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})}(A,R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A)}\{\eta_{\operatorname{Alg}}(A)\}.

The left-hand side is
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{C}})}(L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}-,-)
.
For
M\in\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
, the equivalence constructed above factors as

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{C}})}(L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}(M),-)\xrightarrow{R^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M},*}}

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})}(R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}(M),R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}-)

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{(\eta^{A}_{M})^{*}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})}(M,R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}-),

which shows that
\eta_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}
exhibits
R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}
as right adjoint to
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}
.
∎

Remark A.2.8
.

The adjunction
L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}\dashv R^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
has the following properties:

(i)

For an algebra map
A\to B\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
,
there are commutative diagrams
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}B}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{LM}^{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(L^{\operatorname{Alg}}\phi)^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{LM}^{A}}

and

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}B}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}B}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(L^{\operatorname{Alg}}\phi)^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{R}_{LM}^{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R^{\operatorname{Alg}}L^{\operatorname{Alg}}\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(B)^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R^{A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{R}_{LM}^{A}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}(A)^{*}}
.

(ii)

If the functor
l\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
underlying
L
is fully faithful, then so are

\displaystyle L^{\operatorname{Alg}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}),

\displaystyle L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{D}})

by
A.2.6
. This implies that

L_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})

is fully faithful for all
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}).

(iii)

If
l
admits a fully faithful right adjoint
r
, then the counit
1\to LR
is an equivalence, i.e.
R
is fully faithful by
A.2.5
.

(iv)

Suppose that
R
is fully faithful. Then

R^{\operatorname{Alg}}\colon\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\otimes})

and

R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}\colon\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{D}})\to\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}})

are fully faithful by
A.2.6
. This implies that

\overline{R}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{D}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{C}})

is fully faithful for all
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{D}).

As for
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
,
L^{\operatorname{Alg}}R^{\operatorname{Alg}}A\cong A
(by fully faithfulness of
R^{\operatorname{Alg}}
),

R_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}^{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{D}})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{L^{\operatorname{Alg}}R^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{D}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}({\mathcal{C}})

is fully faithful as well. This is right adjoint to
L^{R^{\operatorname{Alg}}A}_{\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}}
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a symmetric monoidal category and
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
. By
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.3.3.7, Example 4.3.1.15]
, for
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
,
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
is right-tensored over
\mathcal{C}
.
As
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\cong\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}_{\operatorname{rev}}
, we can also consider
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
as left-tensored over
\mathcal{C}
by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.6.3.15, Corollary 4.3.2.8]
.

Lemma A.2.9
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a symmetric monoidal category with geometric realizations (
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}
-indexed colimits) whose tensor product preserves geometric realizations in both variables.
Endow
\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
with the symmetric monoidal structure described in
[
Lur17
, Example 3.2.4.4]
.
For
A,B\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{A\otimes B}({\mathcal{C}}),

where we consider
\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})
as left-tensored over
\mathcal{C}
as described above.

Proof.

By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.3.2.8, Proposition 4.6.3.11, Proposition 4.3.2.7]
,

\operatorname{LMod}_{A\otimes B}({\mathcal{C}})\cong\phantom{}_{A\otimes B}\operatorname{BiMod}{\mathcal{C}}_{1}\cong\phantom{}_{A}\operatorname{BiMod}{\mathcal{C}}_{B^{\operatorname{rev}}}\cong\operatorname{RMod}_{B^{\operatorname{rev}}}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})}).

The involution
(-)^{\operatorname{rev}}\colon\mathcal{BM}\to\mathcal{BM}

[
Lur17
, Construction 4.6.3.1]
restricts to an equivalence
r\colon\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}\cong\mathcal{R}\mathcal{M}
. Postcomposition with
r
yields an equivalence

\operatorname{RMod}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})})

which pulls back to an equivalence

\operatorname{RMod}_{B^{\operatorname{rev}}}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})})\cong\operatorname{LMod}_{B}({\operatorname{LMod}_{A}({\mathcal{C}})}).\qed

A.3
Tensor products of presentable categories and symmetric monoidal structures

By construction of the tensor product on
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
, the forget functor
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
admits a lax symmetric monoidal structure.
For presentable categories
\mathcal{C}
,
\mathcal{D}
, the lax monoidal structure evaluates to a functor

\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}\colon\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}.

We want to describe these functors explicitly.
Recall from
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.17]
and
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.2.6.2, Remark 5.5.2.10]
/
1.1.6
, that for presentable categories
\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}
,

\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}).

Lemma A.3.1
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}
are presentable categories and
L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\to\mathcal{C}
is a localization.
For
c\in\mathcal{C}
and
d\in\mathcal{D}
, the fully faithful functor

\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\xhookrightarrow{L^{*}}\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

sends
\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(c,d)
to

\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(Ly-,c)}\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{const}_{d}}\mathcal{D},

where
y\colon\mathcal{C}_{0}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})
is the Yoneda embedding and
\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{const}_{d}}\mathcal{D}
denotes the unique cocontinuous functor with
\operatorname{const}_{d}(*)=d
.

Proof.

We will deduce this from the proof of
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
.
Suppose first that
\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})
and
\mathcal{D}=\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})
are categories of presheaves on small categories.
By construction of the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
,

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})\cong\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}\times\mathcal{D}_{0}),

and under this identification,

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}\times\mathcal{D}_{0})

is the left Kan extension of the Yoneda embedding
\mathcal{C}_{0}\times\mathcal{D}_{0}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}\times\mathcal{D}_{0})
along the Yoneda embedding

\mathcal{C}_{0}\times\mathcal{D}_{0}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}).

Denote by
y\colon\mathcal{C}_{0}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})
the Yoneda embedding and by
\operatorname{const}_{*}\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})
the unique cocontinuous functor with
\operatorname{const}_{*}(*)=*
and let

\operatorname{const}_{-}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{An},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})),d\mapsto d\times\operatorname{const}_{*}.

For
d\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})
,
\operatorname{const}_{d}
is the unique cocontinuous functor
\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})
with
\operatorname{const}_{d}(*)=d
.
The functor

\displaystyle\nu\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}))

\displaystyle(c,d)

\displaystyle\mapsto\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(y-,c)

is cocontinuous in both variables. As the composition

\mathcal{C}_{0}\times\mathcal{D}_{0}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})\xrightarrow{\nu}\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}))\cong\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}\times\mathcal{D}_{0})

is equivalent to the Yoneda embedding,
\nu=\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}
which proves the statement in case
\mathcal{C}
and
\mathcal{D}
are presheaf categories.

Suppose now that
\mathcal{D}
is an arbitrary presentable category and
\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})
is a presheaf category. Choose a localization
L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})\rightleftarrows\mathcal{D}\colon f
.
The proof of
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
shows that
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{D}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{id}\times f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}){,}\mathcal{D}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}){,}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{id}\otimes L}

commutes, and the right vertical map exhibits
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}
as localization of
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})
at the maps

\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}(c,d\to fLd),\,c\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),d\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}).

By the above, under the identification
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}))
these are precisely the maps

\operatorname{const}^{\mathcal{P}(D_{0})}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{P(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(y-,c)\to\operatorname{const}^{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}_{fLc}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(y-,c),\,d\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}),c\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})

induced by the unit
\operatorname{id}\to fL
.
As for
d\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})
,
pushforward along
\operatorname{const}_{d}
is left adjoint to pushforward along
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}(d,-)
,
F\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}))
is local for the maps

\operatorname{const}^{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)\to\operatorname{const}^{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}_{fLd}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c),\,c\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),d\in\mathcal{D}

induced by the unit
\operatorname{id}\to fL
if and only if
F\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}))
, i.e.
F\cong fL\circ F
.
We therefore obtain a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{D}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{id}\times f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}){,}\mathcal{D}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}){,}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{*}}

This implies that for
c\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),d\in\mathcal{D}
,

\displaystyle\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{D}}(c,d)=L\circ\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}(c,fd)

\displaystyle\cong L\circ\operatorname{const}_{fd}^{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(-,c)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{const}_{d}^{\mathcal{D}}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(-,c),

which shows the statement in case
\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})
a presheaf topos.

Suppose now that
\mathcal{C}
is a general presentable category and choose a localization

L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\rightleftarrows\mathcal{C}\colon f.

Then
L^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
is an equivalence onto the full subcategory on functors for which the unit
id\to fL
induces an equivalence
F\cong F\circ fL
.
By the above and the proof of
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
,

\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

is the full subcategory on objects which are local for the morphisms

\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(-,c)\to\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(-,fLc),\,c\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),d\in\mathcal{D}

induced by the unit
c\to fLc
.
As pushforward along
\operatorname{const}_{d}
is left adjoint to pushforward along
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,-)
, a functor

F\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{D}

is local for these maps if and only if the unit
\operatorname{id}\to fL
induces an equivalence
F\cong F\circ fL
. We therefore a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{P}(C_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y^{*}}

Denote by
l\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}
the left adjoint of
i
.
It was shown in the proof of
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.8.1.17]
that
\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(c,d)=l(\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{D}}(c,fd))
.
We showed above that for
(c,d)\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{D}
,

\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{D}}(c,d)=\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(y-,c)\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}).

In particular, for
(c,d)\in\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\times\mathcal{D}
,

\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{D}}(fc,d)\in\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D},

and hence
i(\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(c,d))=\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{D}}(fc,d)
and

(yL)^{*}\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(c,d)=y^{*}\mu_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0}),\mathcal{D}}(fc,d)\cong\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C_{0})}(y-,fc)\cong\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(Ly-,c).\qed

A.3.1
Monoidal categories and enrichment

In this section, we collect examples for categories which are enriched in other monoidal categories.

Recollection A.3.2
.

By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.2.3.2]
, a monoidal functor

\phi\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty})

induces a functor
\phi^{*}\colon\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}}({\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}})\to\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}}({\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}})
.

For a monoidal category
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}
, the cocartesian fibration
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}}\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}
of operads exhibits
\mathcal{D}
as left
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
-module.
The cocartesian fibration
q\colon\mathcal{M}\to\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}
classifying

\phi^{*}(\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\times_{\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}}\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes})\in\operatorname{LMod}_{\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}}({\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}})

exhibits
\mathcal{D}
as left-tensored (
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.2.1.19]
) over
\mathcal{C}
.

Example A.3.3
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a closed monoidal category and denote by
\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,-)
the internal Hom. If
L^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a monoidal left adjoint (i.e. a monoidal functor such that the underlying functor
L\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
admits a right adjoint
R
), then the induced left tensoring exhibits
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
as enriched (
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.2.1.28]
) over
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
as for
c\in\mathcal{C}
,

R\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,-)\vdash c\otimes L(-).

In particular,
R\circ\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(c,-)
is the
\mathcal{C}
-enriched mapping space functor (
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.2.1.30]
).

The equivalences

(-_{1}\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-)\circ(-_{2}\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-)\cong(-_{1}\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-_{2})\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-

provided by the monoidal structure on
\mathcal{C}
determine an equivalence

\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(-_{2},\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(-_{1},-))\cong\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(-_{1}\otimes-_{2},-).

In particular, the adjunction
x\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-\dashv\underline{\operatorname{map}}_{\mathcal{C}}(x,-)
is
\mathcal{D}
-enriched.

Example A.3.4
.

By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.4.3, Example 3.2.4.4]
,
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
admits a symmetric monoidal structure such that
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is symmetric monoidal. In particular, if
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
are two presentably symmetric monoidal categories,
C^{\otimes}\otimes\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
inherits a closed monoidal structure and the unit maps
\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
yield symmetric monoidal left adjoints

\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to(\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D})^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\to(\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D})^{\otimes}.

This exhibits
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
as enriched over
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
.

Using
Lemma

A.3.1
, we can recover the internal Hom of
\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}
from its
\mathcal{D}
-enrichment:

Corollary A.3.5
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
are presentably symmetric monoidal categories.
Then
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is an enhancement of
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
to a presentably symmetric monoidal category (
[
Lur17
, Example 3.2.4.4]
). Denote by
\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(-,-)
its internal Hom, and by

i_{\mathcal{C}}\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}

the functor induced by the unit
\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{D},*\mapsto 1_{\mathcal{D}}
.
Denote by
\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(-,-)
the
\mathcal{D}
-enrichment of
\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}
, by
\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(-,-)
.
Under the equivalence
\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
,

\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(-_{1},-_{2})\cong\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(-_{1}\otimes i_{\mathcal{C}}(-),-_{2}).

Proof.

Denote by
i_{\mathcal{C}}\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D},i_{\mathcal{D}}\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
the functors induced by the units
\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{C},\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{D}
.
The forget functor
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
is lax symmetric monoidal and therefore induces a lax symmetric monoidal functor
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})
by
[
Lur17
, Construction 3.2.4.1, Proposition 3.2.4.2]
.
(By
[
Lur17
, Construction 3.2.4.1]
, a lax symmetric monoidal functor
\mathcal{T}\to\mathcal{S}
induces a functor
\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{T})\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{S})
of categories over
N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
, and by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 3.2.4.2.2)]
, this is a lax symmetric monoidal functor.)
By construction, this fits into a commutative diagram of lax symmetric monoidal functors
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty},}

where the vertical maps are the forget functors
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L},\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})\to\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}
which are symmetric monoidal (
[
Lur17
, Example 3.2.4.4]
).
In particular, we obtain a symmetric monoidal functor

\mu^{\otimes}_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}\colon\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty})}\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}

enhancing the functor

\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}\colon\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}

from
Lemma

A.3.1
.
Since the functor
\mu^{\otimes}_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}
is symmetric monoidal and natural in
\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}
with respect to cocontinuous, symmetric monoidal functors

\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(c,d)\cong\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(c,1_{\mathcal{D}})\otimes_{\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(1_{\mathcal{D}},d)\cong i_{\mathcal{C}}(c)\otimes_{\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}i_{\mathcal{D}}(d).

Choose a localization
L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})\rightleftarrows\mathcal{C}\colon f
. By
Lemma

A.3.1
, for
c\in\mathcal{C},d\in\mathcal{D}
, under the embedding

\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}),

\mu_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}}(c,d)=i_{\mathcal{C}}(c)\otimes i_{\mathcal{D}}(d)
becomes

\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(Ly-,c),

where
y
denotes the Yoneda embedding
\mathcal{C}_{0}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})
. As pushforward along
\operatorname{const}_{d}\colon\operatorname{An}\to\mathcal{D}
is left adjoint to

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,-)_{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}),

it follows that for
c\in\mathcal{C}
and
d\in\mathcal{D}
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}\left(i_{\mathcal{C}}(c)\otimes i_{\mathcal{D}}(d),\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{C}}(-)\otimes x,a)\right)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})}\left(\operatorname{const}_{d}\circ\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(Ly-,c),\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{C}}(Ly-)\otimes x,a)\right)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})}\left(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(Ly-,c),\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{C}}(Ly-)\otimes x,a))\right)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})}\left(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(L-,c),\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{C}}(L(-)\otimes x,a))\right)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(C_{0})^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})}\left(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(-,f(c)),\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(d,\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{C}}(L-)\otimes x,a))\right)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}\left(d,\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}i_{\mathcal{C}}(Lf(c))\otimes x,a\right)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}\left(d,\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{C}}(c)\otimes x,a)\right),

where we used that

L^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lim}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}_{0}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})

is fully faithful, that
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(L-,c)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})}(-,fc)
, fully faithfulness of the Yoneda embedding, and that
f\colon\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_{0})
is fully faithful.

By definition of
\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(-,-)
and
\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(-,-)
, the right-hand side is isomorphic to

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{D}}(d)\otimes i_{\mathcal{C}}(c)\otimes x,a)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{D}}(d)\otimes i_{\mathcal{C}}(c),\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(x,a)).

This identification is natural in
c
,
d
,
x
and
a
. As
\{i_{\mathcal{C}}(c)\otimes i_{\mathcal{D}}(d),\,c\in\mathcal{C},d\in\mathcal{D}\}
generates
\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}
under small colimits, this implies that

\operatorname{map}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(i_{\mathcal{C}}(-)\otimes x,a)\text{ and }\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{D}}(x,a)

represent the same functor, whence are isomorphic. Their identification is clearly natural in
x
and
a
.
∎

A.3.2
Monoidal structure on presheaves with values in a presentably symmetric monoidal category

We now recall an explicit description of the symmetric monoidal structure on presheaves with values in a presentably symmetric monoidal category which we used in the proof of
1.1.28
.
Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a small symmetric monoidal category and
\mathcal{D}
is a presentably symmetric monoidal category. Then
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
, cf.
1.1.6
. Endow
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
with the Day convolution symmetric monoidal structure (
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.8.1.2]
).

By
[
Lur17
, Remark 2.4.2.7]
,
\mathcal{C}
induces a symmetric monoidal structure on
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
. By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 2.2.6.16]
,
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}^{\otimes})
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure from the symmetric monoidal structures on
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}
and
\mathcal{D}
.
These two symmetric monoidal structures are equivalent:

Lemma A.3.6
.

The equivalence
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{D}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
enhances to a symmetric monoidal equivalence

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{Day}}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})^{\otimes}.

In particular, for
F,G\in\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
and
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
(F\otimes G)(c)
is the left Kan extension of

\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\xrightarrow{F\times G}\mathcal{D}\times\mathcal{D}\xrightarrow{-\otimes_{\mathcal{D}}-}\mathcal{D}

along (the opposite of)

\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{-\otimes_{\mathcal{C}}-}\mathcal{C}.

Proof.

For
\mathcal{D}=\operatorname{An}
, the equivalence of the two symmetric monoidal structures is remarked in
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.8.1.13]
. It can be seen as follows: By
[
Gla16
, section 3]
, the Yoneda embedding enhances to a symmetric monoidal functor
y^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
. It is straightforward to check that the tensor product on
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
preserves colimits in both variables. Whence by the universal property of
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\otimes}
(
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.8.1.12]
),
y^{\otimes}
extends uniquely to a symmetric monoidal functor
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})^{\otimes}
. The underlying functor
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})
is a colimits-preserving extension of the Yoneda embedding and hence an equivalences.

Suppose now that
\mathcal{D}_{0}
is a small symmetric monoidal category and
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}=\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}}
is the symmetric monoidal category of presheaves provided by
[
Lur17
, Corollary 4.8.1.12]
.
By construction of the symmetric monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
,

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{Day}}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}}\cong\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}}.

By
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.8.1.13]
, the right-hand side is equivalent to the symmetric monoidal category
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
provided by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 2.2.6.16]
, where we view
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{op}}=(\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{D})^{\operatorname{op}}
as a symmetric monoidal category via the cartesian monoidal structure on
\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}
and
[
Lur17
, Remark 2.4.2.7]
.
By
[
Lur17
, Remark 2.2.6.8]
and again
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.8.1.13]
, the symmetric monoidal category
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\times\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})^{\otimes}
is equivalent to
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}})
with the symmetric monoidal structure provided by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 2.2.6.16]
.
We now deduce from this the general statement. By
[
NS17
, Theorem 2.2]
, for every presentably symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
, there exists a small symmetric monoidal category
\mathcal{D}_{0}
and a symmetric monoidal localization
L\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
. Denote by
W\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0}))
the
L
-equivalences.
It is shown in the proof of
[
Lur09
, Proposition 4.8.1.15]
that
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{Day}}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}
is the symmetric monoidal localization of
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{Day}}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})
at the morphisms
1\otimes w,w\in W
and

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{Day}}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})\cong\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}}.

The symmetric monoidal localization
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}}\to\mathcal{D}^{\otimes}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})
and the equivalence established above yield a symmetric monoidal functor

c^{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{Day}}\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\otimes}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\operatorname{Day}})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})^{\otimes}.

Since the underlying functor
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{Day}}\otimes_{\operatorname{Pr}^{L}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D}_{0})^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D})\cong\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\otimes\mathcal{D}
equals
\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}\otimes L
,
c^{\otimes}
inverts the morphisms
1\otimes w,w\in W
and hence factors over a symmetric monoidal functor

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\otimes_{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})}\mathcal{D}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{D}).

As the forget functor
\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}^{L})\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
is conservative and symmetric monoidal, this is an equivalence.
The explicit description of
F\otimes G
as left Kan extension is
[
Lur17
, Remark 2.2.6.15]
.
∎

A.3.3
Modules in cartesian categories

In this section, we recall from
[
Lur17
, section 4.2.2]
simplicial models for modules, algebras and groups in cartesian monoidal categories.

Definition A.3.7

(
[
Lur17
, 2.4.1.1]
)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a category with finite products.
Denote by
\mathcal{C}^{\times}\to N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
the cartesian monoidal category associated to
\mathcal{C}
and by
\pi\colon\mathcal{C}^{\times}\to\mathcal{C}
the corresponding cartesian structure
[
Lur17
, Proposition 2.4.1.5]
.

For an operad
\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\to N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})
, denote by
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C})
the full subcategory on functors
F\colon\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{C}
such that for all
o\coloneqq(o_{1},\ldots,o_{n})\in\mathcal{O}^{\otimes}_{<n>}\cong\mathcal{O}^{n}
,
the Segal maps
F(o)\to F(o_{i})
exhibit
F(o)\cong\prod_{i=1}^{n}F(o_{i})
.

Proposition A.3.8

(
[
Lur17
, Proposition 2.4.1.7]
)
.

The composition

\operatorname{Alg}_{/\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{C}^{\times}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\mathcal{O}^{\otimes})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}^{\times}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\mathcal{O}^{\otimes})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}^{\times})\xrightarrow{\pi_{*}}\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C})

induces an equivalence

\operatorname{Alg}_{/\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{C}^{\times}\times_{N(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}}_{*})}\mathcal{O}^{\otimes})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{O}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C}).

Proof.

This is
[
Lur17
, Proposition 2.4.1.7]
, recall that a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets is a weak equivalence in the Joyal model structure on simplicial sets and hence an equivalence of associated categories.
∎

Definition A.3.9

(
[
Lur17
, Definition 4.1.2.5]
)
.

Denote by
\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})
the full subcategory of monoid objects, that is simplicial objects
M\colon\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{X}
such that for all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the face maps

\{M([n])\to M(\{i-1,i\})\}_{1\leq i\leq n}
exhibit
M([n])=\prod_{i=1}^{n}M(\{i-1,i\})
.

Proposition A.3.10

(
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.1.2.10]
)
.

There exists a functor
i\colon\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}
such that for all categories
\mathcal{X}
with finite products,
i^{*}\colon\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes},\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})
factors over an equivalence
\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes},\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})
.

The composite
\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})=\operatorname{Alg}_{/\operatorname{Assoc}}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\operatorname{Assoc}^{\times},\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})
sends an algebra
A\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})
to the simplicial object
[n]\mapsto A^{n}
with

\displaystyle d_{i}\colon A^{n}

\displaystyle\to A^{n-1},

\displaystyle(a_{1},\ldots,a_{n})

\displaystyle\mapsto(a_{1},\ldots,a_{i}a_{i+1},a_{i+2},\ldots,a_{n})

and

\displaystyle s_{i}\colon A^{n}

\displaystyle\to A^{n+1},

\displaystyle(a_{1},\ldots,a_{n})

\displaystyle\mapsto(a_{1},\ldots,a_{i-1},1,a_{i},\ldots,a_{n}).

In particular, under the above equivalence, a group object is an monoid object
M\colon\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{X}
such that
M(\{0\})=*
and if
[n]=S_{1}\cup S_{2}
with
|S_{1}\cap S_{2}|=1
, then
M([n])\to M(S_{i}),i=1,2
exhibit
M([n])=M(S_{1})\times M(S_{2})
. This condition can be checked in the homotopy category of
\mathcal{X}
, whence

\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})\times_{\operatorname{Mon}(\operatorname{ho}(\mathcal{X}))}\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{ho}(\mathcal{X})).

Lemma A.3.11
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a big topos.
A monoid
M\in\mathcal{X}
is a group object if and only if
\tau_{\leq 0}M\in\operatorname{Mon}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
is a group.

Proof.

Choose an exhaustion
\mathcal{X}_{*}\colon\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
of
\mathcal{X}
by topoi.
As for all
\lambda\in\Lambda
,
\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
is closed under finite limits and the truncation functor
\tau_{\leq 0}\colon\mathcal{X}\to\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}
restricts to
\mathcal{X_{\lambda}}\to\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X}_{\lambda}
(
Lemma

1.2.5
), it suffices to prove the statement for
\mathcal{X}
a topos.
As
\operatorname{Mon}(\operatorname{An})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
is closed under small limits (which are computed pointwise), the equivalence

\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}))\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An}))

restricts to an equivalence
\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Mon}(\operatorname{An}))
. Here
\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}
denotes the categories of small limits preserving functors.
The above equivalence restricts further to an equivalence
\operatorname{Grp}(\mathcal{X})\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{An}))
.
By
[
Lur17
, Example 5.2.6.4 and Remark 5.2.6.5]
,

\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{An})\cong\operatorname{Mon}(\operatorname{An})\times_{\operatorname{Mon}(\operatorname{Set})}\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Set}),

whence

\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{An}))\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Mon}(\operatorname{An}))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Mon}(\operatorname{Set}))}\operatorname{Fun}^{\lim}(\mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Grp}(\operatorname{Set})).

The right-hand side is equivalent to
\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})\times_{\operatorname{Mon}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})}\operatorname{Grp}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{X})
.
∎

Definition A.3.12
.

[
Lur17
, Definition 4.2.2.2]

For a category
\mathcal{X}
denote by

\operatorname{LMon}{}(\mathcal{X})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{1},\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X}))

the full subcategory of maps of simplicial objects
M\to A\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{X})
such that

(i)

A\in\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})
.

(ii)

For all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the Segal map
M([n])\to M(\{n\})\cong M(\{0\})
and the map
M([n])\to A([n])
exhibit
M([n])
as

M([n])\cong A([n])\times M(\{0\}).

For
A\in\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})
let
\operatorname{LMon}_{A}(\mathcal{X})\coloneqq\operatorname{LMon}{}(\mathcal{X})\times_{\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})}\{A\}
.

By
[
Lur17
, Proposition 4.2.2.9]
, there exists a functor
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\times\Delta^{1}\to\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}
such that for all categories
\mathcal{C}
with finite products, pullback along
j
induces an equivalence of categories

\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{L}M^{\otimes},\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{LMon}(\mathcal{C}).

Composing with the equivalence from
Proposition

A.3.8
we obtain an equivalence

\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}^{\times}})\cong\operatorname{LMon}(\mathcal{C}).

Since
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\times\Delta^{1}\to\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes}
factors as
\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\xrightarrow{i}\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes}\to\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}
, the diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMod}({\mathcal{C}^{\times}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{L}\mathcal{M}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{LMon}(\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\times})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\operatorname{Assoc}^{\otimes},\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{C})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

commutes.
This implies:

Corollary A.3.13
.

Suppose
\mathcal{X}
is a category with finite products.
For
G\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal{X}^{\times})\cong\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{X})
, there is an equivalence

\operatorname{LMod}_{G}({\mathcal{X}})\cong\operatorname{LMon}_{G}(\mathcal{X}).

This is natural in the algebra
G
and with respect to finite products-preserving functors.

Example A.3.14
.

[
Lur17
, page 656]

The large category of small categories
\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}
is cartesian closed with internal Hom
\operatorname{Fun}(-,-)
(
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.8.1.6]
).

(i)

For categories
\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}
and
\mathcal{E}
, this yields

evaluation

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\times\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}

and
composition maps

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\times\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{E})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{E}).

(ii)

For a category
\mathcal{C}
, the composition

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})\times\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})

allows to define a simplicial object

\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{*}\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}),n\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{n}

which exhibits
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})
as a monoid in
\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}
.
We refer to the corresponding monoidal structure
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{\circ}
on
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})
as the composition monoidal structure.

(iii)

The evaluation
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})\times\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}
allows to construct a simplicial object

\displaystyle\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{*}\times\mathcal{C}\in{{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty})}_{/\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{*}}},

\displaystyle[n]\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{n}\times\mathcal{C}

which exhibits
\mathcal{C}
as left
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{*}
-monoid. Via the equivalence

\operatorname{LMod}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{\circ}}({\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}})\cong\operatorname{LMon}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{*}}(\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty})

from
A.3.13
, this exhibits
\mathcal{C}
as left-tensored over
\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{\circ}
.

(iv)

If
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}
is a monoidal category, denote by
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}_{\operatorname{rev}}
its reverse (
[
Lur17
, Remark 4.1.1.7]
) and consider it as object of
\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal{C})
.
The monoidal structure on
\mathcal{C}
allows to enhance

\mathcal{C}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C}),\,c\mapsto c\otimes-

to a map

\mathcal{C}_{rev}^{\otimes}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{*}\in\operatorname{Mon}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}).

We thereby obtain a symmetric monoidal functor
\mathcal{C}^{\otimes}_{\operatorname{rev}}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})^{\circ}
.

A.4
Sheaf topoi and morphisms of sites

In this section, we record basic terminology and results on sheaf topoi.
All results are immediate consequences from their 1-categorical analogues and the discussion in
[
Lur09
, section 6.2.2]
.

Definition A.4.1

(
[
Lur09
, Definition 6.2.2.1]
)
.

Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is a small category.

•

A
sieve
on an object
c\in\mathcal{C}
is a full subcategory
S\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
such that for all
a\to b\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
with
b\in S
:
a\in S
.

•

A Grothendieck topology
\tau
on
\mathcal{C}
consists of a collection of sieves
\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
on
c
for all objects
c\in\mathcal{C}
such that

(i)

For all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)

(ii)

For
f\colon b\to c\in\mathcal{C}
and
\mathcal{C}^{0}\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
,
f^{*}(\mathcal{C}^{0})\coloneqq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/b}}\times_{{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}}\mathcal{C}^{0}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(b)
.

(iii)

Suppose that
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
and
\mathcal{C}^{0}\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
is a sieve on
c
. If for all
f\colon s\to c\in S\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
,
f^{*}(C^{0})\coloneqq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/b}}\times_{{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}}\mathcal{C}^{0}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(s)
, then
C^{0}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})
.

•

A small category together with a Grothendieck topology is called a site.

A sieve
S
on an object
c\in\mathcal{C}
defines a monomorphism
S\subseteq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})
. This is pointwise an inclusion of connected components, and determines the sieve
S
. We will in the sequel freely identify sieves with the associated subfunctors of
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)
.
We denote by
h_{c}\coloneqq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}
the presheaf represented by
c
.

Definition A.4.2
.

If
(\mathcal{C},\tau)
is a Grothendieck topology, denote by
\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
the full subcategory on functors such that for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
and all sieves
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
, the inclusion

S\subseteq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)=:h_{c}

induces an equivalence

F(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(h_{c},F)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(S,F).

By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7]
,
\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
admits a left-exact left adjoint, whence
\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})
is a topos.
We call this left adjoint
\tau
-sheafification.

It is often convenient to characterise Grothendieck topologies/sheaf topoi in terms of coverages.

Definition A.4.3
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a small category.

(i)

A cover for an object
c\in\mathcal{C}
is a set of maps
\mathcal{T}=\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}
.

(ii)

For a cover
\mathcal{T}=\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}
denote by
S(\mathcal{T})\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
the full subcategory on objects
x\to c
such that there exists
i\in I
such that
q
factors as
x\to c_{i}\to c
. This is a sieve on
c
.

(iii)

A coverage
\tau
on
\mathcal{C}
consists of a set
\tau(c)
of covers for every object
c\in\mathcal{C}
such that the following is satisfied:
For every cover
\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}\in\tau(c)
and every morphism
f\colon b\to c\in\mathcal{C}
, there exists a covering family
\{b_{j}\to b\}_{j\in J}\in\tau(b)
such that for all
j\in J
,
b_{j}\to b\to c\in S(\{c_{i}\to c\})
, i.e. there exists
i(j)\in I
such that

b_{j}\to b\to c
factors as
b_{j}\to c_{i(j)}\to c
.

(iv)

We call a small category
\mathcal{C}
together with a coverage
\tau
a quasi-site.

Every Grothendieck topology determines a coverage by allowing those covering families
\{x_{i}\to x\}_{i\in I}
for which
S(\{x_{i}\to x\}_{i\in I})
is a sieve. Conversely, every coverage determines a Grothendieck topology:

Definition A.4.4
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},\tau)
is a quasi-site.

(i)

If
\rho
is a Grothendieck topology on
\mathcal{C}
, we say that
\tau\subseteq\rho
if for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
and all covering families
\mathcal{X}=\{c_{i}\to c\}\in\tau(c)
,
S(\mathcal{X})\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\rho}(c)
.
For
c\in\mathcal{C}
, let

[\tau](c)\coloneqq\bigcap_{\tau\subseteq\rho}\operatorname{Cov}_{\rho}(c),

where the intersection runs over all Grothendieck topologies
\rho
on
\mathcal{C}
with
\tau\subseteq\rho
.
We call
[\tau]
the Grothendieck topology generated by
\tau
.
It is straightforward to check that
[\tau]
is a Grothendieck topology. As the collection of all sieves forms a Grothendieck topology, the intersection on the right-hand side is over a non-empty set of Grothendieck topologies.

(ii)

If for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,

[\tau](c)=\{S\in\operatorname{Sieve}(c)\,|\,\exists\mathcal{X}\in\tau(c)\text{ s.t. }S(\mathcal{X})\subseteq S\},

we say that
\tau
is a
Grothendieck coverage
.

(iii)

If
\tau
is a coverage on
\mathcal{C}
, a functor
F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}
is a
\tau
-sheaf of for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
and all covering families
\{c_{i}\to c\}\in\tau(c)
, the inclusion
S(\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I})\subseteq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c)
induces an equivalence

F(c)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(S(\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}),F).

Remark A.4.5
.

Suppose that
\tau
is a Grothendieck topology,
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
and
\tilde{S}\in\operatorname{Sieve}(c)
is a sieve with
S\subseteq\tilde{S}
.
For
f\colon x\to c\in S,{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}=f^{*}(S)\subseteq f^{*}(\tilde{S})
, which implies that
f^{*}(\tilde{S})={{\mathcal{C}}_{/x}}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)
, and hence
\tilde{S}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
by the third axiom in the definition of Grothendieck topologies.
This implies that for all coverages
\tau
,

[\tau](c)\supseteq\{S\in\operatorname{Sieve}(c)\,|\,\exists\mathcal{X}\in\tau(c)\text{ s.t. }S(\mathcal{X})\subseteq S\}.

If
\tau
is a Grothendieck topology and
\tilde{\tau}
the associated coverage, then

\tilde{\tau}(c)=\{S\in\operatorname{Sieve}(c)\,|\,\exists\mathcal{X}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)\text{ s.t. }S(\mathcal{X})\subseteq S\},

i.e.
\tilde{\tau}
is a Grothendieck coverage.

If the category
\mathcal{C}
has
enough
pullbacks, there are more explicit characterizations of Grothendieck coverages, see e.g.
[
Pst23
, Definition A.1]
.

The assignment of a Grothendieck topology to a covering family is not one-to-one (but onto).
We now show that it is one-to-one on associated categories of sheaves.

Lemma A.4.6
.

(i)

If
(\mathcal{C},\tau)
is a quasi-site, then
(\mathcal{C},[\tau])
is a site.

(ii)

A functor
F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{An}
is a
[\tau]
-sheaf if and only if it is a
\tau
-sheaf.

Proof.

This is analogous to
[
Lan22
, Theorem 3.14]
, who proved the statement for
\mathcal{C}
a 1-category.
As the collection of all sieves forms a Grothendieck topology, there exist Grothendieck topologies which contain
\tau
.
By definition, every
[\tau]
-sheaf is a
\tau
-sheaf, so it remains to prove the converse.
For
c\in\mathcal{C}
denote by
\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
the collection of sieves
S
on
c
such that for all
f\colon b\to c\in\mathcal{C}
and all
\tau
-sheaves
F
,

F(b)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(h_{b},F)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(f^{*}S,F).

We claim that this defines a Grothendieck topology on
\mathcal{C}
.
Clearly,
{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
and for
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
and
f\colon b\to c\in\mathcal{C}
,
f^{*}(S)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(b)
.
Suppose now that
R\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
is a sieve and
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
such that for all
f\colon s\to c\in S
,
f^{*}(R)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(s)
.
We have to show that for all
q\colon b\to c\in\mathcal{C}
and
\tau
-sheaves
F
,

q^{*}(R)\subseteq h_{b}
induces an equivalence

F(b)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(q^{*}(R),F),

then it follows that
R\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
.
Since
q^{*}(S)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(b)
and for all
t\colon a\to b\in q^{*}(S)
,

t^{*}q^{*}(R)=(q\circ t)^{*}(R)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(a)

by assumption on
R
, it suffices to check this for
q=id
.
Let
\tilde{R}\coloneqq R\times_{h_{c}}S
. This is a subpresheaf of
R
and
S
.
For
f\colon b\to c\in R
,
f^{*}(\tilde{R})\cong f^{*}(S)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(b)
, so there is a commutative diagram of presheaves
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}(\tilde{R})=f^{*}(S)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h_{b}=f^{*}(R)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tilde{R}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

This yields a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underset{f\colon b\to c\in R}{\operatorname{colim}}}f^{*}(\tilde{R})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underset{b\to c\in R}{\operatorname{colim}}}h_{b}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tilde{R}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

The left vertical map is an equivalence as
{\underset{f\colon b\to c\in R}{\operatorname{colim}}}f^{*}\tilde{R}=R\times_{h_{c}}\tilde{R}
(by universality of colimits in
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
) and
R\times_{h_{c}}\tilde{R}=\times_{h_{C}}R\times_{h_{C}}S\cong R\times_{h_{C}}S\cong\tilde{R}
since
R\to h_{c}
is a monomorphism.
Applying a
\tau
-sheaf
F
yields a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underset{f\colon b\to c\in R}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(f^{*}\tilde{R},F)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underset{f\colon b\to c\in R}{\operatorname{lim}}}F(b)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(\tilde{R},F)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(R,F).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

The top horizontal map is an equivalence as for all
f\colon b\to c\in R
,
f^{*}(\tilde{R})=f^{*}(S)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(b)
.
It therefore suffices to show that for all
\tau
-sheaves
F
,
\tilde{R}\subseteq R\subseteq h_{c}
induces an equivalence

F(c)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(\tilde{R},F),

then it follows that
F(c)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(R,F)
for all
\tau
-sheaves
F
.
By universality of colimits in
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
,

\tilde{R}={\underset{f\colon s\to c\in S}{\operatorname{colim}}}R\times_{h_{c}}h_{s}={\underset{f\colon s\to c\in S}{\operatorname{colim}}}f^{*}(R)
.
Since for all
f\colon s\to c\in S
,
f^{*}(R)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(s)
by assumption, this implies that for all
\tau
-sheaves
F
,

\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(\tilde{R},F)\cong{\underset{f\colon s\to c\in S}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(f^{*}R,F)\cong{\underset{f\colon s\to c\in S}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(s,F)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(S,F).

As
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(c)
, the right-hand side is
F(c)
.
This proves that
\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}
defines a Grothendieck topology on
\mathcal{C}
.
By construction, every
\tau
-sheaf is a
\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}
-sheaf and
\tau\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}
.
This implies that
[\tau]\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}
and in particular, every
\tau
-sheaf is a
[\tau]
-sheaf.
∎

Remark A.4.7
.

For a covering
\mathcal{X}=\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}\in\mathcal{C}
,

S(\mathcal{X})\cong{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\check{C}(\sqcup_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c_{i})\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c))\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}).

Indeed: Recall that a map
A\to B\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
is monomorphism if and only if
A\cong A\times_{B}A
. Universality of colimits in
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
therefore implies that

{\underset{\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\check{C}(\sqcup_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c_{i})\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,c))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(-,c)

is a monomorphism, i.e. pointwise an inclusion of connected components.
At
t\in\mathcal{C}
, its image consists precisely of the maps
t\to c
which factor over
c_{i}
for some
i\in I
.

Definition A.4.8
.

If
\tau
is a coverage on an essentially small category
\mathcal{C}
, we denote by

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})

the categories of (hypercomplete)
[\tau]
-sheaves.

By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7, 6.2.1.1/p.666]
and
Lemma

A.4.6
, the inclusions

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})

admit left-exact left adjoints, called
\tau
-(hyper)-sheafification.

Next, we recall how functors between (quasi-)sites induce functors on the associated sheaf topoi. We used this to model
\kappa
-condensed animae on other categories than
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and to compare condensed and sheaf cohomology.

Definition A.4.9
.

•

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}}),(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
are quasi-sites.
A functor
f\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is

(i)

continuous
if for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
and
\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}\in\tau_{\mathcal{C}}(c)
,

\{f(c_{i})\to f(c)\}_{i\in I}\in\tau_{\mathcal{D}}(f(c))
is a cover.

(ii)

covering flat
if the composition

\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{f_{!}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{L_{\mathcal{D}}}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})

of the left Kan extension along
f
with
\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
-sheafification preserves finite limits.

(iii)

A
morphism of quasi-sites
if it is continuous and covering flat.

•

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}}),(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
are sites.
A functor
f\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is

(i)

continuous
if for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
and
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(c)
,

f_{*}(S)\coloneqq\{x\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/f(c)}}\,|\,\exists s\in S\text{ and }x\to f(s)\in{{C}_{/f(c)}}\}

is a
\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
-sieve.

(ii)

covering flat
if the composition

\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{f_{!}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{L_{\mathcal{D}}}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})

of the left Kan extension along
f
with
\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
-sheafification preserves finite limits.

(iii)

A
morphism of sites
if it is continuous and covering flat.

Example A.4.10
.

If
\tau_{1},\tau_{2}
are two Grothendieck topologies (coverages) on a category
\mathcal{C}
such that for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
\tau_{1}(c)\subseteq\tau_{2}(c)
, the
identity

(\mathcal{C},\tau_{1})\to(\mathcal{C},\tau_{2})
is a morphism of (quasi-)sites.

Lemma A.4.11
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}}),(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
are (quasi-)sites,
\mathcal{C}
has finite limits and
f\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is a functor which preserves finite limits.

(i)

Then
f
is covering-flat.

(ii)

Moreover, if
f
is a continuous functor of quasi-sites, then the induced functor of sites

(\mathcal{C},[\tau_{\mathcal{C}}])\to(\mathcal{D},[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}])

is continuous.

Proof.

Since
\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal{D}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})
preserves finite limits, the left Kan extension along
f
,

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})

preserves finite limits by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.3.20]
, hence
f
is covering flat.

Suppose now that
f
is a continuous functor of quasi-sites.
We claim that

\operatorname{Cov}_{f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(c)\coloneqq\{S\in\operatorname{Sieve}(c)\,|\,f_{*}(S)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(f(c))\}

defines a Grothendieck topology
f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
on
\mathcal{C}
.
As
\tau_{\mathcal{C}}\subseteq f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
and
f(f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}])\subseteq[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
, this then implies that
f\colon(\mathcal{C},[\tau_{\mathcal{C}}])\to(\mathcal{D},[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}])
is continuous.
For all
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
f_{*}({{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}})={{\mathcal{D}}_{/f(c)}}
, whence
{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}\in f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}](c)
.
Suppose that
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
S\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
is a covering sieve and
\alpha\colon b\to c\in\mathcal{C}
.
We claim that

(f\alpha)^{*}(f_{*}(S))=f_{*}(\alpha^{*}(S)).

For
x\to f(b)\in(f\alpha)^{*}(f_{*}(S))
, there exist
t\colon s\to c\in S
and a morphism

(x\to f(b)\xrightarrow{f\alpha}f(c))\to(f(s)\xrightarrow{ft}f(c))\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/f(c)}}.

Since
\mathcal{C}
has pullbacks and
f
preserves them, this implies that

x\to f(b)
factors over

x\to f(b\times_{c}s)\to f(b).

As
S
is a sieve,
b\times_{c}s\to b\in\alpha^{*}(S)
, which shows that
x\to f(b)\in f_{*}(\alpha^{*}(S))
.
Conversely, suppose that
u\colon x\to f(b)\in f_{*}(\alpha^{*}(S))
.
Then there exist
i\colon a\to b\in\mathcal{C}
, a morphism

(a\to b\xrightarrow{\alpha}c)\to(s\to c)\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}

with
s\to c\in S
, and a morphism
(x\xrightarrow{u}f(b))\to(f(a)\xrightarrow{fi}f(b))\in{{\mathcal{D}}_{/f(b)}}
.
This shows that
(u\colon x\to f(b))\in(f\alpha)^{*}(f_{*}(S))
, and hence

(f\alpha)^{*}(f_{*}(S))=f_{*}(\alpha^{*}(S)).

As
[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
is a Grothendieck topology, it follows that for all
c\in\mathcal{C},S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(c)
and
\alpha\colon b\to c\in\mathcal{C}
,

\alpha^{*}(S)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(b).

Suppose that
S,T\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
are sieves on
c
such that
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(c)
and for all
\alpha\colon b\to c\in S
,

\alpha^{*}(T)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(b).

We claim that
T\in\operatorname{Cov}_{f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(b)
, i.e.
f_{*}(T)\in[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
, this then proves that
f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
is a Grothendieck topology.
As
[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
is a Grothendieck topology, by the third condition on Grothendieck topologies it suffices to show that for
\beta\colon x\to f(c)\in f_{*}(S)
,

\beta^{*}(f_{*}(T))\in\operatorname{Cov}_{[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(b).

Suppose that
\beta\colon x\to f(c)\in f_{*}(S)
.
By definition of
f_{*}(S)
,
\beta
factors as

x\xrightarrow{j}f(s)\xrightarrow{f(\alpha)}f(c)

with
\alpha\colon s\to c\in S\subseteq{{C}_{/c}}
, and hence

\beta^{*}(f_{*}(T))=j^{*}(f\alpha)^{*}(f_{*}T).

We showed above that
(f\alpha)^{*}(f_{*}T)=(f_{*}(\alpha^{*}(T))).
By our assumption that
\alpha^{*}(T)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{f^{*}[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]}(s)
,
f_{*}(\alpha^{*}(T))\in[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]
, and hence

\beta^{*}(f_{*}(T))=j^{*}(f_{*}(\alpha^{*}(T)))\in[\tau_{\mathcal{D}}]

by the second condition for Grothendieck topologies.
∎

Corollary A.4.12
.

(i)

If
f\colon(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}})\to(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
is a continuous functor of (quasi-)sites, then

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})

\displaystyle\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}),

\displaystyle F

\displaystyle\mapsto F\circ f

restricts to a functor

f_{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C}).

(ii)

If
f
is in addition covering flat, i.e. a morphism of (quasi-)sites, then
f_{*}
restricts further to a functor

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C}),

and

f_{*}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})

is the right adjoint of a geometric morphism.

Notation A.4.13
.

If
f\colon(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}})\to(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
is a morphism of (quasi-)sites, we denote by
f_{*}\colon\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{D}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{(hyp)Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C}),F\mapsto F\circ f
the functor denoted by
f^{*}
in the above lemma and by
f^{*}
its left adjoint.

Proof.

The first statement is obvious from the definition of continuity.
Sheafification after left Kan extension

f_{!}^{L}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{f_{!}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{L_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})

is a left adjoint of

f_{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C}).

If
f
is covering flat, then
f_{!}^{L}
is left-exact. By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.5.1.16.(4)]
, this implies that
f_{*}
preserves hypercomplete objects.
Hypersheafification after left Kan extension

\hat{f}_{!}^{L}\colon\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{f_{!}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{L_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})

is a left-exact left adjoint of

f_{*}\colon\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C}).

(Hypercompletion is left-exact by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.1.1, Proposition 6.5.1.16]
.)
∎

Definition A.4.14
.

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}})
and
(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
are quasi-sites.
A functor
f\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
has the
covering lifting property
if for all
\{p_{i}\colon d_{i}\to d\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
, and all
f(c)\to d\in\mathcal{C}/d
there exists a cover
\{q_{j}\colon c_{j}\to c\}_{j\in J}\subseteq\tau_{\mathcal{C}}
such that for all
j\in J
, there exists
i(j)\in I
such that
h_{f(q_{j})}
factors as

h_{f(c_{j})}\to h_{d_{i(j)}}\times_{h(d)}h_{f(c)}\to h_{f(c)}.

Remark A.4.15
.

If
\mathcal{D}
has all pullbacks and
\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
is stable under pullbacks, i.e. for
\{d_{i}\to d\}\in\tau_{\mathcal{D}}(d)
and
e\to d\in\mathcal{D}
.
\{d_{i}\times_{d}e\to e\}\in\tau_{\mathcal{D}}(e)
, a functor has the covering lifting property if and only if for every
c\in\mathcal{C}
and every cover
\{p_{i}\colon d_{i}\to f(c)\}_{i\in I}\subseteq\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
, there exists a cover
\{q_{j}\colon c_{j}\to c\}_{j\in J}\subseteq\tau_{\mathcal{C}}
such that for all
j\in J
, there exists
i(j)\in I
such that
f(i_{j})
factors as
f(c_{j})\to d_{i(j)}\to f(c)
.

Lemma A.4.16
.

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}})
and
(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
are quasi-sites and
f\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is a functor which has the covering lifting property.
Right Kan extension
f_{*}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{P}(D)
along
f
restricts to functors

{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\to{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\text{ and }\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D}).

Both functors are right adjoints of a geometric morphism.

Proof.

Denote by
f^{*}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}),F\mapsto F\circ f
the pullback along
f
.
If
\mathcal{X}\coloneqq\{d_{j}\to d\}_{j\in J}
is a covering in
\mathcal{D}
, denote by
S(\mathcal{X})\subseteq h_{d}\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})
the subpresheaf on maps
c\to d
which factor over
c\to d_{i}\to d
for some
i\in I
. We will show below that
L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\to f^{*}h_{d})\in\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})
is an equivalence. This then implies that for
F\in\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})}(h_{d},f_{*}F)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(f^{*}h_{d},F)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}}(L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}f^{*}h_{d},F)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}}(L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}f^{*}S(\mathcal{X}),F)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(f^{*}S(\mathcal{X}),F)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})}(S(\mathcal{X}),f_{*}F),

which shows that
f_{*}F
is a
\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
-sheaf. Since colimits in
\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
are universal,
f^{*}h_{d}
is a colimit of representables, and
L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})
preserves colimits, it suffices to show that for all
h_{c}\to f^{*}h_{d},c\in\mathcal{C}
,

f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\times_{f^{*}h_{d}}h_{c}\to h_{c}

is an
L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}
-equivalence. Fix

t\in\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(h_{c},f^{*}h_{d})\cong f^{*}h_{d}(c)\cong h_{d}(f(c))\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{D}}(f(c),d).

By construction,
f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\times_{f^{*}h_{d}}h_{c}\subseteq h_{c}
is the full subpresheaf on maps
r\colon x\to c
such that there exists
i\in I
such that

f(x)\to f(c)\to d

factors over
d_{i}\to d
. Equivalently,
f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\times_{f^{*}h_{d}}h_{c}(x)\subseteq h_{c}(x)
consists of those maps
q\colon x\to c
such that
h_{f(q)}\colon h_{f(x)}\to h_{f(c)}
factors over
h_{d_{i}}\times_{h_{d}}h_{f(c)}\to h_{f(c)}
for some
i\in I
.
By assumption, there exists a cover
\mathcal{Y}\coloneqq\{c_{j}\to c\}_{j\in J}\in\tau_{\mathcal{C}}(c)
such that for all
j\in J
,
h_{f(c_{j})}\to h_{f(c)}
factors over

h_{f(c_{j})}\to h_{d_{i}}\times_{h_{d}}h_{f(c)}\to h_{f(c)}

for some
i=i(j)\in I
.
Denote by
S(\mathcal{Y})\subseteq h_{c}
the associated full subpresheaf, i.e.
S(\mathcal{Y})(x)\subseteq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(x,c)
is the subspace on maps
x\to c
which admit a factorization
x\to c_{j}\to c
for some
j\in J
.
Then

S(\mathcal{Y})\subseteq f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\times_{f^{*}h_{d}}h_{c}\subseteq h_{c}.

As
\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i\in I}
is a
\tau_{\mathcal{C}}
-cover,
S(\mathcal{Y})\subseteq j_{c}
induces an equivalence
L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}S(\mathcal{Y})\cong L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}h_{c}
.
This implies that

L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\times_{f^{*}h_{d}}h_{c})\to L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}h_{c}

admits a section. Since sheafification preserves pullbacks, it preserves monomorphisms (recall that a map
A\to B
