in a category
\mathcal{T}
is a monomorphism if and only if
A\cong A\times_{B}A
).
In particular,
L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\times_{f^{*}h_{d}}h_{c})\to L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}h_{c}
is a monomorphism, and hence an equivalence as it admits a section. This shows that
L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}f^{*}S(\mathcal{X})\cong L_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}f^{*}h_{d}
, and hence right Kan extension restricts to a functor

f_{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C}).

Since sheafification is left exact and
f^{*}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
is also a right adjoint, the composite

f^{*,L}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{f^{*}}\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{L_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})

is a left-exact left adjoint of
f_{*}
.
By
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.5.1.16]
,
f^{*,L}
preserves
\infty
-connective morphisms, whence
f_{*}
preserves hypersheaves, i.e. restricts to a functor

\hat{f}_{*}\colon\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D}).

Hypersheafification after restriction
\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\subseteq\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{f^{*}}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\widehat{(-)}_{\mathcal{D}}}\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})
is a left-exact left adjoint to
\hat{f}_{*}
. Hypercompletion is left-exact by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.1.1, Proposition 6.5.1.16]
.
∎

If in the situation of
Lemma

A.4.16
,
f
is fully faithful, then right Kan extension along
f
is a fully faithful functor
f_{*}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})
: For every
c\in\mathcal{C}
,
c
is a terminal object of
\mathcal{C}\times_{\mathcal{D}}\{c\}
, hence the counit
f^{*}f_{*}\to\operatorname{id}
is an equivalence.
This then implies that right Kan extension restricts to fully faithful functors

\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\hookrightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D}),\text{ and }\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D}).

Corollary A.4.17
.

Suppose that
i\colon(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}})\to(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
is a continuous functor of quasi-sites which has the covering lifting property and
i\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is fully faithful.

(i)

If the restriction
i^{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C}),F\mapsto F\circ i
(
A.4.12
) is conservative, then

\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\cong\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\text{ and }\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})

via restriction and right Kan extension.

(ii)

If the left adjoint of right Kan extension
\hat{i}^{*}\colon\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})
is conservative, then
\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
via right Kan extension.

Proof.

By
A.4.12
and
Lemma

A.4.16
, pullback and right Kan extension along
i
restrict to an adjoint pair

i_{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\colon i^{*}.

As
i
is fully faithful, the right Kan extension
i_{*}
is fully faithful.
Together with conservativity of
i^{*}
, this implies that
i^{*}
and
i_{*}
are mutually inverse equivalences. (It from the triangle identities that the unit and counit are equivalences).
In particular,
i^{*}
and
i_{*}
restrict to mutually inverse equivalences
\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
.

By
Lemma

A.4.16
, right Kan extension also restricts to a functor
\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
. This is a fully faithful right adjoint.
If its left adjoint is conservative, then
i_{*}
is an equivalence by the same reasoning as above.
∎

Corollary A.4.18
.

Suppose that
f\colon(\mathcal{C},\tau_{\mathcal{C}})\to(\mathcal{D},\tau_{\mathcal{D}})
is a continuous functor of quasi-sites that has the covering lifting property.
Suppose that
f\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is fully faithful, and for all
d\in\mathcal{D}
, there exists a cover
\{f(c_{i})\to d\}_{i\in I}\in\tau_{\mathcal{D}}(d)
with
c_{i}\in\mathcal{C}
.

Then right Kan extension along
f
restricts to equivalences

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})\cong\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D}).

Proof.

By
A.4.17
, it suffices to show that the left adjoint
f^{*}
of right Kan extension is conservative.
This left adjoint
f^{*}
sends a hypersheaf
G\in\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
to the hypersheafification of
G\circ f
.
Since
f
is continuous, restriction along
f
restricts to a functor

f_{0}^{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C}),A\mapsto A\circ f.

It therefore suffices to show that if
\phi\colon A\to B\in\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
is such that
f_{0}^{*}(\phi)\colon A\circ f\to B\circ f
is
\infty
-connective, then
\phi
is an equivalence (equivalently,
\infty
-connective).
Being a left-exact left adjoint,
f^{*}_{0}
commutes with homotopy groups. This follows from
[
Lur09
, Proposition 5.5.6.28]
as for
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
\pi_{n}=\pi_{0}\Omega^{n}=\tau_{\leq 0}\Omega^{n}
.
We are therefore reduced to showing that
f_{0}^{*}
restricts to a conservative functor
\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})
.

Fix
d\in\mathcal{D}
choose a
\tau_{\mathcal{D}}
-cover
\{f(c_{i})\to d\}
. Denote by
h\colon\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})
the Yoneda embedding.
For
A\in\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
,

A(d)\cong{\underset{\Delta_{s}}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})}(\check{C}(\sqcup_{i\in I}h(f(c_{i}))\to h(f(d))),A).

As
\Delta_{s,\leq 1}\subseteq\Delta_{s}
is left 1-cofinal (
[
Du23
, Example 6.14]
), for

A\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
,

\displaystyle A(d)\cong\operatorname{Eq}\left(\prod_{i\in I}A(f(c_{i}))\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})}(h(f(c_{i}))\times_{h(d)}h(f(c_{j})),A)\right).

For
i,j\in I
choose a small set
(d_{q})_{q\in Q_{i,j}}\subseteq\mathcal{D}
with an effective epimorphism

\pi\colon\sqcup_{q\in Q_{i,j}}h(d_{q})\to h(f(c_{i}))\times_{h(d)}h(f(c_{j})).

For
q\in Q_{i,j}
choose a cover
\{f(c_{k})\to d_{q}\}_{k\in K_{q}}
.

By left 1-cofinality of
\Delta_{s,\leq 1}\subseteq\Delta_{s}\subseteq\Delta
(
[
Lur09
, Lemma 6.5.3.7]
,
[
Du23
, Example 6.14]
), for
A\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
,

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})}

\displaystyle(h(f(c_{i}))\times_{h(d)}h(f(c_{j})),A)\cong{\underset{\Delta}{\operatorname{lim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})}(\check{C}(\pi),A)

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Eq}\left(\prod_{q\in Q_{i,j}}A(d_{q})\rightrightarrows\prod_{q,r\in Q_{i,j}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})}(h(d_{q})\times_{h(f(c_{i}))\times_{h(d)}h(f(c_{j}))}h(d_{r}),A)\right)

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow\prod_{q\in Q_{i,j}}A(d_{q})

is injective.
The above argument shows that for
q\in Q_{i,j}
, and
A\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
,

A(d_{q})\hookrightarrow\prod_{k\in K_{q}}A(f(c_{k}))=\prod_{k\in K_{q}}f_{0}^{*}A(c_{k})

is injective.
This implies that for
A\in\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})
,

A(d)\cong\operatorname{Eq}\left(\prod_{i\in I}f_{0}^{*}A(c_{i})\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j\in I}\prod_{q\in Q_{i,j}}\prod_{k\in K_{q}}f_{0}^{*}A(c_{k})\right),

which proves that
f_{0}^{*}\colon\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{D}}}(\mathcal{D})\to\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau_{\mathcal{C}}}(\mathcal{C})
is injective.

∎

A.4.1
The condensed and local section topology

Lemma A.4.19
.

For a
\kappa
-light profinite set
X
denote by
\operatorname{Cov}_{\operatorname{cond}}(X)
the collection of sieves
S\subseteq{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}_{/X}}
such that there exists a finite family
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i=1}^{n}\subseteq S\subseteq{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/X}}
such that
\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\to X
is onto.
This defines a Grothendieck topology on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
.

Proof.

This follows from
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.2.1]
.
Since
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
has all pullbacks and coproducts and the forget functor
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}\subseteq\operatorname{CH}\to\operatorname{Set}
preserves them and is conservative, it is straightforward to check that
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
and the continuous surjections satisfy the conditions of
[
Lur18a
, Proposition A.3.2.1]
, which implies that there exists a Grothendieck topology
\tau
on
\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
such that a sieve
S\subseteq{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/c}}
is a covering sieve if and only if there exists a finite collection of morphisms
\{c_{i}\to c\}_{i=1}^{n}\subseteq S\subseteq{{{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}}}_{/c}}
such that

\sqcup_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}\to c
is surjective.
∎

Definition A.4.20
.

Fix an uncountable strong limit cardinal
\kappa
and suppose that
\mathcal{T}\subseteq\operatorname{Top}_{\kappa}
is a full subcategory.
We say that a family
\{X^{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
of continuous maps in
\mathcal{T}
is a

•

local section cover if
\bigsqcup_{i\in I}X^{i}\to X
admits local sections.

•

a
\kappa
-condensed cover if
\bigsqcup_{i\in I}\underline{X^{i}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{X}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets.

Lemma A.4.21
.

Suppose
\lambda\geq\kappa
are uncountable cardinals and denote by
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
the category of
\lambda
-small topological spaces.

(i)

Open coverings (respectively local section coverings) constitute a coverage on
\operatorname{Top}_{\lambda}
, respectively.

(ii)

The local section covers form a Grothendieck coverage.

(iii)

Both coverages generate the same topology, and this topology is coarser than the
\kappa
-condensed topology on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
.

Proof.

If
f\colon Y\to X
is continuous and
X=\bigcup_{i\in I}X_{i}
is an open cover, then
Y=\bigcup_{i\in I}f^{-1}(X_{i})
is an open cover and therefore open covers constitute a coverage.
As isomorphisms are local section maps, and compositions and pullbacks of local section maps are local section maps, local section maps constitute a coverage on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
.
Every open cover is a local section cover. Conversely, if
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
is a local section cover, choose an open cover
X=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_{j}
such that sections
s_{j}
of the identity
\operatorname{id}_{U_{j}}
exist,

U_{j}\xrightarrow{s_{j}}\bigsqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\to U_{j}.

Then
\{s_{j}^{-1}(X_{i})\}_{i\in I,j\in J}
is an open cover and a refinement of
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
.
This shows that local section covers and open covers generate the same topology.
The local section covers form a Grothendieck coverage by
[
Pst23
, Definition A.1, Proposition A.5]
.

Suppose
K
is a
\kappa
-light profinite set,
f\colon K\to X
is a continuous map to a
\lambda
-small topological space and
X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_{i}
is an open cover.
For
i\in I
,
f^{-1}(U_{i})\subseteq K
is open. Since
K
is locally compact, for
k\in K
there exists a compact neighborhood
k\in N_{k}
with
N_{k}\subseteq f^{-1}(U_{i})
for some
i\in I
.
By compactness of
K
, there exists a finite set of elements
k_{1},\ldots,k_{n}\in K
such that
K=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}N_{k_{i}}
.
Hence by
Lemma

2.3.4
,
\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{U_{i}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{X}_{\kappa}
is an epimorphism of
\kappa
-condensed sets.
∎

A.4.2
Slices of sheaf topoi

In this section, we recall that the slice category of a sheaf topos over a representable sheaf is equivalent to the category of sheaves on the respective slice.

Definition A.4.22
.

Suppose that
(\mathcal{C},\tau)
is a site and
c\in\mathcal{C}
.
For
x\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
denote by
\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau,c}(x)
the collection of sieves
\{x_{i}\to x\}\in({{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}})_{/x}
such that the image in
{{\mathcal{C}}_{/x}}
is a
\tau
-sieve.

Denote by
f\colon{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}\to\mathcal{C}
the forget functor.
As

{{{\mathcal{C}_{/c}}}_{/(-)}}\cong{{\mathcal{C}}_{/(-)}}\circ f\colon{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty},

\tau_{c}
defines a Grothendieck topology on
{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
.

Remark A.4.23
.

For general coverages, there is no handy description of the induced topology on the slice, but for Grothendieck coverages, the following holds:
Suppose that
\tau
defines a Grothendieck coverage on a category
\mathcal{C}
and
c\in\mathcal{C}
.
For
d\to c\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
, we say that a family

\{x_{i}\to d\}_{i\in I}\subseteq({{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}})_{/d}\cong{{\mathcal{C}}_{/d}}

is a
\tau_{c}
-cover if the underling family
\{x_{i}\to d\}\subseteq{{\mathcal{C}}_{/d}}
is a
\tau
-cover.
The
\tau_{c}
-covers form a coverage on
{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
and the associated Grothendieck topology is the topology pulled back from the topology
[\tau]
on
\mathcal{C}
generated by
\tau
. It follows that the
\tau_{c}
-covers form a Grothendieck coverage.

By
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.1.6.12]
, the functor
{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}\to{{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}_{/h_{c}}}
induced by the Yoneda embedding

h_{-}\colon\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})

extends to an equivalence

\mathcal{P}({{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}})\cong{{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}_{/c}}
.
The sheaficiation
{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}\xrightarrow{L_{\tau}}\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})
induces a functor

{{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}_{/h_{c}}}\to{{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})}_{/L_{\tau}h_{c}}}.

Lemma A.4.24
.

Suppose
(\mathcal{C},\tau)
is a site.

(i)

The functor

\mathcal{P}({{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}})\cong{{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}_{/h_{c}}}\xrightarrow{L_{\tau/c}}{{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})}_{/L_{\tau}h_{c}}}

factors over an equivalence

{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\tau_{c}}(\mathcal{C}_{/c})\cong{{{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})}_{/L_{\tau}h_{c}}}.

(ii)

If
L_{\tau}h_{c}
is hypercomplete, then this restricts to an equivalence

\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{c}}({{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}})\cong{{\operatorname{hypShv}_{\tau_{c}}(\mathcal{C})}_{/L_{\tau}h_{c}}}.

Remark A.4.25
.

If
\mathcal{C}=\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{C}
is an
(n,1)
-category (
n\in\mathbb{N}
), then
L_{\tau}c\in\tau_{\leq n}\mathcal{X}
is hypercomplete for all
c\in\mathcal{C}
by
[
Lur09
, Lemma 6.5.2.9]
.

Proof of
Lemma

A.4.24
.

This is a straightforward consequence of
[
Lur09
, Corollary 5.1.6.12]
and the description of the sheafification functor provided by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7]
, but we could not find a reference.
For
F\in{{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}_{/h_{c}}}
, the unit
F\to L_{\tau}h_{c}
and the map
F\to c
induce a map
F\to L_{\tau}F\times_{L_{\tau}h_{c}}h_{c}
. These maps exhibit

\mathcal{P}({{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}})\cong{{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}_{/h_{c}}}\xrightarrow{L_{\tau/h_{c}}}{{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})}_{/L_{\tau}h_{c}}}

as left adjoint to

r\colon{{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})}_{/L_{\tau}h_{c}}}\xrightarrow{-\times_{L_{\tau}h_{c}}h_{c}}{{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})}_{/h_{c}}}\hookrightarrow{{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}_{/h_{c}}}.

Since
L_{\tau}
is left-exact,
L_{\tau/h_{c}}\circ r=1
, i.e.
L_{\tau/h_{c}}
exhibits
{{\operatorname{Shv}_{\tau}(\mathcal{C})}_{/L_{\tau}h_{c}}}
as localization of
{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}}}
at the morphisms
F\to L_{\tau}F\times_{L_{\tau}h_{c}}h_{c}
. We will show that for a presheaf
F\in\mathcal{P}({{C}_{/c}})\cong{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}}}
, the map
F\to L_{\tau}F\times_{L_{\tau}h_{c}}h_{c}
exhibits
L_{\tau}F\times_{L_{\tau}h_{c}}h_{c}
as
\tau_{c}
-sheafification of
F
, then the statement follows.

Recall from
[
Lur09
, section 6.2.2.7]
that if
(\mathcal{D},\rho)
is a site,
\rho
-sheafification can be realised as transfinite composition of the functor

(-)^{\dagger,\rho}\colon\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{D})

which sends a presheaf
F
to
x\mapsto{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\rho}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}F(S)
.

For
x\to c\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
,

\displaystyle(F^{\dagger,\tau}\times_{h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau}}h_{c})(x\to c)

\displaystyle=\operatorname{Map}_{{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}}}}(h_{x}\to h_{c},F^{\dagger,\tau}\times_{h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau}}h_{c})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau}}}}(h_{x}\to h_{c}\to h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau},F^{\dagger,\tau})

\displaystyle\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C)}(h_{x},F^{\dagger,\tau})\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C)}(h_{x},h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau})}\{h_{x}\to h_{c}\to h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau}\}

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C)}(S,F)\times_{{\underset{T\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(T,h_{c})}\{h_{x}\to h_{c}\}.

For two covering sieves
S,T\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)
,
S\cap T\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)
as for all
f\colon t\to x\in T
,

f^{*}(S\cap T)=f^{*}(S)\cap f^{*}(T)=f^{*}(S)\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(t).

This shows that
\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)
is cofiltered, whence

\displaystyle{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}

\displaystyle\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C)}(S,F)\times_{{\underset{T\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(T,h_{c})}\{h_{x}\to h_{c}\}

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C)}(S,F)\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C)}(S,h_{c})}\{S\subseteq h_{x}\to h_{c}\})

\displaystyle\cong{\underset{S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}}}}(S\subseteq h_{x}\to h_{c},F\to h_{c})

\displaystyle\cong F^{\dagger,\tau_{c}}(x\to c).

We now deduce from this and the description of the sheafification functors (
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7]
) that
F\to L_{\tau}F\times_{L_{\tau}h_{c}}h_{c}
is the
\tau_{c}
-sheafification of
F
.
For ordinals
\beta
and
F\in\mathcal{P}(C)
let
T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\beta+1}F\coloneqq T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\beta}F^{\dagger,\tau}
and if
\gamma
is a limit ordinal let
T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\gamma}\coloneqq{\underset{\alpha<\gamma}{\operatorname{colim}}}T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\alpha}F
.
For
F\in{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}}}
, define
T_{\alpha}^{{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}}F
analogously.
We show by transfinite induction that for all ordinals
\alpha
, the map
F\to T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\alpha}F\times_{T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\alpha}h_{c}}h_{c}
factors over an equivalence

F\to T^{{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}}_{\alpha}F\cong T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\alpha}F\times_{T^{\mathcal{C}}_{\alpha}h_{c}}h_{c}.

The zero case was shown above, the successor case follows from the above as

\displaystyle T_{\alpha+1}^{{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}}(F)\cong(T_{\alpha}^{\mathcal{C}}(F)\times_{T_{\alpha}^{\mathcal{C}}h_{c}}h_{c})^{\dagger,\tau_{c}}

\displaystyle\cong(T_{\alpha}^{\mathcal{C}}(F)\times_{T_{\alpha}^{\mathcal{C}}(h_{c})}h_{c})^{\dagger,\tau}\times_{h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau}}h_{c}

\displaystyle\cong(T_{\alpha+1}^{\mathcal{C}}(F)\times_{T_{\alpha+1}^{\mathcal{C}}(h_{c})}h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau})\times_{h_{c}^{\dagger,\tau}}h_{c}\cong T_{\alpha+1}^{\mathcal{C}}(F)\times_{T_{\alpha+1}^{\mathcal{C}}(h_{c})}h_{c},

where we used the induction hypothesis, the zero case and that
(-)^{\dagger,\tau}
is left-exact (cf. the proof of
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7]
). The limit case follows from this since the identifications are compatible with the maps
T_{\alpha}\to T_{\beta}
for
\alpha\leq\beta
.
Choose a regular cardinal
\kappa
such that the following hold:
For every
x\in\mathcal{C}
and every covering
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau}(x)
,
the functor

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{An},F\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})}(S,F)

commutes with
\kappa
-filtered colimits, and for every
x\to c\in{{\mathcal{C}}_{/c}}
and every covering
S\in\operatorname{Cov}_{\tau_{c}}(x\to c)
,

\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}/c)\to\operatorname{An},F\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{P}(C/c)}(S,F)

commutes with

\kappa
-filtered colimits. This is possible since
\mathcal{C}
is an essentially small category.
Then for all
F\in\mathcal{P}({{C}_{/c}})\cong{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}}}
,

L_{\tau_{c}}(F)\cong T_{\kappa}F\cong T_{\kappa}F\times_{T_{\kappa}C}\{c\}\cong L_{\tau}F\times_{L_{\tau}h_{c}}\{h_{c}\}\in\mathcal{P}({{C}_{/c}})\cong{{\mathcal{P}(C)}_{/h_{c}}}

by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.2.2.7]
and the above.
The statement on hypercomplete topoi follows from
Lemma

A.4.26
below.
∎

Lemma A.4.26
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a topos denote by
\widehat{\mathcal{X}}\subseteq\mathcal{X}
the category of hypercomplete objects.
For
x\in\widehat{\mathcal{X}}
,

{{\widehat{\mathcal{X}}}_{/x}}\subseteq{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}
is the full subcategory of hypercomplete objects in
{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}
.

Proof.

Denote by
L_{\operatorname{hyp}}\colon\mathcal{X}\to\widehat{\mathcal{X}}
and
L_{\operatorname{hyp},x}\colon{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}\to\widehat{({{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}})}
the hypersheafification functors.
Since
x
is hypercomplete, the hypercompletion
L_{\operatorname{hyp}}\colon\mathcal{X}\to\widehat{\mathcal{X}}
induces a functor

L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}\colon{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}\to{{\widehat{\mathcal{X}}}_{/x}}

left adjoint to the inclusion.
By definition (
[
Lur09
, p. 657]
), the forget functor
{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}\to\mathcal{X}
reflects
\infty
-connective morphisms.
In particular, for
y\to x\in{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}
, the unit
y\to L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}(y)\in{{\widehat{\mathcal{X}}}_{/x}}
is
\infty
-connective.
As
L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}
is left adjoint to the inclusion, for
q\colon t\to x\in{{\widehat{\mathcal{X}}}_{/x}}\subseteq{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}
,

\operatorname{Map}_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}}(-,q)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{{{\widehat{\mathcal{X}}}_{/x}}}(-,q)\circ L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}

inverts
\infty
-connective morphisms, whence
{{\widehat{\mathcal{X}}}_{/x}}\subseteq{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}
consists of hypercomplete objects.
This shows that for all
y\in{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}
, the unit
y\to L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}(y)
induces an equivalence

L_{\operatorname{hyp},{{\mathcal{X}}_{/x}}}(y)\cong L_{\operatorname{hyp},x}(L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}(y))\cong L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}(y),

i.e.
L_{\operatorname{hyp},x}\cong L_{\operatorname{hyp}/x}
.
∎

A.5
Homotopy invariance of gros topos cohomology

In this section, we show that sheaf/gros topos cohomology with constant coefficients is homotopy invariant.
We used this to prove
2.9.3
.

Notation A.5.1
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{X}
is a topos. For a morphism
f\colon Y\to X\in\mathcal{X}
let

f^{*}\coloneqq Y\times_{X}-\colon{{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/Y}}

and denote by
f_{*}
its right adjoint.
As
f^{*}
is left-exact,
f^{*}\dashv f_{*}
stabilizes to an adjoint pair
f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
(
1.3.4
).

For
Z\in\mathcal{X}
let
\pi_{Z}^{*}\coloneqq Z\times-\colon\mathcal{X}\to{{\mathcal{X}}_{/Z}}
. This functor is right adjoint to the forget functor
\pi_{Z,!}\colon{{\mathcal{X}}_{/Z}}\to\mathcal{X}
.
Denote by

\pi_{Z,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/Z}})

the stabilization (
Definition

1.3.3
) of
\pi_{Z}^{*}
.
By
[
Lur17
, Corollary 1.4.4.4]
,
\pi_{Z,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}
admits a left adjoint
\pi_{Z,\operatorname{Sp},!}
and
\pi_{Z,\operatorname{Sp},!}\circ\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\cong\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}\circ\pi_{Z,!}
(
1.5.8
).

Lemma A.5.2
.

Suppose
f\colon X\to Y\in\mathcal{X}
is a morphism in a topos
\mathcal{X}
.

For
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
, the map
f^{*}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(Y,A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,A)
is an equivalence if and only if the unit
A\to f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}}(X,\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}}(X,f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A).

Proof.

We claim that

(A.5.2.1)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}})}(-,\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}})}(-,f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/Y}})}(f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-,\underbrace{f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}}_{\cong\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp},!}-,-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}\circ f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}},-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{f,*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta^{*}-}

commutes, where

\beta\colon\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}\circ f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\to\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp},!}

denotes the Beck-Chevalley transformation of
f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\pi^{X,*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\cong\pi^{Y,*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
and
\eta_{f}
is an adjunction unit for
f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
.

All functors
\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}})^{\operatorname{op}}\times\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})\to\operatorname{Sp}
in the above diagram preserve small limits in both variables:

\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*},f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}},f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
and
\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}
are stabilizations of limit-preserving functors and in particular preserve limits.

f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}},\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp},!}
and
\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}
are left adjoints and therefore preserve colimits.
The cohomology functors preserve small limits in both variables by
1.3.38
. Hence by
[
Lur17
, Proposition 1.4.2.21]
/
Lemma

1.3.39
, it suffices to show that the diagram obtained by applying
\Omega^{\infty}
to the above diagram is commutative, i.e. that

(A.5.2.2)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}})}(-,\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}})}(-,f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/Y}})}(f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-,\underbrace{f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}}_{\cong\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp},!}-,-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}\circ f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-,-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{f,*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta^{*}-}

commutes.
By the triangle identities for
f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\dashv f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
, the top horizontal arrow is the map induced by
f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
.
For all
T\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
,
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}})}(-,\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}T)
and

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}\circ f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-,T)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})}(-,\pi^{*}_{Y,\operatorname{Sp}}f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}-)

are representable.
Hence by definition of the vertical identifications and fully faithfulness of the Yoneda embedding

\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X}),\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}))\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}({\mathcal{X}}),\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}})^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{An})),

it suffices to describe a homotopy between

\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}\circ f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}\cong\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}\circ\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{\pi_{Y}}}\operatorname{id}

and

\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp},!}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}\xrightarrow{\beta}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp},!}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{\pi_{X}}}\operatorname{id}.

This exists by
[
CSY22
, Lemma 2.3.3.(4)]
.
This proves that
A.5.2.2
commutes, and hence so does
A.5.2.1
.
By evaluating
A.5.2.1
at
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}X
in the first variable, we obtain a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}_{{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}}}(X,\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}_{{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}}}(X,f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}_{{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/Y}}}}(Y,\underbrace{f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}}_{\cong\pi_{Y,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}}-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{X}}}(X,-)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}_{{\mathcal{X}}}(Y,-).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}

In particular, for
M\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{X})
,
f^{*}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(Y,M)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{X}}(X,M)
is an equivalence if and only if

\eta_{f}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}}(X,\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}M)\cong\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{X}}_{/X}}}(X,f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}M).\qed

Recollection A.5.3
.

A continous map
f\colon X\to Y
defines a morphism of sites

\displaystyle f^{-1}\colon\operatorname{Op}(Y)

\displaystyle\to\operatorname{Op}(X),

\displaystyle V

\displaystyle\mapsto f^{-1}(V).

Denote by

f_{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(Y)\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X)\colon f^{*},f^{*}\dashv f_{*}

the induced geometric morphism (
A.4.12
) and by
f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}
the stabilization of
f_{*}
(
1.3.4
). By
Lemma

1.5.7
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(Y,A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A).

For
A\in\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(Y)
,
f_{*}A=A\circ f^{-1}
. In particular, for
A\in\operatorname{Ab}(\tau_{\leq 0}\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(Y))
,
\pi_{0}f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A=A\circ f^{-1}
.

The unit
\eta_{f}\colon\operatorname{id}\to f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
induces a natural transformation

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,-)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,f_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-)\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(Y,f^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}-).

For a topological space
X
denote by
c_{X}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Zar}}(X))
the stabilization of constant sheaf functor.

Lemma A.5.4
.

Suppose that
X
is a topological space and denote by
\pi\colon X\times[0,1]\to X
the projection.

(i)

The unit
\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Shv}(X\times[0,1],\operatorname{Sp})}\to\pi_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\pi^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is an equivalence.

(ii)

In particular,
\pi_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\circ c_{X\times[0,1]}\cong c_{X}
.

Proof.

By
[
Lur17
, Variant A.2.10]
, the unit
\operatorname{id}\to\pi_{*}\pi^{*}
is an equivalence.
Hence by construction of the unit for
\pi_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\vdash\pi^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
(
1.3.4
),
\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Shv}(X\times[0,1],\operatorname{Sp})}\to\pi_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\pi^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
is an equivalence.

As
\pi^{*}
is a left-exact left adjoint, the constant sheaf functor for
X\times[0,1]
factors as

\operatorname{An}\xrightarrow{\text{const}_{X}}\operatorname{Shv}(X)\xrightarrow{\pi^{*}}\operatorname{Shv}(X\times[0,1]),

and in particular,
\pi^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\circ c_{X}=c_{X\times[0,1]}
.
It follows from the above that

c_{X}\cong\pi_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\pi^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}c_{X}\cong\pi_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}c_{X\times[0,1]}.\qed

Lemma A.5.5
.

Suppose
\lambda
is an uncountable cardinal. For a
\lambda
-small topological space
X
, denote by

{t}^{*}_{X}\colon\operatorname{Shv}(X)\to{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}

the left adjoint of the geometric morphism induced by the morphism of sites
\operatorname{Op}(X)\subseteq{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
(page
2.5
).
This is fully faithful.

Proof.

The functor
{t}^{*}_{X}
factors as

\operatorname{Shv}(X)\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Op}(X))\xrightarrow{t_{!}}\mathcal{P}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}})\xrightarrow{L_{LS}}\operatorname{Shv}_{LS,x}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}})\cong{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}

where
t_{!}
is left Kan extension along
t\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)\subseteq{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
,
L_{LS}
is sheafification with respect to the Grothendieck topology induced by the local section topology on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
and the right equivalence is
Lemma

A.4.24
.
As the local section covers form a Grothendieck coverage on
\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
(
Lemma

A.4.21
), by
A.4.23
, the local section covers define a Grothendieck coverage on
{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
, and the associated topology agrees with the one pulled back from the local section topology.
The open covers define a Grothendieck pretopology (
[
Pst23
, Definition A.1]
) on
\operatorname{Op}(X)
, and the local section covers define a Grothendieck pretopology on
{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
. The inclusion
t\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)\subseteq{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
defines a morphism of
\infty
-sites in the sense of
[
Pst23
, Definition A.3]
which has the covering lifting property.
Hence by
[
Pst23
, Proposition A.13]
, the precomposition

t_{*}\colon\mathcal{P}({{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/{X}}})\to\mathcal{P}(\operatorname{Op}(X)),F\mapsto F\circ t

commutes with sheafifications.
In particular, for
Y\in\operatorname{Shv}(X)
,

{t}^{X}_{*}{t}^{*}_{X}(Y)={t}^{X}_{*}(L_{\text{LS}}t_{!}Y)=t_{*}(L_{\text{LS}}t_{!}Y)\cong L_{\operatorname{Zar}}(t_{*}t_{!}Y).

As
t
is fully faithful, the unit
\operatorname{id}\to t_{*}t_{!}
is an equivalence.
This implies that the unit
\operatorname{id}\to{t}^{X}_{*}{t}^{*}_{X}
is an equivalence as well.
∎

Corollary A.5.6
.

Suppose
\lambda
is an uncountable cardinal.
Denote by
\text{const}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})
the stabilization of the constant sheaf functor and by
h_{-}\colon\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}\to\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}
the Yoneda embedding.
For
A\in\operatorname{Sp}
,

\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{-},\text{const}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp}}A)\colon(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Sp}

inverts homotopy equivalences.

Example A.5.7
.

The stabilized constant sheaf functor

\text{const}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}((\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}},\operatorname{Sp})

sends an abelian group
A
to the sheaf

\mathcal{C}(-,A^{\delta})\colon(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab}

of continuous functions into the discrete abelian group
A^{\delta}
.

Proof.

Note that a functor
F\colon(\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda})^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Sp}
inverts homotopy equivalences if and only if for
X\in\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}
, the projection
p\colon X\times[0,1]\to X
induces an equivalence
F(X\times[0,1])\cong F(X)
.
Fix
X\in\operatorname{\operatorname{Top}}^{\lambda}
and denote by

p^{*}\coloneqq(X\times[0,1])\times_{X}-\colon{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}\rightleftarrows{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X\times[0,1]}}}\colon p_{*},p^{*}\dashv p_{*}

the associated basechange geometric morphism.
By
Lemma

A.5.2
,

p^{*}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X\times[0,1]},A)

is an equivalence if and only if the unit
\operatorname{id}\to p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}
induces an equivalence

\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}}(h_{X},\pi_{X}^{*}A)\cong\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}}(h_{X},p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X}^{*}A).

Denote by
{t}^{*}_{X}\colon\operatorname{Shv}(X)\rightleftarrows{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}\colon{t}^{X}_{*}
the geometric morphism induced by the morphism of sites
\operatorname{Op}(X)\subseteq{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}
(see page
2.5
), and let

\pi_{X}^{*}\coloneqq h_{X}\times-\colon\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}\to{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}},

\pi_{Y}^{*}\coloneqq h_{Y}\times-\colon\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}\to{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{Y}}}.

By
Lemma

1.5.7
,

\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}}(h_{X},\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}}(h_{X},p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A)

is an equivalence if and only if

{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\eta)\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A)

is. The comutative diagram of sites
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Op}(X)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Op}(X\times[0,1])}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{\operatorname{Top}^{\lambda}}_{/X\times[0,1]}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(X\times[0,1])\times_{X}-}

yields a commutative diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Shv}(X)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Shv}(X\times[0,1])}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X\times[0,1]}}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{t}^{*}_{X}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p^{*}_{\operatorname{Shv}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{t}^{*}_{X\times[0,1]}}

The horizontal maps are fully faithful by
Lemma

A.5.5
. Denote by
{t}^{X}_{*},{t}^{X\times[0,1]}_{*}
their right adjoints.
Fully faithfulness of
{t}^{*}_{X},{t}^{*}_{X\times[0,1]}
implies that

{t}^{X}_{*}\circ p_{*}\circ{t}^{*}_{X}

is right adjoint to
p^{*}_{\operatorname{Shv}}
and

\operatorname{id}\cong{t}^{X}_{*}{t}^{*}_{X}\xrightarrow{{t}^{X}_{*}({\eta})}p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{t}^{*}_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}

is a unit for this adjunction, where
\eta
denotes adjunction unit for
p^{*}\dashv p_{*}
and the left equivalence is the unit for
{t}^{*}_{X}\dashv{t}^{X}_{*}
.
Passing to stabilizations, we obtain that

\tilde{\eta}\colon\operatorname{id}\cong{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}{t}^{*}_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}\xrightarrow{{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}({\eta})}p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{t}^{*}_{X}

exhibits

{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\circ p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\circ{t}^{*}_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}

as right adjoint to
p^{*}_{\operatorname{Shv},\operatorname{Sp}}
. (Note that all functors are left-exact.)
By
Lemma

A.5.4
,
\tilde{\eta}
is an equivalence, whence

{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(\eta)\colon\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(X,{t}^{X}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}p^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A)

is an equivalence for all
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})
with
\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A\in\operatorname{\operatorname{Im}}({t}^{*}_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Shv}(X,\operatorname{Sp})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}))
.

We have shown above that this implies that

p^{*}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X\times[0,1]},A)

is an equivalence for all
A\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda})
with
\pi_{X,\operatorname{Sp}}^{*}A\in\operatorname{\operatorname{Im}}({t}^{*}_{\operatorname{Sp}}{X}\colon\operatorname{Shv}(X,\operatorname{Sp})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}({{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}))
.
As

\pi_{X}^{*}\circ\text{const}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}\cong\text{const}_{{{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}_{/h_{X}}}}\cong{t}^{*}_{X}\circ\text{const}_{\operatorname{Shv}(X)}

(all functors are left-exact left adjoints), it follows that

p^{*}\colon\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X},\text{const}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp}}A)\to\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda}}(h_{X\times[0,1]},\text{const}_{\mathcal{T}^{LS}_{\lambda},\operatorname{Sp}}A)

is an equivalence for all
A\in\operatorname{Sp}
.
∎

A.6
Proof of
2.5.8

In this section, we recall the proof of
2.5.8
from
[
CS19a
, Lecture 3]
.
We start with some preparation.

Lemma A.6.1
.

Suppose
A
is the product of a discrete abelian group and a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
–vector space. For a filtered system of finite sets
(X_{k})_{k\in K}
, the canonical map

{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(X_{k},A)\to\mathcal{C}({\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k},A)

is injective and has dense image where both sides are endowed with the compact open topology.

Proof.

For
k\in K
denote by
\pi_{k}\colon{\underset{k}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}\to X_{k}
the projection.
Suppose that

(f\colon X_{k}\to A),(g\colon X_{l}\to A)

with
g\circ\pi_{l}=f\circ\pi_{k}
.
As
K
is filtered, we can assume that
k=l
.
Let
C\coloneqq X_{k}\setminus\operatorname{Im}(\pi_{k})
. This is finite. As
\emptyset={\underset{l\in K_{/k}}{\operatorname{lim}}}(X_{l}\times_{X_{k}}C)
and
K_{/l}
is filtered, by
Lemma

2.4.17
, there exists
l\to K\in K
with
X_{l}\times_{X_{k}}C=\emptyset
, i.e.
\operatorname{\operatorname{Im}}(X_{l}\to X_{k})\subseteq\operatorname{\operatorname{Im}}(\pi_{k}\colon{\underset{k}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}\to X_{k})
.
This implies that the two maps

f\circ X(l\to k),g\circ X(l\to k)\colon X_{l}\to X_{k}\to A

agree, which proves that the map is injective.
We now show that it has dense image. Choose a metric on
A
(defining the topology).
Supppose that
f\colon{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}\to A
and fix
\epsilon>0
.
For
x\in{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}\to A
, there exists an open neighbourhood
x\in U
such that
f(U)\subseteq D_{\epsilon}(f(x))
. By definition of the limit topology and since
K
is filtered, there exist
k_{x}\in K
,
U_{x}\subseteq X_{k_{x}}
open with
\pi_{k_{x}}^{-1}(U_{x})\subseteq U
.
By compactness of
{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}
, there exists a finite collection
\{x_{1},\ldots,x_{m}\}\subseteq{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}
with
\cup_{j=1}^{m}\pi_{k_{x_{j}}}^{-1}(U_{{x_{j}}})
. Using filteredness of
K
again, we can reduce to the case where
k_{x_{j}}=k_{x_{1}}=:k
for all
1\leq j\leq m
.
That is, we have found
k\in K
, a finite set
\{x_{1},\ldots,x_{m}\}\subseteq{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}
, and a collection of opens
(U_{j})_{1\leq j\leq m}\subseteq X_{k}
such that
\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}\pi_{k}^{-1}(U_{j})={\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}
and for all
1\leq j\leq m
,
f(\pi_{k}^{-1}(U_{j}))\subseteq D_{\epsilon}(f(x_{j}))
.
Let

\displaystyle f_{k}\colon F_{k}

\displaystyle\to A

\displaystyle x

\displaystyle\mapsto\begin{cases}f(x_{j})&x\in U_{j}\setminus\cup_{l=1}^{j-1}U_{l}\\
0&x\notin\cup_{k=1}^{m}U_{k}.\end{cases}

As
{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}=\cup_{j=1}^{m}\pi_{k}^{-1}(U_{j}\setminus\cup_{l=1}^{j-1}U_{l})
, and for
x\in\pi_{k}^{-1}(U_{j}\setminus\cup_{l=1}^{j-1}U_{l})
,

f_{k}(\pi_{k}(x))=f(x_{j})\in D_{\epsilon}(f(x))

(by choice of
U_{j}
), it follows that

\max_{x\in{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k}}d(f(x),f_{k}\circ\pi_{k}(x))<\epsilon
, which proves that the image of

{\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(X_{k},A)\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C}({\underset{k\in K}{\operatorname{lim}}}X_{k},A)

is dense.
∎

Notation A.6.2
.

For a continuous map
Y\to X
and a topological abelian group
A
, denote by
\mathcal{C}(\check{C}(Y\to X),A)
the cosimplicial abelian group given by continous maps from the Čech nerve of
Y\to X
to
A
, and by
[\check{\mathcal{C}}(Y\to X),A]
the unnormalized Moore complex (
[
Lur17
, Definition 1.2.3.8]
) of this cosimplicial abelian group.

Lemma A.6.3

(
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2, 3.3]
)
.

(i)

Suppose
A
is a discrete abelian group and
S\to X
is a continuous surjection between profinite sets.
Then
[\check{\mathcal{C}}(S\to X),A]
augments to a resolution of
\mathcal{C}(X,A)
.

(ii)

If
X
is a compact Hausdorff space and
S\to X
is a continuous surjection from a profinite set
S
, then

[\check{\mathcal{C}}(S\to X),\mathbb{R}]
augments to a resolution of
\mathcal{C}(X,\mathbb{R})
.

Proof.

We proceed as in the proofs of
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2, 3.3]
.
Suppose first that
S\to X
is a continuous surjection of profinite sets and
A
is a discrete abelian group.
We can write

S\to X={\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{lim}}}(S_{j}\to X_{j})

as filtered limit over surjections of finite sets
f_{j}\colon S_{j}\to X_{j}
(see e.g.
[
Man22
, Lemma 2.1.6]
).

For all
j\in J
,
[\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),A]
is a resolution of
\mathcal{C}(X_{j},A)
:

2.4.27
and
1.5.3
imply that for all finite sets
F
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{F}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong\prod_{f\in F}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(*,\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{C}(F,A)

is concentrated in degree
0
. Together with
1.5.13
, this implies that

H^{q}([\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),A])\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{q}(\underline{X_{j}}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

for all
q\in\mathbb{Z}
, i.e.

[\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),A]
augments to a resolution of
\mathcal{C}(X_{j},A)
.
It follows that
{\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{colim}}}[\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),A]
augments to a resolution of
{\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(S_{j},A)
.
Since
A
has the discrete topology, the compact open topology on

\mathcal{C}(\check{C}(S\to X)([p]),A)=\mathcal{C}(\underbrace{S\times_{X}\ldots\times_{X}S}_{p+1\text{ times }},A)

is discrete for all
p\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
.
Lemma

A.6.1
now implies the canonical map

{\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{colim}}}[\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),A]\to[\check{C}(S\to X),A]

is an isomorphism of chain complexes, whence
[\check{C}(S\to X),A]
augments to a resolution of

{\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(X_{j},A)=\mathcal{C}(X,A).

Suppose now that
S\to X
is a surjection from a profinite set
S
to a compact Hausdorff space
X
.
As

H^{0}([\check{C}(S\to X),\mathbb{R}])=\operatorname{Ker}\left(\pi_{2}^{*}-\pi_{1}^{*}\colon\mathcal{C}(S,\mathbb{R})\to C(S\times_{X}S,\mathbb{R})\right)=\mathcal{C}(X,\mathbb{R}),

it suffices to show that

(A.6.3.1)

\displaystyle H^{n}([\check{C}(S\to X),\mathbb{R}])=0\text{ for }n>0.

For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, endow

[\check{C}(S\to X),\mathbb{R}]_{n}=\mathcal{C}(\underbrace{S\times_{X}\ldots\times_{X}S}_{n+1\text{ times }},\mathbb{R})

with the sup-norm.
Fix
n\geq 1
.
We claim that for
0\neq f\in\ker(d_{n})
and
1>\epsilon>0
, there exists

b\in\mathcal{C}(\check{C}(S\to X)([n-1]),\mathbb{R})

with
||b||<(1+\epsilon)||f||
and
||f-d_{n-1}b||<\epsilon||f||
.
Let us first explain how this implies
A.6.3.1
: Fix
0<\epsilon<1
, let
f^{0}\coloneqq f
and define a sequence of elements

(b_{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{1}}\in\mathcal{C}(\check{C}(S\to X)([n-1]),\mathbb{R}),\,(f^{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\in\ker(d_{n})

recursively as follows:
If
(b_{k})_{k\leq m-1}
and
(f^{k})_{k\leq m-1}
have been defined, choose
b_{m}
such that

||b_{m}||<(1+\epsilon)||f^{m-1}||

and

||f^{m-1}-d_{n-1}b_{m}||<\epsilon||f^{m-1}||,

and set
f^{m}\coloneqq f^{m-1}-d_{n-1}b_{m}
.
It follows inductively that for all
k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
||f^{k}||<\epsilon||f^{k-1}||<\epsilon^{k}||f||
, and hence

||b_{k}||<(1+\epsilon)\epsilon^{k-1}||f||.

In particular,
b\coloneqq\sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}b_{k}
exists.
As

\displaystyle||f-d_{n-1}b||

\displaystyle<||\underbrace{f-\sum_{j=1}^{m}d_{n-1}b_{j}}_{=f^{m}}||+\sum_{j>m}||d_{n-1}b_{j}||

\displaystyle<\epsilon^{m}||f||+\sum_{j>m}(n+1)||b_{j}||

\displaystyle<\epsilon^{m}||f||+(n+1)\sum_{j>m}(1+\epsilon)\epsilon^{j-1}||f||

\displaystyle=\epsilon^{m}||f||(1+(n+1)\frac{1+\epsilon}{1-\epsilon})\xrightarrow{m\to\infty}0,

f=d_{n-1}b
.
Note also that

||b||\leq\sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}||b_{k}||\leq(1+\epsilon)\sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}_{0}}\epsilon^{k}||f||=\frac{1+\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}||f||.

We now prove the claim. Suppose first that
X
is profinite and write
(S\to X)={\underset{j\in J}{\operatorname{lim}}}(S_{j}\to X_{j})
as inverse limit of surjections.
For
j\in J
, choose a section
s_{j}\colon X_{j}\to S_{j}
.
This defines a splitting of the augmented simplicial object
\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j})\to X_{j}
. This splitting induces a contracting chain homotopy
h_{j}
of the associated augmented cochain complex
\mathcal{C}(X_{j},\mathbb{R})\to[\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),\mathbb{R}]
, see e.g.
[
Lur18
,
Tag 04SE
]
.
In degree
m
,

h_{j,m}\colon\mathcal{C}(\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j})([m]),\mathbb{R})\to\mathcal{C}(\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j})([m-1]),\mathbb{R})

is pullback along a map
\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j})[m-1]\to\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j})[m]
and in particular of norm
\leq 1
.
For
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the boundary map

d_{m}\colon[\check{C}(S\to X),\mathbb{R}]_{m}\to[\check{C}({S\to X}),\mathbb{R}]_{m+1}

is the alternating sum of the restrictions along the
m+2
projections

\check{C}({S\to X})([{m+1}])=\underbrace{S\times_{X}\times\ldots\times_{X}S}_{m+2\text{ times }}\to\underbrace{S\times_{X}\times\ldots\times_{X}S}_{m+1\text{ times }}=\check{C}(S\to X)([m])

and in particular has norm
\leq m+2
.
Suppose
f\in\ker(d_{n})
and choose
j\in J
and

g_{0}\in[\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),\mathbb{R}]_{n}

with
||g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}-f||<\frac{\epsilon}{4^{n}}||f||
. This is possible since

{\underset{j}{\operatorname{colim}}}[\check{C}(S_{j}\to X_{j}),\mathbb{R}]_{n}\subseteq[\check{C}(S\to X),\mathbb{R}]_{n}

is dense (
Lemma

A.6.1
).
As
d_{n}
has norm
\leq n+2
,

||d_{n}(g_{0}\circ\pi_{j})||=||d_{n}(g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}-f)||\leq(n+2)||g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}-f||<\frac{n+2}{4^{n}}\epsilon||f||.

Choose
k\to j\in J
such that
\operatorname{Im}(\pi_{j}\colon S\to S_{j})=\operatorname{Im}(S_{k}\to S_{j})
. This exists by
Lemma

2.4.17
.
Then

||g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}||_{S}=||g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j})||_{S_{k}}

and

||d_{n}(g_{0}\circ\pi_{j})||_{S}=||d_{n}g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j})||_{S_{k}}.

As
h_{k,n+1}\colon[\check{C}(S_{k}\to X_{k}),\mathbb{R}]_{n+1}\to[\check{C}(S_{k}\to X_{k}),\mathbb{R}]_{n}
has norm
\leq 1
, it follows that

||h_{k,n+1}(d_{n}(g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j})))||_{S_{k}}\leq||d_{n}(g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j}))||_{S_{k}}=||d_{n}(g_{0}\circ\pi_{j})||_{S}<\frac{n+2}{4^{n}}\epsilon||f||_{S}.

Let

b\coloneqq h_{k,n}(g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j}))\circ\pi_{k}.

Since
h_{k,n}
has norm
\leq 1
,

||b||_{S}\leq||g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j})\circ\pi_{k}||_{S}=||g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}||_{S}\leq||f||_{S}+||g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}-f||_{S}<||f||_{S}+\frac{\epsilon}{4^{n}}||f||_{S}<(1+\epsilon)||f||_{S}.

As
\operatorname{id}_{[\check{C}(S_{k}\to X_{k}),\mathbb{R}]_{n}}=d_{n-1}h_{k,n}+h_{k,n+1}d_{n}
,

d_{n-1}b=g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}-(h_{k,n+1}d_{n}(g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j})))\circ\pi_{k},

whence

\displaystyle||f-d_{n-1}b||_{S}

\displaystyle\leq||f-g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}||_{S}+||(h_{k,n+1}d_{n}(g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j})))\circ\pi_{k}||_{S}

\displaystyle\leq||f-g_{0}\circ\pi_{j}||_{S}+||(h_{k,n+1}d_{n}(g_{0}\circ(S_{k}\to S_{j})))||_{S_{k}}

\displaystyle<(\frac{1}{4^{n}}+\frac{n+2}{4^{n}})\epsilon||f||_{S}\leq\epsilon||f||_{S}

by the above.
This proves the claim for
X
profinite.

Suppose now that
X
is a general compact Hausdorff space.
For
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
let

S(n)\coloneqq\check{\mathcal{C}}(S\to X)([n])=\underbrace{S\times_{X}\ldots\times_{X}S}_{n+1\text{ times }}.

Fix
n\in\mathbb{N}_{1}
.
For
x\in X
,
\check{C}(S\to X)\times_{X}\{x\}\cong\check{C}(S\times_{X}\{x\}\to\{x\})
. As
S\times_{X}\{x\}
is profinite, the above applied to
\tilde{\epsilon}\coloneqq\frac{\epsilon}{4}
shows that for all
x\in X
, there exists
b_{x}\colon S(n-1)\times_{X}\{x\}\to\mathbb{R}
with
(d_{n-1}b_{x})(x)=f_{n}(x)
and

||b_{x}||\leq\frac{1+\tilde{\epsilon}}{1-\tilde{\epsilon}}||f||_{S({n-1})\times_{X}\{x\}}<(1+\epsilon)||f||_{S({n-1})}.

By Tietzes extension theorem we can extend
b_{x}
to a map
\tilde{b}_{x}\colon S({n-1})\to\mathbb{R}
with

||\tilde{b}_{x}||_{S({n-1})}\leq||b_{x}||_{S(n-1)\times_{X}\{x\}}<(1+\epsilon)||f||.

Choose an open neighbourhood
x\in U_{x}\subseteq X
such that
||d_{n-1}\tilde{b}_{x}-f||_{S({n-1})\times_{X}U_{x}}<\epsilon||f||_{X}
.
By compactness of
X
we find
x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}\in S(n)
such that
X=\bigcup_{j=1}^{k}U_{x_{j}}
. Choose a partition of unity
1=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\rho_{j}
subordinate to this cover, i.e. for all
1\leq j\leq k
,
\rho_{j}\colon X\to[0,1]
has closed support contained in
U_{j}
.
For
1\leq j\leq k
let

\rho^{n-1}_{j}\colon S({n-1})\to X\xrightarrow{\rho_{j}}[0,1]

and define
\rho^{n}_{j}
analogously.
Let
b\coloneqq\sum_{j=1}^{k}\rho^{n-1}_{j}\tilde{b}_{x_{j}}
.
Then

||b||\leq\max_{j=1,\ldots,k}||\tilde{b}_{x_{j}}||<(1+\epsilon)||f||

and
d_{n-1}(b)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\rho^{n}_{j}d_{n-1}(\tilde{b}_{x_{j}})
, whence

||f-d_{n-1}(b)||=||\sum_{j=1}^{k}\rho_{j}(f-d_{n-1}\tilde{b}_{x_{j}})||<\epsilon||f||.

This proves the claim for
X
compact Hausdorff.
∎

Corollary A.6.4

(
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2, 3.3]
)
.

(i)

If
X
is a (
\kappa
-light) profinite space and
A
is a product of a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space with a discrete abelian group, then
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{C}(X,A)
is concentrated in degree
0
.

(ii)

If
X
is a compact Hausdorff space and
A
is a finite-dimensional normed
\mathbb{R}
-vector space, then
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{(\kappa-)cond}}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{C}(X,A)
is concentrated in degree
0
.

Proof.

We proceed as in the proofs of
[
CS19a
, Theorem 3.2, 3.3]
. By
2.5.4
, it suffices to prove the
\kappa
-condensed statement.
Recall from
2.3.7
that
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})\cong\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\operatorname{cond}}(\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa})

is equivalent to the category of hypersheaves on
\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
with respect to the topology generated by finite, jointly surjective maps.

Lemma

2.1.12
implies that the covers
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
with
I
finite and
\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
are cofinal among the covers of this topology on
\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
.
This implies the following, see e.g.
[
Sta22
,
Tag 03F9
]
:
Suppose
F\in\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Ab})
and
X\in\operatorname{CH}_{\kappa}
. If for all covers
\{X_{i}\to X\}_{i\in I}
with
I
finite and
\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\in\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{\operatorname{Fin}})_{\kappa}
, the Čech complex
[\check{C}(\{X_{i}\to X\}),F]
, that is the unnormalized Moore complex (
[
Lur17
, Definition 1.2.3.8]
) of the cosimplicial abelian group

\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{Set})}(\check{C}(\sqcup_{i\in I}\underline{X_{i}}_{\kappa}\to\underline{X}_{\kappa}),F)=F(\check{C}(\sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}\to X)),

is a resolution of
F(X)
, then
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{*}(\underline{X}_{\kappa},F)=F(X)
is concentrated in degree
0
.

It now follows from
Lemmas

A.6.3
and
2.2.7
that for
A
discrete and
X

\kappa
-light profinite,
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(X,A)=A(X)=\mathcal{C}(X,A)
is concentrated in degree
0
. Analogously, for
X

\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff and
A=\mathbb{R}
,
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(X,A)=A(X)=\mathcal{C}(X,A)
is concentrated in degree
0
.
As condensed cohomology commutes with products in the coefficient groups, this implies the statement.
∎

Recollection A.6.5

(Stalk functors)
.

Suppose
x\in X
is a point. The inclusion
i_{x}\colon\{x\}\subseteq X
defines a morphism of sites
\operatorname{Op}(X)\to\operatorname{Op}(\{x\})
.
Denote by
x^{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}(X)\to\operatorname{Shv}(\{x\})\cong\operatorname{An}\colon x_{*},x^{*}\dashv x_{*}
the induced geometric morphism (
A.4.12
).

As
x^{*}
is the left Kan extension of

\displaystyle\operatorname{Op}(X)\to\operatorname{An},U\mapsto\begin{cases}*&x\in U\\
&x\notin U\end{cases}

along the Yoneda embedding
h_{U}\colon\operatorname{Op}(X)\to\operatorname{Shv}(X)
,

x^{*}(-)={\underset{x\in U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Shv}(X)}(h_{U},-).

By
[
Lur17
, Lemma A.3.9]
, the stalk functors
x^{*}\colon\operatorname{Shv}(X)\to\operatorname{An}
jointly detect
\infty
-connective morphisms.
In particular, the induced functors
x^{*}\colon\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}(X)}\to\operatorname{An},x\in X
are jointly conservative.

For
x\in X
denote by
(-)_{x}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}(X))\to\operatorname{Sp}
the stabilization of
x^{*}
.
As for all
U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)
,
\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{Shv}(X)}(h_{U},-)\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}(X))\to\operatorname{Sp}
is the stabilization of
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Shv}(X)}(h_{U},-)\colon\operatorname{Shv}(X)\to\operatorname{An}
and
x\in U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}
is filtered,

(-)_{x}={\underset{x\in U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\operatorname{map}_{\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}(X))}(\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}h_{U},-)={\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}x\in U\\
U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{Shv}(X)}(h_{U},-).

The inclusion
\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{Shv}(X)
stabilizes to a fully faithful functor
\operatorname{Sp}(\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}}(X))\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}(X))
.
The stalk functors
(-)_{x,\operatorname{Sp}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}(\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}}(X))\to\operatorname{Sp}
are jointly conservative: For
i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,

\Omega^{\infty-i}\circ(-)_{x}=x^{*}\circ\Omega^{\infty-i}\text{ by \lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{geometricmorphismstabilization}},

and the functors
x^{*}\circ\Omega^{\infty-i}\colon\widehat{\operatorname{Shv}}(X)\to\operatorname{An},x\in X,i\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
are jointly conservative by
[
Lur17
, Lemma A.3.9]
and
[
Lur18a
, Proposition 1.3.2.27]
.

2.5.8
is now a straightforward consequence:

Proof of
2.5.8
.

By
2.5.4
, it suffices to prove the
\kappa
-condensed statement.
Note that if
X
is (
\kappa
-light) compact Hausdorff, for all topological abelian groups
A
,
\mathcal{C}_{\kappa/k}(-,A)=\mathcal{C}(-,A)
, respectively.
By construction of the comparison map, it suffices to show that for a
\kappa
-light compact Hausdorff space
X
, the map
\pi_{0}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa}\to{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\in\operatorname{Shv}(X,\operatorname{Sp})
is an equivalence. As
{j}_{*}
is a right adjoint of a geometric morphism and
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
is hypercomplete,

{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}A\in\operatorname{hypShv}(X,\operatorname{Sp})\coloneqq\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{hypShv}(X))\subseteq\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Shv}(X))

is hypercomplete by
[
Lur09
, Proposition 6.5.1.16 (4)]
, so it suffices to show that
\pi_{k}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(A)=0
for
k\neq 0
. This can be checked on stalks (
A.6.5
).
By
Lemma

1.5.7
, the stalk at
x\in X
is

({i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa})_{x}={\underset{x\in U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{sheaf}}(U,{i}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong{\underset{x\in U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa}).

As every open neighbourhood of
x
contains a closed neighbourhood of
x
and vice versa,

{\underset{x\in U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{U}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}x\in C\\
C\text{ clsd nbhd}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{C}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})

where the colimit on the right is over the poset of closed neighbourhoods
C
of
x
in
X
.
We claim that pullback along the inclusions
x\to C
defines an isomorphism

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}x\in C\\
C\text{ clsd nbhd}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{C}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})\cong\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\{x\},\underline{A}_{\kappa})=\underline{A}_{\kappa}[0],

this then implies that
\pi_{k}{j}_{*,\operatorname{Sp}}(A)=0
for
k\neq 0
.

As both sides commute with finite products in
A
, it suffices to prove this for
A=\mathbb{R}
and
A
discrete.
If
A=\mathbb{R}
, then

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{C}_{\kappa},\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\cong\mathcal{C}(C,\mathbb{R})

is concentrated in degree
0
by
A.6.4
, whence

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}x\in C\\
C\text{ clsd nbhd}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}(\underline{C}_{\kappa},\underline{\mathbb{R}}_{\kappa})\cong{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}x\in C\\
C\text{ clsd nbhd}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(C,\mathbb{R})\cong{\underset{{x\in U\in\operatorname{Op}(X)^{\operatorname{op}}}}{\operatorname{colim}}}\mathcal{C}(U,\mathbb{R})\cong\mathcal{C}(\{x\},\mathbb{R}).

Suppose now that
A
is discrete and choose a continuous surjection
Y\to X
from a
\kappa
-light profinite set. This exists by
Lemma

2.1.12
. Then
\check{C}(q)\to X
is a condensed hypercover of
X
by
\kappa
-light profinite sets, and for a closed subspace
Z\subseteq X
,

q_{Z}\colon\underline{Z\times_{Y}X}_{\kappa}\to\underline{Z}_{\kappa}

is an effective epimorphism in
\operatorname{Cond}_{\kappa}(\operatorname{An})
.
As for all
m\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
,
\check{C}(q_{Z})([m])=\underline{\check{C}(q)([m])\times_{X}Z}_{\kappa}
and
\check{C}(q)([m])\times_{X}Z
is a
\kappa
-light profinite space (as closed subspace of the
\kappa
-light profinite space
Y^{m+1}
),
A.6.4
and
1.5.13
imply that for a closed subspace
Z\subseteq X
,

\mathbb{H}_{\operatorname{\kappa-cond}}^{q}(\underline{Z}_{\kappa},\underline{A}_{\kappa})=H^{q}([\check{C}(Y\times_{X}Z\to Z),A])

is the cohomology of the unnormalized Moore complex (
[
Lur17
, Definition 1.2.3.8]
) of the cosimplicial abelian group
\mathcal{C}(\check{C}(Y\times_{X}Z\to Z),A)
.
Since
A
is discrete, the map

{\underset{\begin{subarray}{c}x\in C\\
C\text{ clsd nbhd}\end{subarray}}{\operatorname{colim}}}[\check{C}(Y\times_{X}C\to C),A]\to[\check{C}(Y\times_{X}\{x\}\to\{x\}),A]

is an isomorphism of chain complexes.
∎
